jobs.title: THECB - Director of IT Operations (ITS)
jobs.description:
About the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board

The Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board (THECB) works to ensure that all Texans have access to high-quality, affordable higher education opportunities that prepare students for successful careers and strengthen the state's workforce and economy. Through collaboration with colleges, universities, policymakers, and education partners across Texas, THECB advances initiatives that expand educational opportunity, promote student success, and support the future of higher education.
About Information Technology Services

The Information Technology Services (ITS) Division advances THECB's mission by delivering secure, reliable, and customer-focused technology services that enable agency staff to effectively serve Texas students, institutions, and communities.
Our organization is committed to operational excellence through modern technology, strong governance, strategic partnerships, and continuous improvement. We are modernizing how technology services are delivered by strengthening infrastructure and operational resilience, advancing cloud-first and hybrid infrastructure, improving platform reliability and security, and building a culture centered on accountability, collaboration, innovation, and service excellence.
At THECB, we believe technology is more than infrastructure and support. It is a strategic business partner that enables our agency to better serve students, institutions, and the State of Texas.
About the Role

The Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board is seeking an experienced and collaborative technology leader to serve as the Director of IT Operations. Reporting to the Senior Director of Technology, this position is a key member of the Information Technology Services leadership team and provides strategic leadership and oversight for the agency's IT operations function, including infrastructure, networks, platforms, and enterprise support systems.
The Director is responsible for ensuring the stability, performance, security, and scalability of the technology environment that enables agency business operations and advances THECB's mission, strategic priorities, and service objectives. This position establishes the strategic direction for IT operations by developing goals, objectives, operational policies, procedures, standards, service delivery practices, and performance measures that promote reliable, secure, and efficient technology operations across the agency.
Responsibilities include directing enterprise IT operations and service delivery; overseeing operational risk management, security practices, disaster recovery, and continuity planning; directing financial planning, budgeting, and cost optimization for IT operations; managing vendor relationships, service agreements, and statements of work with external service providers for infrastructure and operational support services; and providing leadership for operational governance, regulatory compliance, and organizational change.
Working collaboratively with ITS leadership, IT Service Delivery, Product Management, Product Engineering, Data Engineering, the Project Management Office (PMO), and agency stakeholders, the Director helps align operational services with business needs and long-term technology strategy while ensuring the consistent delivery of the key platforms and services that agency teams rely on.
This position supervises management and professional staff and exercises significant initiative and independent judgment while serving as a trusted advisor on IT operations, infrastructure, cloud modernization, and operational resilience.
Why Join Our Team

This is an exciting opportunity to help shape how the technology environment that supports the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board is operated, secured, and modernized.
As a member of the ITS leadership team, you'll play a critical role in advancing cloud modernization, strengthening infrastructure and security operations, improving operational resilience, and building a high-performing team focused on delivering reliable, secure, and scalable technology platforms and services.
In this role, you'll have the opportunity to:
Lead the agency's infrastructure and cloud strategy, including the move from on-premises to private and public cloud environments.
Build, mentor, and develop high-performing engineers, administrators, and managers across networking, systems, platforms, and security engineering while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Strengthen operational resilience through disaster recovery, continuity planning, and security practices that protect agency systems and data.
Establish operational standards, service levels, and performance measures that improve reliability and support executive decision-making.
Strengthen the partnership between IT Service Delivery, Product Engineering, Data Engineering, Product Management, and the PMO to deliver the key platforms and services agency teams depend on.
Make a lasting impact by helping technology enable the agency's mission of expanding educational opportunity and supporting higher education across Texas.
If you are passionate about developing people, modernizing infrastructure, strengthening operational resilience, and building technology operations that create measurable business value, we encourage you to apply.
General Description:

Performs highly advanced (senior-level) managerial work for the Information Technology Services (ITS) Division of the Texas Higher Education Coordinating Board (THECB). Serving as the Director of IT Operations, this position provides strategic leadership and oversight for the agency's IT operations function, including infrastructure, networks, platforms, and enterprise support systems. The position is responsible for ensuring the stability, performance, security, and scalability of the technology environment that enables agency business operations and advances the agency's mission, strategic priorities, and service objectives.
Work involves establishing strategic plans, goals, and objectives for IT operations; developing operational policies, procedures, standards, and service delivery practices; and establishing priorities, performance measures, and evaluation tools to assess operational effectiveness, system availability, and service quality.
Responsibilities include directing enterprise IT operations and service delivery; overseeing operational risk management, security practices, disaster recovery, and continuity planning; directing financial planning, budgeting, and cost optimization for IT operations; managing vendor relationships, service agreements, and statements of work with external service providers for infrastructure and operational support services; and providing leadership for operational governance, regulatory compliance, and organizational change. Collaborates with ITS leadership and agency stakeholders to align operational services with business needs and long-term technology strategy, and provides operational input into agency-wide planning efforts.
Supervises the work of others, including management and professional staff. Works under minimal supervision, with extensive latitude for the use of initiative and independent judgment. This position reports to the Senior Director of Technology. Performs other duties as assigned.
General Duties and Responsibilities:

Strategic People Leadership & Talent Strategy - Leads managers, senior individual contributors, or a combination of both by setting leadership expectations, supporting performance management, and guiding workforce and succession planning. Develops leadership capability and subject-matter expertise; aligns talent to strategic needs; and fosters a culture of accountability, inclusion, and continuous improvement.
Strategic Execution, Governance & Resource Alignment - Defines and oversees execution of strategies within assigned domains by establishing goals, priorities, standards, and performance measures. Aligns budgets, staffing, and resources to objectives; ensures compliance and governance; and monitors organizational performance to achieve agency outcomes.
IT Operations & Service Delivery Leadership - Directs enterprise IT operations and service delivery functions that support agency infrastructure, platforms, and end-user technology services. Establishes operational standards and performance expectations to ensure reliable, secure, and efficient technology services that support agency programs and mission-critical activities.
Operational Risk, Security & Continuity Management - Oversees operational practices that protect the integrity, availability, and security of enterprise technology services. Establishes standards and procedures that support operational resilience, risk mitigation, and continuity of services while ensuring alignment with regulatory requirements, internal policies, and enterprise governance expectations.
Financial, Vendor & Resource Management - Directs financial planning, budgeting, and resource allocation for IT operations. Oversees vendor relationships, contractual service agreements, and external service providers to ensure operational services are delivered efficiently and in alignment with organizational objectives and fiscal accountability standards.
Enterprise Collaboration & Operational Alignment - Collaborates with IT leadership, agency executives, and business stakeholders to align operational technology services with organizational priorities. Provides operational insight into agency planning efforts and ensures IT services remain responsive to evolving business and mission requirements.
Performs other duties as assigned.
Knowledge Skills or Abilities:

Knowledge of enterprise infrastructure architecture and operations, including on-premises, private cloud, and public cloud environments.
Knowledge of cloud migration and infrastructure modernization strategies, including rehosting, replatforming, and hybrid cloud approaches.
Knowledge of cloud platforms, such as AWS, Azure, or comparable solutions, and enterprise networking technologies, including connectivity, segmentation, and network security.
Knowledge of systems and platform administration, including servers, virtualization, identity, storage, backup, monitoring, and infrastructure automation.
Knowledge of security engineering, operational risk management, disaster recovery, and business continuity practices within enterprise environments.
Knowledge of IT governance, security, and compliance practices related to infrastructure operations and service delivery.
Skill in leading infrastructure, network, systems, and security engineering teams operating across on-premises, private cloud, and public cloud environments.
Skill in evaluating and guiding hosting, platform, and cloud versus on-premises decisions within enterprise environments.
Skill in managing IT budgets, vendor relationships, service agreements, and statements of work.
Skill in providing hands-on technical leadership, including guiding design, reviewing solutions, and supporting teams through complex challenges.
Skill in coaching and developing engineers and managers to improve technical capability and operational practices.
Skill in managing and prioritizing work across a unified portfolio and roadmap.
Skill in collaborating effectively across IT Service Delivery, Product Management, Product Engineering, Data Engineering, PMO, business, and executive stakeholders.
Ability to provide strategic direction for enterprise infrastructure and operations while remaining actively engaged in technical decision-making and delivery.
Ability to drive modernization through cloud migration and adoption of cloud-native, automated, and hybrid infrastructure solutions where appropriate.

jobs.title: Chief Information Security Officer
jobs.description:
DLA Piper is, at its core, bold, exceptional, collaborative and supportive. Our people are the backbone, heart and soul of our firm. Wherever you are in your professional journey, DLA Piper is a place you can engage in meaningful work and grow your career. Let’s see what we can achieve. Together.

Summary

The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), working in collaboration with and in support of the firm’s strategic initiatives, is a senior executive responsible for protecting DLA Piper’s clients, people, data, reputation, and global business operations by leading a mature, business-aligned information security and cyber risk program. This role sets the strategic direction for the firm’s Information Security Management System, security governance, risk management, incident response, third-party security, data protection, and security awareness programs.

Operating as a trusted advisor to firm leadership, the Office of General Counsel, Information Technology, Information Governance, Risk Management, practice leadership, and global counterparts, the CISO ensures the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of client and firm information while enabling innovation, responsible AI adoption, operational resilience, and exceptional client service. The CISO works closely with, but independently from, the Information Technology function to provide objective risk oversight, policy leadership, executive reporting, and continuous improvement of the firm’s security posture.

Location

This position can sit in our Atlanta, Baltimore, Boston, Chicago, Miami, New York, Northern Virginia, Philadelphia, Raleigh, Short Hills, Washington D.C., or Wilmington office. Candidates must reside within a reasonable commuting distance of their assigned office and be available for periodic travel.

Responsibilities

Sets and executes the enterprise information security strategy for DLA Piper, aligning cyber risk management with firm strategy, client obligations, professional responsibility requirements, regulatory expectations, and operational resilience objectives.
Sets and executes the enterprise information security strategy for DLA Piper, aligning cyber risk management with firm strategy, client obligations, professional responsibility requirements, regulatory expectations, and operational resilience objectives.
Leads the firm’s Information Security Management System and security governance framework, including policy development, risk assessment, control monitoring, executive reporting, audit readiness, certification support, and continuous improvement.
Serves as the senior incident response leader for information security events, ensuring prompt triage, containment, investigation, evidence preservation, root-cause analysis, remediation, lessons learned, and appropriate coordination with the Office of General Counsel, firm leadership, insurers, regulators, law enforcement, vendors, and affected clients when required.
Partners with executive leadership, Information Technology, AI Innovation, AI Governance, Information Governance, Risk Management, Privacy, Procurement, Finance, Human Resources, practice leaders, and global counterparts to embed security-by-design into firm operations, technology investments, client service delivery, and major transformation initiatives.
Provides objective cyber risk advice to firm leadership and governance bodies, translating complex technical risk into clear business, legal, reputational, operational, and client-impact terms that enable timely and informed decision-making.
Oversees enterprise cyber risk identification, assessment, treatment, acceptance, and reporting, including vulnerabilities, threat intelligence, identity and access risk, cloud and infrastructure security, application security, data loss prevention, endpoint protection, email security, ransomware preparedness, and business continuity dependencies.
Leads security oversight of client and firm confidential information, including data classification, access controls, encryption, retention, secure disposal, cross-border data considerations, ethical walls, client outside counsel guidelines, and matter-specific security obligations.
Directs third-party and supplier security risk management in partnership with Procurement, Information Technology, Information Governance, and business owners, ensuring vendors that access firm or client data are assessed, monitored, and held to appropriate security, privacy, contractual, and operational standards.
Guides security review and risk oversight for emerging technologies, cloud services, legal technology, artificial intelligence, automation, analytics, and internally developed tools, ensuring innovation is deployed responsibly and in compliance with firm policies, client requirements, and applicable legal and ethical obligations.
Builds, develops, and leads a high-performing information security organization with the expertise, credibility, accountability, and service orientation required to support a complex, global, partner led professional services environment.
Defines and manages the Information Security team’s operating model, including functional roles, accountability structures, governance routines, service levels, intake and prioritization processes, escalation protocols, on-call expectations, and coordination with Information Technology, Risk, Information Governance, Privacy, Procurement, Human Resources, and practice leadership.
Recruits, develops, coaches, and retains a high-caliber Information Security team with the technical depth, risk judgment, executive presence, discretion, and client-service mindset required to operate effectively in a global law firm environment.
Sets clear goals and performance expectations for the Information Security team, regularly assesses performance against strategic objectives and operational metrics, addresses performance gaps, recognizes strong contributions, and ensures the team has the training, tools, resources, and authority needed to execute effectively.
Provides strategic, operational, and people leadership to the Information Security function, including direct and indirect leadership of security professionals, managers, analysts, advisors, vendors, and cross-functional contributors.
Defines the team’s vision, operating model, service standards, decision rights, escalation paths, and priorities to ensure the function delivers consistent, timely, risk-based, and business-aligned support across the firm. Builds a culture of accountability, confidentiality, trust, excellence, service orientation, continuous improvement, inclusion, and business partnership.
Responsible for onboarding, coaching, performance management, succession planning, professional development, retention, resource allocation, budget input, vendor oversight, and effective delegation across the security program.

Desired Skills  

Deep technical engineering expertise in technology infrastructure, Cloud, zero-trust architecture and cyber defense. Proven ability to leverage frameworks like NIST to build and operate a comprehensive defense in depth capability. Proven ability in change management, building trust with partners and transforming organizations. Experience in a global law firm, professional services firm, financial services institution, technology company, or similarly complex environment strongly preferred. Demonstrated success leading cybersecurity strategy, enterprise risk governance, incident response, regulatory and client-facing security matters, third-party risk, audit/certification programs, security awareness, and high performing teams. Experience advising senior executives, boards, managing partners, or equivalent governance bodies required.

Executive-level knowledge of cybersecurity strategy, governance, risk, compliance, privacy, data protection, incident response, threat intelligence, vulnerability management, identity and access management, cloud and network security, application security, endpoint protection, email security, encryption, logging and monitoring, disaster recovery, business continuity, third-party risk, DevSecOps, modernized secure development practices including AI SDLC, and secure technology adoption. Strong understanding of professional responsibility, client confidentiality, data classification, privilege-sensitive work, outside counsel guidelines, ethical walls, cross-border data considerations, and the security expectations of sophisticated global clients.

Demonstrated ability to translate technical risk into business and legal impact, influence senior stakeholders, lead through ambiguity, make sound risk-based decisions, and communicate with clarity, credibility, discretion, and urgency. Familiarity with ISO/IEC 27001, NIST, CIS Controls, data privacy laws, cyber insurance considerations, AI governance, and emerging legal sector cybersecurity risks strongly preferred. A leader who thrives on learning and is up to date with the fast-evolving technology landscape, especially the changing threats with the advancement of AI. Ability to not only understand security tools/needs, how these are changing but also go back to first principles in solving the underlying problems through innovation.

Demonstrate executive presence, credibility, sound judgment, and professional maturity in all interactions, particularly when advising firm leadership, senior partners, governance bodies, clients, regulators, vendors, and other high-impact stakeholders on sensitive, complex, or time-critical information security matters. Communicate with clarity, confidence, discretion, and appropriate urgency, translating complex technical, legal, operational, and risk issues into concise business terms that enable informed decisions by senior leaders and non-technical audiences. Influence senior leaders and stakeholders through trusted relationships, fact-based analysis, persuasive recommendations, and a firm-first approach that balances client expectations, legal and regulatory obligations, operational realities, risk appetite, and strategic business priorities.

Build alignment across a complex, matrixed, partner-led environment by listening effectively, anticipating concerns, managing competing perspectives, escalating appropriately, and helping leaders reach timely, defensible, and consistently supported decisions. Prepare and deliver executive-level briefings, written updates, risk narratives, Executive Committee materials, client-facing responses, and incident communications that are accurate, audience-appropriate, concise, and aligned with firm standards and confidentiality obligations. Lead difficult or sensitive conversations with diplomacy, composure, courage, and empathy, including situations involving cyber incidents, policy exceptions, risk acceptance, resource tradeoffs, control gaps, or competing leadership priorities.

Minimum Education   

Bachelor’s Degree in Information Security, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, Business, Risk Management, Law, or a related field; equivalent senior leadership experience may be considered, where appropriate.

Preferred Education   

Master’s Degree in MBA, M.S. in Cybersecurity/Information Security, J.D., or other relevant advanced degree preferred.

Certificates

Relevant professional certifications are strongly preferred, such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC, CCISO, GIAC, ISO/IEC 27001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor, or comparable credentials. Demonstrated ongoing professional development in cybersecurity, privacy, risk governance, incident response, cloud security, AI governance, and legal/professional services risk is expected.

Minimum Years Of Experience  

15+ years’ progressive information security, cybersecurity, technology risk, privacy, compliance, or enterprise risk leadership experience, including significant executive-level responsibility for a complex, highly regulated, client-facing organization.

Essential Job Expectations

jobs.title: Senior Vice President, AI & Technology Programs
jobs.description:
Zeno Group is the fiercely independent and global, integrated communications agency, born from PR. We bring together the boldest and brightest talent to help clients across industries and sectors unleash the power of strategic communications. Guided by our "Fearless Pursuit of the Unexpected," we push the boundaries to achieve real business value and societal impact for clients. Winner of the industry’s most coveted awards including the 2024 PRWeek U.S. Outstanding Large Agency of the Year, 2023 PRWeek Purpose Agency of the Year, 2022 PRWeek Global Agency of the Year, 2022 PRovoke Best Large Agency to Work For in North America and a three-time winner of PRWeek’s Best Places to Work. Zeno has also been previously recognized by the Cannes Lions International Festival of Creativity. Zeno is a DJE Holdings Company.

Job Description

SVP, AI & Technology Programs

Do you enjoy helping teams rethink how work gets done? Are you energized by guiding organizations through change, facilitating complex conversations and helping people adopt new ways of working through AI and emerging technologies?

As a SVP, AI & Technology Programs at Zeno, you will play a key role in accelerating AI adoption and business transformation across the agency. Working closely with the Head of AI & Innovation, practice leaders and client teams, you will help identify opportunities where AI can create meaningful impact, design solutions that fit real-world workflows and lead programs that drive lasting change.

This is an opportunity for a strategic and hands-on leader to shape how AI is adopted across the organization, build internal capabilities and help define the future of AI-enabled communications and client service.

The Team You're Joining

AI & Innovation is a growing team building a new practice inside a large organization. We move fast, cover a lot of ground, and hold ourselves to a high standard.

Craft over speed. Efficiency is table stakes. Everyone has the same AI tools. We take every hour AI saves and reinvest it in work that wasn't possible before. The bar is high because the stakes are high.
Build what others can't access. What separates us is the proprietary systems, methodology, and data we build in-house. We license tools when they solve the problem. But the work that differentiates Zeno is built here.
Makers who can hold a room. This role is not heads-down. You'll be facilitating workshops with client teams, presenting to senior leadership, and sitting across from practitioners who need you to understand their work before you prescribe anything. We look for people who are strong technically and equally comfortable communicating what they know to people who don't share their vocabulary.

About The Role

AI Transformation & Program Leadership: Lead workflow transformation programs across Zeno's offices, helping teams identify opportunities to improve how work gets done through AI, automation and emerging technologies.
Workshop Facilitation & Change Management: Facilitate working sessions with teams and stakeholders to map workflows, identify opportunities for improvement and drive alignment around solutions, ownership and implementation plans.
AI Enablement & Training: Design and deliver training programs, workshops and best practices that help employees build confidence, strengthen capabilities and adopt AI-powered ways of working.
Technology Evaluation & Adoption: Evaluate AI tools, platforms and vendor solutions, providing recommendations based on business needs, workflow impact and long-term organizational value.
AI Adoption & Organizational Effectiveness: Monitor adoption, identify barriers and refine programs that drive lasting behavioral change and measurable outcomes.
Client Innovation & Strategic Guidance: Support client teams in AI-related conversations, helping navigate usage standards, implementation considerations and opportunities to enhance client work through AI-enabled solutions.
Governance & Cross-Agency Collaboration: Help ensure AI tools and workflows align with company policies, responsible AI practices and data privacy requirements while partnering with sister agencies on shared initiatives and learning opportunities.

About You

15+ years of experience in technology, operations, consulting, organizational transformation or related fields, including experience leading AI, automation or digital transformation initiatives.
Proven success facilitating workshops and leading large-scale business transformation initiatives across cross-functional teams.
Exceptional communication and presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex technologies into clear, actionable recommendations that build confidence and trust.
Experience engaging with practitioners, client teams and senior leaders, adapting communication styles to meet the needs of different audiences.
Strong understanding of AI tools and their practical applications within business environments, with the ability to evaluate solutions based on workflow impact and organizational needs.
Experience assessing technology solutions and making recommendations regarding implementation, adoption and change management.
Demonstrated ability to drive alignment, maintain momentum and deliver results across complex initiatives.
Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholder groups.
Understanding of communications, marketing, media or professional services environments and the realities of client-service organizations.
Curious, collaborative mindset with a passion for learning, problem solving and helping teams embrace new ways of working.
Commitment to responsible AI adoption and creating meaningful business impact through technology.

Preferred Qualifications

Background in change management, organizational development or business transformation.
Experience designing and delivering training programs across large organizations.
Familiarity with AI governance, responsible AI frameworks and emerging industry best practices.
Experience evaluating and selecting technology platforms for organization-wide deployment.
Prior experience within public relations, communications, advertising, marketing or related agency environments.

jobs.description:
Description

Customer Logistics Security (CLS) protects the physical and digital infrastructure that moves every Amazon package. We are looking for a Technical Program Manager to drive security program execution across Operational Technology (OT) and infrastructure environments, coordinating with engineering teams, business stakeholders, and external partners to deliver outcomes that reduce risk at scale.

You will own the day-to-day execution of cross-functional security programs, managing dependencies, timelines, and stakeholder alignment across internal and external teams.
You will establish and run operating mechanisms that keep programs on track and leadership informed.
You will operate in a space where security requirements intersect with industrial systems, network infrastructure, and physical operations, requiring you to build context quickly and translate between technical and business audiences.

Key job responsibilities

Own end-to-end execution of security programs from planning through delivery, managing scope, timelines, dependencies, and risks across multiple teams.
Establish and maintain operating mechanisms (status cadences, tracking artifacts, escalation paths) that create visibility and drive accountability.
Coordinate with internal engineering teams and external stakeholders to align priorities, secure commitments, and unblock delivery.
Identify and resolve cross-team dependencies and conflicts before they become blockers, escalating with data when needed.
Translate technical security problems into structured program plans with clear milestones, owners, and success criteria.
Drive closure on action items, decisions, and deliverables, ensuring programs maintain momentum through competing priorities.
Communicate program status, risks, and trade-offs to leadership in a clear, concise format that enables decision-making.
Contribute to process improvement by identifying recurring friction in program execution and building mechanisms to prevent it.

About The Team

The OT & Infrastructure Security (OTIS) team is part of Customer Logistics Security (CLS). We secure the operational technology and network infrastructure that powers Amazon's fulfillment, sortation, and delivery network. Our scope includes industrial control systems, facility networks, and the security architecture that protects them. We operate at the intersection of physical operations and cybersecurity, which means the problems are tangible, the scale is massive, and the work matters immediately. The team is collaborative, direct, and outcome-oriented. We value clarity over ceremony, shipped results over activity, and people who build mechanisms that outlast any single project.

Diverse Experiences

Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why Amazon Security?

At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.

Inclusive Team Culture

In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.

Training & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Basic Qualifications

Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
3+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
3+ years of technical product or program management experience

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with programming/scripting (Batch, VB, PowerShell, Java, C#, Chef, Perl, Ruby and/or PHP), or experience in Database like NoSQL and experience managing full application stacks from the OS up through custom applications
Project Management Professional (PMP) or equivalent certification
Experience in a logistics/operations environment
Experience in security, infrastructure, or operational technology domains
Experience managing programs with external stakeholders or partner organizations
Experience with risk-based prioritization and trade-off analysis
Familiarity with industrial control systems, network security, or physical security environments
Experience writing narratives or program documents for senior leadership audiences

As the **Director of IT Infrastructure & Operations** at Brooks Safety Solutions, you will lead the core engine of our enterprise technology ecosystem across Brooks Safety Solutions and its affiliated brands. Reporting directly to the CTO, you will own the end-to-end architecture, reliability, and security of our multi-brand corporate networks, server environments, and IT service desk operations.

We are seeking a hands-on, proactive leader with a strong networking background. In the near term, this role is tactical: learning our current environment, closing gaps (particularly in the network), and keeping critical systems running. Over time, you will own the infrastructure roadmap and help move the technical team from reacting to problems to preventing them.

**Key Responsibilities**

**People Leadership & Organizational Scaling**

* Lead, mentor, and grow a six-member technical team, spanning Network Engineering, Systems/Cloud Engineering, Desktop Support, and IT Service Desk.
* Define career progressions, set technical standards, and shift the team from reactive to proactive: finding and fixing issues before they affect the business.
* Identify skill gaps and scale the team through strategic hiring, structured onboarding, and continuous training.

* Set the strategic roadmap for on-premises, hybrid, and cloud infrastructure across all Brooks Safety Solutions brand locations, plants, and field offices.
* Lead the migration from data center-based infrastructure to Microsoft Azure, including hybrid connectivity between on-premises networks and Azure.
* Supervise core network engineering: SD-WAN, LAN/WLAN, routing/switching, firewalls, and secure site-to-site connectivity.
* Direct server and platform administration across Azure, VMware/hypervisors, Windows/Linux server stacks, Active Directory/Entra ID, Microsoft 365, and enterprise backup/DR pipelines.
* Support the infrastructure behind the company’s move to Microsoft Dynamics 365 (D365).
* Guarantee high availability, low downtime, and rapid RTO/RPO targets for mission-critical manufacturing and enterprise systems.

**End-User Services & IT Help Desk Excellence**

* Own enterprise IT service management (ITSM), establishing clear SLAs, ticketing processes, hardware lifecycles, and automated provisioning workflows.
* Drive first-touch resolution rates and ensure white-glove, customer-obsessed support for all brand business units and remote workers.

* Act as the lead negotiator and manager for all infrastructure-related vendor partnerships, MSPs, telecom/ISP carriers, software licensing, and hardware contracts.
* Monitor performance against vendor Service Level Agreements (SLAs), drive competitive RFPs, and optimize CAPEX/OPEX infrastructure budgets.

**Security, Compliance & Business Continuity**

* Partner closely with information security leadership to enforce endpoint protection, network segmentation, zero-trust principles, and vulnerability patching.
* Build, test, and continuously maintain comprehensive Disaster Recovery (DR) and Business Continuity Plans (BCP) across all operating entities.

**Qualifications & Requirements**

**Required**

* **Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.

* **Leadership:** Proven ability to lead, develop, and hire for a small technical team (Network, Systems, Desktop/Help Desk).

* **Technical Breadth:** Strong background across enterprise networking (Cisco, Fortinet, Aruba, Palo Alto), server administration (Windows Server, Linux, virtualization), and modern workplace technologies (M365, Intune/MECM).
* **Communication & Approach:** Strong communicator who can explain technical issues to business leaders. Proactive: takes ownership of problems and addresses them before they escalate.
* **Vendor & Budget Acumen:** Demonstrated success negotiating multi-year enterprise contracts, managing vendor performance, and handling seven-figure infrastructure budgets.
* **Multi-Site/Multi-Brand Operations:** Experience standardizing infrastructure across acquisitions, subsidiaries, or geographically dispersed physical sites. sites, including warehouses or distribution centers.
* **Frameworks & Methodology:** Deep familiarity with ITIL, NIST cybersecurity standards, and disaster recovery orchestration.

**Preferred**

* **Advanced Networking:** Depth beyond the required minimum, such as designing multi-site networks or leading a network redesign.
* **ERP:** Experience supporting the infrastructure for an ERP implementation; Microsoft Dynamics 365 a plus.

jobs.title: Director, Core IT Integration Delivery Lead
jobs.description:
Job Description

Grant Thornton is seeking a Director, Core IT Integration Delivery Lead to join the team. Approved office locations can be found below.

Grant Thornton GTech’s vision is centered around enabling scalable, secure, and repeatable technology integration for acquired companies. The Core IT Integration Office is responsible for integrating acquired firms into the firm’s enterprise technology environment through a standardized, factory-style model that is governed centrally, executed through partners and in-country teams, and repeatable across the acquisition portfolio.

The Director, Core IT Integration - Technical Delivery Lead owns end-to-end technical delivery across the portfolio. The role is directly accountable for five Core IT components: tenant consolidation, ServiceNow, data migration and archival, network security, and branch office integration. It leads the workstream leads who own each of those components, sets sequencing and architecture direction across them, and manages the implementation partners and in-country resources that perform the work. Seven further Core IT components are delivered by Information Security, People & Culture, and Finance. This role does not deliver those, but is accountable for the sequencing seams between them and its own scope, so that dependencies hold and no entity stalls waiting on an unmanaged handoff.

Execution is delivered through implementation partners and regional resources. The Grant Thornton team owns the standard, the plan, the readiness decisions, the quality of what is delivered, and the outcome for the business. This role directs partner delivery rather than performing it, and is expected to know the technology well enough to review designs, question estimates, validate results, and make decisions under pressure. Scope decisions anchor to four tests: security, cost optimization, standardization, and enabling Global Delivery Center support.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities:

Own the integrated technical delivery plan across the acquisition portfolio, sequencing entities into waves that balance entity priority, size, readiness, dependency, partner capacity, and business impact.
Manage concurrency across entities so that parallel execution stays within the delivery system’s throughput, and re-sequence when readiness, funding, or partner capacity changes.
Own delivery of tenant consolidation, covering migration of acquired Microsoft 365 and Entra tenants into the Grant Thornton tenant, including identity, mail, collaboration content, device management, and associated Azure subscription and workload moves.
Own delivery of ServiceNow onboarding for acquired entities, covering configuration data, service catalog and fulfillment alignment, support group structures, integrations, and transition into the enterprise support model.
Own delivery of data migration and archival, covering the Snowflake-based pipelines that feed system migrations and the durable archival of legacy data for retention, compliance, and future reuse.
Own delivery of network security, covering the Zero-Trust landing zone, regional hub readiness, segmentation, routing, and secure remote access for each acquisition.
Own delivery of branch office integration, covering connectivity, local network and endpoint baseline, site readiness, and retirement of inherited network infrastructure.
Coordinate with the owners of the remaining Core IT components, including identity directory sync, workforce systems, identity governance, security integration phases, intranet, and financial consolidation, managing dependencies and sequencing across those boundaries.
Sequence delivery to run concurrent with Information Security’s phased model rather than behind it, and manage the dependency under which full identity-driven security controls complete only after tenant consolidation.
Hold security review and sign-off as a gate before interconnect and go-live, and resist schedule pressure to bypass it.
Coordinate with the customer relationship management workstream and other capability programs that depend on Core IT sequencing, including where staffing sits outside this team.
Own and mature the integration factory model, increasing the share of each integration that runs to a standard pattern and reducing the variable component that drives cost and schedule risk.
Own the per-entity estimating model, including size banding, and maintain its accuracy by testing estimates against actuals as entities complete.
Manage cost per user and cost per entity as governed delivery metrics, working with partners and sourcing to improve unit economics as volume grows.
Prepare cost estimates, business cases, and variance analysis to support funding decisions made by Integration Office and Chief Technology Office leadership.
Direct implementation partners, systems integrators, and in-country resources through design, build, migration, cutover, and stabilization, holding delivery to enterprise standards, committed dates, and quality expectations.
Review and challenge partner designs, bills of materials, effort estimates, and delivery plans before acceptance, and confirm that what is proposed matches the standard rather than the partner’s default approach.
Support scoping, statement of work development, and commercial negotiation for integration partners, in coordination with sourcing, legal, and Integration Office leadership.
Evaluate delivery partners by region and workstream, maintaining competitive tension, regional coverage, and the ability to scale capacity up and down as the wave plan requires.
Establish readiness gates for each entity covering identity, data, endpoint, application, security, communications, and support coverage, and hold cutover decisions to documented evidence.
Lead cutover execution across workstreams, including runbooks, command center operations, go and no-go decisions, escalation paths, business validation, and defect triage.
Run hypercare after each migration, drive post-cutover issues to resolution, confirm exit criteria, and transition entities cleanly into steady-state support.
Deliver each entity into a condition that allows Global Delivery Center teams to support it at scale, and coordinate the support transition directly with the Global Delivery Center.
Track retirement of inherited infrastructure, licensing, and contracts after migration so that legacy run cost is removed rather than carried.
Run delivery to GTech project and portfolio management standards, including backlog management in Azure DevOps, integrated scheduling, RAID management, and Tier 1 program status reporting.
Represent Core IT technical delivery in enterprise Integration Management Office forums and coordinate waves with peer tracks across Information Security, Data, People & Culture, and Finance.
Provide executive-ready reporting on progress, risk, cost, partner performance, readiness, and stabilization, calling out decisions needed rather than reporting activity alone.
Lead the workstream leads accountable for tenant consolidation, ServiceNow, data migration and archival, and network and branch office integration, setting direction, priorities, and performance expectations.
Build and develop the dedicated Grant Thornton integration team, including recruiting, onboarding, capability development, and bench depth sufficient to run multiple entities concurrently.
Define the operating model between the dedicated Grant Thornton team and partner-supplied regional capacity, and adjust it as the portfolio scales.
Lead delivery across multiple countries and time zones, working through local technology leadership and in-country resources.
Account for jurisdictional requirements in entity planning, including data residency, privacy, statutory retention, local procurement, and equipment import constraints.
Build and maintain working relationships with acquired-firm technology leadership through the transition, providing enough clarity on timing and impact for local teams to plan around the work.
Advise due diligence and pre-close assessment activity led by Enterprise Architecture and other teams, contributing integration sizing, sequencing, and feasibility input without owning the assessment.
Own the post-entity lessons learned process and convert findings into playbook updates, readiness gates, estimating revisions, and backlog items visibly reflected in the next entity’s plan.
Maintain the technical delivery playbooks, standard designs, runbooks, and readiness checklists that make each successive integration faster and more predictable than the last.
Lead cross-functional teams through ambiguity, competing priorities, and acquisition-driven timelines while maintaining controls and decision discipline.
Influence stakeholders across functions without relying on formal authority, ensuring decisions are made in time to protect the schedule.
Maintain high professional standards, protect confidential acquisition information, and communicate with clarity and precision.

Qualifications & Requirements

10+ years of experience in enterprise technology delivery, infrastructure, platform implementation, or technology program leadership, including accountability for multi-workstream delivery.
Demonstrated experience leading concurrent implementations across identity, collaboration, service management, network, and data workstreams, with enough technical depth in each to review designs and make decisions without deferring.
Experience leading Microsoft 365, Entra ID, and Azure migration or consolidation programs, including tenant-to-tenant migration and the identity dependencies that govern sequencing.
Working knowledge of enterprise network security architecture, including segmentation, cloud landing zones, hub topologies, and secure remote access.
Working knowledge of enterprise service management platforms and the configuration data, support structures, and process alignment required to onboard a new entity.
Working knowledge of enterprise data migration and archival patterns, including pipeline-driven migration and long-term retention of legacy data.
Experience directing delivery through third-party implementation partners and offshore teams, including scope definition, deliverable review, estimate challenge, and performance management.
Track record of leading cutovers for business-critical platforms, including readiness criteria, go and no-go decisions, escalation management, and hypercare.
Experience building repeatable delivery models, factory approaches, or standardized playbooks applied across multiple entities or business units.
Experience leading and developing technical leaders, including workstream or team leads.
Strong planning and program management discipline, including backlog management, integrated scheduling, dependency tracking, RAID, and executive reporting.
Experience preparing cost estimates and business cases, and managing delivery against unit-cost targets.
Ability to lead delivery across multiple countries and time zones, working through local leadership and regional resources.
Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive-level decision materials and practical direction to engineering and partner teams.
Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or a related field required; advanced degree or relevant certifications preferred.

Preferred Experience

Experience supporting merger, acquisition, divestiture, or carve-out technology integration, particularly in a serial acquirer or private equity backed environment.
Experience integrating acquisitions across multiple countries, including data residency, language, telephony, procurement, and in-country support considerations.
Familiarity with the platforms in scope, including Microsoft 365 and Entra ID, Azure networking, next-generation firewall and secure access platforms, ServiceNow, and Snowflake.

jobs.title: Sr. Technical Program Manager - Open Source, Kiro
jobs.description:
Description

Kiro Labs is the public home for community-built projects in the Kiro ecosystem - a GitHub organization where Amazon engineers, and over time trusted external contributors, publish the experimental tools, SDKs, MCP servers, CLI extensions, and skill libraries they build on top of Kiro. Thousands of engineers already build for Kiro every day. Almost none of that work has left the building. Kiro Labs is how we open it up: a governed but deliberately low-friction path that moves internal innovation into the open, where a broader community of developers can find it, use it, and build on it.

We're looking for a Technical Program Manager to build that program. You'll own the mechanisms that turn Kiro Labs from a promising side effort into a durable, scalable incubator: the publishing pipeline, the governance model, the lifecycle, and the metrics. You'll be the connective tissue across the Kiro product team, open source strategy, security, legal, marketing, and customer success - diving deep enough technically to understand what contributors are building, and program-managing well enough to get it shipped and keep the org healthy.

Key job responsibilities

Own the publishing pipeline end to end - Design and run the intake process that takes a project from proposal to public repo fit review, security review, license and trademark review, and repo creation - and relentlessly drive down time-to-publish.
Build the governance model - Stand up the review committee, define the fit, quality, and security bar, establish decision rights and response SLAs, and document the entire workflow.
Manage cross-functional dependencies and unblock contributors - Coordinate across product, open source strategy, security, legal/IP, marketing, and customer success. Own the critical path, clear blockers, and give contributors a single, obvious place to get answers.
Own project lifecycle and org health - Define and operate the active, maintenance, and archived states, health monitoring, and the sunset process, so Kiro Labs stays a curated set of working tools rather than a graveyard of abandoned repos.
Define and report on success - Establish the program's KPIs - projects published, external engagement (stars, forks, issues, and PRs from outside Amazon), projects that graduate to broad adoption, time-to-publish, and growth in external awareness of Kiro and report progress, risks, and tradeoffs to senior leadership.
Scale the operation - Introduce automated quality and health checks, write the SOPs, and reduce manual effort so the program runs on mechanisms

About The Team

Kiro Labs sits at the intersection of product, customer success, engineering, and open source for Kiro. It's the external-facing complement to a thriving internal builder culture: the place where the tools Amazon engineers build on Kiro reach a public audience, and where a nascent external community can start to form around the product. This role brings together partners who have each carried a piece of it - open source strategy, the Kiro product team, marketing, and customer success - under a single program owner accountable for making it work.

Basic Qualifications

5+ years of technical product or program management experience
7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
Experience managing programs across cross-functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
Experience presenting metrics and progress to goal to senior leadership

Preferred Qualifications

Experience developing and implementing KPI goals and strategies based on broader organization goals
3+ years of software development experience, or Bachelor's degree in engineering or equivalent
Experience running open source or developer community programs, including GitHub organization administration, open source release and compliance processes, and open source licensing

jobs.title: Director of Information Security
jobs.description:
Description:

The Director of Information Security is a hands-on security leader to own and mature our information security program end to end. In this player-coach role, you will set security strategy and priorities, serve as the organization's primary authority on security risk, and personally engineer many of the controls that protect electronic protected health information (ePHI) and payment card data. You will be accountable for our compliance posture under the HIPAA Security Rule, our alignment with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and NIST SP 800-53, and PCI DSS for our payment environments.

Requirements:

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

* Own the information security program, including its strategy, multi-year roadmap, budget recommendations, and success metrics, aligned with business and clinical priorities.
* Design, deploy, and maintain security technologies including firewalls, EDR, SIEM, IDS/IPS, DLP, email security, and vulnerability management platforms across on-premises and cloud environments.
* Implement and document technical safeguards required by the HIPAA Security Rule, including access controls, audit logging, integrity controls, and transmission security for systems that store or process ePHI.
* Map security controls to the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and NIST SP 800-53, identify gaps, and drive remediation work with system owners.
* Own PCI DSS compliance for cardholder data environments by maintaining network segmentation, hardening in-scope systems, managing quarterly ASV scans and annual assessments, and preparing evidence for QSA reviews or SAQs.
* Lead the HIPAA security risk analysis and risk management process, maintaining a living risk register and communicating risk decisions clearly to leadership.
* Manage vulnerability and patch programs.
* Engineer and maintain identity and access management controls such as MFA, role-based access, privileged access management, and perform access reviews.
* Own the incident response program, including the plan, playbooks, and tabletop exercises, and lead response efforts during security incidents, coordinating breach risk assessments with compliance and legal.
* Prepare for and lead the organization through external audits, OCR inquiries, payer or partner security assessments, and customer security questionnaires.
* Own the third-party risk management program, including security reviews of vendors and Business Associates and the security terms of Business Associate Agreements.
* Contribute to security awareness efforts and advise IT staff on secure practices.
* This role requires occasional travel.
* Other duties as assigned.

**QUALIFICATIONS**

*To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.*

**EDUCATION**

BS in Computer Science, Management Information Systems, or a related field is preferred.

**EXPERIENCE**

Minimum of three years of combined experience in information security, compliance, technology audit, or a related field.

**COMMUNICATION/ TEAMWORK SKILLS**

Be able to establish priorities and successfully complete multiple assignments. Ability to work effectively both independently and also as part of a team. Possess excellent verbal and written communication skills. Strong analytical skills with the ability to collect, organize, analyze, and disseminate significant amounts of information with attention to detail and accuracy. Be able to organize complex work assignments for multiple clients and assure timely and accurate service delivery. Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.

**TECHNICAL SKILLS**

**Required:**

* Working knowledge of the HIPAA Security Rule, the NIST CSF and SP 800-53, and PCI DSS v4.0 requirements.
* Hands-on experience with security tools such as SIEM (e.g., Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel), EDR (e.g., CrowdStrike, Defender), next-generation firewalls, and vulnerability scanners (e.g., Tenable, Qualys, Rapid7).
* Solid understanding of networking (TCP/IP, segmentation, VPNs), Windows and Linux administration, and Active Directory/Entra ID.
* Experience securing cloud environments (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
* Strong written communication skills, including the ability to produce clear documentation for auditors and explain risk to non-technical stakeholders.

**Preferred:**· Relevant certifications such as CISSP, CISM, GIAC (GSEC, GCIH, GCCC), CompTIA Security+/CASP+, HCISPP, or a cloud security certification.· Familiarity with HITRUST CSF.· Scripting or automation experience (PowerShell, Python, Bash) and familiarity with infrastructure-as-code.

**BENEFITS OFFERED:**

* Health Savings Account for High Deductible Medical plan
* Dental
* Vision
* Life Insurance
* Disability Insurance
* Retirement with Company Matching
* Paid Time Off & Holidays
* Employee Assistance Program

jobs.title: Data Program Manager
jobs.description:
Here at Siemens, we take pride in enabling sustainable progress through technology. We do this through empowering customers by combining the real and digital worlds. Improving how we live, work, and move today and for the next generation! We know that the only way a business thrives is if our people are thriving. That’s why we always put our people first. Our global, diverse team would be happy to support you and challenge you to grow in new ways. Who knows where our shared journey will take you?

We are building intelligent systems that bring generative AI into the physical world - merging models, embodiment, and real-time perception into entirely new product experiences. As a Data Program Manager are responsible for all aspects of data acquisition for the next generation of AI products by working on cross-functional DAI (data and artificial intelligence) data programs that support Siemens’ AI and industrial AI initiatives. Here you will partner with applied science, product, engineering, and operations to design and implement pragmatic solutions for acquiring data. You will be a key interface between our product roadmap and external data offerings.  
  
The role will own multiple related workstreams and serve as a liaison across Product, Engineering, Applied Science, Legal, Compliance, Procurement, and external data partners. The Data Program Manager will translate business and product needs into executable data programs, establish operating mechanisms, manage dependencies and risks, and drive programs through delivery.

**Key responsibilities****:**

* Manage complex, cross-functional AI data programs and interconnected workstreams from planning through delivery, aligning evolving requirements with clear objectives, milestones, and operating plans.

* Drive execution across Product, Engineering, Applied Science, Legal, Compliance, Procurement, Security, and other stakeholders, while representing programs in leadership forums.

* Oversee end-to-end data acquisition, annotation, curation, licensing, and readiness, and manage strategic day-to-day relationships with internal and external data owners

* Establish success metrics, requirements, and acceptance criteria for data deliverables to measure progress, quality, readiness, and compliance with organizational policies.

* Identify systemic risks, resolve complex cross-organizational dependencies, and lead regular program reviews to communicate status and decisions to senior leadership.

* Manage budgets, resource planning, and vendor commitments while developing scalable governance models, templates, and operating processes to improve program efficiency.

**Basic Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.

* 4+ years of experience in program management, project management, operations, technology programs, data programs, or a related field.

* Demonstrated experience independently leading complex, cross-functional programs.

* Experience managing multiple workstreams, dependencies, stakeholders, and external partners.

* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including communication with senior stakeholders.

* Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience managing AI, data, software, or technology programs.

* Experience with data acquisition, data annotation, data curation, or data lifecycle programs.

* Experience developing and executing data acquisition strategies that leverage frontier AI models for data discovery, generation, enrichment, transformation, and quality evaluation, with an understanding of when to apply AI-driven approaches versus traditional or human-in-the-loop methods.

* Familiarity with data governance, data privacy, licensing, or responsible AI principles.

* Experience managing strategic vendors or external data providers.

* Experience establishing program governance, operating mechanisms, or standardized processes.

jobs.title: Interim Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
Department Overview:

The mission of the Information Technology Group (ITG) is to develop, implement and maintain technology-based services and solutions to enable OHSU to effectively manage information to accomplish its missions.

Reporting directly to the Senior Vice President and OHSU Chief Information Officer, the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) is a member of the ITG executive leadership team and sets the vision, strategy, and direction for OHSU's core technology infrastructure and architecture. The CTO has broad oversight of technology and infrastructure operations, projects and planning, and holds ultimate responsibility for the technology services components of OHSU's strategic and tactical initiatives. The CTO also positions the organization to adopt emerging technologies in ways that advance OHSU's clinical, research and academic missions.

The most critical function of the role is ensuring the ongoing, 24x7 operation of OHSU systems and networks. A stable, secure and resilient technology environment is vital to business continuity for the university.

The CTO leads the Technology Infrastructure, Design and Engineering (TIDE) Division, which delivers enterprise-wide core technology support including networks, compute and storage, telecommunications support, data centers, design and construction, collaboration and core applications and business continuity.

Function/Duties of Position:

**Technology Management**

The strategic role of the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) is to establish direction and technology vision, to develop and pursue technical standards, to set general direction around core technology architecture and to evaluate and guide the adoption of emerging technologies. The operational role is to create and maintain the structure necessary to ensure business continuity through a stable technology infrastructure.

These roles translate to the following major responsibilities:

* Responsible for defining a robust, scalable, extensible technology architecture that is fully integrated with the wider enterprise architecture and aligned with industry best practices.
* Responsible for defining engineering and technical standards, processes and procedures for core technology, and ensuring consistent adoption across the division.
* Directs the delivery and ongoing reliability of core technology services, systems and networks. Includes oversight of operational procedures and disaster planning. Ensures infrastructure is designed and maintained in accordance with security standards established by the Chief Information Security Officer and broader enterprise architecture strategy.
* Responsible for establishing IT capacity planning to ensure technology infrastructure meets OHSU’s current and future needs. Proactively identifies technical infrastructure risks, emerging requirements and systems issues, and develops solutions.
* Establishes and oversees performance metrics and measurements for division to inform tactical and long-range decision making.
* Manage departmental operating and capital budgets and partner with Vendor Management to oversee strategic technology vendor relationships and contracts.

**Division Leadership**

The Chief Technology Officer (CTO) provides supervision and mentoring to Directors and frontline managers in the division. jobs.title: Director, Infrastructure & IT Operations
jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

The hiring organization is seeking a strategic and hands-on Director, Infrastructure & IT Operations
to lead the technology capabilities that keep digital products, cloud platforms, and internal teams secure, reliable, and productive.

This role oversees cloud infrastructure, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), production operations, bot mitigation, corporate IT, and helpdesk support, while providing architectural leadership across cloud platforms, networking, identity, observability, and operational tooling. This position spans both internal employee technology and the production infrastructure supporting high-traffic, customer-facing applications.

This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States.

Key Responsibilities

Lead teams responsible for cloud infrastructure, SRE, production operations, corporate IT, helpdesk, and bot mitigation, establishing ownership, operational standards, service-level objectives (SLOs), escalation procedures, and performance metrics.
Develop managers, technical leads, and IT staff through coaching, career development, and building a culture of accountability, documentation, automation, and continuous improvement.
Build quarterly and annual infrastructure roadmaps aligned with business priorities, growth, security, reliability, and cost, partnering with engineering, product, data, marketing, finance, HR, legal, and executive leadership.
Own the reliability, scalability, security, performance, and cost-effectiveness of cloud infrastructure, primarily within AWS.
Provide architectural leadership across cloud services, applications, APIs, networking, identity, databases, storage, observability, and integrations while establishing architecture standards, reference patterns, governance, and technical review processes.
Partner with engineering to improve deployment safety, performance, and readiness, driving automation, configuration management, and infrastructure as code.
Lead capacity planning for growth and demand spikes, eliminating single points of failure, undocumented systems, manual processes, and single-source dependencies.
Ensure production and nonproduction environments are properly separated, secured, and monitored, reviewing new systems for architectural fit, supportability, security, and total cost of ownership.
Establish and maintain service-level indicators (SLIs), SLOs, availability targets, and error-budget practices for critical systems.
Improve observability through centralized logging, metrics, distributed tracing, application performance monitoring (APM), and actionable alerting.
Lead major incident management, coordination, executive communication, root-cause analysis, and corrective-action tracking to improve mean time to detect, respond, and recover.
Develop and test backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity procedures, and establish sustainable on-call practices.
Own strategy and tooling for bot mitigation, scraping protection, automated abuse prevention, and traffic-quality management using technologies such as Cloudflare, DataDome, web application firewalls (WAFs), rate limiting, CAPTCHA alternatives, and device fingerprinting.
Partner with cross-functional teams to distinguish malicious automation from legitimate customers, search engines, partners, and approved AI crawlers, establishing monitoring and response procedures.
Oversee internal IT services and helpdesk support, establishing service-level expectations for response times, resolution times, user satisfaction, and backlog reduction.
Manage the employee technology lifecycle, including onboarding, offboarding, equipment provisioning, access management, asset recovery, and device inventory.
Standardize endpoint configuration, encryption, patching, and endpoint detection across laptops, collaboration platforms, productivity software, and telecom services.
Establish consistent identity and access management practices across corporate and production systems, implementing role-based access, least privilege, multi-factor authentication (MFA), periodic access reviews, and secure administrative account handling.
Support vulnerability remediation, security assessments, audits, vendor reviews, incident readiness, and applicable privacy requirements in partnership with legal and security teams.
Manage infrastructure, security, IT, telecom, monitoring, and support vendors, handling evaluations, contract reviews, renewals, licensing, service level agreements (SLAs), and budget management.
Improve cloud cost visibility through tagging, allocation, forecasting, tool consolidation, and contract optimization.

Required Qualifications

10+ years of experience in cloud infrastructure, SRE, platform engineering, DevOps, IT operations, or related disciplines.
5+ years of experience leading engineering or technology teams, including managing managers or technical leads.
Demonstrated experience operating high-traffic, customer-facing platforms in AWS or a comparable cloud environment.
Strong understanding of cloud architecture, networking, identity, security, observability, databases, APIs, storage, and distributed systems.
Experience managing production availability, incident response, root-cause analysis, disaster recovery, and business continuity.
Experience with infrastructure automation, configuration management, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code.
Experience managing corporate IT, employee support, endpoint management, software licensing, and access provisioning.
Experience establishing operational metrics, SLOs, and support standards.
Demonstrated ability to manage vendors, contracts, departmental budgets, and cloud costs.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical risks, architecture, and tradeoffs to executive audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Cloudflare, DataDome, or comparable bot-management and web application protection platforms, including leading bot mitigation or traffic-quality programs.
Experience with AWS services, containerized environments, infrastructure as code, centralized logging, and APM tools (such as AppDynamics).
Experience supporting large-scale consumer subscription, public-record, data-as-a-service, advertising, or ecommerce platforms.
Experience modernizing legacy infrastructure, transitioning systems from external vendors, and consolidating cloud accounts or IT services.
Familiarity with privacy requirements and secure handling of sensitive consumer data.
Experience building or maturing SRE, DevOps, or platform engineering functions.

Measures of Success

Improved availability, performance, and stability of customer-facing platforms.
Reduced impact and infrastructure costs associated with bots, scraping, and automated abuse.
Faster incident detection, response, and recovery, alongside a reduction in recurring incidents.
Enhanced observability with reduced alert noise, validated disaster recovery capabilities, and optimized cloud spend.
Consistent helpdesk performance, reliable onboarding and offboarding, and robust endpoint security and asset tracking.
Strong architecture governance, reduced dependency on undocumented systems or vendors, and demonstrated team development.

Compensation and Benefits

Position Summary

The Senior Manager, Operational Technology (OT) is responsible for the strategic leadership, governance, reliability, cybersecurity, and operational excellence of Energy Transfer's Operational Technology environment across multiple business units, processing facilities, terminals, and pipeline operations. This role provides enterprise leadership for Process Control Networks (PCN), Industrial Control Systems (ICS), SCADA environments, industrial servers, virtualization platforms, and associated OT infrastructure.

The successful candidate will serve as a key liaison between Operations, Engineering, Cybersecurity, and Enterprise IT to ensure OT systems remain secure, reliable, compliant, and aligned with business objectives. This position leads a team of OT professionals while driving strategic initiatives focused on cybersecurity, risk management, infrastructure modernization, operational resilience, and regulatory compliance.

The Senior Manager will provide technical leadership and subject matter expertise for large-scale capital projects, mergers and acquisitions integrations, operational expansions, and cybersecurity initiatives while ensuring adherence to industry best practices and recognized frameworks such as NIST, ISA/IEC 62443, API 1164, and NERC-CIP where applicable.

Develop and execute the enterprise OT strategy in alignment with Energy Transfer's operational, cybersecurity, and business objectives.
Establish long-term roadmaps for OT infrastructure modernization, lifecycle management, system resiliency, and cybersecurity enhancement.
Partner with executive leadership, operations management, engineering teams, and Enterprise IT to drive OT technology adoption and innovation.
Lead OT governance programs, standards development, and enterprise-wide policy implementation.
Serve as the primary escalation point for critical OT infrastructure, cybersecurity, and operational issues.

Operational Technology Management

Provide overall leadership and management of the OT organization supporting multiple operating regions and facilities.
Lead teams responsible for PCN infrastructure, industrial networking, virtualization environments, Windows server platforms, and OT cybersecurity technologies.
Establish performance metrics, service level objectives, and continuous improvement initiatives for OT operations.
Manage vendor relationships, support agreements, licensing programs, technology contracts, and strategic partnerships.
Ensure standardization of OT architectures across facilities while maintaining operational flexibility and reliability.

Cybersecurity & Risk Management
