Establish cybersecurity governance, vulnerability management, threat detection, incident response, and disaster recovery programs for OT systems.
Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory requirements, internal controls, and industry-recognized security frameworks.
Champion cyber risk assessments and mitigation strategies for critical operational assets.

Infrastructure Reliability & Operational Excellence

Drive high availability and reliability initiatives for OT systems supporting 24x7 operations.
Oversee backup, recovery, business continuity, and disaster recovery programs across all OT environments.
Ensure proper lifecycle management and supportability of OT hardware, software, operating systems, and networking infrastructure.
Lead root-cause analysis efforts for critical incidents and oversee implementation of corrective actions.
Support operational readiness activities for new facilities, expansions, and infrastructure upgrades.

Capital Projects & Engineering Support

Serve as OT technical authority for major capital projects, facility expansions, and strategic initiatives.
Ensure all OT and cybersecurity requirements are incorporated throughout project planning, design, construction, commissioning, and startup phases.
Participate in technology evaluations, architecture reviews, and project approval processes.
Provide technical guidance on industrial networking, system integration, virtualization, cloud connectivity, and emerging OT technologies.
Support acquisition integration activities and enterprise technology harmonization efforts.

Leadership & Talent Development

Build, mentor, and develop high-performing OT professionals.
Establish succession planning and employee development strategies.
Foster a culture of safety, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Promote cross-functional collaboration among Operations, Engineering, Cybersecurity, and IT teams.
Lead organizational change initiatives and technology transformation programs.

Minimum 5+ years of leadership experience managing technical teams and enterprise-scale OT programs.

You will lead security operations and incident response initiatives across the organization. This role is ideal for a security leader who confidently addresses critical security incidents and swiftly makes containment decisions. It includes supporting the team's health, operational processes, and cross-function collaborations that foster a strong, high-performing security function.

Serving as a manager on the Cyber Defense & Response team, you will guide the complete incident response lifecycle. You will ensure operational preparedness is maintained to support it. You will convert NVIDIA’s engineering-first, technology-focused, threat-informed defense strategy into practical plans. You will partner closely with skilled incident responders, security engineers, threat intelligence specialists, and product, platform, and engineering teams to safeguard NVIDIA’s corporate, cloud, and product environments.

What You'll Be Doing

Lead day-to-day Cyber Defense & Response (CDR) functions, ensuring operational readiness, execution rigor, and alignment with NVIDIA’s cybersecurity strategy.
Responsible for the incident response lifecycle from start to finish. Act as the point person for critical incidents and lead efforts to investigate, contain, recover, and review the incident afterward.
Increase detection and response efficiency by continuously broadening coverage across on-premises and multi-cloud environments, targeting GPU-accelerated and AI/ML workloads.
Set detection expectations and standards aligned to NVIDIA’s threat landscape, defining monitoring requirements, coverage goals, and compliance requirements.
Own operational performance and outcomes, including MTTD, MTTC, MTTR, detection coverage, alert quality, and false-positive reduction—focused on root-cause improvement.
Run CDR improvements following agile methods, keeping a risk-prioritized backlog and guiding delivery via planning, reviews, and retrospectives.
Drive agentic transformation of manual SOC work — identify repetitive analyst tasks and convert them into automated, event-based AI pipelines.
Partner with Security Engineering to operationalize tooling, automation, playbooks, and post-incident improvements that measurably improve response efficiency.

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or related field, or equivalent experience.
10+ overall years of experience in cybersecurity, including 4+ years managing people within a SOC or incident response function.
Strong technical depth to step into an active incident independently — reading SIEM queries, evaluating automation workflows, investigating alerts, and assessing case quality with deep expertise in SOC-relevant domains (digital forensics & incident response, threat hunting, cloud security, detection engineering, log analysis, malware analysis, or security automation).
Strong knowledge of cloud security (AWS, Azure, GCP, and other CSPs), identity and access management, endpoint protection, and securing containerized or GPU-based AI/ML workloads.

Experience building or improving incident response processes, playbooks, and critical issue workflows.
Proven ability to lead global, 24x7 teams across distributed shift structures using agile practices, with ownership of backlog prioritization and sprint metrics.
Ability to convey complex security concepts clearly to engineers, executives, and legal and compliance partners.

Calm, decisive leadership during high-severity incidents — leading teams, making containment calls under pressure, and presenting clearly across technical and executive stakeholders.
Track record deploying security automation, orchestration, analytics, and AI agentic SOC workflows that measurably reduce manual workload, false positives, analyst toil, and response times.
Experience developing detections and response playbooks for AI/ML systems, coordinating with product or supply‑chain security teams, and integrating or migrating SIEM/EDR across hybrid multi‑cloud environments, including CSP log sources, MDR partners, and co‑managed detection and response models.

Experience in digital health, telehealth, or multi-state healthcare services environments, including familiarity with pharmacy management systems, dispensing technology, or regulated pharmaceutical IT environments

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
Chief Technology Officer | Agentic AI

Executive Leadership | Enterprise AI | Agentic Systems | 0→1 Platform Build

We are partnering exclusively with an early-stage AI company to appoint a Chief Technology Officer
for one of the most ambitious enterprise agentic platforms we have encountered.

The company has spent several years developing its underlying technology and is now entering a pivotal stage of expansion.

The thesis is straightforward but enormous:
As enterprises move from copilots to hundreds or thousands of autonomous agents performing real work, they will require an independent infrastructure layer to orchestrate those agents, connect them securely to proprietary intelligence and tools, govern their behavior, and operate across an increasingly fragmented ecosystem of models and compute.

This company intends to build that layer.

We are looking for an exceptional technical builder, architect and engineering leader
to work directly alongside the CEO and help define what that platform becomes.

This is not a traditional management-oriented CTO appointment
.

The successful individual will remain deeply engaged with architecture and engineering while building an exceptional technical organization around them. You should be equally comfortable debating the architecture of an agent runtime, whiteboarding a distributed system, reviewing critical technical decisions and recruiting world-class engineers.

What You'll Own
Technical vision, architecture and engineering strategy for an enterprise-grade agentic AI platform
Architecture spanning agent runtimes/harnesses, orchestration, state/context, memory, tools/actions, multi-agent systems and human-in-the-loop workflows

Model abstraction and routing across frontier, open-source, specialized and private models
Enterprise intelligence/context infrastructure and secure access to proprietary data
Agent evaluation, observability, guardrails, permissions, reliability and failure recovery
Cloud-native and distributed infrastructure capable of supporting sophisticated production agent workloads
Technical roadmap alongside the CEO, Product and commercial leadership
Recruitment and development of a world-class engineering organization
The transition from an already substantial technical foundation into a category-defining enterprise platform

What We're Looking For

You are likely a CTO, technical founder, VP Engineering, Head of AI/Engineering or exceptional senior technical leader
who has already built sophisticated AI/platform technology.

Most importantly, you have actually built agentic systems
.

We're interested in people who can go significantly deeper than saying their organization uses LangChain, LangGraph, MCP or an LLM API. You understand the underlying abstractions: how agents reason and execute, how state persists, how tools are exposed, how context is managed, how multiple agents coordinate, how failures are contained, how systems are evaluated and how the entire architecture operates reliably in production.

You will ideally bring:
Exceptional software engineering and computer systems fundamentals
Deep production experience with agentic AI / LLM systems

Agent orchestration, runtimes or harness architecture
Distributed systems and platform/infrastructure engineering
Python, Go, Rust and/or TypeScript depth
Cloud-native architecture, Kubernetes and modern infrastructure
Production experience around tools, state, memory, context, evals and observability
Experience taking complex technology from 0→1 and subsequently scaling it

Evidence of building and attracting exceptional engineering teams
Strong product instincts and an ability to translate an ambitious technical thesis into something enterprises can actually deploy
Comfort operating with significant ambiguity, autonomy and ownership

Experience with coding agents, autonomous software development, enterprise AI infrastructure, model routing, AI gateways/control planes, MCP/A2A, RAG/context infrastructure, inference infrastructure or AI developer platforms
would be particularly interesting.

Why This Opportunity?

This is an opportunity to join before the category has been fully defined
, not after.

You won't inherit a mature roadmap and simply manage its execution. You'll have the opportunity to help determine the architecture, technical philosophy, product boundaries and engineering organization of a company pursuing a much larger question:
If AI agents become a new enterprise workforce, what infrastructure will enterprises need to own, control and govern that intelligence?

The CEO is an exceptionally ambitious founder looking for a genuine technical counterpart
, not simply an engineering manager.

There is substantial ownership, direct influence over company strategy and the opportunity to build at the intersection of agents, enterprise intelligence, models, governance and AI infrastructure
.

We are moving quickly and will be deliberately selective.

If you have built sophisticated agentic systems and believe the next generation of enterprise software will be fundamentally agent-driven, I'd like to hear from you.

Apply directly or reach out confidentially with your resume and availability for an initial discussion.

jobs.title: Trauma Program Manager
jobs.description:
**Job Profile Summary**

This role focuses on providing administrative and business support to the organization in order to achieve operational goals. In addition, this role focuses on performing the following Program Management duties: Program management, projects, and coordination of resources to meet accreditation standards, support strategic growth, and service line development. These positions typically support hospital-based programs. A management role that supervises employees focusing on tactical, operational activities within a specified area, with the majority of time spent overseeing area of responsibility, planning, prioritizing and/or directing the responsibilities of employees. Goal achievement is typically accomplished through performance of direct and/or indirect reports. A role that supervises para-professional employees. Responsibilities that typically include: Setting day-to-day operational objectives for team, problems faced may be difficult but typically are not complex, and ensures policies, practices and procedures are understood and followed by direct reports, customers and stakeholders.

**Job Overview**

The Trauma Program Manager is responsible for the development, implementation, and evaluation of the trauma program. This role organizes the services necessary for a multidisciplinary approach to care for critically injured patients.

**Job Description**

**Minimum Qualifications:**

1. Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN) **OR** Master of Science in Nursing (MSN).

2. Massachusetts RN Licensure.

3. Four (4) years of RN experience in a Trauma Center.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

1. Master of Science in Nursing (MSN)

2. Two (2) years of Management Experience.

3. Six (6) years of RN experience in a Trauma Center.

**Duties and Responsibilities:** The duties and responsibilities listed below are intended to describe the general nature of work and are not intended to be an all-inclusive list. Other duties and responsibilities may be assigned.

1. Assesses the quality of care provided to trauma patients, in accordance to protocol, in collaboration with Quality Improvement (QI) team.

2. Identifies performance improvement projects for interdisciplinary collaboration.

3. Works with QI team to identify problems with trauma care and intervene when appropriate or refer problems to the appropriate individual.

4. Facilitates coordination of interdisciplinary trauma performance improvement conferences for the adult trauma service.

5. Identifies deficiencies impeding the maintenance of the trauma center standards and suggests methods for addressing these deficiencies.

6. Facilitates trauma patient transfer process.

7. Coordinates preparation of re-verification application, pre-review questionnaire, and supporting materials for American College of Surgeons trauma center verification when required.

8. Collaborates on the development of trauma transfer protocols.

9. Facilitates and participates in interdisciplinary educational programs for health care professionals and the community concerning all phases of trauma care.

10. Directs outreach and injury prevention programs.

11. May supervise the Trauma Registrar to ensure continuous data entry and maintenance of an updated registry.

12. In conjunction with the Trauma Registrar, provides information for analysis and evaluation of the quality of patient care, including epidemiological and demographic characteristics of trauma patients.

13. Reports data to the MA State Trauma registry and to the National Trauma Data Bank.

14. Manages, as appropriate, the operational and personnel aspects of the trauma program, serving as a liaison to the hospital administration.

15. Actively participates in professional organizations at the State and National levels and promotes the Trauma Division’s stature in these organizations.

16. Assesses needs for trauma educational programs and coordinates these as necessary.

17. Functions as a member of the Emergency Management service given the nature of trauma.

18. Monitors fiscal status of Trauma program including preparing the annual budget, reviewing reimbursement, preparing variance reports, and modifying the business plan for the service in conjunction with the System Director of Surgical Services

19. Collaborates with team to develop program goals.

20. Ensures staff competence through annual evaluations.

21. Initiates and manages change, ensuring appropriate support and resources.

**Physical Requirements:**

1. Occasional lifting of 30-35 lbs and turning patients.

2. Prolonged standing and walking.

3. Occasional twisting, bending, reaching, pushing/pulling, sitting, kneeling, and squatting.

4. Exposure to infectious disease and possible carcinogenic chemicals.

5. Exposure of blood-borne pathogens.

6. Requires fine manual dexterity to lift and maneuver patients.

7. Requires visual and aural acuity necessary to monitor patient care.

**Skills & Abilities:**

1. Knowledge of Care of the Critically Injured Patient.

2. Knowledge of local and state legislative actions, as well as the American College of Surgeons guidelines for Trauma Center performance within a State Trauma System as outlined in the “Resources for Optimal Care of the Injured Patient”.

3. Demonstrated ability to function independently in education and consulting capabilities as well as competency in teaching, education and quality/performance improvement.

4. Proven organizational/management/supervisory skills required.

At Tufts Medicine, we want every individual to feel valued for the skills and experience they bring. Our compensation philosophy is designed to offer fair, competitive pay that attracts, retains, and motivates highly talented individuals, while rewarding the important work you do every day.

The base pay ranges reflect the minimum qualifications for the role. Individual offers are determined using a comprehensive approach that considers relevant experience, certifications, education, skills

jobs.description:
**WE ARE THE NRO**  
For sixty years, the NRO has developed, acquired, launched and operated the satellites that are the foundation for America's advantage and strength in space. Using a diversified architecture of spacecraft, NRO collects and delivers the best space-based intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance content on the planet.  
Learn more at NRO.gov.  
  
**Basic Eligibility For A Position With The NRO**

* You must be a U.S. Citizen
* You must be able to obtain and maintain a TS/SCI security clearance
* You will be subject to pre-employment and periodic drug testing
* You will be subject to pre-employment and periodic polygraph examinations

  
**Where You Will Work**  
The Advanced Systems and Technology (AS&T) Directorate is responsible for discovering, researching, developing, and transitioning revolutionary and innovative technologies to the rest of organization. We have an exciting opportunity for a high performing individual to serve as the Technology Transition & Transfer (T3) Program Manager. Tech Transfer plays a critical role in discovering, on-boarding, and transitioning technology from non-traditional partners across industry, academia, and other government agencies. This position supports NRO's Federal Laboratory, the Space Reconnaissance Lab (SRL).  
The NRO Cadre is collecting resumes for consideration against current and future opportunities for **Non-Supervisor, Technology Transition and Transfer Dept PM, GGS 12-13, occupational series 0801**. More information on the occupational series can be viewed on the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) website.  
**This is a full-time position that is open from 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-19. Resumes must be submitted by 11:59 PM EST on 2026-10-19.**  
  
**Who May Apply**

* This position is open to the public.
* Federal government employees MUST currently be at the grade level or higher as indicated in this announcement. This is NOT a promotion opportunity for current Federal government employees. If selected for the position, Federal government employees will transition laterally at their current grade level and step.
* Federal applicants who exceed the advertised grade may voluntarily request acceptance at the lower grade per IAW DoW 1400.25 Volume 2006.
* The NRO is only accepting external applicants for this job announcement. Current NRO Cadre employees should apply internally.
* This position MAY qualify for the appointment of a reemployed federal annuitant IAW DoWI 1400.25 Volume 300.

  
**What You Will Be Doing**  
As a T3 Program Manager (PM), you will engage across the organization, with other government agencies, national laboratories, industry, and academia to identify capability needs and partnership opportunities. As PM, you will have the opportunity to oversee or participate in contract acquisitions, both FAR and non-FAR based, and may serve as a Contracting Officer’s Technical Representative (COTR) for acquisition and research and development projects to advance current and future intelligence needs.  
The successful candidate will be responsible for one or more programs that comprise multiple research projects. Examples of research areas in include: Autonomy, Data Transport, Remote Sensing, Resiliency & Security, and Foundation Technology. The candidate should have excellent leadership, collaboration, and communication skills, and be willing to engage organizations throughout the Government, academia, and industry. You will be involved in shaping how NRO plans for future technology, research, and development.  
  
**What You Will Need**  
REQUIRED:  

* Bachelor's degree in a science or engineering discipline
* Documented ability to build partnerships across an organization
* Documented ability to lead change and innovation within an organization
* Demonstrated leadership and technical skills.
* Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
* Ability and willingness to travel domestically.

  
DESIRED:  

* Advanced degree in a science or engineering discipline or a related field
* Systems Engineering experience and education/training
* Experience as a program manager or contracting officer's technical representative
* Experience working with academia for research and development
* Experience working with Basic and Fundamental Research
* Experience building partnerships within the Intelligence Community

- Familiarity with In-Q-Tel  

* Familiarity with FAR and non-FAR based acquisitions
* Working knowledge of NRO mission areas

  
Qualifying experience may have been acquired in any public or private sector job, but will clearly demonstrate past experience in the application of the particular competencies/knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to successfully perform and is typically in or directly related to the duties of the position as described above. **Experience must be reflected in your resume.**  
  
Applicants submitting a resume that exceeds the two-page limit per OPM Memorandum, "Merit Hiring Plan," dated May 29, 2025, https://www.opm.gov/chcoc/latest-memos/merit-hiring-plan.pdf will not be eligible for consideration. For more information regarding resume writing, see "Guidance for Applicants on 2-Page Resume" and visit the Resume Help Center.  
  
**Other Information**

* Overtime Statement: MAY be required to work other than normal duty hours, which may include evenings, weekends, and/or holidays.

jobs.title: Senior Director, Global Infrastructure Technology & Operations
jobs.description:
Career-defining. Life-changing.

At iRhythm, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your skills and your career while impacting the lives of people around the world. iRhythm is shaping a future where everyone, everywhere can access the best possible cardiac health solutions. Every day, we collaborate, create, and constantly reimagine what’s possible. We think big and move fast, driven by our commitment to put patients first and improve lives. We need builders like you. Curious and innovative problem solvers looking for the chance to meaningfully shape the future of cardiac health, our company, and your career

About This Role

The Senior Director, Global Infrastructure Technology & Operations will lead iRhythm’s enterprise infrastructure strategy, architecture, operations, and modernization across cloud, networking, data center and hardware, end-user computing, and security infrastructure. This role will ensure that iRhythm’s technology foundation is resilient, secure, compliant, and scalable enough to support 24/7 clinical operations, manufacturing, global commercial growth, and the company’s expanding data and AI capabilities. This senior leadership role combines executive leadership, hands-on technical depth, organizational development, financial stewardship, and close partnership with the Chief Data Officer and head of IT, CISO, Quality/Regulatory, Engineering, and business leaders. The role works hand in hand with the CISO: Security defines the requirements and provides oversight, while Infrastructure delivers and operates the platforms, controls, and services that enable the business.

What You Will Be Doing

Strategy & Leadership

Define and execute a multi-year enterprise infrastructure strategy and roadmap aligned to iRhythm’s business, clinical, data, and AI objectives.
Build, lead, and develop a high-performing infrastructure organization across cloud, network, operations, end-user services, and managed service partners.
Establish infrastructure architecture standards, reference patterns, governance, and operating models across business units and geographies.
Serve as the senior infrastructure advisor to executive leadership, translating strategy, risk, investment, and performance into business terms.

Cloud Infrastructure

Own the enterprise multi-cloud strategy across AWS, GCP, Azure, and Microsoft 365, including landing zones, account and project structure, identity integration, and guardrails.
Lead cloud platform engineering using Infrastructure as Code, automation, infrastructure CI/CD, and policy-as-code.
Drive FinOps practices, including cost visibility, optimization, reserved-capacity strategy, and chargeback/showback.
Enable modern data and AI platforms—including Snowflake, enterprise AI and search platforms, and ML/GPU workloads—with secure, scalable, well-governed infrastructure and private connectivity patterns.
Lead workload migration and modernization from on-premises environments to cloud where appropriate.

Networking & Connectivity

Own enterprise network architecture across corporate offices, clinical and IDTF sites, manufacturing facilities, data centers, and cloud environments, including LAN, WAN, SD-WAN, Wi-Fi, SASE, DNS, and load balancing.
Design secure hybrid and multi-cloud connectivity using Direct Connect, Interconnect, private endpoints, VPN, and transit architectures.
Implement network segmentation and isolation for manufacturing/OT and clinical environments in alignment with Zero Trust principles.
Ensure high availability, performance monitoring, and capacity planning for mission-critical clinical and patient-facing services.

Data Center, Hardware & End-User Computing

Oversee on-premises and colocation data centers, compute, storage, backup, and virtualization platforms, including lifecycle management and rationalization.
Own the hardware asset lifecycle, including procurement, standards, refresh cycles, and secure disposal.
Lead end-user computing across endpoints, MDM, collaboration tools, service desk, and conference room technology to deliver a secure and productive employee experience.
Support infrastructure for manufacturing sites and clinical operations, including device and equipment connectivity where applicable.
Security Infrastructure
Implement, operate, and maintain infrastructure security controls in alignment with the security strategy, policies, and standards set by the CISO.
Own the day-to-day engineering and operation of network and platform security technologies such as firewalls, WAF, proxies/SASE, NAC, and VPN, with the CISO’s team defining requirements, configuration standards, and monitoring.
Embed security by design across infrastructure through hardening baselines, secure configurations, and Infrastructure-as-Code guardrails.
Own timely vulnerability remediation and patching across infrastructure assets, meeting SLAs defined by the Security team.
Operate identity and directory infrastructure, including SSO, MFA, and directory services, in support of the CISO-led Zero Trust and identity roadmap.
Partner with the CISO’s organization during security incidents by providing infrastructure expertise, containment, remediation, logs, telemetry, and integrations needed for detection and response.

Compliance, Quality & Regulated Environments

Ensure infrastructure meets applicable regulatory and compliance obligations, including FDA QMSR (21 CFR Part 820), 21 CFR Part 11, HIPAA/HITECH, SOC 2, ISO 13485, ISO 27001, GDPR/UK GDPR, and other international requirements.
Partner with the CISO, Quality, and Regulatory teams to maintain infrastructure controls and evidence for audits, with Security owning the control framework and this role owning control execution for infrastructure.
Support computer system validation (CSV/CSA) for GxP-relevant infrastructure, along with change control and audit readiness.
Lead infrastructure responses during internal, customer, and regulatory audits.
Protect patient health information through appropriate data residency, encryption, access controls, and logging.

Resilience, Operations & Service Management

Own business continuity and disaster recovery for infrastructure, with defined RTO/RPO targets for clinical and business-critical systems and regular DR testing.
Build observability, monitoring, and alerting practices using SRE principles, SLOs, and error budgets for critical services.
Mature ITSM processes for incident, problem, change, and configuration management using ITIL-aligned practices and tools such as ServiceNow.
Drive automation to reduce toil and improve reliability, speed, and consistency.

Vendor & Financial Management

Own the infrastructure budget across OpEx and CapEx, including forecasting, business cases, and cost optimization.
Manage strategic vendor, cloud provider, telecom, and managed service relationships, including contract negotiation and performance management.
Evaluate emerging technologies and make build, buy, or partner recommendations.

Technology Environment

Our environment spans enterprise infrastructure, cloud, networking, security, end-user computing, data, AI, and regulated clinical and manufacturing systems. Experience with every named technology is not required.

Cloud and platform: AWS, GCP, Azure, Microsoft 365, landing zones, Terraform or similar Infrastructure as Code, CI/CD, policy-as-code, containers, virtualization, and GPU infrastructure.
Netorking and connectivity: LAN/WAN, SD-WAN, Wi-Fi, SASE, DNS, load balancing, Direct Connect, Interconnect, private endpoints, VPN, transit architectures, NAC, firewalls, and WAF.
Data, AI, and analytics infrastructure: Snowflake, Databricks, enterprise AI and search platforms, ML/GPU workloads, private connectivity, and governed data products.
Security and identity: SSO, MFA, directory services, Zero Trust, endpoint management, vulnerability management, security telemetry, logging, and incident response integrations.
Operations and service management: observability, monitoring, SRE practices, SLOs, error budgets, backup and recovery, ServiceNow, ITIL, and disaster recovery testing.
Enterprise integrations and ecosystems: Jira, Confluence, GitLab, Salesforce, QAD, Workday, Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Teams, and other business and clinical platforms.

Required Qualifications

15+ years of progressive experience in enterprise infrastructure, including 7+ years leading multi-disciplinary infrastructure teams at the director level or above.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Proven strength in ability to balance strategic vision with execution excellence, developing organizational capability while creating the capacity, accountability, and focus needed to consistently deliver on business and technology priorities.
Deep hands-on and architectural expertise in at least one major cloud platform, preferably AWS and/or GCP, with experience running multi-cloud and hybrid environments.
Strong background in enterprise networking and hands-on experience engineering and operating security infrastructure in partnership with a security organization.
Proven experience operating infrastructure in a regulated industry such as medical devices, life sciences, pharmaceuticals, healthcare, or financial services.
Working knowledge of FDA regulations, including 21 CFR Part 11 and 21 CFR Part 820, as well as frameworks such as HIPAA, SOC 2, ISO 27001, and NIST CSF.
Track record of leading large-scale transformation programs, including cloud migration, data center consolidation, network modernization, or comparable enterprise initiatives.
Experience owning budgets of meaningful scale and managing strategic technology, cloud, telecom, and managed service vendors.
Excellent executive communication and influencing skills and the ability to translate technical risk, resilience, and investment into business outcomes.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in a medical device, digital health, or connected-device company supporting 24/7 clinical services.
Experience supporting manufacturing or OT networks and familiarity with IEC 62443 or similar OT security practices.
Familiarity with infrastructure for data and AI platforms, including Snowflake, Databricks, ML/GPU workloads, and enterprise AI tools.
Global infrastructure experience across the United States, United Kingdom/Europe, and Asia-Pacific, including data residency requirements.
Certifications such as AWS or GCP Professional Architect, CCIE/CCNP,
MBA or advanced degree.

Location:

Remote - US

Actual compensation may vary depending on job-related factors including knowledge, skills, experience, and work location.

jobs.title: IT Security Program Manager
jobs.description:
Position Overview

The IT Security Program Manager
is responsible for executing and managing the day-to-day operations of Recovery Centers of America's cybersecurity program. Reporting to the manager of infrastructure under the IT OPS director and ensures that RCA's security posture remains compliant with HIPAA, HITECH
, and NIST 800-53
standards while continuously improving the effectiveness of the organization's security controls and risk management framework.

This role will coordinate and perform audits, oversee third-party risk management, manage RCA's security awareness and phishing programs, drive policy governance, and ensure the timely resolution of open risk items and vulnerabilities. The ideal candidate is an organized, hands-on leader with a strong understanding of healthcare security and compliance who can align security initiatives with RCA's mission of saving one million lives.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Program Management & Governance

Manage the daily operations of RCA's cybersecurity program under the guidance of the CISO.
Coordinate and track the completion of internal and external security audits, including HIPAA, SOC 2, and NIST-based assessments.
Maintain and monitor the Information Security Risk Register, ensuring timely resolution of identified issues and mitigation of critical findings.
Lead tabletop exercises and incident response simulations to test and improve RCA's preparedness and business continuity planning.
Collaborate with RCA leadership and department heads to ensure that security policies and controls are understood and effectively implemented across all business units.

Third-Party Risk & Vendor Management

Manage the third-party risk assessment program, ensuring that all vendors with access to PHI or critical systems undergo security evaluation and periodic reassessment.
Review BAAs, security questionnaires, and compliance attestations; ensure corrective action for identified gaps.
Partner with Procurement and Legal to integrate security requirements into new and existing vendor contracts.

Policy, Compliance, and Reporting

Work with the CISO to review, update, and publish information security policies, standards, and procedures in accordance with HIPAA, HITECH, and NIST frameworks.
Develop dashboards and recurring reports to track security metrics, compliance posture, and program maturity for presentation to the CISO and executive leadership.
Monitor and interpret changes to regulatory requirements, ensuring timely updates to RCA's compliance program.

Security Awareness & Training

Administer and optimize RCA's KnowBe4 Security Awareness and Phishing Training Program.
Track user engagement and training completion rates, and provide metrics and recommendations to leadership.
Develop creative awareness campaigns to strengthen RCA's security culture.

Vulnerability & Infrastructure Management

Identify and track critical infrastructure vulnerabilities, working with IT and Infrastructure teams to ensure remediation and continuous monitoring.
Oversee MDM security, ensuring appropriate device controls, encryption, and enforcement of mobile security policies.
Support the CISO in analyzing threat intelligence, vulnerability trends, and endpoint security performance (e.g., CrowdStrike, firewall alerts).

Risk and Compliance Leadership

Ensure continuous compliance with HIPAA, HITECH, and NIST 800-53 / 800-171 requirements.
Coordinate with Compliance, Legal, and Clinical leadership to ensure consistent risk management practices.
Participate in post-incident reviews, documenting lessons learned and recommending process improvements.

Education

Bachelor's degree in Information Security, Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field required.

Experience

Minimum of 5--7 years of progressive experience in cybersecurity, IT risk management, or audit within a regulated environment (preferably healthcare).
At least 2 years in a program management or leadership role overseeing information security functions.
Strong working knowledge of HIPAA, NIST 800-53, HITRUST, and security risk management frameworks.

Certifications (preferred But Not Required)

Security +, CISSP, CISM, CRISC, HCISPP, or equivalent security certification.
PMP or similar project management certification is a plus.

Technical Skills

Understanding of endpoint protection, SIEM tools, MDM platforms (e.g., Intune), and vulnerability management solutions.
Experience with vendor risk tools, audit tracking systems, and compliance reporting.
Familiarity with Microsoft 365 Security Suite, KnowBe4, and GRC platforms.

Core Competencies

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical risks for non-technical stakeholders.
Highly organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple priorities simultaneously.
Demonstrated ability to build cross-functional relationships and drive accountability.
Passionate about RCA's mission and maintaining the privacy and security of patient information

Travel

Limited travel is required for this position
This position is primarily a remote position

This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of all activities, duties, or responsibilities required of the employee. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time, with or without notice, to meet the evolving needs of the organization. Nothing in this job description alters the at-will nature of employment, and either RCA or the employee may terminate the employment relationship at any time, with or without cause or notice.

RCA is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities to enable them to perform the essential functions of their role. Employees or applicants requiring accommodation should contact Human Resources to initiate the interactive accommodation process.

This position primarily involves sedentary work, including extended periods of sitting and computer use. The employee must be able to communicate effectively via phone, video conferencing, and written correspondence.

Non-Discrimination Statement

It is the policy of Recovery Centers of America (RCA) to ensure equal employment opportunity without discrimination or harassment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital status, citizenship, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law.

State Specific Responsibilities

Follows organizational cybersecurity policies, including acceptable use, password management, and multi-factor authentication requirements. jobs.title: Open Rank (Lecturer Track) in Cybersecurity for Cyber-Physical Systems and Founding Program Director
jobs.description:
Title Open Rank (Lecturer Track) in Cybersecurity for Cyber-Physical Systems and Founding Program Director Appointment Status Non-Tenure Track Department IU Columbus Columbus Location Columbus Position Summary

Position Summary

The Division of Behavioral, Health, and Life Sciences at Indiana University Columbus invites applications for a full-time, open-rank non-tenure-track faculty position in Cybersecurity for Cyber-Physical Systems. The successful candidate will be rank of Lecturer, Senior Lecturer, or Teaching Professor, depending upon qualifications, experience, and the applicable Indiana University and academic-unit criteria.

The successful candidate will also receive an initial administrative assignment as Founding Program Director for the proposed B.S. in Cybersecurity for Cyber-Physical Systems
. The position reports to the Head of the Division of Behavioral, Health and Life Sciences.

The proposed 120-credit Bachelor of Science program is designed to prepare students to secure computing systems that monitor or control physical processes. It combines foundations in programming, data structures, operating systems, networks, databases, distributed systems, cloud computing, cryptography, and cybersecurity with required study of embedded and real-time systems, industrial controls, hardware and firmware security, wireless and Internet-of-Things security, operational-technology incident response, security architecture, verification and validation, and system resilience.

The program is intended to serve advanced manufacturing, connected products, automotive and engine systems, industrial automation, robotics, material handling, utilities, healthcare technology, logistics, and other critical-infrastructure environments. Hands-on learning will include laboratory-intensive courses, CPS Security Studios, an isolated instructional cyber range, embedded devices, PLC/HMI equipment, industrial protocols, robotics or equivalent CPS platforms, and a two-semester applied capstone.

The anticipated Spring 2027 assignment will focus primarily on program finalization, student recruitment, curriculum and course development, laboratory planning, partner engagement, and implementation. The initial semester is not expected to include a regular classroom teaching assignment. Following program launch, teaching will be a central responsibility of the position, accompanied by an administrative course release for program leadership.

This is a 10-month academic appointment with a preferred start date of January 1, 2027. Summer program-development and launch responsibilities may be assigned and compensated separately through a summer stipend, subject to approval and available funding.

The position is based at IU Columbus and requires regular on-campus presence for program leadership, recruitment, student engagement, laboratory development, and face-to-face classroom and laboratory instruction.

Primary Responsibilities

Program Development and Implementation

Under the direction of the Division Head, the Founding Program Director will:

Coordinate final development and implementation of the B.S. in Cybersecurity for Cyber-Physical Systems.
Lead preparation and coordination of new-course proposals, CARMIn submissions, remonstrance materials, catalog information, and curricular documentation.
Coordinate development of course schedules, prerequisite sequences, degree maps, and the staged course rotation.
Develop and maintain program assessment processes, curriculum maps, direct-assessment plans, and documentation required for university and state review.
Coordinate laboratory and cyber-range planning, including equipment selection, instructional environments, safety and authorized-use expectations, and integration of laboratory resources into the curriculum.
Support implementation of the program’s Market Launch Plan, including student recruitment, information sessions, school and career-center outreach, campus visits, and laboratory demonstrations.
Coordinate development of advising, transfer, credential, career-pathway, and student-success materials.
Assist with future faculty searches and coordinate the contributions of program faculty under the direction of the Division Head.
Coordinate program review, annual reporting, and continuing curriculum improvement.
Participate, as assigned, in planning and stewardship of externally supported equipment and laboratory resources.

Teaching and Student Success

The faculty member will:

Teach introductory and advanced undergraduate courses supporting the program.
Develop and teach laboratory-centered, project-based, and applied learning experiences.
Teach introductory programming or information-infrastructure coursework and courses in multiple areas of cybersecurity and cyber-physical systems.
Advise and mentor students entering through first-year, transfer, adult, veteran, and technical-career pathways.
Support student retention, progression, credential preparation, career exploration, and timely degree completion.
Supervise or coordinate studios, applied projects, capstones, internships, or employer-informed learning experiences.
Use appropriate in-person, blended, and Canvas-supported instructional practices while maintaining the program’s required face-to-face laboratory experiences.

External and Institutional Engagement

Under the direction of the Division Head, the faculty member will:

Coordinate an employer and education advisory group for the program.
Develop productive relationships with employers, school corporations, career and technical education programs, community colleges, community organizations, and professional associations.
Support transfer-pathway development and continuing coordination with Ivy Tech Community College and Vincennes University.
Coordinate employer-informed projects, guest speakers, facility visits, internships, co-ops, capstone opportunities, mentors, and career activities, subject to partner capacity.
Represent the program at recruitment events, professional meetings, community forums, and appropriate university activities.
Participate in faculty governance and service appropriate to the appointment.

Professional Activity

This is a teaching-focused appointment and does not require a traditional disciplinary research agenda. The successful candidate will be expected to maintain professional currency and engage in scholarship or professional activity that supports teaching, curriculum development, applied student learning, industry collaboration, and the mission of IU Columbus.

Appointment Contingency

This position, the Founding Program Director assignment, and the anticipated January 2027 start date are contingent upon final program approval, continued institutional authorization, and the availability of funding.

About Indiana University Columbus

Indiana University Columbus offers accessible Indiana University degree programs in Columbus, Indiana, and serves students and communities throughout south-central Indiana. The campus emphasizes student success, career-connected education, community engagement, transfer access, and collaboration with regional employers and education partners.

The region provides an especially strong setting for a Cybersecurity for Cyber-Physical Systems program because of its concentration of advanced manufacturing, engineering, connected-product development, automation, logistics, healthcare technology, utilities, and other critical-infrastructure activity.

Basic Qualifications

Basic Qualifications

Applicants must meet one of the following educational and professional preparation pathways:

A terminal degree in computer science, cybersecurity, computer engineering, electrical engineering, informatics, information technology, systems engineering, or a closely related field by the appointment date; or
A master’s degree in a relevant field together with substantial professional experience in cybersecurity, cyber-physical systems, operational technology, embedded systems, industrial automation, connected products, or a closely related area.

Applicants must also demonstrate:

Relevant academic or professional expertise in cybersecurity, cyber-physical systems, operational technology, embedded computing, critical-infrastructure protection, or a closely related field.
The ability to teach introductory programming or information-infrastructure courses.
The ability to teach in at least two of the following areas:
Cybersecurity foundations;
Computer networks and network security;
Operational technology or ICS/SCADA security;
Embedded systems and microcontrollers;
Real-time operating systems;
Industrial automation and controls;
Hardware and firmware security;
Wireless and IoT security;
Secure software development;
Incident response or digital forensics;
Security architecture and critical-infrastructure resilience;
Verification, validation, testing, quality, or functional safety; or
Applied cryptography.

Evidence of, or clear potential for, effective undergraduate teaching and student mentoring.
The ability to develop applied, project-based, or laboratory-centered learning experiences.
The ability to collaborate effectively with faculty, staff, students, employers, educators, and community partners.
The ability to perform the position’s responsibilities through regular on-campus presence at IU Columbus.

Department Contact for Questions

Questions regarding the position may be directed to Dr. Kimdy Le, Division Head, kimle@iu.edu.

Additional Qualifications

Preferred Qualifications

Preference may be given to candidates who demonstrate one or more of the following:

Successful teaching experience at the undergraduate level.
Experience developing or teaching hands-on laboratories, studios, cyber ranges, or project-based technical courses.
Experience with one or more of the following:
PLC and HMI platforms;
Industrial protocols and networks;
Embedded devices and microcontrollers;
FreeRTOS, Zephyr, or comparable real-time operating systems;
Hardware and firmware security;
Robotics or autonomous systems;
Wireless and IoT environments;
Automotive, material-handling, or connected-product networks;
Hardware-in-the-loop or software-in-the-loop testing;
Digital forensics or evidence-preservation environments.

Professional experience in advanced manufacturing, automotive or connected products, engineering services, utilities, healthcare technology, logistics, material handling, building systems, or another critical-infrastructure sector.
Familiarity with NIST operational-technology guidance, the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, the NICE Workforce Framework, ISA-95, ISA/IEC 62443, secure systems engineering, verification and validation, functional safety, business continuity, or system resilience.
Experience with curriculum development, new-program implementation, academic assessment, accreditation or designation preparation, faculty coordination, or academic administration.
Experience developing employer-sponsored projects, internships, co-ops, applied research, or capstone experiences.
Experience recruiting and supporting students in a new or emerging technical program.
Experience developing transfer pathways or working with community colleges, high schools, career centers, or career and technical education programs.
Evidence of successful collaboration with employers, professional associations, schools, or community organizations.
Relevant industry credentials, including Security+, Network+, Linux+, CCNA, GICSP, ISA/IEC 62443 certificates, CISSP, or comparable credentials.
Experience teaching and mentoring students with varied educational, professional, and technical backgrounds.

Salary and Rank Open Rank - Lecturer Track Special Instructions

Application Process

Job description:

**Position Summary**

Serenity Home Health Care is seeking an experienced Director of Information Technology to lead and strengthen the company's internal IT operations. This person will be the senior internal technical owner for Microsoft 365, Microsoft Entra ID, Azure, Azure Virtual Desktop, networking, endpoints, backups, cybersecurity controls, and technology vendors. The goal is to build strong internal IT ownership so Serenity can manage its environment directly while using outside vendors only where specialized support is needed.

What This Role Is Responsible For

The Director will lead the internal IT team, set technical standards, protect Serenity's technology interests, and make sure the organization can operate, monitor, secure, recover, and improve its system without depending entirely on one outside provider.

Cloud and Microsoft Environment

* Provide internal ownership and oversight for Microsoft 365, Microsoft Entra ID, Azure, and Azure Virtual Desktop (AVD).
* Manage administrative access, role assignments, MFA, emergency access, and least-privilege controls.
* Oversee Azure subscriptions, resource access, monitoring, cost visibility, and technical documentation.
* Ensure AVD workspaces, host pools, session hosts, user access, images, patching, and support processes are properly managed.
* Help Serenity evaluate where AVD is still needed and where modern cloud-managed endpoints may be a better long-term solution.

Infrastructure, Network and Endpoints

* Oversee office connectivity, on-premises firewalls, VPNs, switching, Wi-Fi, DNS, and related network services.
* Work with the System Administrator and support staff to maintain reliable Windows devices,printers, servers, and business systems.
* Establish and maintain endpoint standards using Microsoft Entra ID, Intune, BitLocker, Defender, patching, and device compliance where adopted.
* Coordinate troubleshooting for major outages and make sure clear escalation procedures are in place.

Security, Backup and Recovery

* Work with Serenity leadership, compliance/GRC staff, and technical teams to turn security and HIPAA requirements into practical technical controls.
* Review privileged access, security alerts, audit logs, MFA, vendor access, and incident-response procedures.
* Ensure backup coverage is clearly documented and that backup failures are monitored and addressed.
* Make sure restore testing and disaster-recovery testing are performed and documented on a regular schedule.
* Maintain clear recovery procedures for critical systems and services.

IT Team and Vendor Leadership

* Lead and support Serenity's internal IT staff, including the System Administrator and other technical/support roles.
* Define responsibilities, priorities, escalation paths, documentation standards, and operating procedures for the IT team.
* Manage technical relationships with MSPs, cloud providers, security vendors, internet providers, software vendors, and other third parties.
* Review vendor work, access, deliverables, support performance, renewals, and technical dependencies.
* Ensure Serenity retains ownership of its accounts, documentation, configurations, data, backups, and administrative access.

Planning, Reporting and Business Support

* Prepare a practical IT roadmap covering cloud, endpoints, security, network, backup, licensing, and lifecycle planning.
* Monitor technology costs and work with leadership on budgets, licensing, renewals, and investment priorities.
* Provide clear updates to leadership on IT performance, risks, incidents, major projects, costs, and unresolved issues.
* Coordinate technology projects with department leaders while minimizing disruption to employees and business operations.
* Maintain accurate inventories, diagrams, procedures, support contacts, and change records.

**Qualifications**

* Required strong hands-on experience supporting Microsoft cloud and Windows environments.
* Required practical experience with Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Azure administration, identity and access management, and Windows systems.
* Experience supporting or overseeing Azure Virtual Desktop, virtualization, or enterprise remote'desktop environments.
* Solid understanding of networking, VPNs, firewalls, DNS, endpoint security, backup, and disaster recovery.
* Experience leading technical staff, coordinating vendors, and managing business-critical IT services.
* Ability to explain technical problems and recommendations clearly to non-technical leadership.
* Strong documentation, troubleshooting, project-management, and communication skills.

**Preferred**

* Experience in healthcare, home health, or another regulated environment.
* Experience with Microsoft Intune, Defender, Conditional Access, Windows Autopatch/Update forBusiness, and modern endpoint management.
* Experience with HIPAA-related technical safeguards, security reviews, incident response, and vendor access management.
* Microsoft certifications such as AZ-104, AZ-140, AZ-700, SC-300, or similar current cloud/security credentials.
* Experience managing a transition from vendor-led IT operations to a stronger internal IT operating model.

**First 90-Day Priorities**

1. Confirm Serenity-controlled administrative access and review all privileged accounts and vendor access.

2. Complete a current-state inventory of Microsoft, Azure/AVD, networks, servers, endpoints, backups, applications, vendors, and support responsibilities.

3. Confirm backup coverage and complete or schedule documented restore/disaster-recovery testing.

4. Review AVD operations, application dependencies, recurring issues, monitoring, and support procedures.

5. Establish a clear IT responsibility matrix for the Director, System Administrator, support staff, vendors, and leadership.

6. Create a short-term stabilization plan and a longer-term roadmap for Azure/AVD, cloud-managed endpoints, security, networking, and cost control.

7. Begin simple monthly reporting to leaders

**About Us**
============

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.

The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.

**Role Summary**
================

RVT vehicles for Volkswagen Group programs combine RVT zonal and platform ECUs with secondary ECUs (2nd ECUs) supplied by the VWG brands. Every RVT domain team has to integrate against those 2nd ECUs, and all of it depends on a shared network interface definition. Today that definition is largely handed to us by VWG and our domains are mainly taking in what they receive. We need to move to a world where each RVT domain owns its interfaces and changes flow incrementally rather than in large releases.

You will join the SW Systems Architecture team and partner with the interface architecture leads to run the network interface program inside RVT, drive the transition from consuming VWG's definition to domain owned interfaces, roll out the frameworks the architects define for 2nd ECUs, and give domain teams and leadership one current view of where each 2nd ECU stands. The architects set the technical direction. You turn it into a plan, a cadence and a set of artifacts the organization can execute against.

**Responsibilities**
====================

* Own the program plan for taking the RVT network interface to a fully defined and versioned baseline for each VWG program (Package 1, Package 2.1, Package 2.2 and beyond).
* Map out and drive the transition plan, per domain and per program, for moving interface ownership from VWG into the RVT domains, including what has to be true at each step and where the interim dependencies on VWG remain.
* Document and roll out the workflow the architects define for network interface versioning and change management inside RVT, including how incoming VWG interface changes are reviewed, how deltas reach the domains and how changes get closed out.
* Run the domain review cadence for interface changes and chase open items to closure across the domain teams.
* Coordinate network definition change requests from VWG, making sure impact is assessed by the right RVT owners and the outcome gets back to VWG.
* Roll out the framework the architects define for what has to be captured per 2nd ECU (functional spec, network interface needs, SW and HW version plan, OTA compliance, integration prerequisites), drive the domains to fill it in, and roll up the results.
* Maintain the up to date view of 2nd ECU maturity and risk per program that can be escalated to RVT and VWG leadership, and make the gaps visible when information from the brands does not exist.
* Operate the handoff between architecture level definition and the active integration tracking owned by the domain and program TPM teams.
* Set up the forums, status rhythm and documentation for this area, and act as the point of contact for VWG TPM counterparts on networking and 2nd ECU planning.

**Qualifications**
==================

* BS or MS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or a closely related technical field.
* 8+ years of technical program management on products that integrate hardware, software and mechanical systems, including embedded or vehicle programs taken from concept to production.
* Strong organization and the ability to influence and move an organization without direct authority, across every domain team and two parent companies.
* Experience planning and driving multi-step transitions of ownership or process across teams while the program keeps moving.
* Comfort in ambiguity. You can take a framework from the technical leads, turn it into a working process and artifacts, and iterate as the program evolves.
* Enough hands-on software or hardware background to follow architecture discussions and ask the right questions of architects and domain engineers.
* Experience bridging Agile and waterfall processes across partner organizations. Advanced Jira and Confluence.

jobs.title: Sr. Director, Information Technology and Systems
jobs.description:
ICON is looking for a Senior Director of Information Technology and Systems to build and own a unified technology strategy across a fast-growing, multi-division company. You will lead ICON's corporate IT, infrastructure, and information security functions, ensuring our technology stack drives business innovation, protects our systems and data, and scales with the company.
ICON operates across Construction, Technology, and Public Sector divisions, and builds robotic construction systems that are themselves connected, networked products. That makes this role broader than a typical corporate IT seat. You will define the boundary between our enterprise environment and our product environment, set the strategy for commercial and government-regulated work, and scale support through automation and smart architecture rather than headcount ratios as ICON grows significantly over the next two years.
You'll be a senior voice in executive decisions about technology. When leadership weighs a major choice, such as moving infrastructure on-premises or extending government-grade controls across the company, you'll lay out the cost, resourcing, risk, and second- and third-order impacts so the decision is made with full context, and you'll push back when the tradeoffs warrant it.
This role is a full-time, on-site position based at ICON's Austin, TX HQ Campus and will report to the President.
RESPONSIBILITIES Strategy and leadership

Lead and develop the IT, infrastructure, and security teams, including hiring and developing team leads, setting operating principles, and defining service level agreements.
Own the multi-year roadmap for AI tooling and core digital infrastructure, aligned to ICON's divisional strategies and growth plans.
Advise executive leadership on major technology decisions, presenting cost, resourcing, security, and organizational impacts in decision terms.
Lead change management for company-wide technology shifts, including potential expansion of government-regulated environments across the business.
Define clear ownership models for systems and roles that span corporate and divisional needs, deciding what lives in central IT versus within the teams it supports.
Deliver data-driven insights and technology performance reporting (ticket trends, automation impact, cost, and risk) to executive leadership on a regular basis.

Corporate IT and infrastructure

Oversee all corporate IT functions, including end-user support, device management and procurement, SaaS platforms, identity and access management, and enterprise system integrations.
Scale IT support efficiently as the company grows, using automation and self-service to keep support ratios lean.
Partner with People and Recruiting on hiring forecasts so equipment, access, and onboarding are ready for every new hire.
Oversee cloud and on-premises infrastructure across multiple regions, ensuring reliability, performance, scalability, and cost efficiency.
Guide build-versus-buy and SaaS-versus-on-premises decisions, making ownership and support costs explicit before commitments are made.
Lead vendor management, licensing, and technology procurement to maximize value and minimize risk.
Partner with data and analytics teams to ensure enterprise systems and infrastructure support cross-functional business intelligence needs.

Security and compliance

Own ICON's information security posture across corporate and product environments, including network segmentation between enterprise systems and connected product systems.
Ensure compliance with relevant frameworks and standards, including those required for government contracting, and oversee secure environments such as virtual desktop infrastructure for government work.
Demonstrate security and compliance credibility to public sector stakeholders, including government program partners.

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS 12+ years of progressive experience leading technology or information organizations, including 5+ years in a senior leadership role overseeing multiple teams through managers or team leads.
5+ years of experience leading technology teams in regulatory complex environments.
Proven track record managing corporate IT at scale, including enterprise systems, end-user computing, and IT operations, through a period of significant company growth.
Experience overseeing infrastructure and security teams, with working knowledge of network segmentation, cloud platforms, on-premises infrastructure, and the shared responsibility model.
Proficiency with cybersecurity frameworks and compliance requirements.
Demonstrated ability to influence executive decisions, build business cases, and push back with data.
Eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance.

PREFERRED SKILLS & EXPERIENCE Experience supporting or working within a government contracting environment, including standing up or expanding regulated enclaves.
Experience securing and supporting connected products (IoT, industrial controls, or robotics) alongside a corporate environment.
Track record of using automation to scale IT support without proportional headcount growth.
Exposure to enterprise data platforms (such as Palantir Foundry) and the integrations, identity, and infrastructure they depend on.
Strong program management skills, including the ability to set priorities across multiple teams and deliver concurrent initiatives on schedule.
Ability to communicate technical concepts and tradeoffs clearly to non-technical executives and business stakeholders.
Comfort operating in a fast-moving, innovative environment. Experience in construction technology, advanced manufacturing, or deep tech is a plus.

It is our policy to administer all personnel actions, including recruiting, hiring, training, and promoting employees, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin or ancestry, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other legally protected classification in accordance with applicable federal and state laws. jobs.title: Sr. Manager, Customer Success – Healthcare Cybersecurity
jobs.description:
Sr. Manager, Customer Success – Healthcare Cybersecurity

About the Role

The Sr. Manager of Customer Success leads Armis's healthcare customer success portfolio, serving as the strategic bridge between technical teams and healthcare stakeholders (clinical IT, biomedical engineering, compliance, security operations). You'll own portfolio performance across hospital systems and healthcare enterprises, mentor Technical CSMs supporting complex medical device and clinical network environments, and ensure consistent execution of strategies that drive adoption of OT/IT security across hospitals, labs, imaging centers, and clinical workflows. You'll translate healthcare compliance and operational realities into scalable success frameworks.
Key Responsibilities

Own regional ARR planning and attainment for healthcare accounts. Align resources to customer segmentation maturity levels, clinical network complexity, and regulatory timelines; run cadence reviews and intervene early on retention risks tied to medical device visibility or compliance gaps.
Standardize healthcare-specific EBR narratives around clinical network security outcomes (segmentation velocity, device inventory completeness, incident response readiness) and risk metrics. Partner with customers on FDA cybersecurity compliance storytelling and HIPAA/HITECH audit readiness.
Establish and enforce portfolio-level healthcare risk playbooks. Chair recurring risk reviews focused on critical device vulnerabilities, unmanaged endpoint exposure, and segmentation gaps; coordinate cross-functional mitigations with biomedical, IT, and security teams.
Operationalize healthcare network design reviews and security standards across the portfolio. Define best practices for DICOM/HL7 protocol visibility, clinical VLAN segmentation, NAC enforcement, and medical device inventory governance. Scale reusable patterns that accelerate time-to-value for multi-site hospital systems.
Run regional Voice of Customer cadences focused on healthcare-specific use cases. Aggregate clinical IT and biomedical requests into prioritized asks (e.g., remote maintenance security, OT/IT convergence visibility, wireless medical device monitoring); coordinate beta engagements and close feedback loops with Product and clinical advisory boards.
Establish enablement agenda for the healthcare team. Build proficiency baselines on medical device types (imaging, monitoring, therapeutic, lab), clinical communication protocols (HL7, DICOM, IEEE 11073, BACnet, Modbus), healthcare compliance frameworks (IEC 80001, NIST CSF for Healthcare, HIPAA Security Rule), and ensure expert coverage for complex architectures and incident response scenarios.
Own healthcare onboarding standards and playbooks. Define discovery workflows for multi-facility deployments, clinical network assessments, and medical device inventory projects. Measure adoption of best practices across segmentation, patching, and incident coordination.
Scale healthcare vertical frameworks. Tailor strategies for different customer profiles (academic medical centers vs. community hospitals vs. integrated delivery networks) and regulatory contexts (FDA premarket requirements, state healthcare data breach laws, CMS security standards).
Drive customer-to-product feedback loops. Maintain relationships with healthcare advisory boards and clinical IT leaders; advocate for product enhancements around medical device discovery, clinical protocol monitoring, and healthcare-specific compliance reporting.
Model ethical decision-making on healthcare security trade-offs (balancing security hardening against clinical operational continuity). Hold team accountable to balanced customer outcomes and organizational targets.
Cultivate a learning culture. Run retros on customer implementations, institutionalize playbooks for common healthcare scenarios (device compromise, network anomalies, remote access hardening), and build skills roadmaps for Technical CSMs working in healthcare environments.

Qualifications

10+ years in Customer Success, Account Management, Solutions Engineering, or Consulting within B2B SaaS or enterprise cybersecurity, with 5+ years focused on healthcare IT, medical device security, or clinical network environments
.
Proven track record managing technical portfolios and leading teams in healthcare cybersecurity, OT/IT convergence, or medical device security.
Deep understanding of healthcare network infrastructure (clinical VLANs, medical device protocols, segmentation, remote access for biomedical vendors).
Demonstrated fluency with healthcare communication protocols (DICOM, HL7/FHIR, IEEE 11073, BACnet, Modbus) and ability to translate protocol security implications to clinical stakeholders.
Strong knowledge of healthcare compliance frameworks (HIPAA, HITECH, FDA cybersecurity premarket/postmarket guidance, IEC 80001, NIST CSF for Healthcare).
Exceptional ability to manage relationships across technical and clinical stakeholders (biomedical engineers, clinical IT directors, compliance officers, hospital security teams).
Track record of managing large, complex healthcare customer implementations (multi-site systems, high-touch deployments, regulatory audits).
Bachelor's degree in IT, Computer Science, Healthcare IT, Biomedical Engineering, or related discipline (required); advanced degree or equivalent healthcare security experience preferred.

Preferred Attributes

Experience with healthcare-specific cybersecurity or visibility platforms (Claroty, Dragos, Nozomi, or similar OT/medical device security solutions).
Experience working with biomedical engineering teams or clinical IT leadership on device security and network architecture projects.
Familiarity with healthcare incident response workflows and coordination across clinical, IT, and security operations teams.
Knowledge of hospital architecture standards (e.g., AAMI TIR57 guidelines for clinical IT security).
Strategic systems thinker who excels at translating clinical and compliance complexity into scalable operational frameworks.
Exceptional communication skills with ability to present security concepts to non-technical clinical leaders and executive stakeholders.
Data-driven decision-maker with strong portfolio analytics and KPI design experience.
Empathetic leader committed to developing Technical CSMs and building team capability in healthcare-specific domains.

For positions in this location, we offer a base pay of $158,000 - $
208,750, plus equity (when applicable), variable/incentive compensation and benefits. Sales positions generally offer a competitive On Target Earnings (OTE) incentive compensation structure. Please note that the base pay shown is a guideline, and individual total compensation will vary based on factors such as qualifications, skill level, competencies, and work location. We also offer health plans, including flexible spending accounts, a 401(k) Plan with company match, ESPP, matching donations, a flexible time away plan and family leave programs. Compensation is based on the geographic location in which the role is located and is subject to change based on work location.
