jobs.title: Senior Director, Quality Coaching – Technology Innovation and Impact
jobs.description:
Full-time | Washington, DC | Reports to the Senior Vice President, Quality Coaching | Travel: 15–20%

Lead How Technology Can Strengthen Human-connected Coaching

Strada Education Foundation's Quality Coaching team is working to expand access to quality education-to-career coaching. Its work is organized around three change drivers: Transition Coaching, strengthening guidance as learners move from high school into postsecondary education and employment; Postsecondary Education Quality Coaching, strengthening coaching within postsecondary institutions; and Statewide Quality Coaching Models, helping states expand access to quality coaching at scale.

Strada's Principles for Quality Education-to-Career Guidance emphasize outcomes, student agency, universal access, relationships, and the use of data and evidence. New technologies like AI offer cross-cutting capabilities that can strengthen these principles by expanding access and personalization, improving the use of labor market and outcomes information, and augmenting – rather than replacing – the human relationships central to quality coaching.

We are looking for a Senior Director who will lead Quality Coaching's Technology Innovation portfolio, building on Strada's existing research, investments, and partnerships to advance human-centered technology that augments human-connected coaching. The portfolio focuses on three key questions: (1) where and how technology can most effectively augment career coaching; (2) what quality standards and benchmarks should guide career navigation tools; and (3) what data systems and infrastructure are needed to support quality coaching at scale.

As a member of the Quality Coaching leadership team, you will also strengthen the entire portfolio by overseeing the team's Project Manager and providing strategic oversight for grants, impact measurement and learning, and teamwide project management. You will bring rigorous analysis, synthesis, and judgment to complex strategic questions and help translate strategy, evidence, and innovation into measurable impact.

What You'll Do

Lead Technology Innovation Strategy and Portfolio (60%)
You'll develop and lead the strategy and portfolio that helps scale Quality Coaching's three change drivers. That means:

Develop and lead Quality Coaching's Technology Innovation strategy and portfolio, defining priorities and use cases, investments, partnerships, measures of success, and other pathways to scale.
Advance the Technology Innovation learning agenda by building evidence and actionable guidance about how technology can augment human-connected coaching and career navigation.
Determine the quality standards and technical benchmarks that should guide technology-enabled career coaching tools.
Understand the systems, data infrastructure, and appropriate roles for AI needed to support quality coaching at scale.
Assess the career navigation technology ecosystem and identify promising solutions, capabilities, gaps, and emerging opportunities, to help Strada determine whether to partner, invest, or discontinue approaches.
Translate research, investments, pilots, and field learning into practical frameworks and scalable approaches that help states, institutions, schools, and coaching organizations responsibly adopt and integrate human-centered technology.
Serve as Strada's Quality Coaching subject-matter leader on technology and AI, partnering across other departments (Research, Strategy & Innovation, and Impact Investments) and with external partners to advance shared opportunities.
Collaborate with Strada's Learner Engagement team to incorporate what students are saying about their lived experiences into the design, evaluation, and continuous improvement of tech-enabled coaching approaches.

Provide Strategic Analysis, Synthesis and Cross-Team Leadership (15%)
Strong strategy depends on clear thinking and trusted relationships. You will:

Independently frame and analyze complex strategic questions, drawing on research, data, portfolio learning, and partner perspectives to identify patterns, risks, opportunities, and next steps.
Synthesize complex and incomplete information, shape initial responses to cross-functional and organizational requests, and drive issues toward resolution through clear options, tradeoffs, and decision-ready recommendations for the SVP, Quality Coaching and other senior leaders.
Contribute as a member of the Quality Coaching leadership team, identifying connections across the three change drivers and leading cross-functional priorities through influence, clear decision-making, and accountability.
Represent Strada with researchers, funders, policymakers, education leaders, and technology providers to share relevant learning through presentations, publications, partnerships, and convenings.
Lead complex, cross-functional initiatives through influence, establishing clear roles, decision rights, and accountability across internal and external partners.

Advance Impact, Evidence and Portfolio Execution (15%)
You'll help make sure good ideas turn into measurable results. You will:

Provide strategic oversight for Quality Coaching's grants, contracts, and impact investments, working with cross-functional partners to strengthen portfolio coherence, grant development, implementation, learning, and decision-making.
Coordinate Quality Coaching's approach to impact measurement and learning, partnering with Research and initiative leaders to establish clear outcomes, learning questions, measures of success, and evidence-building approaches and to translate findings into decisions.
Manage and develop the Project Manager, Quality Coaching, providing strategic direction for teamwide project and portfolio management, annual planning, progress monitoring, grants coordination, budgets, and other operating systems.
Provide light-touch project management leadership across Quality Coaching, ensuring visibility into major priorities, deliverables, dependencies, risks, resource needs, and decision points while maintaining clear accountability with initiative leaders for substantive strategy and results.
Strengthen connections across the Quality Coaching portfolio by identifying patterns, shared learning, and opportunities that can improve execution and impact across initiatives.

Support Organizational Health and Culture (10%)

Serve as an integrator across Quality Coaching, connecting perspectives and work across initiative leaders and coordinating strategic follow-through on shared priorities.
Foster a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performing team culture grounded in Strada's board-approved principles, valued behaviors, and ways of working.
Contribute to Quality Coaching and organization-wide efforts to strengthen organizational health, employee engagement, collaboration, inclusion, belonging, and continuous improvement.
Support the development and success of colleagues through coaching, feedback, and knowledge sharing while contributing to shared accountability and collective success.

What Success Looks Like in Your First Year

You are advancing a coherent Technology Innovation strategy and portfolio across Quality Coaching's three change drivers, with clear priorities, use cases, intended outcomes, and pathways for testing, learning, adoption, and scale
You have generated actionable frameworks and insights addressing how technology augments human-connected coaching, quality standards and technical benchmarks for career navigation tools, and the systems, data infrastructure, and interoperability needed to support quality coaching at scale
You have strengthened impact measurement and learning across Quality Coaching through clearer outcomes, learning questions, measures of success, and synthesis of evidence to inform strategy, investment, adaptation, and scale
You have established effective oversight of Quality Coaching's grants and portfolio management, with clear visibility into major investments, priorities, deliverables, risks, dependencies, resources, and decision points
You are successfully managing and developing the Project Manager and have established a light-touch PMO function that improves teamwide planning, coordination, accountability, and execution without displacing initiative-level ownership
You are providing high-quality strategic analysis, decision support, and cross-team leadership by independently framing complex questions, producing decision-ready recommendations, and strengthening collaboration across Quality Coaching and Strada

What You Bring

Required

At least 8 years of progressively responsible experience in education technology, innovation, career coaching, student success, workforce development, philanthropy, strategy, and consulting, including significant responsibility for independently leading complex strategic initiatives.
Demonstrated experience developing and executing technology- or AI-enabled strategies and translating innovative ideas into practical pilots, partnerships, investments, and scalable approaches, preferably involving education, coaching, advising, career navigation, or other learner-facing services.
Strong portfolio leadership and execution skills, with experience overseeing complex portfolios, grants or investments, project-management systems, and progress monitoring from strategy through implementation, measurement, and learning.
Highly independent strategic thinker and self-starter who can create structure amid ambiguity, frame and analyze complex questions, synthesize qualitative and quantitative information, assess alternatives and tradeoffs, distinguish signal from noise, and translate analysis into actionable recommendations.
Exceptional synthesis, writing, communication, and presentation skills, with demonstrated ability to translate complex information into concise, compelling memos, analyses, recommendations, presentations, and board-level materials for technical and nontechnical audiences.
Demonstrated experience defining measurable outcomes and learning questions and partnering with research or evaluation experts to use evidence to inform strategy, investment, adaptation, and scale.
Demonstrated experience managing and developing staff and leading complex, cross-functional work by building trusted relationships and successfully advancing shared priorities in a distributed leadership team environment and in a matrixed organization.
Experience managing consultants, grants, vendors, and external partnerships and leading teams and complex initiatives through influence, with a demonstrated commitment to developing others and strengthening team performance.
Knowledge of responsible AI practices and the opportunities, limitations, and risks associated with using technology to serve learners, including privacy, accessibility, transparency, student agency, data interoperability, evidence, and the appropriate role of human relationships in coaching and career navigation.
Demonstrated ability to cultivate, grow, and manage positive, mutually beneficial relationships at all levels of an organization and with partners outside the organization, with strong communication, interpersonal, and relationship management skills, underscored by strong judgment and emotional intelligence.

Nice To Have

An advanced degree, with training in education, technology, innovation, business, public policy, social science, data and analytics, or a related field

Also Important

Commitment to providing equitable pathways to opportunity through postsecondary education and training, particularly for individuals who have faced significant barriers, and demonstrated alignment with Strada's guiding values

--------------------

Joby Flight Research designs, develops, and flight-tests novel aircraft using a software-first autonomy approach. We build and deploy autonomy, perception, planning, and radar systems across conventional, electric, and hydrogen-electric aircraft in both CTOL and VTOL configurations.

**Overview**
------------

Joby is seeking a passionate, driven, entrepreneurial Technical Program Manager to own the integrated development program for a confidential, strategically important new business. The role requires a candidate who thrives in uncertainty, can connect technical readiness with product and service maturation, and can drive alignment across diverse stakeholders - from hardware and software engineering teams to external partners and customers.

  

This role will report directly to the Head of Aircraft Development and dotted line to the General Manager, and will own the program plan end to end: aircraft systems development, software, payload integration, test campaigns, and the path to operational service. This is a high-ownership role for a structured operator who can hold the whole program in their head while driving the details every week.

**Responsibilities**
--------------------

* **Drive the integrated program schedule:** Take ownership of the development plan spanning hardware, software, systems integration, and validation, driving the evolving plan toward full readiness for customers. You will build robust planning frameworks with cross-functional stakeholders, support the development and validation of requirements, and establish comprehensive plans for service introduction
* **Cross-functional integration and bridge-building:** Serve as the essential integrator across aircraft development, payload development, systems engineering, aircraft and platform integration, flight test, and commercial/business development. This requires enough technical fluency to hold credible conversations with deep technical teams, flight test teams, and external technology partners - while keeping program outcomes central to decision-making
* **Operate without a playbook:** Operate at the forefront of a category that doesn't have an established playbook. Scope, prioritize, and problem-solve complex challenges with cross-functional project teams from inception through testing and field introduction, with continuous, proactive management of program risk
* **Proactive risk management:** Identify and assess risk across technology readiness, work scope, manufacturing readiness, partner dependencies, and resource allocation. Run structured trade-off analyses to inform strategic decisions, resolve conflicts, build consensus, and keep teams aligned across all phases and stakeholder groups
* **Coordinate external technical partnerships:** Support engagements with technology suppliers, partners, and customers - translating between partner requirements and internal development plans, and ensuring commitments on both sides are tracked and met
* **Build processes and program structures for scale:** Champion the development of scalable processes and adaptable program roadmaps designed to accommodate a rapid pace of innovation and commercialization
* **Partner with the Business Team:** Serve as the source of truth on program timelines for commercial and government engagements - informing what the business can commit to, by when, and at what confidence level

**Required**
------------

* 4+ years of technical program management experience
* 3+ years of engineering experience, ideally in an aerospace & defense program
* Proven program management experience in advanced technology development - ideally space, aviation, autonomy, or related industries
* Strong ability to manage scope, uncertainty, and complexity - with a record of delivering programs where success wasn't guaranteed
* Solid technical literacy in one or more areas: embedded systems, autonomy/AI, controls, sensing technologies, aerospace systems, wireless communications / RF systems
* Experience with vertical integration, supply chain and manufacturing management
* Exceptional communication skills: able to engage executive leadership, deep technical teams, and external partners with equal fluency
* Demonstrated ability to drive decision-making across stakeholders with diverse priorities
* High-ownership mindset: proactive, reliable, detail-oriented, and comfortable operating in ambiguity
* Bachelor's degree in engineering, computer science, or a related technical field

**Desired**
-----------

* Experience bringing complex hardware/software products through development, integration, and external partnerships
* Advanced degree preferred, but not required

Compensation at Joby is a combination of base pay and Restricted Stock Units (RSUs). The target base pay for this position is $126,600 - $219,300/yr. The compensation package will be determined by job-related knowledge, skills, and experience.

  

Joby also offers a comprehensive benefits package, including paid time off, healthcare benefits, a 401(k) plan with a company match, an employee stock purchase plan (ESPP), short-term and long-term disability coverage, life insurance, and more.

  

Joby is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

jobs.title: Chief Information Officer
jobs.description:
The Chief Information Officer (CIO) is responsible for formulating and leading the company's overall information technology and informatization strategy, ensuring that the enterprise's technology ecosystem, information systems, data infrastructure, and digital capabilities support long-term business goals and operational needs.

This role is typically one of the highest-level technology management positions in the organization. The CIO oversees IT strategy, enterprise systems, data management, information security, technology governance, digital transformation, and IT operations, while collaborating with the CEO, CFO, COO, CTO, and heads of business units to translate technology investments into measurable business value.

Core Responsibilities

I. Information Technology Strategy
- Formulate the company's medium- to long-term IT strategy and annual IT plans.
- Translate business strategies into informatization and technology development plans.
- Establish roadmaps for the development of enterprise IT architecture, systems, and technical capabilities.
- Adjust technology investments and IT resource allocation in line with business growth.
- Ensure alignment between IT strategy and the overall corporate strategy.

II. Enterprise Information Systems Management
- Oversee ERP, CRM, HRIS, financial systems, and other enterprise application platforms.
- Monitor the stability, scalability, and operational performance of core information systems.
- Drive the integration of enterprise systems to reduce redundancy and eliminate technology silos.
- Establish mechanisms for enterprise application lifecycle management.
- Ensure information systems continuously support business development.

III. IT Operations and Infrastructure
- Oversee enterprise IT operations, infrastructure, networks, cloud environments, and end-user services.
- Establish standards for IT service management and operations.
- Ensure the stability, availability, and business continuity of critical systems.
- Oversee the management of IT incidents, problems, and changes.
- Continuously improve IT service quality and operational efficiency.
IV. Data and Information Management

- Formulate strategies for enterprise data management, data governance, and information architecture.
- Establish unified standards for data, data quality, and data security.
- Drive the development of enterprise data platforms, business analytics, and management dashboards.
- Enhance data transparency and cross-departmental data collaboration capabilities.
- Facilitate the use of data to inform operational and strategic decision-making.

V. Information Security and Risk Management
- Lead the enterprise's information security and IT risk management frameworks.
- Establish information security policies, control measures, and risk monitoring mechanisms.
- Oversee cybersecurity, identity management, access control, and data protection.
- Collaborate with security teams to respond to major security incidents.
- Ensure the IT environment complies with corporate policies and applicable regulatory requirements.

VI. Digital Transformation
- Lead enterprise digital transformation and IT modernization initiatives.
- Evaluate the business value of technologies such as cloud computing, AI, automation, and data analytics.
- Drive the digitization and automation of traditional business processes.
- Establish mechanisms for prioritizing digital projects and evaluating investments.
- Ensure digital investments yield tangible operational and business outcomes.

VII. IT Project and Investment Management
- Coordinate major enterprise IT projects and project portfolios.
- Oversee project scope, budget, schedule, risks, and deliverables.
- Establish systems for analyzing IT investment ROI and managing project performance.
- Optimize the IT investment portfolio based on business priorities.
- Advise the CEO and Board of Directors on major technology investments.

VIII. Business-Technology Alignment
- Serve as a key liaison between business teams and the IT organization.
- Deeply understand business needs and drive the implementation of technology solutions.
- Collaborate with business leaders to prioritize systems, data, and technology initiatives.
- Enhance operational efficiency and customer experience through IT capabilities.
- Transition the technology team from a cost center to a driver of business value.

IX. IT Organization and Team Leadership
- Build and lead the enterprise IT organization and management team.
- Design the IT organizational structure, role definitions, and management mechanisms.
- Develop talent in areas such as IT projects, infrastructure, data, security, and enterprise applications.
- Establish frameworks for team performance, talent development, and succession planning.
- Cultivate an IT organizational culture that is high-performing, business-oriented, and innovative.

Qualifications

Education
- Bachelor’s degree or higher in Computer Science, Information Systems, Information Technology, Engineering, Business Management, or a related field.
- MBA, MS in Information Systems, or a related master’s degree is preferred. - Professional certifications such as CISSP, CISM, ITIL, and PMP are preferred.

Work Experience
- 20+ years of experience in Information Technology, IT operations, enterprise systems, or digital transformation.
- 15+ years of experience in senior IT management or enterprise technology leadership.
- Experience in enterprise-level IT strategy, system implementation, and IT governance.
- Experience managing large-scale IT organizations, multi-regional teams, or complex enterprise environments.
- Experience in budgeting, technology investment, vendor management, and large-scale project management.

Core Competencies
- Information Technology Strategy

- Enterprise Architecture

- Technology Investment
- Business-Technology Alignment

jobs.title: Interim Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
Department Overview

The mission of the Information Technology Group (ITG) is to develop, implement and maintain technology-based services and solutions to enable OHSU to effectively manage information to accomplish its missions.

Reporting directly to the Senior Vice President and OHSU Chief Information Officer, the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) is a member of the ITG executive leadership team and sets the vision, strategy, and direction for OHSU's core technology infrastructure and architecture. The CTO has broad oversight of technology and infrastructure operations, projects and planning, and holds ultimate responsibility for the technology services components of OHSU's strategic and tactical initiatives. The CTO also positions the organization to adopt emerging technologies in ways that advance OHSU's clinical, research and academic missions.

The most critical function of the role is ensuring the ongoing, 24x7 operation of OHSU systems and networks. A stable, secure and resilient technology environment is vital to business continuity for the university.

The CTO leads the Technology Infrastructure, Design and Engineering (TIDE) Division, which delivers enterprise-wide core technology support including networks, compute and storage, telecommunications support, data centers, design and construction, collaboration and core applications and business continuity.

Function/Duties of Position

Technology Management

The strategic role of the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) is to establish direction and technology vision, to develop and pursue technical standards, to set general direction around core technology architecture and to evaluate and guide the adoption of emerging technologies. The operational role is to create and maintain the structure necessary to ensure business continuity through a stable technology infrastructure.

These Roles Translate To The Following Major Responsibilities

Responsible for defining a robust, scalable, extensible technology architecture that is fully integrated with the wider enterprise architecture and aligned with industry best practices.
Responsible for defining engineering and technical standards, processes and procedures for core technology, and ensuring consistent adoption across the division.
Directs the delivery and ongoing reliability of core technology services, systems and networks. Includes oversight of operational procedures and disaster planning. Ensures infrastructure is designed and maintained in accordance with security standards established by the Chief Information Security Officer and broader enterprise architecture strategy.
Responsible for establishing IT capacity planning to ensure technology infrastructure meets OHSU’s current and future needs. Proactively identifies technical infrastructure risks, emerging requirements and systems issues, and develops solutions.
Establishes and oversees performance metrics and measurements for division to inform tactical and long-range decision making.
Manage departmental operating and capital budgets and partner with Vendor Management to oversee strategic technology vendor relationships and contracts.

Division Leadership

The Chief Technology Officer (CTO) provides supervision and mentoring to Directors and frontline managers in the division. These directors and managers have day-to-day, functional responsibility for their areas and their perspectives are best focused on their individual specializations. The CTO’s role is to ensure that the collective group works in a unified, collaborative, cohesive direction.

ITG Executive Management

The Chief Technology Officer (CTO) is a member of the ITG executive management team, which collectively strives toward the common goals, strategies and vision of ITG and OHSU. Works with executive management to determine and execute the strategic goals and initiatives in support of the broader organization.

As part of the executive team, the CTO will gain a broad view of OHSU’s IT strategies and operations, which they must translate to efforts, direction and oversight within the division.

The CTO represents ITG executive management on committees and other groups.

Required Qualifications

Education and Experience

Master’s degree in information technology or related field; OR
Bachelor’ s degree in information technology or related field and significant experience in Information Technology.
Minimum of 8 years of progressively responsible management positions in information technology.
Three years of experience in technology management at senior management level, including budgeting and financial reporting.
Experience evaluating business requirements, technology options, operating models, costs, risks, and governance considerations. Significant organizational and management skills, specifically within a large organization.
Experience developing and implementing IT strategies.
IT project/program management experience to successfully manage small- and large-scale applications projects.
Experience in a complex technology environment.

Skills And Abilities

Broad range of knowledge of IT systems, networks, telecommunications.
Effective leadership of highly skilled management and technical personnel in overseeing the development and implementation of technology strategy and planning.
Superior oral, written and communication skills.
Ability to operate in a highly stressful environment, demonstrating good judgment and creative/original thinking to address the demands of the business.
Ability to influence, motivate and provide clear direction.
Ability to use tact and diplomacy to maintain effective working relationships.
Skilled in overseeing multiple projects with budget responsibilities.
Demonstrated skill in managing operational and capital budgets.
Must have knowledge of ITIL service management concepts.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience managing in a union environment.
Experience in an academic health system, healthcare, higher education, or similarly complex regulated environment.
Expert knowledge in information technology (systems, telecommunications, networks).
Knowledge of healthcare, research and academic environments and applications.
Knowledge of quality management and performance improvement techniques.

Additional Details

Location: This position is eligible for hybrid-remote work, the work location will primarily be remote with with occasional meetings and events onsite at various OHSU locations.

Benefits

Healthcare for full-time employees covered 100% and 88% for dependents.
$50K of term life insurance provided at no cost to the employee.
Two separate above market pension plans to choose from.
Paid time off - 208 hours per year, prorated for part-time.

9 paid holidays per year.
Substantial Tri-Met and C-Tran discounts.
Employee Assistance Program.

Why apply to OHSU?

We are Oregon's only public academic health center.

In addition to caring for patients, we lead groundbreaking research. We also train the next generation of health care professionals. As Portland's largest employer, we give you opportunities to learn and advance in a system of hospitals and clinics across Oregon and Southwest Washington.

All are welcome.

OHSU welcomes people of all ages, ethnicities, genders, national origins, religions and sexual orientations. We are striving to build an anti-racist, multicultural institution and encourage people with diverse backgrounds to apply.

jobs.title: Vice President of Enterprise IT
jobs.description:
Company Description
Ashar Urban Futures Lab (Ashar UFL) is India’s first venture studio dedicated to the urban built environment, spanning UrbanTech, PropTech, ConstructionTech, Material Alternatives, DesignTech, and Climate Infrastructure. In a context where India adds the equivalent of one Chicago to its urban footprint every year but receives minimal innovation capital for the built world, Ashar UFL exists to bridge this gap. Backed by Ashar Group’s large-scale real estate and infrastructure operations, the studio offers founders live testbeds in active developments, deep operator access, and proximity to policy. Ashar UFL supports startups from ideation through piloting, validation, and scaling within the systems that shape Indian cities. It is a platform for urban problem-solvers who want to build solutions that define the future of cities.
Role Description
The Vice President of Enterprise IT is a full-time remote role responsible for leading the end-to-end technology vision and execution across Ashar UFL’s venture studio and portfolio initiatives. This position oversees enterprise IT architecture, infrastructure, applications, and security to ensure resilient, scalable, and compliant technology environments. The role includes developing and implementing IT strategies aligned with business objectives, managing IT operations, and standardizing tools and platforms for ventures and internal teams. The Vice President of Enterprise IT will collaborate closely with leadership, founders, and cross-functional teams to enable data-driven decision-making, streamline workflows, and support digital innovation across the built environment. Day-to-day responsibilities include directing IT projects, managing vendor relationships, optimizing budgets, and building a high-performing IT function that supports rapid experimentation and deployment.
Qualifications

Strong foundation in Information Technology, including enterprise systems, infrastructure, cloud platforms, cybersecurity, and data management.
Demonstrated experience in IT Management, with a track record of leading IT teams, overseeing operations, and managing vendors and service providers.
Proven ability in IT Strategy and Strategic Planning to align technology roadmaps with organizational goals and portfolio needs.
Solid Project Management skills to plan, execute, and deliver complex IT initiatives on time and within budget.
Experience implementing technology solutions in dynamic, innovation-focused environments such as venture studios, startups, or high-growth organizations.
Ability to work effectively in a remote, distributed setting, with strong communication and stakeholder management skills.
Relevant academic background in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field; advanced degrees or professional certifications (e.g., PMP, ITIL, CISSP, TOGAF) are an advantage.
Familiarity with UrbanTech, PropTech, or related sectors and an interest in how technology can transform cities and the built environment is highly beneficial.

jobs.title: Deputy Director of Information Technology
jobs.description:
**Overview**

Deputy Director of Information Technology

**Boone County, Missouri**

Boone County is seeking an experienced technology leader to serve as **Deputy Director of Information Technology**. This is a senior leadership position responsible for supporting the Director in the strategic direction, administration, and day-to-day operations of the County’s technology services.

As second in command of the department, the Deputy Director plays a key role in shaping the County’s technology strategy, leading managers and major initiatives, overseeing critical support functions, and ensuring reliable, secure, and effective technology services across County government. This position serves as Director in their absence.

What You’ll Do

In this role, you will:

* Supervise managers responsible for **Information Technology, GIS, Mail Services, and Facilities Security**.
* Lead and support departmental operations, staffing, payroll, budgeting, personnel administration, contracts, and major technology projects.
* Partner closely with the Director on **strategic planning, technology priorities, vendor relations, contract negotiations, and organizational initiatives**.
* Work with County leadership to identify technology needs, establish priorities, evaluate system capacity, and plan future equipment and technology investments.
* Help establish and maintain standards for computer hardware, software, systems, and technology services.
* Oversee the County’s GIS operations, including GIS data quality, web services, programming, and related centralized services.
* Provide leadership for Mail Services operations serving County facilities.
* Oversee Facilities Security technology, including electronic access control, alarms, and video security systems.
* Manage complex projects and help ensure departmental goals and service expectations are met.
* Build strong working relationships with County departments, vendors, employees, and members of the public.

What We’re Looking For

The successful candidate will bring strong leadership skills along with broad knowledge of modern information technology operations. We are looking for someone who can balance strategic thinking with the practical demands of managing people, projects, budgets, and critical technology services.

Strong candidates will have experience with areas such as:

* IT leadership and project management
* Application development and enterprise systems
* Networks, servers, telecommunications, and desktop technologies
* Relational databases and cloud-based solutions
* Website and content management technologies
* GIS principles and systems
* Information security and technology compliance
* Budgeting, contracts, procurement, and vendor management
* Hiring, developing, supervising, and evaluating staff
* Large-scale organizational or technology initiatives

The position requires strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to establish productive working relationships across departments and with the public.

Minimum Qualifications

* Bachelor’s degree in **Computer Science, Business, Administration, or a closely related field**
* Five years of information technology services experience
* Personnel management experience, preferably in a government environment

Preferred Qualifications

* Advanced degree in **Business or Public Administration**
* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science or a closely related field
* Five years of personnel management experience, preferably in government

Additional Requirements

This position works primarily in a professional office environment and requires the ability to travel between County locations. A valid ability to operate a vehicle in accordance with County vehicle policies is required.

Why Boone County?

This is an opportunity to take on a highly visible leadership role supporting technology and essential services throughout Boone County government. The Deputy Director will have the opportunity to influence long-term technology strategy while working closely with County leadership and an experienced team of technology professionals.

**Benefit-eligible employees receive** paid vacation, 14 paid holidays, enrollment in the County Employees Retirement Fund, two matching deferred compensation plans, low- or no-cost employee health insurance options, County-paid employee dental coverage, subsidized dependent premiums, and County-paid life and long-term disability insurance.

Apply

Apply by clicking the **Apply Now** link or visiting www.boonemo.gov/hr. You will be directed to Boone County’s online application system, where you can create or log in to your applicant profile.

Questions? Call **(573) 886-4395**. Please contact us in advance if you need an accommodation to complete the application process.

Pay: $97,094.00 - $100,027.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Flexible schedule
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

* Do you have a bachelor's degree in computer science or a related field

* personnel management: 5 years (Required)

Work Location: In person

**The application window is expected to close on:** 10/15/2026Members of the Finance organization at select locations will generally be expected to follow a hybrid work model, which includes two days of in-office attendance each week, with limited exceptions.
  
  
**Your Impact:**  
Cisco is seeking a Senior Manager, Finance PMO, to provide strategic support to the SVP of Corporate Finance and the broader FP organization. This high-impact leadership role is responsible for driving organizational transformation, innovation, and operational excellence at scale. You will run critically important programs across global Finance teams and cross-functional partners, ensuring transparency and alignment with corporate objectives.
  
By demonstrating critical thinking and operational difficulty, you will reduce organizational friction, standardize operational practices, and champion the adoption of AI and new technologies to enable scalable automation and predictive insights. You will serve as a key partner to teams across Finance (including Corporate, GTM, and Product FP) and cross-functional organizations such as IT, People, Engineering, and Pricing. Your success will be defined by your ability to plan and implement effectively, encouraging collaboration across teams with varied strengths to drive transformative change.
  
  
Corporate Finance Project and Program Management
  
  

* Role Definition& Process Mapping: Partner with departmental teams to systematically define key roles and responsibilities. Conduct comprehensive current-state process mapping to uncover operational bottlenecks and dependencies.
* Annual Strategic Alignment: Act as a primary partner in the execution and monitoring of the Annual Company Plan, ensuring all finance-led initiatives are rigorously aligned with corporate strategic objectives.
* Goal Execution: Facilitate the annual Corporate Finance goal-setting process and be responsible for the execution and tracking of these objectives.
* Cross-Functional Leadership: Run sophisticated, cross-functional programs in collaboration with partners from IT, Engineering, Sales, and global Finance teams.
* Ad Hoc Initiatives: Lead high-priority, ad hoc strategic projects to support critical Finance leadership requirements as they emerge.

Corporate Finance Operational Excellence& Transformation
  
  

* End-to-End AI Automation: Drive the AI automation lifecycle wherever possible, translating manual, repetitive, or legacy workflows into streamlined, AI-assisted operations across FP and broader enterprise functions.
* Organization-Wide AI Scaling: Evangelize and implement the AI automation roadmap across the entire company, ensuring local automation successes are scaled into global, platform-level capabilities.
* Metrics& Enablement: Ensure the achievement of success criteria and metrics through partner enablement and rigorous process management.
* Scalable Solutions: Partner with internal and cross-functional teams to implement scalable, automated solutions that leverage AI to improve decision-making.

Communication& Alignment
  
  

* Organizational Design: Support the strategic build and development of the Corporate Finance organization to ensure it effectively scales with Cisco’s growth.
* Executive Facilitation: Facilitate executive-level communications, including the preparation of agendas and content for leadership meetings and Corporate Finance all-hands sessions.
* Reporting: Provide, transparent reporting on project progress, risks, and performance outcomes to eadership.

**Minimum Qualifications:**  

* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, or a related field.
* 8+ years of experience in Strategy, Operations, FP, or Management Consulting, including at least 3 years of direct support to a senior executive (VP/SVP level).
* Demonstrated expertise in running company-wide strategic planning cycles and leading large-scale, cross-functional programs.
* Outstanding communication and presentation skills, with a validated ability to craft compelling, high-level narratives for executive audiences.
* Deep experience in process optimization and driving technology-led transformation within a Finance or Operations organization.
* Ability to operate with a high degree of independence, manage ambiguity, and thrive in a fast-paced, sophisticated environment.

**Preferred Qualifications:**  

* Proficiency with project management tools and financial systems.
* Validated experience demonstrating data and implementing AI or automation tools within a finance environment.
* Validated ability to build dashboards, cross-departmental KPIs, and present unified progress narratives to the CFO, CIO, and other C-suite executives.
* SQL or Python experience is considered a strong asset.

Why Cisco?
  
  
At Cisco, we’re revolutionizing how data and infrastructure connect and protect organizations in the AI era – and beyond. We’ve been innovating fearlessly for 40 years to create solutions that power how humans and technology work together across the physical and digital worlds. These solutions provide customers with unparalleled security, visibility, and insights across the entire digital footprint.
  
Fueled by the depth and breadth of our technology, we experiment and create meaningful solutions. Add to that our worldwide network of doers and experts, and you’ll see that the opportunities to grow and build are limitless. We work as a team, collaborating with empathy to make really big things happen on a global scale. Because our solutions are everywhere, our impact is everywhere.
  
We are Cisco, and our power starts with you.

jobs.title: Program Manager, Inventory Strategy and Ops
jobs.description:
At Compass, our mission is to help everyone find their place in the world. Founded in 2012, we’re revolutionizing the real estate industry with our end-to-end platform that empowers residential real estate agents to deliver exceptional service to seller and buyer clients.

Compass International Holdings is seeking a Lead, Inventory Product, Data & Ops to make sure our inventory products work as promised across all ten brands, and to rebuild how that work gets done with AI.

You will report to the Director, Inventory Product, Data & Ops. This team owns the technical and operational backbone of listing distribution: when a listing moves from an agent to the MLS, our agent platform, our brand websites, and portals, we make sure it happens correctly, on time, and per the seller's instructions. The Director sets roadmap priorities and MLS strategy. You own the operating engine underneath it: testing and validating what ships, helping build the AI systems that run our daily processes, keeping our reporting accurate, and keeping every workstream documented, tracked, and organized.

This is a hybrid seat. You understand the business well enough to know what matters to an agent and a seller, and the technology well enough to sit with Product and Engineering, read a spec, and see where it will break. You are AI-first by default. Not someone who only uses AI to move faster on their own work, but someone who builds, stress tests, and deploys AI systems.

Every inventory program Compass International Holdings runs depends on the product doing what we told agents and clients it would do. This role is how we know it does. It is also how a small team operates at national scale: by letting AI run the work that used to take people, and freeing leadership to focus on where the product and the MLS landscape go next.

**At Compass You Will**
-----------------------

### **Inventory Product Testing & Validation**

* Own day-to-day execution of QA testing and quality validation (including secret shopping) for inventory products across the MLS, agent platform, brand websites, and portals
* Build and maintain standard testing practices: test plans, scenario libraries, pass/fail criteria, defect severity levels, and readout templates, so every test runs the same way no matter who runs it
* Coordinate offshore testing teams: scope the work, write clear test instructions, set turnaround expectations, and review output against a quality bar
* Partner with Product and Engineering as new features approach release; read requirements, map the scenarios and edge cases that need coverage (by brand, market, MLS rule set, listing status, and seller instruction), and get tests designed before launch rather than after
* Organize test readouts: synthesize results, prioritize defects by business impact, and bring a clear recommendation to the Director, Product, and brand stakeholders
* Track defects to resolution and confirm fixes in production through regression testing
* Apply AI to testing itself, from generating scenario coverage off a requirements doc to automating repeatable checks and secret shopping

jobs.title: Chief Information Security Officer
jobs.description:
DLA Piper is, at its core, bold, exceptional, collaborative and supportive. Our people are the backbone, heart and soul of our firm. Wherever you are in your professional journey, DLA Piper is a place you can engage in meaningful work and grow your career. Let’s see what we can achieve. Together.

Summary

The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), working in collaboration with and in support of the firm’s strategic initiatives, is a senior executive responsible for protecting DLA Piper’s clients, people, data, reputation, and global business operations by leading a mature, business-aligned information security and cyber risk program. This role sets the strategic direction for the firm’s Information Security Management System, security governance, risk management, incident response, third-party security, data protection, and security awareness programs.

Operating as a trusted advisor to firm leadership, the Office of General Counsel, Information Technology, Information Governance, Risk Management, practice leadership, and global counterparts, the CISO ensures the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of client and firm information while enabling innovation, responsible AI adoption, operational resilience, and exceptional client service. The CISO works closely with, but independently from, the Information Technology function to provide objective risk oversight, policy leadership, executive reporting, and continuous improvement of the firm’s security posture.

Location

This position can sit in our Atlanta, Baltimore, Boston, Chicago, Miami, New York, Northern Virginia, Philadelphia, Raleigh, Short Hills, Washington D.C., or Wilmington office. Candidates must reside within a reasonable commuting distance of their assigned office and be available for periodic travel.

Responsibilities

Sets and executes the enterprise information security strategy for DLA Piper, aligning cyber risk management with firm strategy, client obligations, professional responsibility requirements, regulatory expectations, and operational resilience objectives.
Sets and executes the enterprise information security strategy for DLA Piper, aligning cyber risk management with firm strategy, client obligations, professional responsibility requirements, regulatory expectations, and operational resilience objectives.
Leads the firm’s Information Security Management System and security governance framework, including policy development, risk assessment, control monitoring, executive reporting, audit readiness, certification support, and continuous improvement.
Serves as the senior incident response leader for information security events, ensuring prompt triage, containment, investigation, evidence preservation, root-cause analysis, remediation, lessons learned, and appropriate coordination with the Office of General Counsel, firm leadership, insurers, regulators, law enforcement, vendors, and affected clients when required.
Partners with executive leadership, Information Technology, AI Innovation, AI Governance, Information Governance, Risk Management, Privacy, Procurement, Finance, Human Resources, practice leaders, and global counterparts to embed security-by-design into firm operations, technology investments, client service delivery, and major transformation initiatives.
Provides objective cyber risk advice to firm leadership and governance bodies, translating complex technical risk into clear business, legal, reputational, operational, and client-impact terms that enable timely and informed decision-making.
Oversees enterprise cyber risk identification, assessment, treatment, acceptance, and reporting, including vulnerabilities, threat intelligence, identity and access risk, cloud and infrastructure security, application security, data loss prevention, endpoint protection, email security, ransomware preparedness, and business continuity dependencies.
Leads security oversight of client and firm confidential information, including data classification, access controls, encryption, retention, secure disposal, cross-border data considerations, ethical walls, client outside counsel guidelines, and matter-specific security obligations.
Directs third-party and supplier security risk management in partnership with Procurement, Information Technology, Information Governance, and business owners, ensuring vendors that access firm or client data are assessed, monitored, and held to appropriate security, privacy, contractual, and operational standards.
Guides security review and risk oversight for emerging technologies, cloud services, legal technology, artificial intelligence, automation, analytics, and internally developed tools, ensuring innovation is deployed responsibly and in compliance with firm policies, client requirements, and applicable legal and ethical obligations.
Builds, develops, and leads a high-performing information security organization with the expertise, credibility, accountability, and service orientation required to support a complex, global, partner led professional services environment.
Defines and manages the Information Security team’s operating model, including functional roles, accountability structures, governance routines, service levels, intake and prioritization processes, escalation protocols, on-call expectations, and coordination with Information Technology, Risk, Information Governance, Privacy, Procurement, Human Resources, and practice leadership.
Recruits, develops, coaches, and retains a high-caliber Information Security team with the technical depth, risk judgment, executive presence, discretion, and client-service mindset required to operate effectively in a global law firm environment.
Sets clear goals and performance expectations for the Information Security team, regularly assesses performance against strategic objectives and operational metrics, addresses performance gaps, recognizes strong contributions, and ensures the team has the training, tools, resources, and authority needed to execute effectively.
Provides strategic, operational, and people leadership to the Information Security function, including direct and indirect leadership of security professionals, managers, analysts, advisors, vendors, and cross-functional contributors.
Defines the team’s vision, operating model, service standards, decision rights, escalation paths, and priorities to ensure the function delivers consistent, timely, risk-based, and business-aligned support across the firm. Builds a culture of accountability, confidentiality, trust, excellence, service orientation, continuous improvement, inclusion, and business partnership.
Responsible for onboarding, coaching, performance management, succession planning, professional development, retention, resource allocation, budget input, vendor oversight, and effective delegation across the security program.

Desired Skills  

Deep technical engineering expertise in technology infrastructure, Cloud, zero-trust architecture and cyber defense. Proven ability to leverage frameworks like NIST to build and operate a comprehensive defense in depth capability. Proven ability in change management, building trust with partners and transforming organizations. Experience in a global law firm, professional services firm, financial services institution, technology company, or similarly complex environment strongly preferred. Demonstrated success leading cybersecurity strategy, enterprise risk governance, incident response, regulatory and client-facing security matters, third-party risk, audit/certification programs, security awareness, and high performing teams. Experience advising senior executives, boards, managing partners, or equivalent governance bodies required.

Executive-level knowledge of cybersecurity strategy, governance, risk, compliance, privacy, data protection, incident response, threat intelligence, vulnerability management, identity and access management, cloud and network security, application security, endpoint protection, email security, encryption, logging and monitoring, disaster recovery, business continuity, third-party risk, DevSecOps, modernized secure development practices including AI SDLC, and secure technology adoption. Strong understanding of professional responsibility, client confidentiality, data classification, privilege-sensitive work, outside counsel guidelines, ethical walls, cross-border data considerations, and the security expectations of sophisticated global clients.

Demonstrated ability to translate technical risk into business and legal impact, influence senior stakeholders, lead through ambiguity, make sound risk-based decisions, and communicate with clarity, credibility, discretion, and urgency. Familiarity with ISO/IEC 27001, NIST, CIS Controls, data privacy laws, cyber insurance considerations, AI governance, and emerging legal sector cybersecurity risks strongly preferred. A leader who thrives on learning and is up to date with the fast-evolving technology landscape, especially the changing threats with the advancement of AI. Ability to not only understand security tools/needs, how these are changing but also go back to first principles in solving the underlying problems through innovation.

Demonstrate executive presence, credibility, sound judgment, and professional maturity in all interactions, particularly when advising firm leadership, senior partners, governance bodies, clients, regulators, vendors, and other high-impact stakeholders on sensitive, complex, or time-critical information security matters. Communicate with clarity, confidence, discretion, and appropriate urgency, translating complex technical, legal, operational, and risk issues into concise business terms that enable informed decisions by senior leaders and non-technical audiences. Influence senior leaders and stakeholders through trusted relationships, fact-based analysis, persuasive recommendations, and a firm-first approach that balances client expectations, legal and regulatory obligations, operational realities, risk appetite, and strategic business priorities.

Build alignment across a complex, matrixed, partner-led environment by listening effectively, anticipating concerns, managing competing perspectives, escalating appropriately, and helping leaders reach timely, defensible, and consistently supported decisions. Prepare and deliver executive-level briefings, written updates, risk narratives, Executive Committee materials, client-facing responses, and incident communications that are accurate, audience-appropriate, concise, and aligned with firm standards and confidentiality obligations. Lead difficult or sensitive conversations with diplomacy, composure, courage, and empathy, including situations involving cyber incidents, policy exceptions, risk acceptance, resource tradeoffs, control gaps, or competing leadership priorities.

Minimum Education   

Bachelor’s Degree in Information Security, Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, Business, Risk Management, Law, or a related field; equivalent senior leadership experience may be considered, where appropriate.

Preferred Education   

Master’s Degree in MBA, M.S. in Cybersecurity/Information Security, J.D., or other relevant advanced degree preferred.

Certificates

Relevant professional certifications are strongly preferred, such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC, CCISO, GIAC, ISO/IEC 27001 Lead Implementer or Lead Auditor, or comparable credentials. Demonstrated ongoing professional development in cybersecurity, privacy, risk governance, incident response, cloud security, AI governance, and legal/professional services risk is expected.

Minimum Years Of Experience  

15+ years’ progressive information security, cybersecurity, technology risk, privacy, compliance, or enterprise risk leadership experience, including significant executive-level responsibility for a complex, highly regulated, client-facing organization.

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
At Journal Technologies, we believe our technology can be a force for good in the world ensuring the proper and efficient functioning of some of the most foundational aspects of society - the courts and justice system.

We create and implement enterprise software that supports the administration of justice, currently in the United States, Canada, and Australia. While our eSeries product suite enables governments and their employees to deliver continued foundational court processes, our R&D focuses on leveraging emerging possibilities with technology to improve access and efficiency.

Headquartered in Los Angeles, Journal Technologies is a long-time, wholly-owned subsidiary of Daily Journal Corporation (NASDAQ: DJCO). We also have a major office in Logan, Utah, a team in Melbourne, Australia, an office in Victoria, Canada and a growing number of remote staff across North America.

Under our next generation of leadership, we're implementing a vision for the company that prioritizes building an extraordinary workplace with empowered people at the heart of our business. Great people want to collaborate with great people, and we are actively looking for smart, motivated people who care deeply about the work they do.

**Chief Technology Officer**

The Chief Technology Officer leads technology strategy, architecture, product development, and engineering across Journal Technologies. This leader sets and champions the technical vision, brings strong product and engineering thinking to every initiative, and ensures the company's platforms remain secure, reliable, and positioned for growth. The CTO works cross-functionally with every department and plays a central role in building out the new technology team described above, helping recruit talent and shape how new ideas are evaluated, developed, and scaled.

**What you'll do**

* Develop and lead a multi-year technology vision and roadmap aligned with the long-term goals of Journal Technologies and drive it across the organization.
* Bring a customer-centric, problem-first approach to product development, ensuring teams deeply understand user needs before committing to solutions.
* Identify emerging technologies and market opportunities that strengthen existing products and open new areas of value for the company.
* Advise executive leadership on technology investments, build-versus-buy decisions, and potential acquisitions or partnerships.
* Define architectural vision and principles, ensuring systems are configurable, repeatable, scalable, secure, appropriately modular, and engineered to upgrade and evolve over time.
* Apply platform thinking by promoting reusable services, APIs, and shared components that serve multiple products and business units.
* Own the modernization of the Company's technology portfolio, balancing investment in existing platforms with technical debt, modernization, consolidation, and next-generation capabilities.
* Lead the engineering organization with a culture grounded in ownership, craftsmanship, continuous improvement, and pragmatic decision-making.
* Maintain and advance modern engineering practices, balancing speed of delivery with quality, reliability, and security.
* Support our organization-wide transition to Agile methodologies and Scrum-at-Scale.
* Serve as a true partner to other departments, building alignment on priorities, timelines, and resources across the organization.
* Translate complex technical concepts into clear business terms for non-technical stakeholders, and bring business context back to technical teams.
* Build, lead, and develop a high-performing technology organization, including organizational design, leadership development, succession planning, workforce strategy, and recruitment of critical technical capabilities needed for the Company's future.
* Ensure appropriate standards for security, privacy, compliance, and data governance, including requirements common to courts, government agencies, and criminal justice systems (such as CJIS).
* Oversee technology investment, performance, and operational resilience, ensuring resources are aligned with priorities and systems remain reliable, scalable, and prepared for business continuity.
* Establish effective technology governance and risk management, partnering with Security, Cloud Operations, IT, Legal, and business leaders to manage architectural, cybersecurity, regulatory, and third-party technology risks.

**Qualifications & Skills**

* 12+ years of software engineering experience, with at least 5 years in senior technical leadership roles (CTO, VP of Engineering, Head of Engineering, or similar).
* Proven experience leading and scaling engineering organizations and enterprise software platforms.
* Deep expertise in software and systems architecture, including distributed systems, cloud-native design, APIs, and data platforms.
* Strong product sense, with experience making customer-driven product decisions.
* A track record of setting a compelling technical vision and rallying teams and executives around it.
* Proven success working cross-functionally, with excellent communication skills and the ability to engage executives, engineers, customers, and partners alike.
* Background in government technology, justice or court systems, legal technology, or other regulated public sector markets is highly desirable.
* Experience incubating new products or working in a startup, innovation lab, or venture environment is preferred.
* Hands-on experience applying AI, machine learning, and data-driven technologies to real products is preferred.
* Experience working within Agile teams or formal training in Scrum or Agile methodologies
* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree is a plus.
* Given the highly collaborative nature of this role, preference will be shown for candidates able to work on a regular/hybrid basis from our Los Angeles headquarters.

jobs.title: Director of Information Technology
jobs.description:
Founded in 1981 in partnership with whistleblowers, the Project On Government Oversight (POGO) is a nonpartisan independent watchdog that works to expose waste, corruption, abuse of power, and other instances where the government fails to serve the public. We champion reforms to achieve a more effective, ethical, and accountable federal government that safeguards constitutional principles. POGO has an over $7 million annual budget that supports a staff of over 50 employees.

POGO is looking for a talented Director of Information Technology to play a crucial role in advancing POGO’s mission by providing strategic leadership on IT and oversight of our IT systems and infrastructure. You will help POGO better leverage technology by being responsible for: developing and implementing IT strategies to support the organization's goals; ensuring the security, compliance, and integrity of our systems and data; and optimizing technology resources to enhance not only operational efficiency but also the impact of our work. This position reports directly to the Vice President (VP) of Finance and Administration.

We encourage potential applicants to apply even if they only have experience or familiarity in some of the areas described below. We fully recognize that many great candidates will not have experience in all of the areas we list, or may have relevant experiences and skills that we have not listed or considered.

Responsibilities include:

Set POGO’s multi-year technology strategy and roadmap in alignment with the strategic plan, and translate it into annual priorities, investments, and measurable outcomes.
Advise the executive leadership team on the organization’s technology posture, including the tradeoffs among operational stability, speed of adoption, cost, compliance obligations, and organizational capacity, and bring recommendations with clear options and costs.
Own the organization’s cybersecurity program: set the risk posture and security roadmap, direct the virtual CISO engagement, oversee risk assessment and penetration testing, maintain cyber insurance readiness, and report on risk to executive leadership.
Author and maintain the organization’s technology, data governance, cybersecurity, and acceptable use policies, and lead their adoption across the organization in coordination with Legal and Human Resources.
Define POGO’s compliance posture for data protection and privacy, accessibility, PCI DSS, and related obligations, and serve as the organization’s internal advisor on technology-related legal and regulatory questions in partnership with Legal.
Identify where technology can materially increase the impact of POGO’s investigative, policy, and advocacy work, and scope, source, or build solutions — including data collection, pipelines, automation, and analysis tooling — in partnership with program leadership.
Set the organizational framework for information architecture, records, and data management, and lead cross-departmental adoption of technology standards, with teams owning their own structures within it.
Lead the IT team: supervise and develop the IT team, set priorities and service standards for the function, and ensure they have the capacity, skills, and succession depth to meet organizational needs.

Qualifications include:

Minimum of 8 years of progressive IT experience, including at least 3 years in a leadership role with responsibility for technology strategy, budget and staff, preferably at a nonprofit, law firm, or other organization with comparable sensitivity around data.
Demonstrated experience setting and executing technology strategy aligned to organizational goals, and presenting options and recommendations to executive leadership.
Demonstrated experience owning a cybersecurity program, including risk assessment, policy development, incident response planning, and directing external security advisors.
Demonstrated experience with technology governance and compliance, including data protection and privacy, PCI, and accessibility obligations, and working in partnership with legal counsel.
Demonstrated experience owning a technology budget, leading vendor selection and contract negotiation, and making build, buy, and sourcing decisions.
Strong working knowledge of modern cloud-first enterprise environments, including Microsoft 365 and Entra, sufficient to direct, evaluate, and hold accountable technical work performed by others.
Demonstrated experience supervising and developing technical staff.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to translate technical matters for non-technical executives and staff and to build consensus across departments.
Commitment to creating, maintaining, and otherwise fostering an inclusive work environment.
Commitment to justice, equity, diversity and inclusion.
(+) Legal, compliance, or privacy background or credential (e.g., CIPP), or experience serving as a technology advisor to legal teams preferred but not required
(+) Experience identifying and delivering technology solutions that increase program impact in research, policy, advocacy, or investigative settings, including data pipelines, automation, and analysis tooling preferred but not required.

This position is eligible for remote work from anywhere within the United States provided you are available during POGO’s work hours of 9AM-6PM in the Eastern Time Zone. Otherwise, the position and POGO are based in Washington, DC.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Vice President, Revenue Cycle Technology Operations leads the enterprise functions responsible for translating EnableComp's technology strategy into scalable, reliable, and measurable operational performance across revenue cycle service lines. Reporting to the Executive Vice President, Operations, this role owns the Technology Operations vision, investment portfolio, governance, and value-realization framework while setting the strategic direction, operating expectations, and performance framework for work delivered through EnableComp's global vendor partners. THE JOB RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE

Sponsor pilots and phased rollouts, establish readiness and scale criteria, and make data-informed decisions to expand, revise, pause, or retire solutions.

Build a continuous-improvement culture that uses performance data, frontline feedback, client insight, and market developments to identify and deliver the next generation of operational capabilities.

Other duties as required.

REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's degree in business, healthcare administration, information systems, engineering, or a related field required; advanced degree (MBA or similar) preferred.

12+ years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare revenue cycle management, healthcare operations, technology-enabled services, or a related environment, including 5+ years leading at the senior director or vice president level.

Demonstrated success building and leading an enterprise technology-operations, digital-transformation, automation, or operational-excellence portfolio with measurable business outcomes.

Timely and regular attendance.
