jobs.title: Material Technology Director
jobs.description:
About Samsung Austin Semiconductor

Samsung is a world leader in advanced semiconductor technology, founded on the belief that the pursuit of excellence creates a better world. At Samsung Austin Semiconductor, we are Innovating Today to Power the Devices of Tomorrow.

Come innovate with us!

Position Summary

Samsung Austin Semiconductor is seeking a Director of Material Technology to lead the site’s supplier and raw material quality organization supporting high-volume semiconductor manufacturing. The Director is the site-level authority for raw material quality and supplier technical performance across a broad portfolio of direct materials, including bulk and specialty gases, bulk and specialty chemicals, slurries, pads, precursors, targets, wafers, and photo-related materials.

This leader directs a multidisciplinary organization of engineers and technicians and works closely with Manufacturing, Process Engineering, Purchasing, Logistics, Quality, the onsite analytical laboratory, Samsung Korea, and a global supplier base. The role protects manufacturing from material-related quality risk while enabling new technology introduction, supply-chain resilience, localization, and cost reduction.

Role And Responsibilities

Here’s What You’ll Be Responsible For:

Material Quality Strategy & Governance

Establish and execute the site strategy for raw material and supplier quality supporting current and future semiconductor technologies.
Own the governance framework, policies, decision rights, and escalation pathways for qualification, specifications, supplier change control, incoming quality, and material disposition.
Develop long-term technical roadmaps aligned with future technology nodes, capacity expansion, and supply-chain strategy.
Identify emerging material and supplier risks and ensure mitigation plans are in place before manufacturing impact.

Supplier Qualification, Performance & Development

Direct the end-to-end qualification strategy for new materials, new suppliers, alternate sources, and new supplier manufacturing locations.
Oversee supplier lifecycle management from qualification through performance monitoring, development, requalification, escalation, and phase-out.
Establish risk-based supplier segmentation to set surveillance, audit, and development requirements.
Establish supplier scorecards and KPIs, and lead executive quality reviews for strategic or underperforming suppliers.
Develop supplier capability roadmaps and improvement plans to reduce material variability and meet future technology requirements.
Lead quality-matching activities to ensure consistent material performance across supplier manufacturing locations and alignment with Samsung Korea.

Specifications & Supplier Change Management

Own raw material specifications, critical quality attributes, acceptance criteria, sampling requirements, and test methods, ensuring they evolve with process sensitivity and technology-node requirements.
Direct technical evaluation of supplier Certificates of Analysis and define requirements for supplier statistical control of critical parameters.
Own governance of supplier changes, including process, raw material, site, equipment, packaging, and formulation changes, and ensure PCNs are reviewed for manufacturing and reliability risk.
Establish risk-based qualification requirements for supplier changes and approve or delegate approval authority accordingly.

Non-Conforming Material & Disposition Authority

Establish and maintain the site process for containment, evaluation, and disposition of non-conforming raw materials.
Serve as senior escalation authority for high-risk decisions involving hold, release, use-as-is, deviation, return, replacement, or scrap.
Ensure disposition decisions weigh manufacturing risk, process sensitivity, inventory position, and supply continuity, with appropriate traceability and documentation.

Supplier Audit Program

Direct the global audit and surveillance program for critical raw material suppliers, with audit strategy based on material criticality, performance, and business risk.
Ensure assessments cover quality systems, manufacturing and contamination controls, change management, traceability, SPC, and business continuity against ISO 9001, IATF 16949, and Samsung requirements.
Determine supplier qualification status based on audit findings and ensure corrective actions are verified for effectiveness.

Incoming Material Quality & Excursion Prevention

Establish the strategy for incoming material verification based on material criticality, supplier capability, historical performance, and process sensitivity.
Partner with the onsite analytical laboratory on testing requirements, sampling strategies, and method development capable of detecting contamination at levels appropriate for advanced semiconductor manufacturing.
Establish statistical monitoring of supplier CoA data, incoming test results, and material trends, with defined escalation and containment thresholds, to identify drift before it impacts manufacturing.
Ensure correlation between supplier data, onsite laboratory results, and manufacturing performance, and use this data to drive supplier management decisions.

Root Cause Analysis & Corrective Action

Provide executive oversight for significant material-related excursions and supplier quality events.
Ensure rigorous root cause analysis using structured methodologies such as 8D, 5-Why, fishbone, and fault-tree analysis.
Drive containment, corrective and preventive action, and verification of effectiveness, ensuring supplier actions address systemic causes.
Maintain CAPA governance and deploy lessons learned across materials, suppliers, and manufacturing organizations.

Supply Continuity & Cost Optimization

Identify single-source, geographic, capacity, logistics, and supplier business-continuity risks, and establish contingency strategies for critical materials.
Direct qualification of alternate materials, suppliers, manufacturing locations, and bridge specifications to reduce supply risk.
Partner with Purchasing and Logistics to manage material risk during shortages and supply-chain disruptions.
Partner with Purchasing on sourcing strategies, supplier localization, and technical cost reduction, ensuring cost initiatives undergo appropriate qualification and risk evaluation.

New Technology Introduction & Fab Readiness

Lead raw material readiness for new technologies, product introductions, capacity expansions, and Fab startup activities.
Ensure new material requirements are identified early enough to support technology qualification schedules.
Ensure supplier capacity, quality systems, analytical capability, packaging, transportation, and import requirements are ready ahead of production ramp.
Support technology transfer and material matching between Samsung manufacturing operations.

Organizational Leadership & Cross-Functional Partnership

Lead a multidisciplinary organization of engineers and technicians, establishing organizational structure, staffing strategy, KPIs, and succession plans.
Recruit, develop, and retain technical talent; coach managers and technical experts and build training programs that strengthen organizational capability.
Promote a culture of ownership, technical rigor, continuous improvement, and disciplined decision-making.
Represent Material Technology in site-level discussions and provide senior leadership with clear assessments of material quality, supplier risk, and supply continuity.
Serve as the senior technical interface with strategic suppliers and represent the site with Samsung Korea on material quality and technology matters.
Resolve cross-functional issues where material quality, manufacturing priorities, supply constraints, and commercial considerations intersect.

Skills And Qualifications

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor’s degree in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related technical discipline.
15+ years of experience in semiconductor manufacturing, including significant experience in supplier quality, materials engineering, process engineering, or related technical functions.
10+ years of progressive leadership experience, including responsibility for technical teams, managers, or organizations.
Demonstrated experience with supplier qualification and development, material specifications, supplier change management, and non-conforming material disposition in a high-volume manufacturing environment.
Strong knowledge of SPC, process capability, root cause analysis, and structured problem-solving methodologies.
Experience managing senior-level supplier relationships and resolving complex quality, technical, and supply issues.
Demonstrated ability to communicate technical risk, business impact, and recommendations to executive leadership.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree or Ph.D. in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related technical discipline.
Experience with advanced-node semiconductor manufacturing, greenfield Fab startup, major expansion, or technology transfer.
Direct experience with semiconductor raw materials and the analytical methods used for trace contamination and high-purity material characterization.
Experience leading global supplier qualification and audit programs; lead auditor certification or equivalent.
Working knowledge of ISO 9001, IATF 16949, or comparable quality management systems.

Individual base pay rates will depend on factors including duties, work location, education, skills, qualifications and experience. Total compensation for this position will include a competitive benefits package and may include participation in company incentive compensation programs, which are based on factors to include organizational and individual performance.

Total Rewards

Wellness incentives and MORE

All positions at Samsung Austin Semiconductor are full-time on-site.

jobs.description:
Cincinnati Country Day School is an equal opportunity employer that actively seeks employees who reflect and support our mission-driven commitment to academic excellence and to creating and maintaining a diverse and inclusive community. CCDS pays competitively and provides an excellent benefits package. Applicants must be eligible to work in the United States.

  

**Director of Technology**
--------------------------

**Position**
  
Cincinnati Country Day School (CCDS) seeks a visionary, collaborative, and strategic technology leader to serve as its director of technology. Reporting to the head of school and serving as a member of the school's leadership team, the director of technology provides leadership, planning, management, and oversight for all aspects of the school's technology program, infrastructure, cybersecurity, instructional technology initiatives, and technology support services. The director of technology will develop and execute a comprehensive technology strategy that advances the school's mission, enhances teaching and learning, supports operational excellence, safeguards institutional data, and ensures the reliability and scalability of the school's technology ecosystem. The ideal candidate combines strong technical expertise with exceptional leadership, communication, project management, and strategic planning skills. This is a 12-month, full-time administrative position.  
  
  
  
**Responsibilities**

jobs.title: Legal Operations Program Manager, M&A Integrations
jobs.description:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.

We are looking for a high-impact Legal Operations Program Manager to join our expanding Legal Operations Team and sit at the center of our mergers & acquisitions (M&A) activity! This is a strategy-to-execution role focused on post-acquisition integration: bringing acquired companies' legal teams, legal entities, contracts, litigation and matters, outside counsel relationships, and compliance obligations into the Lyft Legal organization. To be clear, this is a business and organizational M&A integration role, not a systems or technology integration role. You will serve as the operating backbone for Legal across our most strategic transactions, owning the legal workstream of M&A integration in partnership with Lyft's Corporate Development Integration Management Office (IMO), along with the intake and governance layer that connects the Legal team to deal work. The ideal candidate is detail oriented, proactive, and able to drive outcomes across multiple concurrent acquisitions in ambiguous, high-stakes environments with a collaborative and transparent approach. Some key areas include: M&A integration program management, program leadership across concurrent deals, cross-functional and deal team engagement, outside counsel and vendor management across jurisdictions, legal entity management and governance, and building a repeatable M&A integration operating model that scales with company growth. This position reports to the Head of Legal Operations.

As the company scales, the volume and complexity of strategic transactions — acquisitions, cross-border expansion, and new market entry — continues to increase. This role establishes a centralized operating model for the legal side of M&A integration that ensures:

* Acquisitions are integrated into Lyft Legal with discipline, completeness, and a clear critical path
* Legal is embedded early in each deal, from diligence through post-close, with strong planning-to-execution across multiple teams to deliver strong business results and manage risk
* The organization scales without inheriting unmanaged legal, contractual, or compliance risk from acquired companies

**Responsibilities:**
---------------------

* **M&A Integration Program Management**
  + Own the legal workstream of M&A integration across global acquisitions, from integration planning during diligence through post-close, in partnership with Corporate Development's Integration Management Office (IMO)
  + Build legal M&A integration roadmaps with clear dependencies and critical path, covering people, entities, contracts, matters, and compliance obligations, and stand up governance, reporting, and escalation frameworks for each acquisition
  + Prepare and lead leadership readouts on the legal integration status of each acquisition in scope
  + Track the retirement of inherited legal risk and post-close obligations, and codify repeatable legal M&A integration playbooks to improve speed, quality, and predictability
* **Program Leadership & Execution**
  + Act as the control tower across concurrent acquisitions, ensuring legal integration work is resourced, sequenced, and prioritized appropriately across teams
  + Build and manage integrated plans, milestones, and KPIs, and drive execution across multiple complex, cross-functional deal workstreams simultaneously
  + Proactively identify risks, dependencies, and bottlenecks, holding teams accountable while maintaining strong cross-functional relationships
  + Maintain high-quality documentation, decision logs, and scalable processes
* **Cross-Functional Engagement & Deal Support**
  + Partner across Corporate Development, Finance, People, Tax, Security, and the business to understand each deal's integration plan and identify impacts on the Legal team's people, processes, and organization
  + Support diligence and signing-to-close workstreams, including data room logistics, tracking conditions to close, and managing transaction document repositories
  + Coordinate a hub-and-spoke model that maps acquired legal team members, contracts, and matters to the appropriate Lyft Legal functional owners, surfacing risks and tradeoffs early
  + Support the organizational integration of acquired legal teams, including role mapping, reporting lines, onboarding, and adoption of Lyft Legal policies and ways of working
* **Outside Counsel / Vendor Management**
  + Work cross-functionally with Legal, Procurement, and Accounting to manage outside counsel and vendor relationships for deal and post-acquisition matters, including engagement agreements, alternative fee arrangements, associated budgets, compliance with billing guidelines, and related internal and external communications
  + Rationalize the acquired company's outside counsel and legal vendor relationships against Lyft's panel and billing guidelines, and manage multi-jurisdictional and cross-border engagements (including U.S., UK, EU, and Nordic counsel)
  + Partner closely with our Legal Operations eBilling Specialist to transition acquired matters and spend onto Lyft's e-Billing and matter management processes
* **Entity Management & Governance**
  + Support legal entity integration, rationalization, registered agent and entity management, corporate housekeeping, and governance harmonization for newly acquired entities
  + Partner with Corporate, Tax, and Finance to maintain accurate entity records and ensure post-close compliance and reporting obligations are met
* **Operating Model, Technology & Reporting**
  + Help stand up and evolve the Legal M&A integration operating model, defining best practices for integration governance, intake, and cross-functional operating rhythms — introducing structure without slowing teams down
  + Own the intake and prioritization layer for legal M&A integration work, defining criteria (impact, risk,

jobs.title: Director of IT - Legal, Compliance & Workplace Applications
jobs.description:
About Marvell

Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.

At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead.

Your Team, Your Impact

The Enterprise Applications group is the strategic technology partner for the company's core business functions, responsible for the full application lifecycle from roadmap and selection through implementation, integration, and ongoing operations across HR, Finance, Marketing, Legal, Compliance, and Workplace Management. Led by the Senior Director of Enterprise Applications, the group works closely with business stakeholders to deliver scalable, reliable, and modern solutions that drive operational efficiency and support compliance and growth. A key priority for the group is the active integration of AI capabilities into enterprise platforms and processes embedding intelligent automation, copilots, and AI-augmented workflows to reduce manual effort, improve decision-making speed, and unlock new levels of productivity across the organization.

What You Can Expect

Strategic Planning & Roadmap

Define and own a multi-year application roadmap for Legal, Compliance, Facilities, and Physical Security domains, aligned to corporate strategy and risk priorities.
Conduct portfolio assessments, identify capability gaps, and prioritize investments based on business impact, cost, and risk.
Develop and manage a demand management process in partnership with business stakeholders.

Legal & Compliance Applications

Lead selection, implementation, and optimization of matter management, contract lifecycle management (CLM), e-billing, and regulatory compliance platforms.
Ensure applications meet audit, data retention, eDiscovery, and regulatory reporting requirements (e.g., SOX, GDPR, CCPA).
Partner with Legal Operations and the General Counsel’s office to streamline workflows and reduce manual processes.

Facilities & Workplace Technology

Oversee business applications supporting real estate portfolio management, space planning, workplace experience, lease administration, and facilities maintenance.
Drive integrations between facilities systems (IWMS/CAFM) and corporate HR, finance, procurement and other enterprise platforms.
Support capital project tracking and facility lifecycle management capabilities.

Delivery & Operations

Lead cross-functional project teams (engineers, architects, vendors, business analysts) through the full SDLC, from requirements through production support.
Establish SLAs, KPIs, and operational health metrics for supported applications; drive continuous improvement.
Manage vendor relationships, contract negotiations, and license compliance for the application portfolio.

Stakeholder Engagement

Build trusted relationships with functional leaders across Legal, Compliance, and Facilities/Workplace.
Facilitate steering committees, executive briefings, and governance reviews.
Maintain a collaborative working relationship with the CLO and CSO organizations to ensure alignment on shared compliance and operational requirements
Act as a change agent, driving adoption and capability maturity across the supported functions.

Required

What We're Looking For

12+ years of progressive IT experience, with at least 5 years in business application ownership or enterprise application leadership roles.
Demonstrated experience delivering solutions in two or more of the following domains: Legal/CLM, Compliance, Facilities/IWMS, or Physical Security.
Strong program management skills; experience leading complex, multi-workstream implementations.
Proven ability to engage and influence senior business stakeholders and translate business requirements into technology strategies.
Experience managing vendor relationships and technology contracts.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills; able to present to executive audiences.

Preferred

Experience with platforms such as Conga, TeamConnect, Salesforce Legal, Workiva, Archibus, Planon, ServiceNow (Legal/GRC modules), or similar.
Familiarity with GRC frameworks (ISO 27001, NIST, SOC 2) and regulatory environments (SOX, GDPR, CCPA).
Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, or a related field; MBA or advanced degree a plus.
Experience in high-growth technology, financial services, healthcare, or similarly regulated industries.
PMP, ITIL, or equivalent certification.

Expected Base Pay Range (USD)

165,180 - 247,500, $ per annum

The successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location and market conditions. The expected base pay range for this role may be modified based on market conditions.

This role is eligible to participate in Marvell's bonus and equity plans, including a new hire equity grant and annual equity refreshers, ensuring you are rewarded for your contributions and remain invested in the company's long-term success.

Additional Compensation And Benefit Elements

Marvell is committed to providing exceptional, comprehensive benefits that support our employees at every stage - from internship to retirement and through life’s most important moments. Our offerings are built around four key pillars: financial well-being, family support, mental and physical health, and recognition. Highlights include an employee stock purchase plan with a 2-year look back, family support programs to help balance work and home life, robust mental health resources to prioritize emotional well-being, and a recognition and service awards to celebrate contributions and milestones. We look forward to sharing more with you during the interview process.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status.

Any applicant who requires a reasonable accommodation during the selection process should contact Marvell HR Helpdesk at TAOps@marvell.com.

These tools must not be used to record, assist with, or enhance responses in any way. Our interviews are designed to evaluate your individual experience, thought process, and communication skills in real time. **The C.W. Williams Community Health Center, Inc.**

The CIO will ensure that technology, data, cybersecurity, and digital health solutions support high-quality, accessible, equitable healthcare. This is an opportunity for a healthcare technology leader who can move comfortably between **executive-level strategy and day-to-day IT problem solving**. * Continuously assess the technical portfolio to identify opportunities for system consolidation, standardization, and improved cost and risk management.
* Translate the needs of clinical and business stakeholders into technology solutions that maximize patient and operational outcomes.

* Mentor managers and staff on clinical IT standards and methodologies, fostering a culture of accountability and high-quality customer service.
* Manage vendor contracts and operating and capital budgets to optimize resource allocation and maximize return on investment.

* Other duties and/or projects as assigned.
* Adheres to HMH Organizational competencies and standards of behavior.

**Education, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Required:**

* Bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Systems, Business Administration, or other related fields; or equivalent (4 years) relevant experience may be accepted in place of a bachelor's degree.
* Minimum of 9 years of experience (13 years of experience if no degree) leading Healthcare Applications projects/strategies, including progressive experience consulting or a leadership role in healthcare, clinical informatics, or strategic/business consulting.
* Minimum of 5 years of managerial experience in an informatics role, including computer system implementation, support, and maintenance.
* Strong ability to manage success across a portfolio of initiatives with a deep understanding of network business and clinical objectives.
* Prior experience leading large teams of individuals and the ability to manage staff effectively.
* Experience working with business and clinical stakeholders to understand their needs and translate them into technology solutions.
* Demonstrated ability to articulate goals, plan and implement processes to achieve those goals, and recognize and assess the implications of confounding variables.
* Results-oriented - creates a culture of true accountability that leads to clear ownership for driving action and delivering results. Inspires a passion for excellence.
* Ability to persevere in difficult situations, overcome obstacles, and reach high levels of performance when faced with stressful work situations and time pressure.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, strong organizational skills, and attention to detail.
* Independent working ability with strong time management skills.
* Proficient computer skills that include but are not limited to Google Suite and/or Microsoft Office platforms.

**Education, Knowledge, Skills and Abilities Preferred:**

* Master's degree in computer science, Information Systems, Business Administration, or other related fields.

**Licenses and Certifications Preferred:**

* Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL) Foundations.
* Epic Certification.

ABOUT 321 THE AGENCY

321 is a full-funnel creative agency built for brands that operate in complex, regulated industries — healthcare, insurance, legal services, home services, entertainment, and travel and tourism. Technology is central to how 321 competes and grows. With a proven track record across the space domain, the Company, through organic growth and portfolio expansion, has built over 300 spacecraft, delivered over 260 kilograms of payload to the lunar surface, and provided precision navigation expertise that has guided spacecraft across our solar system.

  

**Key Responsibilities**

**Program Planning & Execution**

* Drive resolution of cross-functional issues and blockers

**Minimum Requirements**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or related technical field, four additional years of experience may be substituted for a degree
* Minimum of 15 years of experience in technical program management or software program management
* Experience managing complex software development programs
* Understanding of software development lifecycle and agile methodologies
* Experience with Jira
  

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in aerospace, embedded systems, or flight software development
* Master's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or MBA
* Microsoft Project
* PMP, CSM, or similar program management certification
* Familiarity with spacecraft systems and integration processes
* Experience working with government customers or in regulated environments
* Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills
* Demonstrated ability to drive results in cross-functional environments

* Strong organizational and time management skills
* Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
* Data-driven decision making and analytical thinking
* Proactive problem-solving mindset
* Leadership without direct authority
* Technical credibility with engineering teams

jobs.title: Regional Director of Information Technology Services
jobs.description:
**Job Description**
-------------------

***Join Hilo Benioff Medical Center and be part of a team that proudly cares for our friends, family, and neighbors across East Hawaiʻi.***

Hilo Benioff Medical Center is seeking an experienced Regional Director of ITl Services to lead and oversee technology operations across the East Hawaii Region. This is a fully on-site position based in Hilo, Hawaii, responsible for ensuring reliable, secure, and high-performing information technology (IT) services that support clinical care, patient safety, and business operations. This position reports to the Regional Chief Information Officer and supports regional facilities including Ka’u Hospital, Honoka’a Hospital, East Hawaii Health Clinics and Yukio Okutsu State Veterans Home, playing a critical role in advancing technology capabilities that directly impact patient care and operational excellence.

The IT Director will also drive strategic initiatives, including infrastructure modernization, cybersecurity, and service excellence in a complex healthcare environment.

The East Hawaii Region recently transitioned to Epic as the organization’s electronic health record (EHR) system. This position works in collaboration with the EHR Director who owns Epic application strategy, build, optimization, training, and application support. The IT Director owns the technical platform and operational services that Epic depends on in addition to the technology services required for the facilities.

jobs.title: Program Manager Center for Cellular Language Intelligence
jobs.description:
The Program Manager provides comprehensive operational support for the Center for Cellular Language Intelligence. This position manages the planning of the Center's portfolio of scientific programs and initiatives while also providing support to program operations, resource allocation, and event planning. The Program Manager collaborates with institutional leadership, faculty, researchers, and external partners to advance the Center's mission through cross-departmental leadership, program development, and operational excellence, ensuring the successful execution of strategic priorities and scientific activities. This position requires strong independent judgment and problem-solving skills; strong interpersonal, communication and organizational skills; concurrent management of projects; and ability to prioritize functions.  
  
The ideal candidate will possess experience managing complex scientific or academic programs, coordinating high-level operations, and leading multi-faceted projects. Strong communication, organizational, analytical, and problem-solving abilities are highly desirable.  
  
**Why Us?**  
At UT MD Anderson, the Program Manager contributes directly to the advancement of innovative scientific research and strategic initiatives that support the institution's mission. This role offers opportunities to collaborate with renowned researchers and leaders, manage high-impact programs and events, develop leadership capabilities, and support meaningful work that advances science, education, and operational excellence while maintaining a strong commitment to professional growth and work-life balance.  

* Employer-paid medical coverage starting day one for employees working 30+ hours/week, plus optional group dental, vision, life, AD&D, and disability insurance.
* Accruals for PTO and Extended Illness Bank, plus paid holidays, wellness, childcare, and other leave options.
* Tuition Assistance Program after six months of service and access to extensive wellness, fitness, and employee resource groups.
* Defined-benefit pension through the Teachers Retirement System, voluntary retirement plans, and employer-paid life and reduced salary protection programs.

  
**JOB SPECIFIC COMPETENCIES**  
  
**Center Program Management:**  

* Provides strategic and operational support for the Center for Cellular Language Intelligence by working with the Center leaders to develop, implement, and oversee administrative processes that support the Center's mission and long-term objectives.
* Manages the execution of strategic and operational plans, ensuring alignment with institutional priorities while promoting organizational growth and operational efficiency.
* Assist the Program director with budget planning and administration, monitors expenditures, manages procurement activities, and ensures compliance with institutional policies.
* Coordinates communications that promote the Center's research, educational programs, and strategic initiatives through institutional announcements, websites, newsletters, presentations, and marketing materials.
* Serves as the primary administrative liaison between the Director and institutional leadership, faculty, industry partners, funding agencies, and external collaborators.
* May supervise administrative staff and support personnel, comprising recruitment, training, performance management, and professional development.

  
**Program and Event Management:**  

* Plans, manages, and oversees the Center's portfolio of scientific meetings, symposiums, seminar series, workshops, retreats, advisory board meetings, and other special events.
* Coordinates all aspects of program logistics, involving speaker recruitment and scheduling, travel arrangements, venue management, audiovisual services, catering, registration, vendor coordination, and on-site event operations.
* Ensures successful execution of all Center-sponsored activities while maintaining high standards of quality, fiscal responsibility, and participant experience.

  
**Operations Support:**  

* Provides high-level support to the Center Executive Director by managing complex calendars, coordinating meetings, prioritizing competing responsibilities, and ensuring timely completion of strategic initiatives.
* Coordinates domestic and international travel, prepares detailed itineraries, and manages logistics for the Director, visiting faculty, collaborators, and advisory board members.
* Maintain confidential information and monitor critical deadlines, correspondence, reports, and other executive priorities.

  
Performs other duties as assigned.  
  
**COMPETENCIES:**  

* Analytical Thinking - Gather relevant information systematically; break down problems into simple components; make sound decisions.
* Inspire Trust - Show consistency among principles, values, and behavior; gain the confidence and trust of others.

Oral Communication - Express ideas clearly and concisely in groups and one-to-one conversations; create an environment with open channels of communication.  

* Strategic Thinking - Define strategic goals and issues clearly; apply broad knowledge and experience when addressing strategic issues; foresee obstacles and opportunities relating to change or improvement.
* Written Communication - Convey information clearly and concisely through both formal and informal documents; adapt writing style to fit the audience.

  
**Service Orientation:**  

* Provide service to our customers, patients, patient caregivers, referring physicians and each other, in a reliable, responsive, safe, friendly and courteous manner.
* Always promotes collegiality by demonstrating respect and professionalism to others.
* Models safe, ethical behavior, mitigating risk to the institution through sound business practices, and adherence to MD Anderson's Standards of Conduct, institutional policies and procedures.
* Meets time and attendance expectations and responds to requests in a timely manner, communicating expectations

jobs.title: Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery, VP - Technology Resilience and Enterprise Technology
jobs.description:
Blackstone is the world’s largest alternative asset manager. Blackstone seeks to deliver compelling returns for institutional and individual investors by strengthening the companies in which the firm invests. Blackstone’s over $1.3 trillion in assets under management include global investment strategies focused on real estate, private equity, credit, infrastructure, life sciences, growth equity, secondaries and hedge funds. Further information is available at www.blackstone.com. Follow @blackstone on LinkedIn, X (Twitter), and Instagram.

Business Description

Blackstone Technology & Innovations (BXTI) is the technology organization at the core of Blackstone’s businesses and growth initiatives. We design and deliver enterprise platforms and services that manage risk, create efficiency, and improve transparency across the firm and its global community of investors and portfolio companies.

BXTI operates with an entrepreneurial mindset—collaborative, fast‑moving, and outcome‑driven—while maintaining the rigor required to support a complex global enterprise. We value leadership, accountability, and continuous improvement, and we expect our leaders to help the firm maintain its competitive edge.

Job Description

Blackstone Technology & Innovations (BXTI) is seeking a highly experienced and strategic Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Leader to establish, drive, and continuously grow the firm’s technology resilience capabilities across infrastructure, applications, platforms, cloud services, and end-user technology.

This role is responsible for ensuring that technology services can withstand, respond to, and recover from operational disruptions, cyber incidents, infrastructure failures, third-party outages, and other business-impacting events. This role includes being accountable for the overarching frameworks, processes, recovery strategies, and governance structures, while working closely with each technology tower to ensure adherence to program.

Reporting into the firm’s Enterprise Technology function with a dotted line into the firm’s global Business Continuity Leader, this position owns technology recovery readiness across the technology estate and serves as the primary leader for technology continuity and disaster recovery governance. The successful candidate will build a culture of resilience, establish measurable recovery capabilities, drive accountability with service owners, and ensure that continuity planning evolves alongside the firm’s technology modernization efforts.

Key Responsibilities

Technology Resilience Strategy & Governance

Develop and maintain the technology resilience strategy, roadmap, standards, and operating model.
Establish governance frameworks, policies, and controls that align business continuity, disaster recovery, operational resilience, cyber recovery, and crisis management capabilities.
Define technology resilience metrics, key risk indicators, and executive reporting.
Ensure resilience requirements are embedded into architecture reviews, platform design decisions, cloud adoption initiatives, and technology transformation programs.
Drive continuous improvement based on testing outcomes, incidents, audits, and emerging threats.

Technology Recovery Planning

Ensure and track that every critical application, platform, infrastructure service, and technology team has documented, maintained, and approved recovery plans.
Establish standards for Recovery Time Objectives (RTOs), Recovery Point Objectives (RPOs), service criticality classifications, recovery dependencies, and minimum viable operating levels.
Support the maintenance and validation of a technology service inventory that maps applications, infrastructure, cloud services, vendors, and business dependencies.
Ensure all service owners understand their recovery obligations and remain accountable for plan quality and readiness.
Drive collaboration with Business Units, Corporate Functions, and individual offices to prepare for BCP events based on specific needs of impacted groups, teams, and locations.

Disaster Recovery Readiness

Lead the firm’s technology disaster recovery program across cloud infrastructure, on-premise platforms, core applications, network services, end-user technology, and collaboration platforms.
Work with the firm’s Chief Architect to validate that recovery architectures, failover capabilities, backup solutions, and resiliency patterns meet business requirements.
Partner with engineering and infrastructure teams to identify individual points of failure and remediation priorities.
Drive technology resilience requirements into platform lifecycle management and modernization efforts.
Support internal audits, risk assessments, client due diligence requests, and regulatory reviews related to resilience and recovery preparedness.
Establish reporting processes that provide visibility into preparedness, testing results, residual risks, and remediation progress.

Testing & Exercising

Develop and maintain a comprehensive testing program for all critical technology services.
Establish standards for tabletop exercises, simulation exercises, technical failover tests, cyber recovery exercises, and full-scale disaster recovery events.
Ensure each technology domain maintains documented test schedules, test plans, results, lessons learned, and remediation actions.
Facilitate executive and technology leadership participation in crisis simulations and recovery exercises.
Track remediation actions through completion and validate risk reduction outcomes.

Operational Resilience & Crisis Management

Serve as the technology point of contact during major incidents and crisis events.
Coordinate cross-functional technology recovery efforts during disruptive events.
Partner with Cyber Security, Infrastructure, Cloud, Operations, and Engineering teams during incidents and technology outages.
Support executive crisis management teams with impact assessment, recovery planning, and readiness reporting.
Provide clear executive-level communications regarding technology recovery status, risks, and dependencies.

Required Experience

About Salesforce

Salesforce is the #1 AI CRM, where humans with agents drive customer success together. Here, ambition meets action. Tech meets trust. And innovation isn’t a buzzword — it’s a way of life. Ready to level-up your career at the company leading workforce transformation in the agentic era? You’re in the right place! Agentforce is the future of AI, and you are the future of Salesforce.

Job Description

Role Overview

As the Director of AgentExchange Security & Labs, you will serve as a strategic architect and operational lead for our global platform innovation program and driving ecosystem security. This is a high-impact Individual Contributor (IC) role designed for a visionary operator who excels at driving cross-functional alignment without direct reporting authority.

You will be responsible for guiding matrixed teams to own the end-to-end lifecycle of Labs solutions and Security Review operational processes—from identifying critical market gaps to scaling adoption across the Trailblazer ecosystem. Strategic Guidance & Ecosystem Governance

Multi-Year Roadmap Advisory: Set and champion the 2–3 year strategic vision for the Labs portfolio, ensuring close alignment with core corporate initiatives and platform releases.
Executive GM Partnership: Act as a strategic advisor to Cloud GMs and Product Management teams on Labs investment strategies, retirements, and how the portfolio drives ecosystem value.
Cross-Functional Influence: Build and maintain highly durable, collaborative partnerships across matrixed organizations, including Legal, Product Security, Marketing, Solution Engineering, and Trailblazer Community teams.

Security Review Program & Operations

Escalation Management: Serve as the designated lead for high-priority partner security escalations, unblocking technical reviews and resolving critical vulnerabilities with executive stakeholders.
Commercial Fee Architecture: Own the business and operational strategy for the Security Review fee structure, balancing ecosystem growth with program cost-recovery objectives.
Ecosystem Security Guardrails: Partner deeply with Product Managers and Product Security to optimize the technical baseline, significantly reducing the cycle time for complex ISV and Labs solutions to clear the AgentExchange Security Review.

AI-Accelerated Program Architecture

AI Tooling & Automation Strategy: Architect and own the AgentExchange Security & Labs AI-tooling roadmap to automate highly repetitive operational processes and scale ecosystem programs.
Advanced Content Automation: Lead the strategy for leveraging generative AI to build "Content-in-a-Box" deployment kits (including demo scripts, technical blog posts, and enablement decks), maintaining strict brand voice while shortening go-to-market timelines.

Data-Driven Insights & Reporting

Data Synthesis at Scale: Direct the harmonization of large, disparate datasets into clear, actionable, executive-ready "sources of truth" dashboards.
Strategic Lifecycle Actions: Translate ecosystem telemetry into definitive operational recommendations, such as sunsetting underperforming solutions or doubling down on trending technical categories.

Ecosystem Engagement & Thought Leadership

Public Representation: Present as a trusted platform expert at major community events and conferences (e.g., Dreamforce, World Tours, Community Dreamin’ events), demonstrating the "Art of the Possible" using Labs solutions.
Demand Generation Strategy: Coordinate with Marketing teams to drive visibility, organic demand, and community engagement for high-impact Labs solutions via social channels and the Trailblazer network.

Required Experience & Qualifications

10+ Years of Leadership: Extensive experience in program management, technical product management, or GTM strategy within a high-growth SaaS enterprise.
Proven Influence Without Authority: Documented success leading massive, cross-functional matrixed initiatives and aligning executive stakeholders up to the SVP/EVP level without direct reports.
Security Program Experience: Strong background navigating complex software security reviews, managing high-stakes client/partner escalations, or designing program operational structures.
AI & Automation Fluency: Practical, hands-on experience embedding LLM/AI workflows into business operational workflows to compress cycle times or scale organizational output, backed by measurable lift metrics.
Salesforce Ecosystem Expertise: Deep architectural and conceptual familiarity with the Salesforce platform (Admin, Developer, and Architect personas), AgentExchange, and the Trailblazer ecosystem.
Preferred Certifications: Salesforce Certified Administrator, Platform Developer I, and Platform Developer II.

Unleash Your Potential

When you join Salesforce, you’ll be limitless in all areas of your life. Our benefits and resources support you to find balance and be your best , and our AI agents accelerate your impact so you can do your best . Together, we’ll bring the power of Agentforce to organizations of all sizes and deliver amazing experiences that customers love. Odyssey has an exciting opportunity providing Advisory and Assistance Services supporting the US Space Force and its mission to protect and defend National Security Interests in Space as a **Space Domain Awareness Battlespace Intelligence (SDA BI) Acquisition Program Manager** in support of the US Space Force, Space Systems Command’s Battle Management, Command, Control, Communications, and Battlespace Intelligence (BMC3I) Acquisition Delta.

This position provides Advisory and Assistance Services (A&AS) support to plan, acquire, deliver, and sustain battlespace intelligence capabilities that enhance SDA decision advantage, accelerate the transition of AI-enabled prototypes into operational capability, and strengthen interagency and coalition partnerships in support of acquisition activities. In this role, you will blend expertise in program management, defense acquisition strategy, cloud-based modeling and simulation, and joint space communications operations to deliver multi-mission solutions to capability delivery challenges in a dynamic mission environment.

This is a full-time position based at 2424 Garden of the Gods Road in Colorado Springs, CO, with the opportunity for occasional telework at the discretion of the Government.

  
Responsibilities:

An A&AS contractor is a knowledgeable and trusted advisor to the Government. As an **SDA BI Acquisition Program Manager**, you will work closely with the Government Program Manager and other stakeholders, providing Advisory and Assistance Services to deliver cutting-edge solutions at the intersection of Defense Acquisition and Artificial Intelligence. Your duties may include, but are not limited to:

* Lead and support program planning, execution, and delivery for USSF Battlespace Intelligence initiatives, developing and maintaining integrated program plans, schedules, and budgets to ensure alignment with strategic goals and compliance with relevant DoD directives.

jobs.title: Chief Information Security Officer, Global
jobs.description:
**About Vantage**
=================

Vantage powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

**Cybersecurity Department**
----------------------------

The Information Security function safeguards Vantage’s global digital infrastructure, customer trust, and operational resilience as the company scales across 19+ markets. The team partners closely with Technology, Risk, Legal, Compliance, Data Center Operations, and business leadership to ensure security is embedded into every stage of the customer, construction, and operations lifecycle — protecting the critical infrastructure that powers the world’s hyperscale and enterprise cloud customers.

**Position Overview**
---------------------

The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) provides strategic leadership for the organization’s information security program. This role is responsible for defining and executing the enterprise-wide security strategy, protecting critical assets, ensuring regulatory compliance, and managing cyber risk across all business operations. The CISO collaborates with executive leadership, IT, risk, compliance, and business units globally to align security initiatives with organizational objectives while fostering a culture of security awareness and operational excellence. The CISO champions innovation in security technologies and maintains a proactive posture against emerging cyber threats, ensuring the company’s resilience and reputation.

You will build a capability, not run a report. The benchmark you create will sit behind pricing, product decisions, and executive reporting across a growing global portfolio — and you will decide what it covers, how it is governed, and when it is strong enough to stand behind. Few roles offer this combination of commercial substance, methodological ownership, and visibility at one of the industry’s fastest-scaling companies.

As Vantage's CISO, you will own enterprise security as a board-level, business-critical mandate — not a back-office IT function. You will be the executive voice translating cyber risk into business risk for the CEO and Board, carrying direct accountability for regulatory disclosure and personal liability exposure under frameworks like the SEC Cybersecurity Disclosure Rule. Your remit spans the full convergence of Vantage's environment: traditional IT alongside the operational technology, building management, and physical control systems that run our data centers, plus the cloud-native and multi-tenant security architecture that underpins compliance attestations and due diligence for hyperscale customers.

You will own security posture through the lens of growth — leading due diligence and integration for greenfield markets and acquisitions across 19+ markets — while positioning security as a driver of innovation and competitive differentiation through AI-enabled threat foresight rather than purely reactive defense. Finally, you will own security as a commercial enabler, partnering with Sales and Legal so that Vantage's security posture becomes a trust differentiator that helps win and retain the world's largest hyperscale and enterprise cloud customers.

**What Success Looks Like**
---------------------------

* Develop and execute the enterprise information security strategy, ensuring alignment with business objectives and regulatory requirements.
* Lead and manage the global information security team, including security architects, analysts, engineers, and specialists, providing guidance, mentorship, and performance oversight.
* Oversee the design, implementation, and monitoring of security programs, policies, procedures, and controls to safeguard corporate assets, data, and infrastructure.
* Identify, assess, and mitigate cyber risks, vulnerabilities, and threats, maintaining enterprise-wide risk visibility and reporting to the executive team and board.
* Partner with IT, legal, compliance, risk management, and business units to ensure security considerations are embedded in all operational and strategic initiatives.
* Lead incident response planning and execution, including threat detection, containment, investigation, and post-incident analysis.
* Evaluate emerging security technologies, trends, and regulatory changes, recommending adoption or adjustments to the security strategy.
* Drive security awareness and training programs across the organization to strengthen the security culture.
* Establish metrics, reporting, and continuous improvement processes to measure the effectiveness of security programs.
* Represent the organization externally to regulators, auditors, partners, and industry groups on security matters.
* Promote a culture of continuous improvement, innovation, and adherence to company values.
* Perform additional duties as assigned by management.

**Job Requirements**
--------------------

* Advanced degree in Information Security, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or related field; relevant experience may substitute for education.
* 15+ years of progressive experience in information security, IT risk management, or related fields, with at least 5–7 years in a senior leadership role.
* Demonstrated experience developing and executing enterprise-wide security strategies, including regulatory compliance (e.g., GDPR, ISO 27001, NIST, SOC 2).
* Expertise in security technologies, threat intelligence, risk management, cloud security, network security, application security, and incident response.
* Proven ability to lead, mentor, and develop high-performing global security teams.
* Strong collaboration, communication, and executive stakeholder management skills in complex or matrixed org

jobs.title: Program Manager / Research Professional
jobs.description:
**Department**

BSD IPP - Finance

**About the Department**

The Institute for Population and Precision Health (IPPH), located in the Biological Sciences Division, integrates a wide spectrum of factors such as human health behaviors, environmental factors, social and economic factors, policies, and genetic determinants of health, into studies focused on the treatment and prevention of disease, as well as the maintenance of wellness. Leveraging and integrating the University of Chicago’s considerable institutional strength in population science with research spanning diverse fields such as genetic medicine, cancer epidemiology, microbiome, and epigenomics, the Institute will have the common goal of improving human health outcomes. Another major goal of the Institute will be to develop a new multidisciplinary training program to equip researchers with emerging tools and methods to conduct precision health research within a population health framework. Our faculty lead research projects in biostatistics, epidemiology, and health services research and participate in interdisciplinary teams with faculty in other departments to address complex problems in health and healthcare, in our communities and around the globe.

**Job Summary**

The Program Manager/Research Professional works closely with the Institute Director to manage two main research programs. The NIH-funded P30 Chicago Center for Health and Environment (CACHET) has five separate but inter-related areas of responsibility: 1) Administrative Core (AC), 2) Community Outreach and Engagement Core (COEC), 3) Integrative Health Sciences Facility Core (IHSFC), 4) Biomarkers Core (BC), and Pilot Project Program Core (PPPC). This position is a principle contributor in developing specific research project requirements and is responsible for all aspects of the project from development through delivery. Perform complex study and data collection methods.  
  
The incumbent also provides oversight for a broad range of the University of Chicago Research Bangladesh (a non-government organization in Bangladesh that is a global health and research institute) functions including financial management of grants, compliance, and working with the URB Board and the URB Administrative Team in Bangladesh to execute on strategic initiatives.  
  
This at-will position is wholly or partially funded by contractual grant funding which is renewed under provisions set by the grantor of the contract. Employment will be contingent upon the continued receipt of these grant funds and satisfactory job performance.

**Responsibilities**

* In concert with the PI, develop objectives and design of research and data collection procedures. Provide high-level administrative support through the management of processes that support the conceptualization, initiation, and execution of project goals.

**About FlightSafety International**

FlightSafety International is the world’s premier professional aviation training company and supplier of flight simulators, visual systems and displays to commercial, government and military organizations. The company provides training for pilots, technicians and other aviation professionals from 167 countries and independent territories. FlightSafety operates the world’s largest fleet of advanced full-flight simulators and award-winning maintenance training at Learning Centers and training locations in the United States, Canada, France and the United Kingdom.

**Purpose of Position**
-----------------------

The Program Manager’s primary role is to effectively manage and supervise a team of certified instructors within the assigned program(s), to ensure delivery of training meets or exceeds client and customer needs. The Program Manager is also responsible for development, modification, maintenance and delivery of program course material and assists in the certification of flight training devices, as applicable, to support training delivery.

**Tasks and Responsibilities**
------------------------------

* Manage daily training and checking activities of instructors, including regular monitoring of scheduling and schedule changes, ensuring schedule optimization, managing availability and staffing through review and approval/denial of leave and time off requests, conducting team meetings or other routine communications with instructors regarding their daily work, and resolving client and/or instructor questions and conflicts using management discretion, independence, and Company policy.
* Manage program instructors’ performance by providing timely formal and informal feedback and coaching, conducting observations of instructor training and checking activities, preparing annual and mid-year performance appraisals, and when appropriate, preparing and managing performance improvement plans.
* Hold instructors accountable to comply with FlightSafety policies and procedures by recommending disciplinary action to DOT/DOMT and conducting disciplinary meetings and/or counseling/coaching with direct reports.
* Recommend annual merit-based salary changes for instructors using discretion within budget parameters and policies provided by FlightSafety.
* Support Scheduling Specialist in organizing, planning, and assigning instructors to customer training events and as aligned with instructor training and qualifications. Monitor instructor schedules and coordinate with Scheduling Specialist as needed to ensure instructor schedule stability.
* Regularly review program staffing and anticipate changes in personnel and customer demands to recommend program staffing changes to DOT/DOMT and Center Manager.
* Review qualifications of, interview, and evaluate instructor candidates for hire; recommend hiring decisions.
* In partnership with Director of Standards (DOS)/Director of Maintenance Standards (DOMS), evaluate and approve all new and existing instructors for certification of program-required training activities; provide any additional training to ensure readiness to teach subjects/courses on instructor training schedule.
* Educate and influence instructors’ use of available technology and effective training delivery methods in classroom, briefing, and simulator instruction.
* Maintain expert-level knowledge of (i) the program aircraft and its original equipment manufacturer (OEM), (ii) applicable courseware, training documentation, technology, and equipment; (iii) technological and regulatory developments impacting training delivery, and (iv) the key customers receiving training under the program and overall demands for training in the program.
* Liaise between FlightSafety and customer contacts regarding training needs and expectations; make real-time discretionary decisions to address customer/client requests; coordinate back with DOT/DOMT, Account Managers, Relationship Managers, and/or Instructors as appropriate.
* Maintain instructor qualifications in accordance with FlightSafety Quality Management System (QMS) processes and procedures and applicable regulatory requirements; conduct training and/or checking activities as needed or assigned.
* Manage development, implementation, modification, presentation, and ongoing sustainment of courseware, training documentation, and training devices associated with the program to align with effective training delivery and regulatory requirements.
* Assists the Manager of Flight Training Devices (MFTD) in validating and resolving Flight Training Devices (FTD) discrepancies as assigned by DOT from time to time.
* Analyze status of all current projections/plans and keep the DOT/DOMT apprised of any problem areas or issues and provide updates as requested or needed by the DOT/DOMT.

**Minimum Education**
---------------------

* One of the following educational/experience qualifications must be met:
* Bachelor’s degree is preferred (or its educational equivalent if issued outside the U.S. or Canada). A degree in business or aviation management is preferred.
* Three (3) years’ related experience and/or training; or
* Equivalent combination of education and experience in the aviation or training/education field.
* Current pilot and instructor certificates and ratings necessary to provide training for all aircraft within the assigned program.
* For Maintenance PMs, A&P Mechanic License is preferred.

**Minimum Experience**
----------------------

* Minimum of six (6) months’ work experience in a teaching/training environment. Experience within teaching/training environments for adult learners is preferred.
* Minimum of two (2) years’ experience as appropriate in the program field as a pilot, aircraft maintenance technician or cabin safety function. Other aviation industry related experience will be considered.

jobs.description:
### **Job Description:**

Saab is seeking a Principal Program Manager (PM) to be responsible for the profitable execution of programs within the Surveillance division. This position will work onsite from our East Syracuse, NY office.

  
  

The successful candidate will have demonstrated experience in the design, development, fielding, and lifecycle management of large-scale, complex ground-based and/or airborne/air-traffic with an in-depth knowledge of military and/or commercial radar systems, markets, and technologies through several years of working in this domain. Experience supporting civil aviation, Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) programs, international air service organizations, and associated civil infrastructure or construction activities is highly desirable.

  
  

The role may encompass programs spanning defense, civil aviation, and commercial surveillance applications, including radar systems, FAA capabilities, international air service organizations, and associated ground infrastructure and civil works.

  
  

Responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

  
  

* Provide overall leadership and accountability for assigned program portfolios, including cost, schedule, technical performance, customer satisfaction, and profitable growth.
* Establish and govern program strategy, budgets, execution plans, and performance metrics, ensuring alignment with business objectives and customer requirements, including effective use of EVM/EVMS for internal and external reporting.
* Lead complex, multidisciplinary programs spanning the design, development, manufacturing, integration, installation, deployment, modernization, and sustainment of ground-based and airborne/air-traffic radar and Air Traffic Management systems.
* Drive business growth and capture strategy across defense, civil aviation, commercial radar, and Air Traffic Management markets by identifying new opportunities, developing competitive proposals, and leveraging customer, market, and competitive intelligence.
* Build and maintain strategic customer and industry relationships with the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), international air service organizations, military and civil aviation customers, and major industry primes to strengthen existing programs and identify new opportunities.
* Provide executive-level oversight of program execution, ensuring adherence to established processes and successful management of requirements, risk, integration, operational readiness, site acceptance, field deployment, regulatory considerations, and customer commitments.
* Lead cross-functional collaboration across engineering, operations, contracts, finance, quality, supply chain, construction/civil works, sales, product management, and other organizations to optimize resources and achieve portfolio objectives.
* Oversee infrastructure and civil works activities supporting radar and Air Traffic Management deployments, including site development, construction, facilities, utilities, installation, and subcontractor execution.
* Develop and lead high-performing program management teams, including mentoring and developing program leaders, making talent recommendations, and fostering accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
* Ensure program execution reflects the unique requirements of defense and civil aviation environments, with emphasis on performance, reliability, quality, cost, schedule, regulatory compliance, and successful customer outcomes.
* Represent the organization with senior customers and stakeholders, supporting business and program activities across multiple time zones and traveling internationally as required.
  

  

**Compensation Range:** $165,700 - $223,800

The compensation range provided is a general guideline. When extending an offer, Saab, Inc. considers factors including (but not limited to) the role and associated responsibilities, location, and market and business considerations, as well as the candidate's work experience, key skills, and education/training.

### **Skills and Experience:**

**Basic Qualifications:**

  
  

* Bachelors degree in an Engineering, Business or related discipline is required. Master's degree/MBA is preferred.
* 12+ years of experience in surveillance systems, including radar, civil aviation, and FAA capability production programs/project management.
* Experience transitioning the production of products from one location to another.
* Experience in Risk and Opportunity management.
* Experience with surveillance defense programs is required, experience with Direct commercial and Foreign Military Sales is a plus.
* Experience with various federal contracting processes to include EVMS, ECP/RFV, FAR, OTAs, SAPs, CRADAs, WPP, etc.
* Excellent oral and written communication skills.
* Excellent organization and time management skills, attention to detail while tracking multiple interdependent functions, and ability to follow-up action items and requests.
* Must be self-motivated, enthusiastic, possess a strong work ethic and constant desire to learn.
* Must hold or be able to obtain U.S. Secret security clearance, TS/SCI is a plus.
* Strong business acumen and effectiveness working well with all levels of people in the organization.
* Domestic and international travel required up to 10-15% annually.

**Citizenship Requirements:**

Must be a U.S. citizen. Applicants selected may be subject to a government security investigation and must meet eligibility requirements for access to classified information.

**Drug-Free Workplaces:**

Saab is a federal government contractor and adheres to policies and programs necessary for sustaining drug-free workplaces. As a condition of employment, candidates will be required to pass a pre-employment drug screen.

### **Benefits:**

Saab provides an excellent working environment offering professional growth opportunities, competitive wages, work-life balance, a business casual atmosphere and comprehensive benefits.

Job Description

POSITION OVERVIEW

The Director, Cybersecurity GRC manages the people, processes, and technology related to Momentive Software's Cybersecurity GRC group — overseeing governance, risk, and compliance activities including client audit support, RFP response, internal IT audit, and contract review. This role carries out GRC activities in alignment with the Firm's business objectives, regulatory requirements, and strategic goals, with a focus on recognized cybersecurity frameworks and contractual compliance.

The Director serves as the process owner for all IS GRC-related projects and activities and assists the CISO in planning, developing, and overseeing the cybersecurity program. The role integrates across Cybersecurity, Information Technology, new business development, the Office of General Counsel, and the professional responsibility function. In addition to ongoing governance and operational oversight, this position supports strategic alignment with the business, cybersecurity outreach, and expert guidance to internal and external stakeholders. As a strategic partner to the business, this role helps Momentive win and retain enterprise clients, support growth and M&A readiness, and position the GRC program as a business enabler — not just a compliance function.

Key Responsibilities

GRC Program Leadership

Maintain direct responsibility for all aspects of IS GRC, including governance, risk assessment, compliance, and audit support.
Ensure continual improvement of the cybersecurity program through effective application of technology, systems, processes, personnel development, and leadership.
Provide cybersecurity services that meet or exceed the Firm's professional, contractual, regulatory, and certification requirements.
Manage the Firm's IS GRC people, processes, and technology infrastructure, including creation and review of IS GRC standards, guidelines, and operating procedures.
Serve as the business owner for IS GRC toolsets, platforms, and processes.
Manage the IS GRC team budget.
Consult with Legal regarding acceptable contract terms and conditions related to cybersecurity.

ISMS & System Governance

Lead the System Governance Virtual Team, promoting continual ISMS improvement across the Firm.
Provide direction on risk assessment requirements and assistance evaluating risk treatment plans.
Provide input on the selection and design of IS controls.
Provide input on metrics developed to monitor and test the effectiveness of the Firm's IS controls.
Define documentation requirements to ensure compliance with ISMS requirements.
Advise the team on client contractual requirements and Firm commitments relative to GRC practices.
Assist the team in developing systems and processes that ensure ISMS compliance and continual improvement.
Maintain the Firm's Cybersecurity Management System (ISMS), including the creation and review of policies, standards, and procedures.
Enforce, monitor, and report on compliance with the Firm's ISMS.
Partner with the Director, AI Governance to co-develop and align AI policies, assess AI-related risks, and integrate AI governance practices into the ISMS framework.

Cybersecurity Operations & Engineering Integration

Work closely with Cybersecurity Operations and Engineering teams to define, develop, and facilitate efficient and effective service delivery.
Oversee integrated vendor and other risk assessment activities in coordination with technical teams.
Liaise with system and business owners to ensure new platforms comply with Firm cybersecurity requirements.
Serve within the Firm's Computer Cybersecurity Incident Response Team (CSIRT).

Compliance & Audit

Oversee cybersecurity risk assessments and provide audit mechanisms for the cybersecurity process.
Meet published SLAs for the provisioning and support of cybersecurity GRC operations and activities.
Provide evidence and expert support for client audits, RFP responses, and regulatory reviews.
Track compliance with applicable regulatory schemes and monitor changes in legislation and accreditation standards.

Cybersecurity Awareness & Culture

Manage the cybersecurity awareness program, including phishing simulation and constituent outreach initiatives.
Initiate, facilitate, and promote activities that foster cybersecurity awareness across the organization.
Maintain and contribute to the Firm's cybersecurity-related information repositories.

Leadership & People Management

Mentor and lead members of the Cybersecurity GRC group through effective performance reviews, development opportunities, and a culture of performance excellence.
Direct reports include TPRM Advisors, who manage third-party risk management activities across the organization; this role carries full people management accountability for that team.
Transform executive priorities into operational GRC initiatives with clear vision, support, and expectation-setting.
Provide status reports and relevant metrics to the CISO.
Serve in a proactive, consultative role to other business units and constituents.
Provide exemplary service to internal and external stakeholders, demonstrating empathy, respect, professionalism, and expertise.

Strategic Planning & Roadmap

Maintain situational and environmental awareness; implement appropriate tactics and strategies to protect the organization and support roadmap development.
Strike an appropriate balance between strategic leadership and operational contribution, using a hands-on approach to solving problems and meeting deliverables.
Participate in defining the Firm's DR/BCP practices as required.
Provide innovation within the cybersecurity realm.

Required

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

10-12+ years of experience in cybersecurity, with 3-5 years in a leadership or program management role.
Thorough knowledge of professional management practices including supervisory techniques, leadership principles, and employment practices.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including public speaking and the ability to convey complex cybersecurity concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
Ability to think and communicate strategically about the role of cybersecurity in a global organization.
Ability to quickly assess an organization's capability-maturity level and apply that knowledge to RFPs, audits, contract reviews, and internal operations.
Proficiency in at least one major EGRC/ITGRC platform (e.g., ServiceNow GRC, Archer, OneTrust, LogicGate).
Comprehensive understanding of major cybersecurity frameworks: NIST CSF, CIS Controls, SOC2T2, and COBIT.
Familiarity with common regulatory schemes including GDPR, PCI-DSS, GLBA, FISMA, HIPAA, and ITAR.
Advanced understanding of technical controls, how they address risk, and how they map to framework and regulatory requirements.
Broad understanding of TCP/IP, DNS, common network services, and foundational infrastructure concepts.
Knowledge of server, workstation, and Active Directory technologies as they relate to cybersecurity controls.
Familiarity with common cybersecurity monitoring technologies: SIEM, IDS, log management, and vulnerability assessment.
Ability to gather and analyze facts, define problems, draw conclusions, and recommend solutions.
Ability to maintain objectivity and composure under pressure.
Ability to set priorities independently given broad executive requirements.

Preferred
