jobs.description:
**Introduction**
----------------

The Maryland Department of General Services (DGS) supports State and local government agencies, as well as local non-profit organizations and the citizens of Maryland, by providing facilities management, real estate and surplus property services, as well as security and law enforcement for State buildings. DGS is also responsible for a full spectrum of facilities, engineering, design and construction services, almost $1 billion in annual contract administration, and overseeing the State procurement process. Here at DGS, we truly Do Great Service… Consider joining our team!

  

**This is a Management Service position which serves at the pleasure** **of the Appointing Authority (“at-will”). To apply, see the Further Instructions section below.**

  

**GRADE**
---------

STD 24

**LOCATION OF POSITION**
------------------------

Office of Energy and Sustainability

301 West Preston Street

Baltimore, MD 21201

**Main Purpose of Job**
-----------------------

The Maryland Department of General Services (DGS) is seeking a talented and experienced Director to provide executive leadership and creative vision for the Office of Energy and Sustainability (OES). The Director will develop and oversee programs and activities to cost-effectively reduce energy consumption and greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions in compliance with certain state environmental laws, regulations, and policies. Major programs and initiatives include, but are not limited to: purchasing electric power; advancing and overseeing energy performance contracting and energy-reduction initiatives for all state agencies; increasing sustainable purchasing; and installing infrastructure for state fleet electric vehicles. The Director will identify and secure funding for programs while overseeing the office’s budget. The Director will provide leadership across State government, while also working collaboratively with staff and management from all state agencies to help achieve the State’s climate and energy management goals, including collaboration with other agencies and State climate initiative groups. This position may also be assigned the management of new programs and staff as programs develop in the future.

  
  

The Office of Energy and Sustainability (OES) is responsible for the following functions:

* Purchase electricity, including renewable power, for all State agencies.

  
  

* Oversees the State’s Energy Performance Contracting program and manages the State Energy Database.

  
  

* Chairs the Maryland Green Purchasing Committee.

  
  

* Installs electric vehicle charging infrastructure for the State fleet.

  
  

* Performs energy audits and develops decarbonization plans for State facilities.

**DESIRED OR PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
---------------------------------------

*Strong preference will be given to applicants who possess the following* *preferred qualification(s)**. Include clear and specific information on your application regarding all qualifications*

  
  

* Demonstrated leadership experience managing comprehensive energy, sustainability, or climate mitigation initiatives within a large public-sector agency or complex organization. This includes experience with setting strategy, managing program budgets, leading staff, and evaluating operations to meet statutory emissions and energy-reduction goals.

jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager, AWS Hardware Engineering Services, Specialized Platforms and Servers
jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Amazon Web Services (AWS) Hardware Engineering is a fast growing and leading-edge research and development team that creates enterprise compute and storage server designs for our innovative web service and e-commerce technology platforms. Our designs are industry-leading in terms of performance, frugality and operational excellence, and are critical to the success of the AWS business and the hundreds of thousands of customers who use utility computing today.  
  
We are seeking an experienced Technical Program Manager (TPM) to define and build the next generation of our cloud servers. Our success depends on our highly respected server infrastructure; we’re handling massive scale and rapid integration of emergent technologies.  
  
The ideal TPM candidate will be an experienced program manager who is skilled in managing hardware product development teams across several geographic regions using a variety of suppliers. The successful candidate will be an innovative self-starter and leader. The candidate will be familiar with the cloud computing industry and AWS offerings and will be passionate about providing the best possible customer experience at the best cost. The candidate will have an obsession with data and precise analysis and will use these as inputs to make decisions.  
  
Key job responsibilities  

* You manage large, complex technology initiatives, delivering critical solutions, significant improvements, new mechanisms, or deprecating systems that are no longer needed.
* You successfully manage all stages (from concept to delivery).
* You work closely with your customers to understand their short and long term business goals and product needs.
* You are responsible for the delivery of platforms through driving and coordinating the efforts of an interdisciplinary team across hardware design, component development, firmware, test, and qualification, along with external suppliers and design partners to develop, deploy at scale, and provide ongoing operational support for the servers you deliver.
* You are actively involved in the sustaining operational health of the platforms you support
* You understand the architecture of the systems you work with (e.g., workflows, APIs, runtime characteristics, design limitations, and maintenance requirements). You influence team technical priorities and business strategy through data-driven contributions.
* You communicate ideas effectively, verbally and in writing, to a wide range of audiences including Directors and VPs. You foster a constructive dialogue, harmonize discordant views, and lead the resolution of contentious issues (build consensus). You partner successfully with customers, stakeholders, and engineering teams.
* Your program management practices set a great example to others. You routinely and efficiently deliver the right things. You define clear goals and objectives. You drive crisp decisions in your program area about what projects move forward and in what priority order. You proactively identify risks and bring them to the attention of your team and stakeholders with plans for mitigation before they become roadblocks.
* You are a simplifier. You judiciously add, refine, and remove procedures. By applying project management best practices, you increase the productivity and effectiveness of the teams you work with.

  
A day in the life  
What you will do: As a TPM on the Specialized Platforms and Servers Hardware Engineering team you will be responsible for leading AWS EC2 Enterprise fleet operations and hardware product development programs in a highly cross-functional environment which includes internal customers, external vendors and technology partners. You’ll provide leadership in the application of new technologies to large scale server deployments in a continuous effort to deliver a world-class customer experience at a world-class cost point. This is a fast-paced challenging position, and you’ll work with thought leaders in multiple technology areas. You’ll have high standards for yourself and everyone you work with, and you’ll be constantly looking for ways to improve your product’s performance, quality and cost. Using data and key metrics, you will also drive and measure process improvements that enhance our operational effectiveness. You will work in a dynamic, challenging, and fast-changing organization. We’re changing an industry, and we need leaders who are ready for this challenge and who want to reach beyond what is possible today.  
  
Why you will love it: You will have exposure to teams and leaders across the entire company. You will be a part of a leading edge research and development team. You will see many aspects of the Amazon business. You will have a direct impact on our bottom line and the ability to improve things for our developers. You will be part of a growing, fast paced, and fun team. You will have ownership and responsibility for defining and executing processes that deliver both savings and productivity for Amazon.  
  
About the team  
You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. You’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.  
  
Why AWS  
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

AWS Utility Computing (UC) provides product innovations — from foundational services such as Amazon’s Simple Storage Se

jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager (SW/FW) , AWS Hardware Engineering
jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Every server in an AWS data center runs firmware, and someone has to decide how a new version of it safely reaches millions of machines. That is this role: you will own how firmware ships across the AWS server fleet, and you will design the mechanisms that make it predictable and safe at that scale.  
  
We build the software that lives closest to the hardware, including BMC, BIOS, and the controllers that manage power, cooling, sensors, and health on every server and rack we deploy. Writing that firmware is only half the problem. Getting a new version onto millions of machines, in the right order, at the right time, without disrupting a single customer, is the other half. That half is yours.  
  
Your real product is the mechanisms. You will design the repeatable machinery that gets every release to the finish line without heroics: a release calendar the whole organization plans against, quality gates with clear criteria a build must clear before it goes anywhere near production, a staged rollout model that limits exposure if something goes wrong, and one shared view of where every release stands so nobody has to ask. You will define how teams hand off to each other, how a blocker gets escalated and by when, and how we know a rollout is actually healthy rather than just finished.  
  
Every server in an AWS data center runs firmware, and someone has to decide how a new version of it safely reaches millions of machines. That is this role: you will own how firmware ships across the AWS server fleet, and you will design the mechanisms that make it predictable and safe at that scale.  
  
We are looking for an experienced Senior Technical Program Manager to own firmware release and deployment across our firmware teams. You will work across firmware engineering, hardware engineering, manufacturing partners, service teams, and security to make firmware delivery predictable, repeatable, and safe at fleet scale.  
  
We build the software that lives closest to the hardware, including BMC, BIOS, and the controllers that manage power, cooling, sensors, and health on every server and rack we deploy. Writing that firmware is only half the problem. Getting a new version onto millions of machines, in the right order, at the right time, without disrupting a single customer, is the other half. That half is yours.  
  
Your real product is the mechanisms. You will design the repeatable machinery that gets every release to the finish line without heroics: a release calendar the whole organization plans against, quality gates with clear criteria a build must clear before it goes anywhere near production, a staged rollout model that limits exposure if something goes wrong, and one shared view of where every release stands so nobody has to ask. You will define how teams hand off to each other, how a blocker gets escalated and by when, and how we know a rollout is actually healthy rather than just finished.  
  
You will get to decide what good looks like here, then make it stick. That means finding the places where coordination happens by memory or by meeting and replacing them with something documented, measured, and ideally automated. It means using every release and every operational surprise as evidence, turning what you learn into a permanent change to the process or the tooling instead of a one-time fix. And it means holding a high bar with engineering teams who do not report to you, which you will earn through being right and being useful rather than through org chart authority.  
  
What makes this different from most program management jobs:  
  

* You will work where software meets physical hardware. A bad firmware rollout does not just throw an error, it can take a machine offline, so the bar for getting it right is unusually high.
* Your scope is the whole fleet. Decisions you make about release process apply to millions of servers across every AWS region.
* You are building the mechanisms, not inheriting them. There is real room to design how this works rather than administer someone else's process.
* You will get deep in the technology. This is a hands-on technical role with engineers, not a status-reporting role.

  
If you like turning messy, high-stakes coordination into something that runs predictably, and you want to see your work land at a scale very few places can offer, we would like to talk to you. AWS engineers are shaping the way people use computers and designing the future of cloud computing technology, come help us make history!  
  
Key job responsibilities  
Own firmware release and deployment end to end, from a completed code change through qualification to a fully deployed fleet.  
Publish and maintain the release schedule that the firmware teams plan against, and drive agreement on scope, sequencing, and dependencies between them.  
Define the quality gates a release must pass at each stage, including hardware qualification and validation at our manufacturing partners, and hold teams to the entry and exit criteria.  
Build and run the reporting that shows where every release stands, how much of the fleet is on the current version, and what is blocking progress, and present that to senior leadership on a regular cadence.  
Own escalation for release blockers, including issues raised by manufacturing partners, and drive them to closure against a defined response time.  
Turn what we learn from each release and each operational issue into a lasting change to the process, the gates, or the tooling.  
Partner with firmware, hardware, manufacturing, security, and service teams to resolve competing priorities and keep releases moving.  
Find the coordination that happens manually today and replace it with automation.

jobs.description:
JOB REQUISITION

Houston Technology Audit & Advisory Senior Manager

LOCATION

HOUSTON

ADDITIONAL LOCATION(S)

Job Description

You Belong Here

The Protiviti Career provides opportunity to learn, inspire, and advance within a collaborative and inclusive culture. We hire curious individuals for whom learning is a passion. We lean into our mission: We Care. We Collaborate. We Deliver.

At every level, we champion leaders who live our values of integrity, inclusion, innovation, and commitment to success
. Imagining our work as a journey, we believe integrity guides our way, inclusion moves us forward together, innovation creates new destinations, and our commitment to success empowers us to deliver on our vision to be the most trusted global consulting firm.

Where We Need You: 

Protiviti is looking for a Technology Audit & Advisory Senior Manager to join our growing team.

What You Can Expect: 

As a Senior Manager, you’ll partner with our clients to manage risk associated with their use of technology. You'll develop strategies to solve complex business problems using new ways of thinking, and devise solutions to support your clients' needs through analytics, automation or the latest tools and methods.  You’ll develop lasting relationships with client personnel and further these relationships through quality product delivery.  You’ll foster a network within the business community and serve as an ambassador of Protiviti in the market. You will also be a mentor and provide performance development to teams as you oversee the successful completion of project work plans.

At Protiviti, Technology Audit & Advisory Focuses On

Helping clients better manage risks associated with their use of technology, protecting and enhancing enterprise value.
Innovation: identifying solutions to client problems related to technology, helping them to rethink how technology processes are managed by incorporating AI and automation.
Technology enablement: Incorporating analytics, AI, automation and other new tools and methods in the execution of audit work for our clients, enabling a deeper, broader, more efficient, and more insightful analysis of our clients’ technology risks.
Staying current: We support a broad set of potential certifications and related trainings for our team, equipping our technology audit organization to stay at the forefront of emerging risks and trends.

Consultants In Technology Audit & Advisory Work With Clients To Assess, Identify Risk, Advise, And Consult On Different Technology-related Topics, Including

Cybersecurity
Cloud Assurance
Project Risk Advisory
Technology Risk Management and Assessment
IT General Controls (ITGC)
AI and Data Governance
Data Privacy
Technology Regulations
Enterprise Applications
Technology Resilience
IT Sarbanes-Oxley Compliance
Emerging Technologies
2nd Line Controls Governance
Technology Enablement

What Will Help You Be Successful: 

You enjoy identifying areas of business and technology risk, and opportunities to improve efficiency, increase performance, and help clients better utilize all technologies. 
You are motivated to learn and interested in all things related to data and technology, including the latest trends and developments. 
You are passionate about building relationships with clients and providing exceptional experiences.
You have an inherent interest in project management and team leadership.
You promote a positive team culture that fosters open communication among all engagement team members. 
You create development opportunities for others, including participating in the creation and rollout of training, and ways for your team to improve our clients and communities.
You have interest in contributing to the preparation of client proposals and strategies to win new business.
You excel at identifying opportunities to integrate product solutions and resources to improve client service capabilities.
You have interest in working with a diverse portfolio of clients across multiple industries.
You are versed in leveraging AI to enhance personal productivity as well as internal audit and SOX activities, including planning, fieldwork and reporting.

Do Your Talents Include the Following? 

Demonstrated experience with: 
Leading teams in implementing IT audit methodologies and developing necessary audit deliverables, including process flows, work programs, audit reports, and control summaries.   
Sarbanes-Oxley Act provisions and methodologies for achieving compliance, in particular the technology implications and requirements. 
Commonly used internal control frameworks, including COBIT, ISO 27001, NIST CSF, CIS, ITIL, etc. 
A passion for:
The latest trends and developments in data and technology, including high-growth topics of cybersecurity, cloud, data governance, privacy, analytics, enterprise applications (e.g., SAP, Oracle, Workday, Salesforce, Microsoft Dynamics etc.), disaster recovery, systems development methodologies etc. 
Analytics and technology enablement (automation, AI/ML etc.). 
Evaluating, summarizing, organizing, and interpreting data.
Establishing and cultivating business relationships and a professional network, including with senior executives. 
Successfully pursuing business development opportunities and identifying and implementing strategies to obtain new work or clientele.
Ability to translate and communicate technology topics and audit issues to client personnel, including executives. 
Leadership and direct supervisory experience of teams including conducting performance appraisals, mentoring and coaching, oversight and review of work, coordination across teams, and understanding how to motivate.  

Your Educational and Professional Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in relevant discipline (e.g., Accounting, Finance, Information Technology, Cybersecurity, or business-related field.)
7+ years working in technology audit, consulting, assurance services, risk and control programs, or related field, either in professional services or industry. 
Proficiency in Microsoft Office suite applications. Secondary emphasis on Vision and Access.
Proficiency in PowerBI, Tableau, Alteryx, Python, RPA Solutions, and other Analytics tools strongly preferred.
Professional Certification such as CIA, CRMA, CISA, CISM, CISSP, or similar strongly preferred.

Our Hybrid Workplace

Protiviti practices a hybrid model, which is a combination of working in person with a purpose and working remotely. This model creates meaningful experiences for our people and our clients while offering a flexible environment. The ratio of remote to in-person requirements varies by client, project, team, and other business factors. Our people work both in-person in local Protiviti offices and on client sites, which can include local or out-of-state travel based on our projects and client requests and commitments.

Protiviti is not registered to hire or employ personnel in the following states – West Virginia, Alaska.

$118,000.00 - $189,000.00

Our annual bonus plan provides eligible employees additional cash and/or discretionary stock compensation opportunities. Below is the bonus target opportunity for this job.

14%

The total cash range is estimated from the sum of the base salary range plus the bonus target opportunity. Below is the estimated total cash range for this job.

We are seeking an experienced IT Audit leader with deep technical expertise across cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, cloud infrastructure, and emerging technology risks.

The role requires someone who can operate at both the strategic and technical levels: developing audit strategies and emerging-risk perspectives while also understanding the underlying technology well enough to challenge technical teams and perform sophisticated audit procedures.

Lead complex IT audits involving cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, cloud infrastructure, technology resiliency, systems architecture, and related emerging technologies.

Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.

Job Summary

The Director of Technology Program Management (TPM) for Infrastructure Products & Services (Infrastructure) within the Global Product Organization (GPO) serves as a trusted advisor, partner, and source of leverage to the Infrastructure organization. The Director will help drive and scale cross-functional initiatives, as well as build deep partnerships across the company, analyze nuanced issues, and synthesize data to strategically execute technical program deliverables on time and within budget. jobs.title: Fractional Chief Information Officer
jobs.description:
Rare is a global leader in community-led conservation. For more than 50 years, we have partnered with local communities worldwide to strengthen their stewardship of the lands and waters they depend on.

Today, Rare works in some of the world’s most biodiverse places, where climate risks are high and community-led conservation can deliver the greatest impact. We combine community-driven solutions with behavioral science, partnerships, financing, and practical innovation to create the conditions for conservation to succeed. By helping make local leadership the foundation of conservation, we strengthen resilience for people and nature.

As Rare seeks to scale these critically needed and effective conservation solutions, the organization is committed to modernizing our use of technology scale. The Fractional CIO will lead Rare’s transition from fragmented, locally managed systems to an integrated technology and operating environment built for intelligence at scale. This work will modernize the systems that underpin Rare’s work delivering impact to hundreds of thousands of people in dozens of countries. To achieve this transition, the role will concentrate on implementing Rare’s FY27 priorities:

Building and rolling out Salesforce for grants management
Selecting and implementing a global HRIS
Providing strategic guidance for Rare’s org-wide Microsoft 365 rollout, already underway
Guiding Rare’s Automation and Applied AI strategy

We are looking for a senior technology leader to drive key systems efforts while putting in place the governance and internal capacities needed for the long term. This is a delivery role, not an advisory one. You will own outcomes, manage implementation partners, and make architecture and investment decisions.

Reporting to the Senior Vice President of Strategy and Organizational Development, you will be supported by a cross-functional team with clear, complementary roles:

Rare’s Vice President of Technology:
and Rare’s Technology team will serve as the primary technical partner and will ensure alignment with Rare’s broader technology environment.
The Vice President of Learning and Development:
will lead change management and staff adoption.
The Director of Systems and Special Projects:
will bring knowledge of Rare’s systems and drive project management.
Leaders from Finance, Talent, Development, and Programs:
will guide process decisions and champion adoption within their teams. External implementation partners will bring specialized expertise and additional delivery capacity.
External implementation partners for Salesforce and a HRIS will bring specialized expertise and additional delivery capacity.

Expected Outcomes of the Engagement

Salesforce grants management designed, built, and rolling out.
Establish a consistent, transparent process from funding opportunity through grant closeout, delivered in phases in partnership with Development, Finance, and Programs. You will select and manage the implementation partner, ensuring high-quality delivery and value for money.
A global HRIS selected, contracted, and moving into implementation.
Lead requirements gathering, vendor selection, contracting, and implementation planning in partnership with Talent and other business owners, leaving Rare with a well-governed program underway.
Microsoft 365 strategically guided, not directly led.
The rollout is already underway and will remain with the internal project team. Your role will be to provide strategic guidance on governance, integration, and alignment with Rare’s broader technology architecture.

To support the implementation of these systems and sustain them over time, you will:

Establish clear decision rights and named owners for core platforms, data, integrations, security, vendors, and technology investments.
Define a coherent technology architecture, including standards for access, privacy, security, and business continuity, as well as authoritative sources for priority organizational data.
Recommend a technology operating model that identifies the leadership, staffing, capabilities, and external support Rare will need after the fractional engagement concludes.
Develop a short, prioritized set of automation and AI opportunities, with clear recommendations about where Rare should invest, scale, adapt, or stop.

Primary Responsibilities

Deliver Priority Systems

Lead Salesforce grants management design, implementation, and phased rollout, including selecting and managing the implementation partner ,
in partnership with Development, Finance, and Programs.
Guide HRIS requirements, vendor selection, contracting, implementation planning, and initial rollout in partnership with Talent and other business owners.
Hire and oversee implementation consultants for Salesforce and HRIS, ensuring delivery quality and value for money.
Provide light strategic guidance to the internal team leading Microsoft 365 migration and adoption.
Work with business owners to simplify and standardize priority processes before configuring technology around them.

Establish Governance and Integration

Develop and maintain technology governance practices in partnership with the Vice President of Technology, ensuring governance decisions are grounded in Rare’s existing environment.
Define platform ownership, product ownership, decision rights, data stewardship, and accountability across enterprise, regional, and country levels.
Establish lightweight governance for architecture, integrations, data, security, privacy, access, vendors, and technology investments.
Define how core platforms connect and which systems serve as authoritative sources for priority organizational data.
Incorporate cybersecurity, compliance, business continuity, and risk management into system and vendor decisions.

Enable Adoption and Internal Ownership

Partner with the Vice President of Learning and Development, who will lead change management, to ensure communication, staff engagement, and role-based support are built into each implementation.
Work closely with the Vice President of Technology and Technology team to align new platforms with Rare’s existing infrastructure, security, and support model.
Recommend a sustainable technology operating model and identify internal technology skills needed for Rare following the fractional engagement.

Guide Automation and Applied AI

Identify a small number of practical opportunities for automation and AI to improve staff effectiveness, organizational decision-making, or program delivery.
Align AI investments with Rare’s technology architecture, information governance, security, and change management approach.

Future Priorities

After gaining traction on the delivery of the FY27 priorities, assess Rare’s current technology strategy and present recommendations for the next phase of strategic priorities, investments, and implementation.

Experience and Qualifications

Over 10 years of senior technology leadership experience as a CIO, CTO, technology transformation leader, or equivalent advisor.
Demonstrated success leading enterprise systems modernization from strategy and architecture through implementation, adoption, and benefits realization.
Experience with Salesforce-based business platforms and HRIS selection and implementation.
Working knowledge of Microsoft 365 and SharePoint, system integration, enterprise data governance, cybersecurity, privacy, identity and access management, vendor management, and technology risk.
Experience coordinating internal teams, business owners, consultants, and vendors across multiple initiatives.
Experience working in a globally distributed or federated organization; nonprofit, international development, or conservation experience is helpful but not required.
Practical understanding of responsible AI and automation, including how to assess potential value, risks, and organizational readiness.

Leadership Approach

The successful candidate will be:
Strategic and hands-on, able to move between executive decisions and implementation detail.
Enterprise-minded while grounded in the needs of staff, programs, regions, and country teams.
Decisive and pragmatic, with the judgment to simplify, sequence, and stop work when evidence warrants it.
Effective at delivering results through cross-functional teams rather than relying on direct authority.
Committed to responsible, secure, inclusive, and sustainable uses of technology.
Impact oriented with a passion for Rare’s mission and the people we serve.

Time Commitment

The role will be 15-20 hours per week over the course of 11 months: November 2026 through September 2027.

How to Respond

Interested candidates should submit a résumé and a brief letter of interest (no more than one page) outlining:
Relevant experience leading comparable systems modernization efforts, particularly Salesforce and HRIS implementations, with examples of engagements and results achieved.
Availability from November 2026 through September 2027, including the ability to commit approximately 15–20 hours per week.
Proposed fees on an hourly, monthly, or engagement basis.

Please also provide names and contact information for two professional references.

Candidates responding on behalf of a firm should identify the individual who would serve as Fractional CIO and describe the roles of any additional team members.

Please send application materials to Renee Baiorunos at rbaiorunos@rare.org by October 23, 2026
. Selected candidates will be invited to discuss their experience, proposed approach, and fit with Rare’s cross-functional team.

jobs.description:
Posted Monday, October 5, 2026 at 12:00 AM

**Company Overview**
  
  
Performance Contracting Group is a national employee-owned specialty contractor that offers quality services and products to the commercial, industrial, and non-residential construction markets. We are committed to recruiting, developing, and advancing employees from a diversity of backgrounds and experiences, as well as supporting a culture of safety and inclusiveness that allows you to contribute to your fullest potential. We place high value on training and professional development, encouraging you to broaden and strengthen your unique skill sets so you can fully realize your potential.

The Director, IT Engineering provides enterprise leadership for the software, data, integration, and Microsoft Dynamics 365 capabilities that enable PCG’s business operations. The role is accountable for designing, building, integrating, modernizing, and sustaining secure, scalable, and reliable solutions. This leader establishes disciplined engineering practices, clear ownership, and outcome-based roadmaps that accelerate business value while improving quality, maintainability and cost effectiveness.

**Leadership Mandate**

Build an integrated enterprise engineering capability with persistent ownership of custom software, business applications, enterprise data pipelines and products, APIs and integrations, and the Microsoft Dynamics 365 platform. Set direction, establish operating expectations, and ensure internal teams and partners are accountable for measurable business outcomes, technical quality, secure delivery, operational readiness, and sustainable lifecycle management.

**Strategic Outcomes**
======================

* Faster delivery of business capabilities through modern software engineering, reusable components, automation, and clear alignment to enterprise priorities.
* Clear ownership and outcome-based roadmaps for custom software, Microsoft Dynamics 365, enterprise data products, APIs, and integrations.
* Reliable, secure, and maintainable applications supported by consistent architecture, development, testing, release, monitoring, and support practices.
* Trusted, governed, and reusable enterprise data that enables reporting, analytics, automation, AI, and better operational decisions.
* A simplified integration environment that reduces point-to-point interfaces, improves data flow, and connects Dynamics 365 with core enterprise and field systems.
* A high-performing engineering organization with strong technical leadership, talent development, financial discipline, and accountability for business outcomes.

**Key Accountabilities**
========================

* Engineering Strategy & Operating Model: Publish and maintain a rolling 18–24-month roadmap for software, data, integration, and Dynamics 365 capabilities; review priorities, capacity, dependencies, risks, and expected business outcomes with technology and business leaders at least quarterly.
* Software Engineering: Ensure 100% of actively developed applications have an accountable owner, documented architecture, product backlog, support model, security classification, lifecycle status, and measurable service objectives. Establish automated build, test, security, and deployment controls for all material production releases.
* Microsoft Dynamics 365 Engineering: Own the platform roadmap, solution architecture, configuration, extensions, Power Platform components, security roles, integrations, data, release calendar, and partner delivery. Review customizations quarterly and require documented business justification, ownership, testing, and lifecycle plans for all approved extensions.
* Data Engineering: Assign accountable owners and service measures to all critical data products and pipelines. Monitor data quality, freshness, availability, lineage, security, and failed processing daily; maintain remediation plans for measures below target.
* Integration & API Engineering: Maintain a current inventory of production APIs, interfaces, events, owners, dependencies, service levels, and lifecycle status. Review integration health monthly and deliver an annual plan to retire redundant or unsupported point-to-point interfaces.
* Engineering Quality & Operations: Set and report monthly measures for delivery lead time, deployment frequency, failed changes, production defects, availability, incident recovery, automated test coverage, vulnerabilities, and recurring incidents. Require documented production-readiness approval before release.
* Architecture, Security & Governance Partnership: Ensure 100% of material solutions complete required architecture, security, data governance, resiliency, and operational reviews before production approval; track exceptions to an accountable owner and target resolution date.
* Talent & Culture: Maintain workforce and succession plans for critical roles, complete quarterly talent reviews, establish annual development objectives for all team members, and reduce single-person dependencies through documented cross-training and coverage plans.

**Leadership Expectations**
===========================

* Translate business priorities and operational needs into clear software, Dynamics 365, data, and integration strategies, roadmaps, investment decisions, and executable plans.
* Create clarity around solution ownership, engineering decision rights, service boundaries, data stewardship, integration responsibilities, technical standards, escalation paths, and definitions of done.
* Balance delivery speed with security, reliability, maintainability, user experience, cost, and long-term enterprise architecture.
* Engage business stakeholders early, frame operational problems before selecting solutions, and favor standard Dynamics 365 capabilities where they meet business needs before introducing customization.
* Communicate complex engineering topics in plain business language and provide transparent visibility into delivery, capacity, risk, quality

**Chief Technical Officer (CTO)**

**Job Description:**

Thompson Gray Inc is seeking a senior and technically accomplished **Chief Technical Officer (CTO)** to support our G-TEAD (Global Tactical Edge Acquisition Directorate) effort at **Ft. Belvoir, VA**.

The CTO serves as the primary technical point of contact; the central "belly button" connecting G-TEAD Headquarters, including contracts, Contracting Officer's Representatives (CORs), and deputy leadership, with the Thompson Gray support team. This role demands both deep technical acumen and exceptional information management skills: the CTO must be able to draw from multiple data streams across the G-TEAD enterprise, synthesize that information, and disseminate it clearly and accurately to the right stakeholders at the right time. The ideal candidate is as comfortable reviewing technical deliverables and contract performance as they are briefing senior leadership or coordinating across a distributed team. This is a high-visibility, high-trust role at the heart of G-TEAD's operations.

**Full-Time/Part-Time:** Full-Time Onsite

**Clearance:** Secret (TS/SCI preferred)

**Salary:** $200,000- $220,000

**Worksite Details:** Onsite

**Location:** Ft. Belvoir, VA

**Travel Requirement:** Periodic travel to G-TEAD field locations and Army installations as mission requirements dictate.

* Serve as the senior technical authority and primary point of integration between G-TEAD HQ leadership; including contracts, CORs, and deputy leadership and the Thompson Gray support team.

* Evaluate technical products, deliverables, and performance data from multiple sources across the G-TEAD enterprise and translate findings into clear, actionable information for leadership.

* Experience in a technical lead, chief engineer, or senior advisor role supporting an Army or joint acquisition organization.

jobs.title: DIREITIN - Director, IT Infrastructure
jobs.description:
**The Opportunity**
===================

**Ascension Property Services** is a fast-growing, acquisition-built platform of skilled-trades operating companies spanning electrical, mechanical, plumbing, and property services. The platform currently comprises roughly 20 operating companies and approximately 1,500 employees across multiple offices and field locations and continues to grow through acquisition. Day-to-day IT services are delivered by the Company's managed services provider (MSP).

The **Director of Information Technology** is the Company's internal IT leader, reporting to the Chief Financial Officer. The role owns the technology function for the platform: managing the MSP relationship and holding it to its service levels; integrating newly acquired and legacy operating companies onto the Company's standard IT platform; and owning the cybersecurity program that protects the enterprise from phishing, business email compromise, and payment fraud. This is a high-visibility position within the Office of the CFO, with regular exposure to executive leadership, the private-equity sponsor's deal team, and lenders.

**Position Summary**
====================

* Serve as the Company's internal owner of information technology: set IT strategy, standards, budget, and priorities across the platform.
* Manage the MSP relationship: govern service levels (SLAs), performance, and cost, and hold the provider accountable for reliable, high-quality service to the Company and all operating companies.
* Integrate new and legacy operating companies onto the Company's standard IT platform, systems, and controls.
* Own cybersecurity and risk: establish the controls and safety net that protect the business from phishing, social engineering, and payment/wire fraud.

**Key Responsibilities**
========================

* **Managed Services Provider (MSP) Management and Service Delivery**

* Own the relationship with the Company's managed services provider (MSP) as the internal executive accountable for IT service delivery across all operating companies.
* Define, govern, and enforce service levels (SLAs), response and resolution targets, escalation paths, and performance reporting; hold the MSP accountable to the contracted standards.
* Review and approve the MSP scope, service catalog, and pricing; manage the contract, renewals, and change orders; ensure the Company receives the service it is paying for.
* Run regular service reviews with the MSP; monitor ticket volumes, uptime, response times, and end-user satisfaction; and report performance to leadership.
* Serve as the escalation point for major incidents and service failures; drive root-cause resolution and corrective-action plans.
* Ensure MSP delivery is standardized and consistent across all sites and newly acquired operating companies.

* **Operating-Company Onboarding and Platform Integration (M&A)**

* Own IT integration for newly acquired operating companies: current-state assessment, cutover planning, and migration onto the Company's standard platform (identity, email, network, endpoints, and business systems), directing the MSP as the delivery resource.
* Develop a repeatable IT integration playbook with Day-1 / Day-30 / Day-90 checklists to accelerate onboarding and reduce integration risk.
* Consolidate and standardize disparate legacy domains, email tenants, applications, and toolsets onto common platforms; retire redundant infrastructure and licenses.
* Standardize identity and access management (single sign-on, multi-factor authentication, role-based access) across every operating company.
* Partner with corporate development, finance, and operating-company leadership on IT diligence input, integration timelines, and transition-services-agreement (TSA) exit.

* **Cybersecurity, Risk, and Fraud Prevention**

* Own the enterprise cybersecurity program and ensure appropriate, consistent controls across all operating companies, whether delivered internally or through the MSP.
* Direct email security and anti-phishing controls; run continuous phishing simulations and mandatory security-awareness training for all employees.
* **Prevent payment fraud:** implement controls against business email compromise (BEC), wire / ACH fraud, and vendor or banking-detail change fraud, working with finance and accounts payable on verification, call-back, and dual-control procedures.
* Ensure endpoint detection and response (EDR), multi-factor authentication, patch management, least-privilege access, and secure backup and disaster recovery are in place, and validate that the MSP is delivering them.
* Establish incident-response and business-continuity plans; run tabletop exercises; define breach escalation and notification protocols.
* Align the program to a recognized framework (for example, NIST CSF or CIS Controls); manage cyber-insurance requirements, vendor risk (including the MSP's own security posture), and periodic security assessments.
* Provide clear, periodic risk and posture reporting to the CFO, executive leadership, the sponsor deal team, and the Board.

* **Infrastructure, Networks, and End-User Computing**

* Oversee, through the MSP, the network, connectivity, cloud, and telephony across headquarters, branch offices, and distributed field / job-site locations.
* Ensure reliable management of the endpoint and mobile-device fleet and field technology, and dependable connectivity for a mobile, field-based workforce.
* Ensure backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity for business-critical systems.

* **Applications, Data, and Business Systems**

* Support and rationalize core business applications (accounting, project management, payroll / HRIS, service dispatch, and estimating).
* Partner with finance and operations on system consolidation, reporting, and data integrity across operating companies.
* Support the data-governance and reporting needs of the Office of the CFO.

**Measures of Success (First 12 Months)**
========================

jobs.title: Vice President, Technology and Innovation
jobs.description:
**About Bodwé Group Companies**

Bodwé is the Professional Services Group of Mno-Bmadsen, the investment enterprise and a wholly owned instrumentality of the Pokagon Band of Potawatomi. We are architects, planners, consultants, designers, engineers, scientists, and federal contractors, committed to growing the economy and legacy of the Pokagon Band and supporting its more than 6,000 citizens. We provide value by integrating expertise across the natural and built environment lifecycle—from pre-development and planning to design, procurement, construction, and operations. By integrating expertise across architecture, engineering, construction, and facility management, we deliver holistic, end-to-end solutions that drive efficiency and deliver distinctive outcomes.

**Position Summary**

The Vice President of Technology & Innovation leads how Bodwé uses technology to improve the way we pursue, plan, manage, and deliver work. This leader identifies, evaluates, implements, and scales technologies that improve quality, efficiency, collaboration, decision-making, and client outcomes across the organization.

This is not primarily an IT leadership role. The position is focused on how technology is used throughout the business and how it can improve the performance of Delivery, Growth, Enterprise, and the people closest to our clients and projects. The role will build an integrated technology and innovation capability that connects AEC production technology, BIM and CAD, artificial intelligence, automation, data, digital workflows, training, and organizational adoption. Cybersecurity, federal compliance, and IT infrastructure are critical requirements and guardrails within this work.

The position reports to the Executive Vice President, Enterprise, and carries an enterprise-wide mandate. It works in close partnership with Delivery leadership, technical leaders, and project teams, so that technology decisions stay connected to how the work is actually done. BIM Managers, CAD Managers, and the IT Operations Lead report to this role.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

The following inexhaustive list of duties represents a sample of work routinely performed by this role:

**Technology Strategy and Innovation**  

* Develop and lead Bodwé’s technology and innovation strategy in direct support of the company’s business, growth, and delivery objectives.
* Establish and maintain a multi-year technology roadmap aligned with Bodwé’s strategic plan and evolving operating model.
* Identify technologies and workflows that can materially improve quality, productivity, client service, and organizational capacity.
* Track emerging AEC, AI, automation, and digital-delivery technologies and determine where Bodwé should invest, pilot, partner, or wait.
* Develop business cases for technology investments, including expected value, cost, implementation requirements, risks, and measurable outcomes.
* Build a structured process for moving ideas from evaluation to pilot, implementation, adoption, and continuous improvement.

**Digital Delivery and AEC Technology**  

* Lead Bodwé’s BIM, CAD, and related digital-delivery capabilities, with BIM Managers and CAD Managers as direct reports.
* Align BIM and CAD standards, tools, workflows, and training across disciplines, markets, and offices.
* Reduce legacy organizational and technical silos by building shared technology capabilities that support multiple disciplines and project types.
* Partner directly with technical leaders and project teams to identify production challenges and develop practical technology solutions.
* Expand the digital-delivery function over time as needs emerge in areas such as GIS, computational design, data analytics, and digital project delivery.

**AI, Automation, and Process Improvement**  

* Lead the responsible adoption of AI and automation across Bodwé, evaluating both commercially available tools and internally developed solutions.
* Identify repeatable work that can be improved through automation, AI, integrated workflows, or better use of existing technology.
* Partner with Delivery, PMO, Growth, Enterprise, and other functions to build technology-enabled workflows that reduce administrative effort and increase professional capacity.
* Establish and maintain governance for AI use, particularly where client, proprietary, Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), or other regulated data is involved.
* Measure whether technology implementations actually improve work rather than simply increase the number of tools in use.

**Adoption, Training, and Organizational Capability**  

* Own the organizational change required to convert technology investment into measurable business value.
* Develop implementation and adoption strategies for major technology initiatives.
* Establish training programs that build real proficiency, not just software awareness.
* Create communities of practice and SME networks that let practitioners participate directly in technology improvement.
* Establish feedback mechanisms so technology evolves based on actual project and operational experience.

**Technology Governance, Investment, and Vendors**  

* Lead internal IT operations, with the IT Operations Lead as a direct report, setting priorities for end-user support, infrastructure, and service delivery.
* Own the enterprise technology intake and approval process, including review criteria and investment prioritization.
* Manage the software and platform portfolio: maintain the inventory, consolidate overlapping tools, and own the renewal calendar.
* Develop and manage the technology budget; forecast needs, track spend, and make procurement recommendations that balance capability with cost.
* Evaluate vendors, negotiate contracts and statements of work, and hold technology partners, including the managed services provider, to defined service levels.

##### **About Peraton**

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Job Description

The Senior IT Director II, Operations Delivery & Reliability is a senior leadership role accountable for the platforms on which the enterprise builds, hosts, and runs software — and for the controls, lifecycle, and quality disciplines that keep the technology estate reliable, compliant, and current. The role owns Tower 4 (Application & Developer Platforms) and Tower 5 (Service Reliability & Technology Stewardship) of the IT Infrastructure Services operating model. This Level II Senior Director leads other director- and senior-manager-level leaders across application hosting and platform engineering, integration, DevOps and automation, observability, and the enterprise service-management, configuration, asset, lifecycle, and technology-controls functions.

This role pairs a build-and-run platform mandate with an independent stewardship mandate: enabling development teams to deliver software quickly and safely, while governing the change, incident, configuration, compliance, and lifecycle disciplines that protect service quality across every tower. The successful candidate is equally comfortable commanding a Sev-1 major-incident bridge, setting the roadmap for the enterprise ITSM and observability platforms, and briefing executive leadership on reliability, technical-debt, and license-compliance posture.

Key Responsibilities

Tower 4 — Application & Developer Platforms (build, host, and run software)

Own the application hosting and platform estate — web, database, and big-data hosting, PaaS, and middleware — ensuring the platforms that host enterprise software are secure, performant, and scalable.
Own support for SaaS and third-party applications, providing consistent operational ownership, vendor coordination, and service levels across the third-party application portfolio.
Own enterprise integration and batch services — APIs, messaging, ETL/ELT, and scheduled batch processing — as the connective tissue between applications and data.
Own the DevOps and CI/CD toolchain and the platform-engineering and automation function, giving delivery teams self-service pipelines, infrastructure-as-code, and release automation to build, test, and ship software safely and quickly.
Own the enterprise GenAI platform — the shared, governed foundation for AI-enabled capabilities (model access, orchestration, and guardrails) — in partnership with the Office of the CTO on AI governance (AI TRiSM).
Own the observability platform — enterprise monitoring, logging, tracing, and telemetry — providing the signal that underpins reliability, capacity, and performance decisions across all towers.

Tower 5 — Service Reliability & Technology Stewardship (controls, lifecycle, and quality)

Own the enterprise ITSM platform (e.g., ServiceNow) as the system of record for IT service management, including its health, roadmap, and adoption across all towers and affiliate entities.
Own the core service-management processes — incident, problem, and change management — and lead the Major Incident Management function, including Sev-1/Sev-2 command, executive communications, and post-incident review.

Own IT asset and software license management — hardware and software inventory, entitlement and true-up positioning, and license compliance — in partnership with FinOps and vendor management on cost and renewal exposure.

Coordinate the technology-controls response for compliance, audit, and vulnerability management — evidence, control attestation, and remediation — partnering with Information Security and Internal Audit / Risk. (This role coordinates and remediates technology controls; it does not replace second-line security or audit functions.)
Own workforce IAM operations — joiner/mover/leaver provisioning, access-request fulfillment, and periodic access certification — partnering with the infrastructure towers that own the underlying identity infrastructure (Active Directory, DNS, federation) and with Information Security on IAM policy.

Cross-Tower Leadership, Sourcing & Governance

Own and mature the tower-level KPI/scorecard — platform availability and SLO attainment, MTTR, change success rate, major-incident frequency, CMDB accuracy, license-compliance position, and vulnerability-remediation SLA — and use the data to drive investment, staffing, and process decisions.

Represent Operations Delivery & Reliability in the Architecture Review Board, Change Advisory Board, and Risk & Resilience Committee, and in executive and leadership forums, preparing clear, data-backed materials and recommendations.

7+ years of progressive IT leadership experience, with direct experience in application platforms / platform engineering and/or IT service management and service reliability within a complex, matrixed organization.
Prior experience managing and leading other director-level or senior-manager-level technical leaders.
Hands-on depth in several of: application hosting (web/database/middleware), PaaS, enterprise integration / APIs and batch, DevOps / CI-CD and automation, observability/monitoring, and cloud-native application platforms.
Strong ITSM/ITIL foundation — incident, problem, change, configuration, and service-level management — with ServiceNow platform ownership experience strongly preferred; ITIL 4 certification a plus.
Demonstrated experience leading Major Incident Management (Sev-1 command) and running structured problem- and post-incident-review processes.
Experience with IT asset and software license management, technology lifecycle / currency management, and coordinating compliance, audit, and vulnerability remediation with security and audit partners.
Familiarity with IAM operations (joiner/mover/leaver provisioning, access certification) and its interplay with identity infrastructure and information security.

Demonstrated experience managing partner-delivered / outsourced application support and run operations, including SLA and performance governance; managed-services transition experience a strong plus.
Proven experience translating strategy into an execution roadmap, with strong business and financial acumen; TBM/FinOps familiarity a plus.
Excellent executive presence, written and verbal communication, and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to influence senior leaders.
Experience with Lean / continuous-improvement methodologies (e.g., Lean Six Sigma) is a plus.

jobs.description:
TS/SCI

Overview

This position supports the IRMPO as a planning authority and expert advisor for formalizing and maturing the Department Research Security Program in compliance with National Security Presidential Memorandum-33 (NSPM-33, United States Government-Supported Research and Development National Security Policy), the Creating Helpful Incentives to Produce Semiconductors (CHIPS) and Science Act, and other research security policies, regulations, and statutes.

Background

The Insider Risk Management Program Office (IRMPO), a component of the Deputy Assistant Secretary for Security, Insider Risk and Continuity (OSIRC) serves to mitigate the risk to personnel, facilities, property, information, and assets through increased initiatives in various security fields via issuance of U.S. Department of Commerce-wide security policies and the application of a multi-disciplined security programs extending from the Headquarters to the operating units. IRMPO plans and implements policies by developing procedures and delivering a wide range of services for the Office of the Secretary and other nationwide Departmental bureaus.

Responsibilities

Although other general duties within the scope of the position may be assigned, primary responsibilities include:

Review and assess Research Security Program Plans and procedures.
Develop and manage the content for a Research Security Awareness Training program for Department of Commerce employees and associates.
Work with staff to develop a more comprehensive Research Security compliance program.
Assist in preparation of requested materials for the Department’s Research Security and Insider Risk mission.
Assist in development of policies and guidance related to the Department’s Research Security and Insider Risk mission.
Assist in staffing and tracking Interagency, Task Force(s), and National Security Council taskings.
Attend interagency and internal Research Security and Insider Risk working groups as may be required.
Evaluate the efficiency and effectiveness of Research Security Programs, make recommendations for improvement, and implement approved initiatives.

Qualifications

Approximately eight years of relevant professional experience, including approximately four years of Research Security experience.

Federal Research Security experience at the Department/Agency headquarters level is preferred.
Experience in a scientific or education research environment.
Four years of supervisory experience preferred.
Demonstrated ability to communicate clearly, concisely, and effectively with a variety of audiences, both verbally and in writing.
Exceptional writing skills and proficiency with Microsoft 365 applications; this is a writing-intensive position.

Security Clearance: Top Secret (TS) security clearance with SCI crossover eligibility (not simply SCI eligible). This requires an in-scope background investigation and either currently SCI-indoc’d or read out of SCI within the past 23 months.

Bachelor of Science (BS) degree in a scientific, technical, or engineering discipline
required. Candidates with a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree may qualify with four additional years of relevant professional experience, for a total of at least 12 years of relevant experience. Master’s degree preferred.

jobs.title: Senior Manager - IT Audit
jobs.description:
Job Description

Our Internal Audit Group is a worldwide function with 400+ team members and offices across nine countries within American Express. Our mission is to protect and enhance organizational value by providing independent, objective, risk-based assurance, advisory services and to influence the way the company manages risk.

We are committed to growing our audit staff significantly as we continue to expand and enhance the Internal Audit Group. Our assurance and risk professionals have diverse backgrounds including internal controls, consumer compliance, technology, operational risk, financial accounting, data analytics, and banking operations. Our audit teams align to key risk areas and business units to ensure IAG can provide comprehensive and risk-based audit coverage. In addition, IAG has a Professional Practices group responsible for managing audit operations, quality, and standards; regulatory relations; reporting; training and professional development; and key internal capabilities and technologies.

About The Role

Our Internal Audit group is seeking an eager Senior Manager - IT Audit in New York City, Phoenix, AZ, Charlotte, NC or Sandy, UT. This role will audit technology and application controls integrated into first-line and second-line business processes within an integrated audit with other audit disciplines. The ideal candidate will have strong problem- solving skills, excellent attention to detail, and the ability to communicate audit results effectively.

Responsibilities

Act as an Auditor in Charge (AIC) on more complex audits and/or lead multiple simultaneous low-risk audits, executing and managing the audit engagement end-to-end, planning audit projects, defining objectives and scope, and coordinating with control groups and external auditors to ensure effective execution; conduct L1 reviews
Analyze/review audit results and documentation to evaluate effectiveness and efficiency, synthesizing audit findings
Lead audit client meetings and walkthroughs
Develop test steps, audit findings, and the audit report in accordance with IAG policies and procedures
Guide team on how to validate and execute corrective actions / Management Action Plans (MAPs) are impactful, sustainable, and improve the control environment of the business unit
Support business monitoring activities with audit leadership, tracking key metrics to identify control issues and trends; stay up to date with evolving industry trends, external news and regulatory changes, and analyze the impact to the business exams
Delegate tasks to team members; guide Senior/Staff in assessing risks, evaluating control design, and executing audit tests; review and provide feedback on work papers
Serve as a People Leader, providing mentorship, coaching, and career development support for direct reports
Effectively coach, teach, mentor, and develop less experienced colleagues and co-sourced resources in geographically diverse locations across all aspects of their role, the audit and analytic lifecycle, audit methodology and best practices
Conduct post-audit feedback discussions with audit team members to provide actionable feedback, support development, and recognize accomplishments
Guide team to proactively and routinely communicate task status, roadblocks, challenges, suggesting potential solutions to the team
Begin to develop subject matter expertise in a specific line of business
Serve as the first level of escalation, effectively navigating problems and difficult conversations
Attend report / issue conversations with management, work with Director / Team Leader to communicate and action on next steps
Report on assigned tasks in client reporting meetings; assist with preparing materials for Regulatory exams
Follow-up with management to ensure management action plans are closed effectively and timely

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

6+ years of audit experience
Prior experience working at a Big Four / G-SIB
Demonstrates strong written and verbal communication skills to deliver deliverables with quality, and actionable value-add feedback to management on issues, opportunity areas, and deficiency solutions
Effectively leads a team in a fast-paced environment to drive business results, utilizing related project management skills, employing creative thinking, and the ability to work on competing priorities
Applies critical thinking to break-down complex problems into components, and solve using data analysis, process, risk control knowledge, and experience to drive risk-based conclusions and decisions
Applies control theory and professional auditing practices throughout the audit lifecycle
Understands regulations, regulatory risks, accounting, and financial industry best practices relevant to the business, including emerging technology and data considerations, and incorporates into the audit approach to enhance outcomes
Experience with technology control testing including automated processing, interface inputs, reports, application security, business continuity and third parties

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with data analytic tools, data visualization, key risk indicators (KRIs), key performance indicators (KPIs), information systems / technology, and scorecards / dashboards, etc.
Interest in working with data, interpreting results, analytic best practices and experience with data analytics tools and data visualization
Professional certification: CISA, CPA, CIA, CISM, CISSP or other technology-focused certification.

Employment eligibility to work with American Express in the United States is required as the company will not pursue visa sponsorship for these positions.

At American Express, our culture is built on a 175-year history of innovation, shared values and Leadership Behaviors, and an unwavering commitment to back our customers, communities, and colleagues. From delivering differentiated products to providing world-class customer service, we operate with a strong risk mindset, ensuring we continue to uphold our brand promise of trust, security, and service.

The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) is recruiting an executive leader for the role of Deputy Chief Information Officer (DCIO). The DCIO shapes the future of the Agency's digital infrastructure and information technology that enable America's return to the moon, sustaining presence in orbit around the earth, and advancement of science and discovery.

U.S. Citizens, Nationals or those who owe allegiance to the U.S.

Vulnerability Management

Security Architecture

Data, Metrics, & Change Management

Demonstrate return on investment and uncover opportunities for further automation or process improvement.

At Prologis, we don’t just lead the industry—we define it with a 1.3 billion square foot portfolio and an annual throughput of approximately $3.2 trillion. We create the intelligent infrastructure that powers global commerce, seamlessly connecting the digital and physical worlds. From agile supply chains to energy solutions, our ecosystems help your business move faster, operate smarter and grow sustainably. With unmatched scale, innovation and expertise, Prologis is a category of one—not just shaping the future of logistics but building what comes next.

**Job Title:**

Director, IT Governance, Risk and Compliance

**Company:**

Prologis

**A day in the life**

The Director, IT Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) leads Prologis’ global IT GRC program and team, reporting to the CISO. This role establishes governance, risk, and compliance priorities across the countries where Prologis operates and partners with global business and technology teams to strengthen technology risk and control oversight. The Director works closely with Security, Infrastructure, Internal Audit, Legal, HR, Risk, Finance, and business leadership to address regulatory, audit, third-party, and information risk requirements. The role also modernizes and scales GRC processes through AI, automation, workflow improvements, and system integrations to improve efficiency, reporting, and control effectiveness.

**Key responsibilities include:**

* Lead the global IT GRC program and establish strategy and priorities across governance, technology risk, compliance, and assurance.
* Lead IT risk and controls oversight within the Three Lines Model, including risk assessments, control requirements, risk acceptance and exceptions, control monitoring, remediation oversight, and leadership reporting aligned with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0 and applicable regulatory and audit requirements.
* Oversee global technology compliance and assurance activities, including SOX, IT general controls (ITGC), GDPR, DORA, HIPAA, SWIFT, India’s Information Technology Act, and disaster recovery governance and testing oversight
* Govern third-party and cyber supply chain risk, data protection and information risk, investigations, eDiscovery, and technology and cybersecurity support for investor Operational Due Diligence (ODD) assessments and requests.
* Monitor emerging technology risks and evolving regulatory requirements, assess their impact on Prologis, translate applicable changes into GRC and control requirements, and advise leadership on implications.
* Modernize and scale GRC processes by applying AI, workflow automation, and system integrations to improve efficiency, reporting, control monitoring, and control effectiveness.
* Lead and develop the GRC team, manage GRC technology and vendors, and oversee security awareness and IT policy governance, including training campaign planning, communications coordination, and IT policy and procedure governance.

**Building blocks for success**

**Required:**

* 10+ years of relevant experience in IT governance, risk, compliance, IT audit, or related disciplines.
* 3+ years of people-management experience.
* Demonstrated experience leading enterprise GRC programs.
* Experience with the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0 and the Three Lines Model.
* Experience with SOX, IT general controls, and technology-related regulatory requirements in a global environment.
* Experience applying AI, workflow automation, and system integrations to streamline GRC processes, improve reporting, strengthen control monitoring, or increase operational efficiency.
* Ability to influence executives and collaborate effectively across technology, Internal Audit, Legal, HR, Risk, Finance, and other global business functions.
* Ability to exercise sound judgment and discretion when handling sensitive matters.

**Preferred:**

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant experience.
* Relevant GRC, audit, risk, or cybersecurity certification.
* Ability to learn quickly and adapt to evolving regulatory and technology requirements in a global environment.
* Demonstrates willingness and capability to leverage emerging technology, automation, and AI tools to improve efficiency, quality, and speed. Exercises sound judgment, creative thinking, and accountability for outcomes.

**Hiring Salary Range of:**

$168,000 - $232,000. Salary and whole compensation package (bonus target & LTI (Long Term Incentives) to be determined by the candidate’s location, education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.
