jobs.title: Director of IT Architecture
jobs.description:
As the technical Director of IT Architecture, you will be responsible for leading the overall IT architecture strategy for our dynamic, growing healthcare organization. This individual will be tasked with designing systems that align with business goals, regulatory requirements, and emerging industry technologies. This role manages a talented team of IT Network, Cloud, and Systems Architects, overseeing the design, implementation, and optimization of all enterprise technology solutions. The Director works closely with IT leadership and business stakeholders to drive innovation, improve system interoperability, optimize cost and enhance security across the healthcare organization.

**RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Strategic Leadership & Technology Roadmap:**

* Define and execute a comprehensive IT architecture strategy aligned with business, clinical, and operational goals.
* Lead and manage a team specializing in network, cloud, and systems architecture, ensuring seamless collaboration and efficiency.
* Establish and enforce IT governance, standards, and best practices to ensure compliance with industry regulations (HIPAA, HITECH, HITRUST, etc.).
* Evaluate and integrate emerging technologies (microservices, AI, ML) to improve healthcare delivery and operational efficiency.
* Provide strategic direction for IT infrastructure, ensuring high availability, scalability, and performance optimization.
* Strong financial acumen, ensuring positive ROI for Architecture-led initiatives.

**Architectural Leadership & Implementation:**

* Responsible for all aspects of the Network Architecture, ensuring secure, reliable, and high-performance network infrastructure to support healthcare applications and data exchange.
* Responsible for all aspects of the Cloud Architecture initiatives, including hybrid and multi-cloud strategies, ensuring compliance, cost optimization, and interoperability with on-premises systems.
* Guide Systems Architecture development, ensuring robust design, security, and integration of core business and healthcare applications, including EHR/EMR (Epic).

**Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement:**

* Act as the primary liaison between IT architecture teams and IT leadership, translating business needs into technology strategies.
* Partner with IT Security team to develop and enforce security frameworks that protect patient data and mitigate cybersecurity threats.
* Partner with Cloud team to establish common tooling and automation (e.g., CloudFormation, AWS CDK, AWS Landing Zone Accelerator, Terraform, Kubernetes, Docker, Jenkins).
* Work closely with software vendors, system integrators, and cloud service providers to optimize technology investments.
* Foster collaboration across cross-functional IT teams, ensuring alignment with infrastructure, security, and application teams.

**Performance Management & Risk Mitigation:**

* Establish KPIs and performance metrics to evaluate the effectiveness of IT architecture initiatives.
* Identify and mitigate risks related to network vulnerabilities, cloud security, and system failures.
* Optimize IT spending by implementing cost-effective solutions.
* Continuously assess system performance and scalability to meet the growing demands of healthcare operations.

**REQUIRED EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:**

* Bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Technology, Healthcare Informatics, or a related field.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in IT architecture, including at least 5 years in a leadership role managing network, cloud, and systems architecture teams preferably within a healthcare organization.
* Network Architecture: Strong experience with SD-WAN, VPNs, firewalls, network security protocols, and healthcare data exchange networks.
* Cloud Architecture: Strong experience with AWS, Well-Architected Framework, and hybrid cloud solutioning.
* Demonstrated history of assessing, testing, implementing modern platform visibility solutions (DataDog, Dynatrace, New Relic, Prometheus / Grafana).

**PREFERRED EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:**

* Master's degree preferred.

**CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS PREFERRED:**

* Recent certifications in relevant cloud platforms (AWS Certified: Solutions Architect Professional, AWS Security Specialty, etc Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect, etc.).
CISSP, CCNP, HITRUST, or FinOps Certification.  

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES (KSAs):**

* Systems Architecture: Expertise in the M365 suite, server infrastructure, virtualization, storage solutions, disaster recovery, and healthcare IT standards (HL7, FHIR, DICOM, etc.).
* Security & Compliance: Knowledge of HIPAA & HITRUST compliance, and cybersecurity frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO27K). Ability to work cross-functionally with the BMCHS Information Security Team to define and design according to industry best-practice.
* Fluency in Agile, waterfall, and industry standard tooling (e.g., Jira, Project, Confluence).
* Strong leadership and team management skills. You are a thought-leader and a mentor.
* Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities. You have excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.
* Strategic thinker with strong problem-solving and analytical skills. You see the big picture and how it affects patient care and our bottom line.

##### **About Peraton**

Peraton is a next-generation national security company that drives missions of consequence spanning the globe and extending to the farthest reaches of the galaxy. As the world’s leading mission capability integrator and transformative enterprise IT provider, we deliver trusted, highly differentiated solutions and technologies to protect our nation and allies. Peraton operates at the critical nexus between traditional and nontraditional threats across all domains: land, sea, space, air, and cyberspace. The company serves as a valued partner to essential government agencies and supports every branch of the U.S. armed forces. Each day, our employees solve the most daunting challenges that our customers face. Visit peraton.com to learn how we’re keeping people around the world safe and secure.

##### **About The Role**

Peraton is a leading provider of Information Operations (IO) and Irregular Warfare (IW) capabilities to the U.S. government. Comprised of strategic communications professionals, Psychological Operations (PSYOP) and Military Information Support Operations (MISO) practitioners, data analysts, and campaign managers that bring a multidisciplinary approach to planning, executing, and assessing strategic communications operations, this program integrates Information Related Capabilities (IRC) across multiple domains, environments, and geographic boundaries, leveraging data-driven frameworks, multi-source analytics, and evidence-based reporting to advance influence objectives on behalf of the Department of Defense (DoD) and Intelligence Community (IC).

  

**Responsibilities:**

  

Peraton is seeking a senior Program Manager to provide overall contract leadership and oversight of strategic communications operations. The Program Manager will direct all contractor personnel, resources, and deliverables while serving as the primary interface between the contract team and the Sponsor. The ideal candidate has experience managing large, dispersed teams within the Intelligence Community, strong organizational and communication skills, and the ability to drive performance in a fast-paced, operationally sensitive environment.

  

**Key Responsibilities of this role include:**

* Planning, directing, and overseeing all contractor personnel, resources, and deliverables to ensure performance objectives are met on schedule and within budget;
* Serving as the primary point of contact between the contractor and the Sponsor's Contracting Officer Technical Representative (COTR) and Government Task Manager (GTM);
* Developing and maintaining the Program Management Plan, Monthly Contract Status Reports, and other program-level deliverables in accordance with contract requirements;
* Managing a large, dispersed team across multiple specialty areas, ensuring appropriate staffing levels, personnel qualifications, and adherence to security and compliance requirements;
* Identifying and mitigating programmatic risks, implementing corrective actions, and driving continuous process improvement across all contract task areas.
  

\*\*\*This position is contingent upon award of contract\*\*\*

##### **Qualifications**

**Required Qualifications:**

* TS/SCI with Poly, active and current.
* Bachelor's degree in business administration, finance, communications, or another relevant business or communications discipline.
* Minimum 12 years of project management experience, which must include Four (4) years of experience managing contracts for government customers within the Intelligence Community.
* Demonstrated experience in managing a large, dispersed team with different specialty areas.
* Demonstrated experience in providing timely reports, and knowledge of information management systems.
  

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Master's degree in business administration, finance, communications, or another relevant business or communications discipline.
* Two (2) years of experience managing projects under the direction of the Sponsor.
* Experience using the Sponsor's business systems.
* Certified in project management – Project Management Professional (PMP) or equivalent.
* Experience using data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau or Microsoft Power BI).

##### **Details**

**Target Salary Range:** $135,000 - $216,000. This represents the typical salary range for this position. Salary is determined by various factors, including but not limited to, the scope and responsibilities of the position, the individual’s experience, education, knowledge, skills, and competencies, as well as geographic location and business and contract considerations. Depending on the position, employees may be eligible for overtime, shift differential, and a discretionary bonus in addition to base pay.

**Benefits Statement:** Peraton offers eligible employees a variety of benefits including medical, dental, vision, life, health savings account, short/long term disability, EAP, parental leave, 401(k), paid time off (PTO) for vacation, and company paid holidays. Use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools of any kind during Peraton interviews is strictly prohibited unless the candidate has obtained prior written authorization. Position Description

Harris County Universal Services (Universal Services) is transforming the way the County does business and seeking an experienced and strategic Senior IT Project Manager to join our team.

Universal Services is the enterprise IT solutions center for the departments and offices of Harris County, providing Information Technology, Public Safety and Justice Technologies, 311 Constituent Engagement Services, Fleet Services, and Records and Information Governance Services.

Harris County is the third largest and most diverse county in the nation, with a population of more than 4.7 million. Harris County Commissioners Court, the County’s governing body, directs a budget of more than $4 billion providing essential services including flood control, infrastructure, healthcare, housing, and justice administration.

Job Overview

This Universal Services position reports into the Enterprise Project Management Office (EPMO). The primary purpose of the Senior IT Project Manager role is to lead, oversee and ensure the successful delivery and management of enterprise technology projects. The Senior IT Project Manager must deliver projects within scope, on time and within budget. The Senior IT Project Manager is responsible for the creation, organization, execution, and completion of assigned projects, in accordance with the EPMO standards and methodology. This includes managing the project team, establishing milestones and target dates, communicating with and preparing reports to stakeholders about the project, and adjusting as necessary to meet new requirements and scope changes.

Implement a project communication plan.

Ensure that project goals are in line with business objectives.
Ensure that project goals are achieved.
Assign duties and responsibilities to project personnel and define the scope of their authority.
Direct and coordinate the activities of project personnel to ensure projects progress on schedule and within budget.
Review status reports prepared by project personnel and modify schedules or plans as required.
Establish standards and procedures for project reporting and documentation.
Benchmark project management performance continuously to identify the potential for improvements and increase capability in project and portfolio management.

jobs.description:
### **Company Background**

Censys’ mission is to be the one place to understand everything on the internet. Frustrated by the lack of trustworthy Internet intelligence, we set out to create the industry’s most comprehensive, accurate, and up-to-date map of the Internet. Today, Censys delivers real-time Internet intelligence and actionable threat insights to global governments, over 50% of the Fortune 500, and leading threat intelligence providers worldwide.

As Director of IT & Business Enablement, you'll own the systems, tools, and technology experience that power every team at Censys. Your mandate: make our internal tools fast, reliable, and easy to use — and make sure we're getting maximum leverage out of AI across everything we run. You understand that availability and usability are often in tension, and you know how to balance both without slowing the business down.

You'll own the full lifecycle of our internal technology stack — from endpoint provisioning and SaaS tooling to the adoption, integration, and optimization of AI across our systems. You're the person every employee turns to for equipment and tooling needs, and the person finance turns to for software utilization and budget decisions. You're energized by automating the boring stuff and building systems that act as force multipliers for the company.

### **Responsibilities**

* Own, build, and scale the team and systems supporting Censys's IT infrastructure
* Own company technology needs end-to-end: new hire equipment, IT onboarding, and the tools that keep employees productive
* Hire, mentor, and develop members of the IT team to support evolving needs of our global workforce
* Own the complete endpoint lifecycle: provisioning, application deployment and endpoint patching, and asset retirement
* Manage and administer identity systems that enable access to corporate systems and infrastructure
* Enable secure AI adoption across the company: identify where AI can improve internal tools and workflows, lead integration of AI capabilities into our systems, and continuously optimize existing AI tooling for effectiveness and ROI
* Evaluate, select, and manage the internal tooling and software stack, ensuring the right tools are in place and being used effectively
* Own software and hardware budget planning and vendor management in partnership with finance
* Build and maintain documentation for IT processes, systems, and support workflows
* Develop and deliver internal training on tools and systems to drive adoption
* Other duties as assigned

**Skills/Experience you’ll have:**

* 10+ years of experience in IT management, systems administration, or technology operations, including 5+ years leading a team
* Proven experience owning endpoint lifecycle management (provisioning, deployment, retirement) at scale, ideally for a fully or hybrid-remote workforce
* Hands-on experience managing a modern SaaS tooling stack (identity/access management, MDM, collaboration tools, etc.) and making build-vs-buy / consolidate-vs-expand decisions
* Demonstrated experience integrating AI tools into business workflows (not just using AI tools personally, but leading adoption across a team or company –e.g., rolling out AI-powered support tools, automating workflows with AI, evaluating AI vendor tooling)
* Experience managing software/hardware budgets and vendor relationships, with the ability to translate technical decisions into cost and ROI terms for finance and leadership
* Strong track record of building documentation, processes, and support systems from scratch
* Excellent cross-functional communication skills, and comfortable being the technical translator between engineering, finance, and non-technical employees

Job Family:Behavioral Health

Overview

The Clinical Training Program Manager plays a crucial role in developing, implementing, and delivering training programs to enhance the skills and knowledge of staff working within the behavioral health division. This position is designed to ensure that staff are well-equipped to provide high-quality mental health and enabling services, with a specific focus on equitable and inclusive clinical practices. The Clinical Training Program Manager will serve as the conduit for academic programs seeking to place interns with the agency and provide clinical supervision to students. This position will provide direct supervision for early career clinicians and student interns, participating in recruitment, hiring, and evaluation. In addition, this position provides clinical care for up to two sessions per week.

Key Role Responsibilities

* Lead the development, implementation, and ongoing refinement of a behavioral health training program. Deliver trainings to providers within the behavioral health division that are grounded in evidence-based practices and align with divisional priorities and provider learning needs.
* Stay abreast of the latest research, trends, and best practices in behavioral health to ensure training content is current and relevant.
* Evaluate the effectiveness of training programs through feedback, assessments and measurable outcomes.
* Collaborate with other behavioral health professionals across the agency to create comprehensive and effective training materials. Customize training programs based on the unique requirements and goals of different organizations and funders.

* Maintain standards for provision of CEU in accordance with social work and professional counselor licensing boards for the state of MD. Track and issue CEU for training participants as appropriate.
* Provide direct supervision for early career clinicians and student interns and partner with the Senior Director of Behavioral Health in the recruitment, hiring, and evaluation of behavioral health staff and interns.
* Provide clinical services to a small caseload of clients for up to two sessions per week. Provide clinical coverage for staff as indicated.
* Completes documentation of services in a legible manner in accordance with established formats and required timeframes within the client’s electronic health record. Ensure that documentation accurately reflects billable services provided.

Key Agency Responsibilities

In addition to role responsibilities, each staff member of Health Care for the Homeless has the following responsibilities as a part of their employment:

* Models and reinforces the Health Care for the Homeless “core values” of dignity, authenticity, hope, justice, passion and balance
* Actively participates in performance improvement activities and actively participates in advocacy activities that support the mission of Health Care for the Homeless
* Performs other duties on an as-needed basis
* Protects our client’s personal health information by maintaining compliance with HIPAA and other relevant Health Care related IT security regulations

Knowledge, Experience, and Skills

Formal Education and Training

* Master’s degree in social work
* Active license in the state of Maryland (LCSW-C) with supervisory designation

Experience

* Three years of experience in the evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment of chronic mental illness and substance abuse
* Five years of experience supervising staff and/or interns, where there was emphasis on provision of training and ongoing education
* Experience working with homeless and/or low-income individuals and families
* Familiarity with adult learning principles and instructional design

Skills

* Able to work independently as a social worker on an interdisciplinary team
* Strong knowledge of various mental health disorders, treatments, and interventions
* Willingness to integrate relevant principles into practice such as Harm Reduction, Motivational Interviewing and Housing First
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills
* Strong organizational and time management skills
* Able to cope with interruptions and be a team player
* Flexible approach, working with several cross-disciplinary teams in a collaborative style
* Demonstrate comfort with change by approaching it optimistically and helps their supervisees to do the same. Proactively seeks to clarify unclear aspects of change in a productive, collaborative manner.
* Able to work with clients who have significant mental health challenges, manage crisis situations and assess for safety

**Location and Remote Eligibility**

Fully remote candidates within the United States will be considered if they demonstrate substantial experience leading large-scale Workday implementations as a project manager, program manager, engagement manager, or delivery lead.

At Connect Centric, we are more than just consultants—we are partners committed to our clients' success. We take a hands-on approach, working closely with our clients to transform strategies into measurable, real-world outcomes. As a strategy execution team, we take full ownership of every initiative from start to finish, ensuring that our clients see tangible results, not just ideas.

**Position Description**
========================

Connect Centric is seeking a Senior Program Manager to lead enterprise Human Capital Management (HCM) initiatives for our client, with a primary focus on UKG and Workday. You will oversee multiple HCM workstreams, connecting implementation plans, platform enhancements, integrations, reporting, governance, and operational readiness across the program.  
  
This role requires direct experience supporting both UKG and Workday initiatives.

**What You Will Do**
====================

* Lead complex, cross-functional HCM programs and projects involving UKG, Workday, and related workforce management capabilities.
* Develop and manage integrated program plans, implementation roadmaps, schedules, milestones, budgets, dependencies, risks, and issues across HCM workstreams.
* Facilitate program governance and decision forums; prepare decision materials, document decisions, track actions, and provide status updates to senior leaders.
* Partner with business and technology stakeholders, vendors, and workstream project managers to clarify scope, align priorities, resolve risks and issues, and maintain delivery momentum.
* Coordinate requirements, configuration decisions, business workflows, integrations, data validation, testing, and implementation readiness for UKG and Workday initiatives.
* Oversee cutover coordination, operational transition planning, and post-implementation stabilization across the HCM program.
* Prepare executive reports, dashboards, decision logs, and risk, assumption, issue, and dependency (RAID) logs; communicate delivery progress, tradeoffs, decisions, and adoption impacts.
* Support HCM process improvement, change management, stakeholder readiness, training coordination, and adoption planning.
* Develop and maintain program standards, templates, governance routines, tools, and delivery methodologies that improve consistency and readiness.
* Assess workforce processes, platform issues, data considerations, vendor capabilities, and platform roadmaps; recommend practical solutions to complex HCM challenges.
* Ensure work products meet business needs, quality expectations, compliance requirements, data integrity standards, configuration expectations, and delivery commitments.
* Balance competing HCM programs, platform enhancements, implementation activities, and stakeholder needs.

**Required Qualifications**
===========================

* Bachelor’s degree and at least eight years of experience in program management, project management, business analysis, technology delivery, or a related field, including demonstrated experience supporting enterprise HCM platforms.
* Strong experience supporting both UKG and Workday initiatives, including implementation planning, enhancements, requirements definition, configuration coordination, business process alignment, and integration coordination.
* Experience coordinating HCM testing, data validation, security and access considerations, reporting, stakeholder readiness, training support, adoption, issue resolution, and post-implementation stabilization.
* Hands-on experience using UKG and Workday to support program delivery, platform reporting, issue tracking, stakeholder communications, governance, testing coordination, cutover planning, and executive decision support.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex HCM programs or projects involving HR, payroll, finance, operations, technology teams, vendors, and senior leaders.
* Working knowledge of core HR, payroll, time and attendance, absence management, benefits, talent, workforce scheduling, reporting, and employee self-service processes.
* Strong understanding of scope, schedule, budget, risk, issue, dependency, resource, change, benefits, and stakeholder management.
* Experience supporting Agile or other delivery methodologies in enterprise platform, ERP, HRIS, payroll, workforce management, or HCM environments.
* Experience preparing and presenting executive reports, dashboards, status updates, decision materials, risk summaries, and implementation readiness updates.

**Preferred Qualifications**
============================

* PMP, PgMP, SAFe, Agile, Scrum, Prosci, ITIL, Workday, UKG, HRIS, or a similar certification.

**Position Details**

* Position Type: Full-time W-2 employment. Independent contractor or 1099 arrangements are not available for this position.
* Location: Washington D.C. / Remote for Exceptional Candidates outside of commuting radius.
* This position is hybrid (2x per week)
* Pay Rate: $130K - $140K

jobs.title: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) – BCG Federal
jobs.description:
**Locations**: Washington | Boston

Who We Are

Boston Consulting Group partners with leaders in business and society to tackle their most important challenges and capture their greatest opportunities. BCG was the pioneer in business strategy when it was founded in 1963. Today, we help clients with total transformation-inspiring complex change, enabling organizations to grow, building competitive advantage, and driving bottom-line impact.  
  
To succeed, organizations must blend digital and human capabilities. Our diverse, global teams bring deep industry and functional expertise and a range of perspectives to spark change. BCG delivers solutions through leading-edge management consulting along with technology and design, corporate and digital ventures—and business purpose. We work in a uniquely collaborative model across the firm and throughout all levels of the client organization, generating results that allow our clients to thrive.

What You'll Do

The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) serves as the primary executive authority on enterprise cybersecurity strategy, risk governance, and federal compliance for BCG Federal. Reporting regularly to the Government Security Committee (GSC) and executive leadership, the CISO holds direct authority to define and approve the federal IT security boundary, manage enterprise risk, and escalate unresolved security exposures. Operating as an executive peer alongside business and technology leaders, the CISO balances client mission enablement with rigorous defense compliance mandates.

The CISO leads a dedicated cyber organization of approximately 25 professionals and directs the strategic security interface between BCG Federal and BCG Global IT and Security. In this capacity, the CISO ensures our streamlined cloud environment—primarily Microsoft 365 GCC-High, Azure Government, and AWS DevOps pipelines—remains properly isolated and compliant with Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) standards, while safely leveraging global shared capabilities where permitted.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Executive Governance & GSC Advisory:** Define enterprise security strategy, deliver regular security and compliance briefings to the Government Security Committee (GSC), and maintain risk governance aligned with federal missions and strategic corporate growth.
* **Team Leadership & Cyber Operations:** Direct a ~15-person cybersecurity organization across core functions, including security operations, compliance, cloud security architecture, IAM, and vulnerability management.
* **Global Parent Alignment & Boundary Integrity:** Partner with BCG Global CISO and IT leadership to maintain boundary isolation, data barriers, and access controls separating BCG Federal enclaves from commercial global infrastructure.
* **Cloud Architecture & Enclave Protection:** Oversee the security architecture and boundary controls for a focused cloud environment centered on Microsoft 365 GCC-High, Azure Government, and AWS DevOps pipelines, ensuring strict protection of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and export-controlled data.
* **Federal Compliance & Audit Ownership:** Own enterprise compliance for NIST SP 800-171, NIST SP 800-53, DFARS 252.204-7012, and CMMC Level 2, leading System Security Plan (SSP) maintenance, SPRS scoring, and C3PAO/federal audit readiness.
* **Technology Controls Administration:** Collaborate with Legal, the Facility Security Officer (FSO), and leadership to administer the Technology Control Plan (TCP) and ensure systems adhere to DCSA security requirements and governance obligations.
* **Business Development & Mission Enablement:** Partner with capture and client delivery teams to architect compliant, secure solutions for client enclaves and support proposal responses.
* **AI Security Governance:** Provide security and compliance oversight for vetting, deploying, and governing AI tools, LLMs, and emerging technologies within CUI-constrained environments.
* **Supply Chain & Third-Party Risk (SCRM):** Oversee vendor risk assessments, software supply chain security, and FedRAMP cloud service provider evaluations across subcontractors and external integrations.

What You'll Bring

* Experience: 7–10+ years of IT security and information assurance experience, including 2–4+ years operating within the Defense Industrial Base (DIB) or a directly comparable national security environment.
* People Leadership: 7+ years of demonstrated success directly managing multi-disciplinary IT teams, setting operational rhythms, and mentoring technical leads.
* Cloud & Infrastructure Mastery: Strong architectural knowledge of Microsoft GCC-High / Azure Government (Entra ID, Purview, Defender, Intune) and foundational AWS DevOps/IAM security baselines.
* Regulatory Expertise: In-depth understanding of NIST SP 800-171, DFARS 7012, CMMC Level 2, and DCSA oversight requirements.
* Clearance: Active Top Secret clearance required
* Education & Certifications: Bachelor’s degree in a relevant technical or government/business discipline. Recent coursework in AI and Cybersecurity a plus.

Additional info

At BCG, our people and relationships are at the heart of everything we do. We believe that in-person collaboration plays an important role in our culture, mentorship, and professional development.

For this role, you will generally be expected to work from a BCG office or in person with clients on a regular basis (typically around 50% of working time), depending on business needs and in line with local policies and practices.

jobs.title: Field Chief Technology Officer (CTO)
jobs.description:
**Field Chief Technology Officer (CTO)**
========================================

*US-Remote*

Reports to: Chief Executive Officer

**Who We Are**
--------------

At 8th Light, we bring life to the best ideas.

Founded in 2006 and headquartered in Chicago, we are a technology solutions provider that partners with organizations to solve meaningful challenges and drive sustainable growth. From early-stage startups to global enterprises, we work across industries to optimize our clients’ digital products through product strategy innovation, experiential design, AI solutions, and deep engineering expertise.

Our commitment to quality means we deliver solutions we’re truly proud of, while our curiosity sparks innovation and breakthrough thinking. 8th Lights thrive in an environment that champions continuous education, fueling our growth through mentorship and hands-on work. We foster an open, collaborative culture grounded in honesty that builds trust, and believe true success is measured by the outcomes we create for our clients.

If this kind of work and our kind of people energizes you, you’ve found the right place.

**Who You Are**
---------------

You’ve spent 10+ years in custom software consultancies, and you’ve been a regular presence on both sides of the business: in the room helping win the work, and in delivery helping build it. You know how to pitch a client honestly and then stand behind what you promised.

You’re highly articulate and commercially fluent. You can talk architecture with a skeptical engineering lead in one meeting and talk ROI with a client’s CEO in the next, and both walk away trusting you. You understand how technical choices shape whether a project makes money because you’ve had to make those calls yourself.

Your technical judgment comes from years of hands-on work, and you keep it current in two ways: you read widely, and you keep doing the work. “Doing” might be a few hours each week staying sharp with new tools, or it might be real delivery responsibility on a live engagement. Either way, you don’t run on knowledge that stopped accruing years ago.

You’re comfortable leading by influence rather than authority. You may not be our deepest expert on any single topic, and that’s fine, because your value shows up differently:

* You ask experienced technologists the kind of sharp questions that send them back to their desk thinking.
* You know a good deal across a wide range of subjects and connect ideas others keep separate.
* You’re an excellent communicator, in writing and on your feet.
* You bring out people’s best work through interpersonal connection and high standards.

Your name carries some weight in the communities you’re part of. When you write or speak, senior engineers pay attention, and a few of them want to come work with you.

This is primarily a market-facing role. You’d rather be out in the market shaping where we go than waiting inside for an assignment.

**What You’ll Do At 8th Light**
-------------------------------

We win work by earning technical trust before a contract is ever signed, and by being genuinely present in the market the rest of the time. This role carries both. You’ll report to the CEO and work most closely with the CEO, the VP of Growth, our practice Partners, and senior technologists.

Your primary focus will require you to:

* Join deal teams to help win new engagements. In a pitch that can mean proposing an architecture, shaping scope, sequencing the work into sensible stages, or recommending how to staff it. On our most important accounts, you’ll stay a technical presence the client trusts well after the work begins.
* Represent us and build relationships in the market. Give talks, write, and show up in person at events. In-person presence matters here, and writing alone won’t carry the role.
* Shape and sharpen what we sell. Turn what you’re seeing in the market into clearer, more current offerings, and keep our position honest: agentic products, deep platform expertise.
* Work with our Growth team to help identify and build relationships with platform and AI partners that put us in front of the right work and keep our teams current.
* Drive our go-to-market direction rather than wait for it. Bring a point of view and help us continuously iterate on where we should show up, what we should say, and which opportunities are worth chasing.

Internally, your footprint is lighter but real. You’re the standard other technologists measure themselves against, and you’re a mentor to those working on their business leadership and impact. You’ll weigh in from time to time on technical job standards and career pathing. You’ll start without direct reports and lead through influence, and as we grow, the role could grow into leading a small team.

**Strongly Preferred Skills**
-----------------------------

We’d particularly like to hear from applicants with:

* A track record of pitching and winning enterprise engagements inside a consultancy
* A public technical presence: talks you’ve given, things you’ve written, communities you help lead
* Experience shaping the service offerings or the technical point of view a firm takes to market
* Relationships with cloud or AI platform partners, and the standing that comes with them
* A working grasp of where AI and agentic tooling is heading, enough to judge where the real opportunities are
* Experience mentoring senior technical talent and raising the bar around them

**Compensation**
----------------

Our pay range for the Field CTO role is $230,000–$287,500 USD, plus 20–30% variable compensation based on performance.

**Travel Expectation**
----------------------

This role involves regular but not frequent travel, mostly for in-person events, client pitches, and the occasional team gatherings.

**How You’ll Be Supported**
---------------------------

At 8th Light, our culture is built on the belief that our collective growth and well-being are the drivers of our future.

jobs.title: Director of IT
jobs.description:
Description:

### **POSITION SUMMARY**

Serve as the trusted technology adviser and primary internal IT resource across all HarborChase Communities and the corporate office. Provide oversight and hands-on support for the technology utilized by approximately 200 associates across 18 communities in 8 states, while partnering with third-party IT providers for larger infrastructure, architecture, cybersecurity, and specialized projects.

### **ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS**

* Ensure computers and end-user technology are properly configured, deployed, maintained, repaired, replaced, and inventoried for new and existing users.
* Function as the primary Help Desk for all technical questions, troubleshooting, and support needs across the organization.
* Serve as the primary point of contact for network communications, connectivity, internet service, and technology-related outages.
* Manage IT equipment procurement, inventory, product lifecycle, shipping, receiving, and replacement planning to support business needs.
* Manage onboarding and offboarding of associates, including computers, phones, accounts, system access, and equipment, ensuring a positive user experience.
* Manage third-party IT contracts and vendors, including service levels, renewals, pricing, performance, and negotiation of terms.
* Administer and coordinate upgrades to technical systems and maintain accurate documentation of the technology environment.
* Manage computer installations, repairs, purchases, and technology procurement for all communities.
* Coordinate technology installations and connectivity for new community construction, openings, renovations, and acquisitions, including network, internet, telephone, access control, cameras, POS, and other technology systems as applicable.
* Coordinate with external IT partners on larger infrastructure, architecture, cybersecurity, and specialized technology projects; serve as the internal project owner.
* Configure and maintain network addressing and connectivity requirements for applications and installed technology.
* Manage all company cell phones, including setup, troubleshooting, devices, plans, and contracts.
* Maintain accurate records of IT assets, vendors, service contracts, software licenses, warranties, service providers, and renewal dates.
* Evaluate technology solutions and make recommendations that improve reliability, security, efficiency, user experience, and cost management.

### **NON-ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS**

* Lead by example and demonstrate the HarborChase values of **Respect, Attentiveness, Integrity, Stewardship, and Excellence**.
* Provide responsive, professional, solutions-oriented service to associates at every level of the organization.
* Take ownership of technology issues from initial troubleshooting through resolution or appropriate escalation.
* Maintain professional knowledge and affiliations related to information technology and senior living.
* Support organizational initiatives and participate in meetings or activities as required.
* Work in a safe, responsible, and professional manner while maintaining appropriate confidentiality and security of company information.
* Support a safe and secure environment for residents, associates, and visitors.

### **QUALIFICATIONS, SKILLS & EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS**

* Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience may be considered.
* At least five years of progressive IT experience, preferably in a multi-site organization. Experience in Senior Living, Healthcare, Hospitality, or another multi-location service organization is preferred.
* Strong hands-on experience with hardware, software, networking, telecommunications, mobile devices, Microsoft 365, and end-user support. Experience with Yardi, Sherpa, or similar business applications is a plus.
* Ability to manage vendors, service providers, contracts, procurement, and technology-related expenses while independently prioritizing multiple issues and projects.
* Strong leadership, problem-solving, organizational, and customer service skills.
* Ability to make independent decisions, take ownership, and determine when issues should be resolved internally or escalated to an external IT partner.
* Ability to communicate effectively with all levels of management, associates, vendors, outside technology partners, and other contacts.
* Ability to travel periodically to company locations as business needs require.

jobs.title: Director of Technology & AI Automation
jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Director of Technology & AI Automation oversees FEI's technology infrastructure and leads the identification, implementation, and adoption of AI and automation solutions across the institution. This role bridges traditional IT operations (systems, networks, data security) with practical AI deployment, including building and running the AI automation layer that supports enrollment marketing and student outreach. The Director ensures all technology is reliable, secure, and aligned with FEI's operational, marketing, and compliance requirements.

Duties & Responsibilities

Technology Operations

* Oversee day-to-day IT operations, including systems, networks, and data security.
* Ensure institutional data systems (SIS, CRM, LMS) are integrated and functioning reliably, including integrations needed for marketing AI tools.
* Develop and enforce data security and privacy practices, including for AI tool usage.
* Manage vendor relationships for IT infrastructure, SIS, and AI/automation platforms, and coordinate with vendors and technical support to resolve issues.
* Manage the technology budget, including AI tool licensing and infrastructure costs.
* Supervise IT and automation support staff or contractors.

AI Implementation

* Lead the planning and rollout of AI and automation initiatives across departments.
* Partner with department leaders (Marketing, Admissions, Financial Aid, Academics) to assess workflows and identify processes suited for automation.
* Research and recommend off-the-shelf or lightly customized AI solutions.
* Lead implementation projects from pilot through full deployment.
* Maintain an inventory of active AI tools and their institutional use cases.

Marketing & Enrollment Automation

* Build and manage AI agent workflows for inbound and outbound admissions and marketing outreach.
* Configure multilingual AI scheduling for admissions appointments and information sessions.
* Use AI tools to support social media content planning and website content creation.
* Deploy AI-driven surveys to gather student and prospect feedback.
* Work with the CMO to align AI automation efforts with enrollment marketing goals.
* Monitor AI agent performance and refine scripts, prompts, and workflows over time.

Training, Reporting & Compliance

* Develop training materials and lead onboarding sessions for staff using new AI tools.
* Measure and report on the impact of deployed AI solutions (efficiency, response time, conversion).
* Ensure technology, AI practices, and AI-generated content comply with applicable federal, state, and accreditor requirements and FEI brand standards.

Position Requirements

Education

* Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Marketing, or related field required; Master's preferred.

Experience

* 5+ years in IT management, technology operations, technology implementation, or marketing automation, including team or vendor oversight.
* Demonstrated experience rolling out software or AI tools to non-technical teams.
* Experience with AI agent, chatbot, or AI content tools strongly preferred.
* Higher education or regulated-industry experience a plus.

Technology

* Proficient with common workplace technology and software, including IT infrastructure management, SIS/CRM/LMS platforms, AI agent and chatbot platforms, marketing automation tools, content creation software, and project management software.
* Comfortable learning and using institutional systems related to admissions, financial aid, and student records.
* Adapts readily to new software and technology as institutional systems evolve.

Skills & Attributes

* Strong leadership, project management, and cross-departmental coordination skills.
* Strategic thinker able to balance innovation with operational stability.
* Strong writing and content sensibility for student-facing communication.
* Comfortable testing and iterating on AI prompts and scripts.
* Analytical mindset with the ability to translate results into plain-language reporting.
* Patient, effective trainer for staff at varying technical comfort levels.
* Sound judgment on data security and regulatory compliance.

Pay: $100,000.00 - $125,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Flexible schedule
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Professional development assistance
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

**Head of IT & Security**

**About us:**  
At Fullbay, our mission is simple — to create safer roads for our families and yours. As leaders in the heavy-duty repair industry, we power shops with technology that helps them run smarter and more efficiently. As an AI-First company, we invite artificial intelligence to eliminate friction, spark innovation, and drive efficiencies in every conversation— for our teams and our customers. Fullbay is the number one cloud-based shop management software for commercial repair shops and is growing fast. This is an exciting opportunity to join a high-performing team and help shape the next phase of growth for the company.

  

**Position Overview:**

Fullbay's Security and IT Manager owns two functions that are usually split across two people: the security program that keeps Fullbay's systems, people, and customer data safe, and the IT operations that keep the business running day to day. Reporting to the VP of IT, this role designs the security and IT program from the ground up and owns its execution end-to-end — there's no existing playbook to inherit and no separate team to hand the work to.

This role is well-suited to someone who has built a security program before, not just operated inside one — someone comfortable being the primary responder when an MDR alert escalates, the person who leads SOC 2 through an actual audit, and the same person who's also the company's escalation point when someone's laptop won't image. This is a player-coach role: you set the standards, and you personally execute the work.

Success here looks like passing SOC 2 audits with no major findings, on schedule; security incidents that get triaged, contained, and resolved fast enough that they stay incidents, not breaches; IT support that doesn't make employees wait, with devices provisioned before day one and tickets closed without a saga; and a risk posture leadership can see clearly at any time, not just when an audit forces the question.

**The Right Wrench for the Job**

A shop's most dangerous moments are never the ones people see coming. The person who wires the electrical panel, checks the fire suppression, and makes sure the alarm actually calls someone when it goes off isn't thinking about any one repair — they're thinking about what keeps the whole building standing. This role does that for Fullbay's systems and data, and then still picks up the phone when someone's laptop won't turn on.

You're the right fit if you've built a security program from a blank page before — not just operated inside one someone else designed — and you know the difference between a control that looks good on paper and one that actually holds up when an auditor or an attacker tests it. You can walk into a SOC 2 evidence review in the morning, triage a real MDR alert at noon, and still be the person who gets a new hire's laptop imaged and ready before their first day.

This isn't the role for someone who wants to own strategy and hand off the keyboard. If your instinct is to write the policy and let someone else enforce it, this isn't your shop. But if you're the kind of person who'll design the program, defend it to an auditor, and still crawl under the desk to fix a network cable — we'd like to talk.

**Primary Duties & Responsibilities:**

* Security Program Ownership: Design, build, and continuously improve Fullbay’s security program using NIST CSF 2.0 as the governance architecture and CIS Controls v8.1 (IG1 to IG2) as the tactical execution roadmap.
* Security Operations Oversight: Manage Fullbay’s always-on MDR platform, which provides automated threat detection and triage across endpoints and cloud environments. Serve as the primary responder for escalated alerts requiring human judgment, and lead investigation, containment, and remediation for confirmed incidents, including participation in an on-call rotation for high-severity escalations.
* SOC 2 Readiness and Audit Management: Lead all SOC 2 readiness activities including control mapping, evidence collection, gap remediation, and audit firm coordination for Type I and Type II engagements.
* Tool and Platform Governance: Own and configure Fullbay’s security tooling stack, including the MDR platform, MDM, email security, anti-phishing, and security awareness training. Tune and maintain tools to Fullbay standards, and evaluate new tools or vendors as needed.
* Policy and Standards Development: Author, maintain, and enforce information security policies, standards, and procedures across the organization. Ensure policies align with regulatory requirements and audit frameworks.
* Identity and Access Management: Oversee IAM posture across Google Workspace, including passkeys, MFA, SSO, and privileged access controls, including MDM and Apple Business Manager configuration.
* Incident Response: Develop and own the incident response plan. Serve as the primary responder for security events escalated by the MDR platform or identified through other internal monitoring. Lead response activities and post-incident reviews.
* Risk Management: Maintain a risk register. Identify, assess, and track security risks across people, process, and technology. Communicate risk posture to the VP of IT and senior leadership.
* Security Awareness: Oversee the security awareness training program, including phishing simulations and compliance-based training cycles.
* Vendor and Third-Party Risk: Assess security posture of third-party vendors and new software applications. Maintain a vendor risk inventory and drive remediation for identified gaps.
* End-User IT Support: Serve as the primary escalation point for company-wide technical support, resolving hardware, software, network, and account issues for employees across the organization.

**Position Summary**

The SSVF Program Manager provides strategic and operational leadership for Veterans Bridge Home's Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF) program, ensuring high-quality, veteran-centered services that prevent and end homelessness among veterans and their families. Reporting to the Market Executive Director, this position is responsible for the day-to-day management of the SSVF grant, including program operations, staff supervision, compliance, quality assurance, and community partnerships. The Program Manager will work directly with the Compliance department and Finance team. The Program Manager ensures services are delivered in accordance with Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) regulations, Housing First principles, and Veterans Bridge Home policies while maintaining a strong focus on measurable outcomes and continuous improvement.

This position serves as the operational leader for the SSVF program by fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and innovation. Working closely with internal departments and community partners, the Program Manager develops strategies to improve housing stability, enhance program performance, strengthen partnerships, and ensure responsible stewardship of federal grant resources. The Program Manager contributes to Veterans Bridge Home's mission by connecting service members, veterans, and their families to the communities where they live and thrive. This is a grant-funded position.

**Primary Responsibilities**

Program Leadership

* Provide operational leadership for the Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF) program, ensuring services are delivered in accordance with VA regulations (38 CFR Part 62), grant requirements, organizational policies, and a Housing First, veteran-centered approach.
* In collaboration with the Triangle Market Executive Director, assist with developing annual program goals, operational plans, and performance objectives aligned with organizational priorities.
* Monitor program performance and implement continuous quality improvement initiatives to enhance veteran outcomes.
* Lead program meetings, case consultations, and operational planning sessions to ensure consistent, high-quality service delivery.
* Promote equitable, timely, and veteran-centered services across all assigned service areas.
* Oversee delivery of both Rapid Re-Housing (RRH) and Homelessness Prevention (HP) services, ensuring the balance between service models aligns with SSVF Program Office priorities and available grant funding.
* Direct coordinated outreach efforts to identify and engage eligible veterans who are experiencing or at imminent risk of homelessness.

Grant Administration & Operations

* Oversee program intake, eligibility determinations, and referral processes to ensure timely, equitable, and consistent access to services.
* Ensure eligibility determinations meet SSVF requirements, including veteran status, household income at or below 50% of Area Median Income (AMI), and literally homeless or imminent-risk status under the “but for” standard.
* Partner collaboratively with the Compliance team to ensure adherence to grant requirements, support quality assurance activities, and prepare for monitoring visits and audits.
* Maintain awareness of grant expenditures, fund utilization, and program capacity by collaborating with Finance to support operational planning and ensure services remain aligned with grant requirements.
* Oversee the appropriate, compliant, and timely use of Temporary Financial Assistance (TFA), including rental assistance, security and utility deposits, utility payments, moving costs, and emergency housing assistance.
* Monitor program documentation, reporting requirements, and operational performance while identifying opportunities for continuous improvement.
* In conjunction with Compliance, complete, accurate, and timely submission of required reports and program data.

Staff Leadership

* Supervise, coach, and develop assigned staff.
* Foster a collaborative, inclusive, and mission-driven team culture.
* Conduct regular supervision meetings and annual performance evaluations.
* Support employee engagement, accountability, retention, and professional development.

Performance Management & Veteran Services

jobs.title: Senior Vice President of Technology
jobs.description:
**Who We Are**
==============

  

We're Personified: a managed IT + cybersecurity services provider for campaigns, non-profits, and mission-aligned organizations. Our mission is to lead technology and security programs for our clients, enabling them to focus on their mission-critical work.

We act as an extension of our client teams — we handle all the responsibilities a traditional internal IT team would. We're in our clients' Slacks, we're on a first-name basis with them (and their pets), we're new hires' first point of contact, and we're the first stop for tech and cybersecurity issues. We aim to build trust, and we leverage this to keep the bad actors out.

Some of the biggest names in the progressive space have leaned on us as their trusted IT + cybersecurity partner. We are looking for top IT talent as we continue to scale our team.

**About the Role**
==================

  

Personified is looking for a Senior Vice President of Technology to run the operational core of our technology organization: engineering, client support, cybersecurity, and IT operations. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who has run these functions inside a managed service provider before and knows exactly what breaks at scale: ticket queues, on-call rotations, security posture, tooling debt, and how to fix it without slowing the team down.

You'll report to the CTO and own execution across four functional leaders and the day-to-day delivery. You are the person who makes sure the trains run on time, the team is accountable, and our 97% client retention rate stays exactly where it is, or gets better.

This role exists because Personified is growing past the point where one person can run every function directly. We need someone who has done this before, who can walk into a room of client support engineers or a security incident and immediately know what questions to ask.

  

**Key Responsibilities**
========================

  

* **Client Support & Service Delivery** — Ensure the team hits our response-time and resolution standards across every client tier. Own escalation paths, staffing models, and the systems (like our Halo ticketing platform) that keep support predictable and measurable.
* **Engineering** — Oversee infrastructure, systems engineering, and technical delivery. Set standards for process discipline, documentation, and accountability across the engineering team.
* **Cybersecurity** — Own the operational security posture across our client base: monitoring, incident response, vulnerability management, and compliance readiness. Make sure security isn't a side conversation — it's built into how we operate.
* **IT Operations** — Drive the shift from manual, reactive IT operations toward automation and repeatable processes. Reduce the operational load on the team while improving consistency for clients.
* **People leadership** — Directly manage functional leaders across these four areas. Set clear expectations, run a real performance management cadence, and build a bench of leaders under you who can eventually run without your direct involvement.
* **Cross-functional operations** — Be the connective tissue between functions that too often operate in silos. When a client issue touches support, engineering, and security at once, you're the person who makes sure it gets resolved as one coordinated response, not three separate ones.
* **Metrics and accountability** — Build and own the operational scorecard for technology delivery: response times, resolution rates, security incidents, retention impact. Bring data, not anecdotes, to every conversation with the CTO.
* **Travel** or work or present onsite as needed to support business needs, ensure continuity of service, and represent Personified to our clients and partners at the highest level.

**Skills + Experience**
=======================

  

* 8+ years in technology operations leadership, with at least 4 in a managed service provider (MSP) environment, you understand ticket economics, SLAs, multi-client environments, and the specific pressure of supporting many organizations at once rather than one.
* Direct people-management experience across multiple technical functions simultaneously (not just one discipline). You've managed managers, not just individual contributors.
* A track record of taking an under-disciplined operation and making it measurably more consistent, without making it slower or more bureaucratic.
* Real fluency in cybersecurity operations; you don't need to be the deepest technical expert in the room, but you need to know enough to ask sharp questions and hold a security leader accountable.
* Experience building or scaling IT automation — you should be able to speak concretely about a time you replaced manual process with something repeatable.
* A communication style that is direct and specific. You document decisions. You don't let vague problems stay vague.

**What Would Make You a Great Fit Here**

* You've worked with or served mission-driven, nonprofit, or advocacy organizations before, and you understand why 'the client hired us so they never have to think about IT again' is a real design principle, not a slogan.
* You're comfortable in a smaller, fast-moving company where your title doesn't insulate you from doing real work.
* You believe good process makes teams faster, not slower, and you can tell the difference between bureaucracy and discipline.
* You want to build a team, not just manage one that already exists.

**Reporting Structure**

This role has direct management authority over the functional leaders in Client Support, Engineering, Cybersecurity, and IT Operations. It reports to the CTO, who retains direct ownership of Technical Programs and Training/Content, along with technology strategy, senior-level accountability, and cross-company initiatives.

**Benefits**

* Remote work environment
* Competitive pay, bonus eligible
* Healthcare packages contributed to by Personified
* Optional 401K matched by

**About the Team**

OpenAI's Vendor Security team helps internal teams work securely with external products, services, and partners. Our work spans software, infrastructure, hardware, professional and managed services, vendor-provided workforces, data, and research. We build the programs and products that help teams understand vendor risk and put effective safeguards in place, protecting our customers, employees, and the company.

**About the Role**

We are looking for a Vendor Security Technical Program Manager who can make sound security decisions and turn recurring vendor-security problems into tools and practices that work.

You will independently lead vendor-security engagements: understand the business need, investigate the actual data and access, recommend a practical path, and work with the responsible owners until the safeguards are verified. You will also use what you learn to build and improve bounded tools and workflows, with priorities agreed with the Vendor Security lead.

This is an individual-contributor role for someone who combines technical judgment with useful delivery. You should be comfortable taking a position, explaining the tradeoff, and changing your mind when the evidence changes. Success means internal teams can use vendors securely, reuse work that still applies, and understand what needs to happen next.

**In this role, you will:**

* Own vendor security engagements from understanding the business need through scopingal exceptions and risk acceptance to the appropriate decision owners.
* Understand vendor use cases, workflows, user journeys, data flows, identities, access, integrations, and supply-chain dependencies. Identify plausible attack paths and their consequences for OpenAI.
* Assess relevant architectures, configurations, controls, logs, and operational practices. Test whether the evidence supports the security claims that matter to the engagement, and make gaps and uncertainty clear.
* Develop practical treatments, including changes to the operating model, data exposure, access, architecture, vendor choice, controls, or containment. Drive implementation with the responsible owners and verify that the treatment works.
* Build reusable security patterns with clear applicability, safeguards, evidence requirements, exceptions, and review triggers.

* Use Codex or comparable AI-assisted tools to build, inspect, test, and maintain practical improvements to scoping, evidence checks, routing, decision reuse, or treatment tracking. Investigate failures and own the result through adoption, continued operation, and explicit handoff or retirement.

**You might thrive in this role if you:**

* Understand security principles and controls, including data protection, access management, application security, prevention, detection, and response. Can reason about architecture, identity, APIs, data flows, logging, integrations, and whether controls work.

jobs.title: WattBridge- Senior Director, Information Technology
jobs.description:
About WattBridge

The global energy landscape is rapidly changing, and we're here to accelerate that change. From the decommissioning of high-carbon power assets, accelerated expansion of renewable energy resources as baseload power, to the advent of the prosumer. The volatility on today's energy grid has never been greater. WattBridge was conceived by power industry experts to enable the sustained integration of highly efficient, reduced carbon dispatchable power generation assets on our national energy grid.

Position Summary

WattBridge, the world’s preeminent LM6000 delivery platform, is seeking a Senior Director, Information Technology to develop, implement, and own the company’s information technology (IT), cybersecurity and data strategy that will support the origination, development and commercial operations of a full power delivery platform focused on data center campus style development. WattBridge developed, financed, built, owned and operated the world’s largest LM6000 portfolio consisting of 2400 MW’s from 2019 thru 2026. The platform raised over $2BN in capital and is now partnered with Energy Capital Partners as our majority sponsor. With competitive advantages in secured power equipment as an OEM, a proven track record in building out a 2400 MW portfolio, and a fully vertically integrated execution platform, we are well positioned to be highly successful in the data center industry.

The primary focus of this role is developing and leading the separation of IT and cybersecurity services from Parent Company under the Transition Services Agreement (TSA), stands up an independent, cloud-native technology platform within twelve months of close, and then runs that platform through a small internal team and a managed service model. The position builds enterprise-grade IT, cybersecurity, and governance from the outset, secures operational technology (OT) at the company's generation assets, and establishes the controls, reporting, and data foundation expected of a private equity-backed company preparing for future capital markets activity.

Reports to
: Vice President Business Development.

Work Location:
Remote United States

Position Responsibilities

Serve as WattBridge's TSA workstream lead for IT and cybersecurity, coordinating with the PROENERGY counterpart and owning monthly service reviews
Deliver the IT and cybersecurity exit milestones within the 12-month TSA term, including an independent Microsoft 365 tenant, a live MSP contract, and full endpoint migration
Build and execute the 90-day transition plans required before each TSA exit, including knowledge transfer, data migration, and systems access cutover
Enforce WattBridge data ownership and portability rights, ensuring all company data is extracted and validated before TSA systems access ends
Track TSA service levels, cost-plus charges, and scope changes, escalating issues through the governance model defined in the agreement
Define WattBridge's technology strategy and roadmap under the principle of outsourcing infrastructure while owning data and insights
Select cloud-native, low-administration platforms that employee growth and beyond without re-platforming
Partner with Finance, Commercial, Development, and HR leaders to select and deploy core business systems, including ERP, HRIS, project and pipeline management, and document management
Embed AI capabilities from day one, including Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption, a governed AI use-case pipeline, and an enterprise data and analytics foundation (Power BI)
Plan the technology footprint for asset operations if O&M transitions from PROENERGY, including CMMS, asset performance monitoring, and predictive maintenance (AMPS / PI)
Establish and lead the cybersecurity program, including policies, standards, risk management, identity and access management, and incident response
Oversee the managed detection and response (MDR/SOC) partner, Microsoft Defender endpoint protection, vulnerability management, and the incident response retainer
Secure OT/ICS environments at generation assets, including deployment of passive OT monitoring (Claroty or Dragos) and IT/OT segmentation
Ensure compliance with NERC CIP and other applicable regulatory requirements for generation assets, and support audits and regulatory inspections
Run security awareness training and phishing simulation for all employees and contractors
Establish IT governance aligned with NIST CSF, including IT general controls (ITGCs) that support lender reporting, audit, and future SOX readiness
Build and manage the IT and cybersecurity operating and capital budgets, including the one-time Day-1 infrastructure and end-user equipment plan
Report technology risk, cybersecurity posture, and program status to the executive team, PE sponsor, and board as required
Develop business continuity and disaster recovery capability, including backup (Azure Backup), recovery objectives, and tested recovery plans
Lead competitive selection of a Houston-based managed service provider and define contract scope, service level agreements, and performance reporting
Negotiate and manage all technology vendor, licensing, and telecommunications agreements for value and security compliance
Hire, lead, and develop IT staff, setting goals, standards, and on-call expectations
Deliver a consistent onboarding experience as the company scales through each hiring wave, from equipment and accounts on day one to security training

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, or a related field
Minimum 15 years of progressive IT experience with 5+ years in IT leadership roles
Proven experience leading an IT carve-out, divestiture separation, or standing up IT for a new or spun-off company
Hands-on experience negotiating, governing, and exiting transition services agreements
Strong background building and leading cybersecurity programs, including OT/ICS security
Deep knowledge of the Microsoft cloud ecosystem (Microsoft 365, Entra ID, Intune, Defender, Azure)
Experience selecting and managing MSP and MDR/SOC providers against defined service levels
Working knowledge of NERC CIP compliance and critical infrastructure regulatory requirements

jobs.title: WattBridge- Senior Director, Information Technology
jobs.description:
**WattBridge- Senior Director, Information Technology**

**About WattBridge**

The global energy landscape is rapidly changing, and we're here to accelerate that change. From the decommissioning of high-carbon power assets, accelerated expansion of renewable energy resources as baseload power, to the advent of the prosumer. The volatility on today's energy grid has never been greater. WattBridge was conceived by power industry experts to enable the sustained integration of highly efficient, reduced carbon dispatchable power generation assets on our national energy grid.

**Position Summary**

WattBridge, the world’s preeminent LM6000 delivery platform, is seeking a Senior Director, Information Technology to develop, implement, and own the company’s information technology (IT), cybersecurity and data strategy that will support the origination, development and commercial operations of a full power delivery platform focused on data center campus style development. WattBridge developed, financed, built, owned and operated the world’s largest LM6000 portfolio consisting of 2400 MW’s from 2019 thru 2026. The platform raised over $2BN in capital and is now partnered with Energy Capital Partners as our majority sponsor. With competitive advantages in secured power equipment as an OEM, a proven track record in building out a 2400 MW portfolio, and a fully vertically integrated execution platform, we are well positioned to be highly successful in the data center industry.

The primary focus of this role is developing and leading the separation of IT and cybersecurity services from Parent Company under the Transition Services Agreement (TSA), stands up an independent, cloud-native technology platform within twelve months of close, and then runs that platform through a small internal team and a managed service model. The position builds enterprise-grade IT, cybersecurity, and governance from the outset, secures operational technology (OT) at the company's generation assets, and establishes the controls, reporting, and data foundation expected of a private equity-backed company preparing for future capital markets activity.

**Reports to**: Vice President Business Development.

**Work Location:** Remote United States

**Position Responsibilities**

* Serve as WattBridge's TSA workstream lead for IT and cybersecurity, coordinating with the PROENERGY counterpart and owning monthly service reviews
* Deliver the IT and cybersecurity exit milestones within the 12-month TSA term, including an independent Microsoft 365 tenant, a live MSP contract, and full endpoint migration
* Build and execute the 90-day transition plans required before each TSA exit, including knowledge transfer, data migration, and systems access cutover
* Enforce WattBridge data ownership and portability rights, ensuring all company data is extracted and validated before TSA systems access ends
* Track TSA service levels, cost-plus charges, and scope changes, escalating issues through the governance model defined in the agreement
* Define WattBridge's technology strategy and roadmap under the principle of outsourcing infrastructure while owning data and insights
* Select cloud-native, low-administration platforms that employee growth and beyond without re-platforming
* Partner with Finance, Commercial, Development, and HR leaders to select and deploy core business systems, including ERP, HRIS, project and pipeline management, and document management
* Embed AI capabilities from day one, including Microsoft 365 Copilot adoption, a governed AI use-case pipeline, and an enterprise data and analytics foundation (Power BI)
* Plan the technology footprint for asset operations if O&M transitions from PROENERGY, including CMMS, asset performance monitoring, and predictive maintenance (AMPS / PI)
* Establish and lead the cybersecurity program, including policies, standards, risk management, identity and access management, and incident response
* Oversee the managed detection and response (MDR/SOC) partner, Microsoft Defender endpoint protection, vulnerability management, and the incident response retainer
* Secure OT/ICS environments at generation assets, including deployment of passive OT monitoring (Claroty or Dragos) and IT/OT segmentation
* Ensure compliance with NERC CIP and other applicable regulatory requirements for generation assets, and support audits and regulatory inspections
* Run security awareness training and phishing simulation for all employees and contractors
* Establish IT governance aligned with NIST CSF, including IT general controls (ITGCs) that support lender reporting, audit, and future SOX readiness
* Build and manage the IT and cybersecurity operating and capital budgets, including the one-time Day-1 infrastructure and end-user equipment plan
* Report technology risk, cybersecurity posture, and program status to the executive team, PE sponsor, and board as required
* Develop business continuity and disaster recovery capability, including backup (Azure Backup), recovery objectives, and tested recovery plans
* Lead competitive selection of a Houston-based managed service provider and define contract scope, service level agreements, and performance reporting
* Negotiate and manage all technology vendor, licensing, and telecommunications agreements for value and security compliance
* Hire, lead, and develop IT staff, setting goals, standards, and on-call expectations
* Deliver a consistent onboarding experience as the company scales through each hiring wave, from equipment and accounts on day one to security training

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, or a related field
* Minimum 15 years of progressive IT experience with 5+ years in IT leadership roles
* Proven experience leading an IT carve-out, divestiture separation, or standing up IT for a new or spun-off company
* Hands-on experience negotiating, governing, and exiting transition service
