jobs.title: Director, IT Applications
jobs.description:
Drive Technology Innovation and Build High-Performing Teams at Liberty Dental Plan

Are you a strategic technology leader who excels at developing people, partnering with the business, and delivering enterprise applications that drive measurable results? Liberty Dental Plan is seeking a Director, IT Applications
to lead a critical portfolio of business applications while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Reporting to the VP, Application Development
, this highly visible leadership role combines technology strategy, operational excellence, and people leadership. You will help shape the future of our application landscape, strengthen business partnerships, and guide a talented team responsible for delivering reliable, secure, and scalable solutions that support our members, clients, and organization.

About The Role

The Director, IT Applications is responsible for leading the delivery, support, maintenance, and ongoing evolution of enterprise applications across assigned business areas. This role ensures applications meet business needs, service level commitments, quality standards, and security requirements while supporting operational performance and organizational growth.

The ideal candidate brings a combination of healthcare payer industry knowledge, strong people leadership capabilities, business acumen, and experience managing vendor relationships and enterprise application portfolios.

Location:
Remote

Reporting Relationship:
VP, Application Development

What You'll Do

Technology Strategy & Application Leadership

Lead the delivery, support, maintenance, and optimization of critical business applications.
Serve as the product owner for assigned application platforms, establishing strategic priorities, modernization initiatives, and technology roadmaps.
Partner with business leaders to understand requirements, identify process bottlenecks, and recommend technology solutions that improve efficiency and productivity.
Balance business priorities, operational stability, modernization efforts, and technical debt reduction.
Guide application strategy and influence technical direction in partnership with technical teams and stakeholders.

Operational Excellence

Ensure applications meet agreed-upon service level expectations for availability, performance, incident response, and production support.
Oversee release planning, production readiness, ongoing maintenance, and enhancement activities.
Maintain strong controls around data integrity, compliance, security, and system management.
Monitor application health, technical debt, and remediation efforts while communicating risks and progress to leadership.
Identify and proactively address operational and delivery risks to ensure successful outcomes.
Support audits, client reviews, regulatory inquiries, proposal responses, and new client implementation activities.

Vendor & Stakeholder Management

Build and maintain strong relationships with vendors, business leaders, and cross-functional partners.
Manage third-party resources and consulting relationships to support delivery and operational objectives.
Partner with compliance, security, infrastructure, architecture, governance, and business operations teams to ensure alignment and execution.
Navigate competing priorities effectively while maintaining strong stakeholder relationships and transparency.

People & Team Leadership

Lead, coach, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of technology professionals.
Create an environment where employees feel supported, empowered, and accountable for results.
Establish clear expectations and provide ongoing performance feedback and development opportunities.
Foster collaboration, trust, continuous learning, and professional growth.
Delegate effectively while developing future leaders and building organizational capability.
Recognize and celebrate team contributions while maintaining a high-performance culture.

What You'll Bring

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business, or a related field.
10+ years of experience in IT applications, application support, systems delivery, or a related discipline.
5+ years of people leadership experience.
Strong understanding of application delivery, support, operations, and service level management.
Experience with software development lifecycles, release management, production support, and application maintenance practices.
Experience managing vendors, budgets, resources, operational risks, and delivery governance.
Ability to build trusted relationships with business leaders, technical teams, and external partners.
Strong communication, problem-solving, decision-making, and leadership skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Healthcare payer experience, including Medicare and/or Medicaid environments.
Dental payer experience strongly preferred.
Experience supporting delegated healthcare models and healthcare operations.
Experience with Health Solutions Plus (HSP) and healthcare payer administration platforms highly preferred.
Experience participating in audits, regulatory reviews, RFP responses, and client-facing initiatives.
Experience with Agile delivery methodologies.
Familiarity with Azure, APIs, web portals, management information systems, and database technologies.
Experience collaborating with Scrum Masters and Project Managers.
Experience with DevOps practices and modern application delivery approaches.
Previous experience working with Conduent or similar healthcare technology partners is a plus.

What Success Looks Like

Successful candidates will be able to:

Build strong partnerships across business and technology teams.
Develop and retain engaged, high-performing employees.
Deliver reliable, secure, and business-focused technology solutions.
Balance competing priorities while maintaining operational excellence.
Drive innovation and modernization without losing focus on stability and service quality.
Lead with integrity, sound judgment, and a commitment to organizational success.

Why Join Liberty Dental Plan?

At Liberty Dental Plan, we believe our people are our greatest asset. We are committed to creating an environment where employees can grow professionally, contribute meaningfully, and make an impact. You'll join a collaborative organization where leadership is measured not only by results, but by the ability to develop talent, strengthen relationships, inspire innovation, and create lasting business value.

As the Director, IT Applications, you'll have the opportunity to influence enterprise technology strategy, lead meaningful transformation initiatives, mentor future leaders, and help advance solutions that support the health and well-being of the communities we serve.

Ready to make a lasting impact? Apply today and help shape the future of technology at Liberty Dental Plan.

Qualifications

Location

Our employees are distributed in office locations in multiple markets across the United States. We are unable to hire or allow employees to work outside of the United States.

What Liberty Offers

Happy, healthy employees enhance our ability to assist our members and contribute more actively to their communities. That’s why Liberty offers competitive and attractive benefit packages for our employees. We strive to care for employees in ways that promote wellness and productivity.

Our first-class benefits package supports employees and their dependents with:

Competitive pay structure and savings options to help you reach your financial goals.
Excellent 401(k) retirement benefits, including employer match, Roth IRA options, immediate vesting during the Safe Harbor period, and access to professional financial advice through Financial Engines.
Affordable medical insurance, with low-cost premiums for employee-only coverage. Liberty subsidizes the cost for eligible dependents enrolled in the plan.
100% employer-paid dental coverage for employees and eligible dependents.
Vision insurance with low-cost premiums for employee-only coverage and dependents.
Company-paid basic life and AD&D insurance, equal to one times your base salary, with options to purchase additional supplemental coverage.
Flexible Spending Accounts for healthcare and dependent care expenses.
Voluntary benefit programs, including accident, critical illness, and hospital indemnity insurance.
Long-term disability coverage.
Expansive wellness programs, including company-wide wellness challenges, BurnAlong memberships, and gym discounts.
Employee Assistance Program (EAP) to support mental health and well-being.
Generous vacation and sick leave policies, with the ability to roll over unused time.
10 paid company holidays.
Tuition reimbursement for eligible educational expenses.
Remote or hybrid work options available for various positions.

Compensation

In the spirit of pay transparency, the base salary range for this position is $150,000 - $200,000 a year,
not including fringe benefits or potential bonuses. At Liberty, your final base salary will be determined by factors such as geographic location, skills, education, and experience. We are committed to pay equity and also consider the internal equity of our current team members when making final compensation decisions.

Please note that the range listed represents the full base salary range for this role. Typically, offers are not made at the top of the range to allow for future salary growth.

Liberty Dental Plan commits to maintaining a work environment that acknowledges all individuals within the workplace and will continue to engage in practices that are inclusive of all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We strive to have every person within the organization have a sense of belonging while encouraging individuals to unleash their full potential. Liberty will leverage diverse perspectives in building high performance teams and organizational culture.

Liberty Dental Plan will continue to strengthen and develop external partnerships by providing equitable health care access and improving population health in the communities we serve.

We comply with all applicable laws and regulations on non-discrimination in employment, recruitment, promotions, and transfers, as well as work authorization and employment eligibility verification requirements.

Sponsorship and Relocation Specifications

Liberty Dental Plan is an Equal Opportunity Employer / VETS / Disabled.

No relocation assistance or sponsorship available at this time.

jobs.title: Field Chief Technology Officer (CTO)
jobs.description:
US-Remote

Reports to: Chief Executive Officer

Who We Are

At 8th Light, we bring life to the best ideas.

Founded in 2006 and headquartered in Chicago, we are a technology solutions provider that partners with organizations to solve meaningful challenges and drive sustainable growth. From early-stage startups to global enterprises, we work across industries to optimize our clients’ digital products through product strategy innovation, experiential design, AI solutions, and deep engineering expertise.

Our commitment to quality means we deliver solutions we’re truly proud of, while our curiosity sparks innovation and breakthrough thinking. 8th Lights thrive in an environment that champions continuous education, fueling our growth through mentorship and hands-on work. We foster an open, collaborative culture grounded in honesty that builds trust, and believe true success is measured by the outcomes we create for our clients.

If this kind of work and our kind of people energizes you, you’ve found the right place.

Who You Are

You’ve spent 10+ years in custom software consultancies, and you’ve been a regular presence on both sides of the business: in the room helping win the work, and in delivery helping build it. You know how to pitch a client honestly and then stand behind what you promised.

You’re highly articulate and commercially fluent. You can talk architecture with a skeptical engineering lead in one meeting and talk ROI with a client’s CEO in the next, and both walk away trusting you. You understand how technical choices shape whether a project makes money because you’ve had to make those calls yourself.

Your technical judgment comes from years of hands-on work, and you keep it current in two ways: you read widely, and you keep doing the work. “Doing” might be a few hours each week staying sharp with new tools, or it might be real delivery responsibility on a live engagement. Either way, you don’t run on knowledge that stopped accruing years ago.

You’re Comfortable Leading By Influence Rather Than Authority. You May Not Be Our Deepest Expert On Any Single Topic, And That’s Fine, Because Your Value Shows Up Differently

You ask experienced technologists the kind of sharp questions that send them back to their desk thinking.
You know a good deal across a wide range of subjects and connect ideas others keep separate.
You’re an excellent communicator, in writing and on your feet.
You bring out people’s best work through interpersonal connection and high standards.

Your name carries some weight in the communities you’re part of. When you write or speak, senior engineers pay attention, and a few of them want to come work with you.

This is primarily a market-facing role. You’d rather be out in the market shaping where we go than waiting inside for an assignment.

What You’ll Do At 8th Light

We win work by earning technical trust before a contract is ever signed, and by being genuinely present in the market the rest of the time. This role carries both. You’ll report to the CEO and work most closely with the CEO, the VP of Growth, our practice Partners, and senior technologists.

Your Primary Focus Will Require You To

Join deal teams to help win new engagements. In a pitch that can mean proposing an architecture, shaping scope, sequencing the work into sensible stages, or recommending how to staff it. On our most important accounts, you’ll stay a technical presence the client trusts well after the work begins.
Represent us and build relationships in the market. Give talks, write, and show up in person at events. In-person presence matters here, and writing alone won’t carry the role.
Shape and sharpen what we sell. Turn what you’re seeing in the market into clearer, more current offerings, and keep our position honest: agentic products, deep platform expertise.
Work with our Growth team to help identify and build relationships with platform and AI partners that put us in front of the right work and keep our teams current.
Drive our go-to-market direction rather than wait for it. Bring a point of view and help us continuously iterate on where we should show up, what we should say, and which opportunities are worth chasing.

Internally, your footprint is lighter but real. You’re the standard other technologists measure themselves against, and you’re a mentor to those working on their business leadership and impact. You’ll weigh in from time to time on technical job standards and career pathing. You’ll start without direct reports and lead through influence, and as we grow, the role could grow into leading a small team.

Strongly Preferred Skills

We’d particularly like to hear from applicants with:

A track record of pitching and winning enterprise engagements inside a consultancy
A public technical presence: talks you’ve given, things you’ve written, communities you help lead
Experience shaping the service offerings or the technical point of view a firm takes to market
Relationships with cloud or AI platform partners, and the standing that comes with them
A working grasp of where AI and agentic tooling is heading, enough to judge where the real opportunities are
Experience mentoring senior technical talent and raising the bar around them

Compensation

Our pay range for the Field CTO role is $230,000–$287,500 USD, plus 20–30% variable compensation based on performance.

Travel Expectation

This role involves regular but not frequent travel, mostly for in-person events, client pitches, and the occasional team gatherings.

How You’ll Be Supported

At 8th Light, our culture is built on the belief that our collective growth and well-being are the drivers of our future.

Our wellness package is designed with the Whole YOU in mind and includes:
A robust L&D program featuring unlimited access to thousands of books, courses, and expert-led training on the O'Reilly learning platform.
Annual financial stipend and time allotment for learning & development
Coworking support for our global team
Flexible PTO with floating company holidays
12 weeks of new parent leave available for eligible employees

See our full list of Benefits.

8th Light Hubs and Geographies

8th Light’s culture is rooted in strong connections that extend across our teams, regions, and beyond client work. We are a distributed team across the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom, with hubs in Chicago, London, Los Angeles, New York, and Seattle.

If you are hired into a hub, you will be part of a team with regular rituals around co-working and community building. For team members outside of those cities, we offer access to coworking spaces to foster continued collaboration and connection across our global team.

We hope to see you apply!

A Note on Your Privacy

At 8th Light, one of our core values is Honesty that builds trust
— and that shapes how we approach hiring. We want you to have a clear picture of who we are , what we're looking for , and how we handle your information throughout the process.

Before submitting your application, please take a moment to review our Global Candidate Privacy Notice. By applying, you acknowledge that you've read it.

jobs.title: Senior IT Project Manager
jobs.description:
Role Overview

The Senior IT Project Manager
leads the design, development, and implementation of information systems across the full system development life cycle, from requirements through go-live and transition to operations. Supported systems may include Medicaid Management Information Systems (MMIS), eligibility and enrollment systems, enrollment broker platforms, learning management systems, web portals, and data and reporting solutions. This role manages multi-year federal, state, and corporate projects with budgets of $500,000 and higher.

This is a full-time position located in the United States.

Key Responsibilities

Lead the initiation, planning, execution, and closing of IT and professional services projects across the entire system development life cycle (SDLC), covering requirements, design, development, testing, deployment, and post-implementation support.
Serve as the primary liaison among the end client, vendors, stakeholders, and the hiring organization, managing communications and progress reporting to ensure project success, client satisfaction, and a positive team experience.
Define and develop project scope, deliverables, tasks, resource plans, schedule baselines, and expenses, while managing resource allocations and providing timely performance feedback.
Monitor project budgets and hours to meet target gross margin goals, accurately forecast resource utilization and revenue recognition, and review and approve client and subcontractor invoices.
Apply Waterfall, Agile/Scrum, or hybrid delivery methodologies based on client requirements, coordinating backlog, sprint, and release planning with product owners.
Facilitate requirements gathering and elicitation sessions, maintain a Requirements Traceability Matrix (RTM), and partner with business analysts, developers, solution architects, and quality assurance (QA) teams to translate business requirements into technical designs.
Identify, track, and mitigate project risks, including technical risks, system interfaces, integrations, and environment dependencies.
Ensure all project deliverables meet organization standards and client specifications, overseeing system, integration, and user acceptance testing (UAT), defect triage, and go/no-go readiness decisions.
Coordinate with third-party vendors, system integrators, and client IT organizations, and define statements of work (SOWs) for subcontract partners.
Support federal oversight activities as applicable, including Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) certification, Advance Planning Documents (APDs), and Independent Verification and Validation (IV&V) reviews.
Collaborate with technical, organizational change management (OCM), and training teams to ensure end-user readiness for system launch.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Business, or Program/Project Management, or equivalent work experience.
Project Management Professional (PMP)® Certification.
At least 7 years of experience managing IT projects for external customers, including at least 5 years managing system implementations.
Demonstrated experience successfully managing IT projects exceeding $500,000 in budget.
Proven track record of delivering at least one large-scale system implementation from initial requirements through go-live.
Experience managing projects with federal government, state government, and private-sector clients.
Working knowledge of software development, system integration, APIs, and data flows sufficient to engage credibly with technical teams.
Ability to communicate technical issues clearly to non-technical executives and program staff.
Demonstrated consultative, conflict management, customer service, and negotiation skills to achieve mutually agreeable solutions.
Superior writing and verbal communication skills, along with strong organization, prioritization, and time management abilities under pressure and tight deadlines.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and collaborate effectively across diverse personalities and organizational levels.
Proficiency with project management and delivery tools, such as Jira, Azure DevOps, Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or ServiceNow.
Familiarity with cloud-based and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) implementations.
An AI-forward mindset with the ability to effectively and responsibly leverage AI tools and technologies to support project planning, documentation, analysis, communication, and overall daily project management activities.

Preferred Qualifications

Agile certification, such as PMI Agile Certified Practitioner (PMI-ACP)®, Certified ScrumMaster® (CSM), or SAFe®.
Health and Human Services (HHS) or Medicaid systems experience (such as MMIS, eligibility and enrollment, enrollment broker, or data and reporting systems).

Physical Demands and Working Conditions

Regularly required to sit, stand, talk, hear, and utilize technology tools such as a laptop computer for extended periods.
Specific vision requirements include close vision and the ability to adjust focus.
Ability to occasionally lift up to 20 pounds.
Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

jobs.title: Senior Vice President of Technology
jobs.description:
Who We Are

We’re Personified: a managed IT + cybersecurity services provider for campaigns, non-profits, and mission-aligned organizations. Our mission is to lead technology and security programs for our clients, enabling them to focus on their mission-critical work.

We act as an extension of our client teams — we handle all the responsibilities a traditional internal IT team would. We’re in our clients’ Slacks, we’re on a first-name basis with them (and their pets), we’re new hires’ first point of contact, and we’re the first stop for tech and cybersecurity issues. We aim to build trust, and we leverage this to keep the bad actors out.

Some of the biggest names in the progressive space have leaned on us as their trusted IT + cybersecurity partner. We are looking for top IT talent as we continue to scale our team.

About the Role

Personified is looking for a Senior Vice President of Technology to run the operational core of our technology organization: engineering, client support, cybersecurity, and IT operations. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who has run these functions inside a managed service provider before and knows exactly what breaks at scale: ticket queues, on-call rotations, security posture, tooling debt, and how to fix it without slowing the team down.

You'll report to the CTO and own execution across four functional leaders and the day-to-day delivery. You are the person who makes sure the trains run on time, the team is accountable, and our 97% client retention rate stays exactly where it is, or gets better.

This role exists because Personified is growing past the point where one person can run every function directly. We need someone who has done this before, who can walk into a room of client support engineers or a security incident and immediately know what questions to ask.

Key Responsibilities

Client Support & Service Delivery
— Ensure the team hits our response-time and resolution standards across every client tier. Own escalation paths, staffing models, and the systems (like our Halo ticketing platform) that keep support predictable and measurable.

Engineering
— Oversee infrastructure, systems engineering, and technical delivery. Set standards for process discipline, documentation, and accountability across the engineering team.

Cybersecurity
— Own the operational security posture across our client base: monitoring, incident response, vulnerability management, and compliance readiness. Make sure security isn't a side conversation — it's built into how we operate.

IT Operations
— Drive the shift from manual, reactive IT operations toward automation and repeatable processes. Reduce the operational load on the team while improving consistency for clients.

People leadership
— Directly manage functional leaders across these four areas. Set clear expectations, run a real performance management cadence, and build a bench of leaders under you who can eventually run without your direct involvement.

Cross-functional operations
— Be the connective tissue between functions that too often operate in silos. When a client issue touches support, engineering, and security at once, you're the person who makes sure it gets resolved as one coordinated response, not three separate ones.

Metrics and accountability
— Build and own the operational scorecard for technology delivery: response times, resolution rates, security incidents, retention impact. Bring data, not anecdotes, to every conversation with the CTO.

Travel
or work or present onsite as needed to support business needs, ensure continuity of service, and represent Personified to our clients and partners at the highest level.

Skills + Experience

8+ years in technology operations leadership, with at least 4 in a managed service provider (MSP) environment, you understand ticket economics, SLAs, multi-client environments, and the specific pressure of supporting many organizations at once rather than one.

Direct people-management experience across multiple technical functions simultaneously (not just one discipline). You've managed managers, not just individual contributors.

A track record of taking an under-disciplined operation and making it measurably more consistent, without making it slower or more bureaucratic.

Real fluency in cybersecurity operations; you don't need to be the deepest technical expert in the room, but you need to know enough to ask sharp questions and hold a security leader accountable.

Experience building or scaling IT automation — you should be able to speak concretely about a time you replaced manual process with something repeatable.

A communication style that is direct and specific. You document decisions. You don't let vague problems stay vague.

What Would Make You a Great Fit Here

You've worked with or served mission-driven, nonprofit, or advocacy organizations before, and you understand why 'the client hired us so they never have to think about IT again' is a real design principle, not a slogan.

You're comfortable in a smaller, fast-moving company where your title doesn't insulate you from doing real work.

You believe good process makes teams faster, not slower, and you can tell the difference between bureaucracy and discipline.

You want to build a team, not just manage one that already exists.

Reporting Structure

This role has direct management authority over the functional leaders in Client Support, Engineering, Cybersecurity, and IT Operations. It reports to the CTO, who retains direct ownership of Technical Programs and Training/Content, along with technology strategy, senior-level accountability, and cross-company initiatives.

Optional 401K matched by Personified

Cell phone stipend

Annual learning & development stipend

jobs.title: Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) – BCG Federal
jobs.description:
Locations
: Washington | Boston

Who We Are

Boston Consulting Group partners with leaders in business and society to tackle their most important challenges and capture their greatest opportunities. BCG was the pioneer in business strategy when it was founded in 1963. Today, we help clients with total transformation-inspiring complex change, enabling organizations to grow, building competitive advantage, and driving bottom-line impact.

To succeed, organizations must blend digital and human capabilities. Our diverse, global teams bring deep industry and functional expertise and a range of perspectives to spark change. BCG delivers solutions through leading-edge management consulting along with technology and design, corporate and digital ventures—and business purpose. We work in a uniquely collaborative model across the firm and throughout all levels of the client organization, generating results that allow our clients to thrive.

What You'll Do

The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) serves as the primary executive authority on enterprise cybersecurity strategy, risk governance, and federal compliance for BCG Federal. Reporting regularly to the Government Security Committee (GSC) and executive leadership, the CISO holds direct authority to define and approve the federal IT security boundary, manage enterprise risk, and escalate unresolved security exposures. Operating as an executive peer alongside business and technology leaders, the CISO balances client mission enablement with rigorous defense compliance mandates.

The CISO leads a dedicated cyber organization of approximately 25 professionals and directs the strategic security interface between BCG Federal and BCG Global IT and Security. In this capacity, the CISO ensures our streamlined cloud environment—primarily Microsoft 365 GCC-High, Azure Government, and AWS DevOps pipelines—remains properly isolated and compliant with Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) standards, while safely leveraging global shared capabilities where permitted.

Key Responsibilities

Executive Governance & GSC Advisory: Define enterprise security strategy, deliver regular security and compliance briefings to the Government Security Committee (GSC), and maintain risk governance aligned with federal missions and strategic corporate growth.
Team Leadership & Cyber Operations: Direct a ~15-person cybersecurity organization across core functions, including security operations, compliance, cloud security architecture, IAM, and vulnerability management.
Global Parent Alignment & Boundary Integrity: Partner with BCG Global CISO and IT leadership to maintain boundary isolation, data barriers, and access controls separating BCG Federal enclaves from commercial global infrastructure.
Cloud Architecture & Enclave Protection: Oversee the security architecture and boundary controls for a focused cloud environment centered on Microsoft 365 GCC-High, Azure Government, and AWS DevOps pipelines, ensuring strict protection of Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) and export-controlled data.
Federal Compliance & Audit Ownership: Own enterprise compliance for NIST SP 800-171, NIST SP 800-53, DFARS 252.204-7012, and CMMC Level 2, leading System Security Plan (SSP) maintenance, SPRS scoring, and C3PAO/federal audit readiness.
Technology Controls Administration: Collaborate with Legal, the Facility Security Officer (FSO), and leadership to administer the Technology Control Plan (TCP) and ensure systems adhere to DCSA security requirements and governance obligations.
Business Development & Mission Enablement: Partner with capture and client delivery teams to architect compliant, secure solutions for client enclaves and support proposal responses.
AI Security Governance: Provide security and compliance oversight for vetting, deploying, and governing AI tools, LLMs, and emerging technologies within CUI-constrained environments.
Supply Chain & Third-Party Risk (SCRM): Oversee vendor risk assessments, software supply chain security, and FedRAMP cloud service provider evaluations across subcontractors and external integrations.

What You'll Bring

Experience: 7–10+ years of IT security and information assurance experience, including 2–4+ years operating within the Defense Industrial Base (DIB) or a directly comparable national security environment.
People Leadership: 7+ years of demonstrated success directly managing multi-disciplinary IT teams, setting operational rhythms, and mentoring technical leads.
Cloud & Infrastructure Mastery: Strong architectural knowledge of Microsoft GCC-High / Azure Government (Entra ID, Purview, Defender, Intune) and foundational AWS DevOps/IAM security baselines.
Regulatory Expertise: In-depth understanding of NIST SP 800-171, DFARS 7012, CMMC Level 2, and DCSA oversight requirements.
Clearance: Active Top Secret clearance required
Education & Certifications: Bachelor’s degree in a relevant technical or government/business discipline. Recent coursework in AI and Cybersecurity a plus.

Additional info

At BCG, our people and relationships are at the heart of everything we do. We believe that in-person collaboration plays an important role in our culture, mentorship, and professional development.

For this role, you will generally be expected to work from a BCG office or in person with clients on a regular basis (typically around 50% of working time), depending on business needs and in line with local policies and practices.

We aim to provide a dynamic and collaborative environment that fosters connection and teamwork.

*** For US locations only ***

In the US, we have a compensation transparency approach.

Total compensation for this role includes base salary, annual discretionary performance bonus, retirement contribution, and a market leading benefits package described below.

The base salary range for this role begins at $225,000 in our lowest cost US region and goes up to $ 262,500 in our highest cost US region. Your recruiting contact can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process.

This is an estimated range, however, specific base salaries within the range depend on various factors such as experience and skill set. It is not common for new BCG employees to be hired at the high-end of the salary range. BCG regularly reviews its ranges to ensure market competitiveness.

In addition to your base salary, your total compensation will include a bonus of up to 45% and a generous retirement contribution that starts at 10%. Senior Directors/Executive Directors are also eligible for a Firm Performance Bonus.

All Of Our Plans Provide Best In Class Coverage

Zero dollar ($0) health insurance premiums for BCG employees, spouses, and children
Low $10 (USD) copays for trips to the doctor, urgent care visits and prescriptions for generic drugs
Dental coverage, including up to $5,000 in orthodontia benefits

Reimbursement for gym memberships and other fitness activities
Fully vested Profit Sharing Retirement Fund contributions made annually, whether you contribute or not, plus the option for employees to make personal contributions to a 401(k) plan
Paid Parental Leave and other family benefits such as elective egg freezing, surrogacy, and adoption reimbursement
Generous paid time off including 12 holidays per year, an annual office closure between Christmas and New Years, and 15 vacation days per year (earned at 1.25 days per month)
Paid sick time on an as needed basis

Boston Consulting Group is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, age, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity / expression, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under national, provincial, or local law, where applicable, and those with criminal histories will be considered in a manner consistent with applicable state and local laws.

jobs.title: Head of IT — Connected Care
jobs.description:
### **Job Title**

Head of IT — Connected Care

### **Job Description**

The Head of IT for Connected Care is the most senior IT leader embedded in Philips’ Connected Care business unit, which encompasses patient monitoring systems, clinical decision support, telehealth platforms, and hospital workflow solutions. Reporting to the Group CIO with a strong dotted line to the BU CEO, this role owns the end-to-end IT strategy, delivery, and operations for Connected Care. The BU operates at the frontier of real-time clinical data, edge computing, and AI-driven patient surveillance—placing unique demands on IT architecture, cybersecurity, and interoperability. The role balances enterprise platform consumption (SAP S/4, Salesforce, Workday) with BU-specific needs in connected device ecosystems, cloud-to-edge architectures, and clinical data integration. This is a Vice President (EL1) position within the Philips IT Leadership Team. In addition, the Head of IT is the designated AI & Data Champion for Connected Care - the single accountable leader who owns the BU's AI and data agenda end to end: partnering with the business to identify and prioritize high-value AI use cases, building AI solutions, organizing and governing the BU data estate, standing up a dedicated BU-centric AI team, and acting as the connective tissue to the enterprise AI & Data organization and the AI Center of Excellence (COE).

**Your role:**

  

**IT Strategy & Business Alignment**
------------------------------------

* Own the BU's IT strategy and get it delivered. It has to line up with the BU's commercial targets , its clinical and product innovation plans, and the Group IT three-pillar model: AI & Data Factory, Platform Operations, Digital Product Engineering.
* Be the BU CEO's IT counterpart. Much of the job is translation, turning what the business, the clinic and the field organisation need into a funded, sequenced set of commitments, then holding to them .
* Get the enterprise platforms adopted inside the BU without pretending the BU is generic . Service contracts, installed-base management, order management and workflow integration are where standard configuration hits its limits. Make those trade-offs explicitly, and in the open.
* Shape the BU's digital product engineering agenda together with the BU's leaders . AI and ML built into the products should run on shared services from the AI & Data Factory; a local rebuild of what already exists centrally is the failure mode to head off .
Set the IT direction for the services business: field service, remote service, and the recurring-revenue models attached to them  

  

**Delivery & Portfolio Governance**
-----------------------------------

* Govern the BU IT portfolio across Run and Improve, ensuring service stability for mission-critical patient monitoring systems while driving transformation programs on time and within budget.
* Lead the BU’s participation in the SAP S/4 transformation, owning BU-specific process design for subscription-based business models, installed-base management, and service logistics.
* Manage BU IT budgets under the consumption-based charging model with transparent cost attribution and predictable financial performance.
Oversee vendor and partner relationships specific to Connected Care, including clinical IT vendors, interoperability partners, and cloud/edge infrastructure providers.  

  

**AI & Data Championship, Data & Digital Enablement**
-----------------------------------------------------

* Own the AI agenda visibly. The business unit should know who is accountable for it, what the plan is, and what it is worth.
* Work with business, clinical, commercial and service stakeholders to find, qualify and rank AI use cases. Keep a governed pipeline behind it, with real business cases, value at stake and adoption numbers, rather than a list of experiments nobody has costed.
* Build and lead a BU AI team: AI product owners, data engineers, ML and GenAI engineers, and translators who can sit between a clinical workflow and a model without losing either.
* Get the BU's data estate into shape. Productised data assets, quality, lineage, stewardship, and integration into the enterprise data mesh, so clinical, product, commercial and operational data can be used for AI rather than cleaned up for it every time.
* Work with the AI & Data Factory to move BU use cases faster, GenAI in the workflow included. Put AI into IT operations too: monitoring, incident triage, agentic workflows.
* Use the platforms, reference architectures, MLOps and LLMOps tooling and responsible-AI guardrails the AI & Data Factory and the AI COE already provide. Don't rebuild them. Push BU requirements back into the enterprise plan instead.
* Raise AI literacy across the business unit. That means enablement, reusable patterns, prompt and solution libraries, and people who will sit down with a clinical, commercial or service team, or with a developer or citizen developer, and work through it. The AI COE backs this.
Run the traffic both ways with the enterprise AI and data teams: escalate what the BU needs, bring back what the enterprise has built, and get security, privacy, responsible-AI and regulatory requirements designed in early instead of reviewed late.  

  

**Cybersecurity, Interoperability & Regulatory Compliance**
-----------------------------------------------------------

* Ensure IT systems and connected device ecosystems meet FDA, MDR, HIPAA, and healthcare interoperability standards (HL7 FHIR, IHE profiles), with particular attention to clinical device cybersecurity.
* Own the BU IT risk posture, including medical device cybersecurity, data privacy, business continuity, and compliance with Philips’ enterprise governance framework.
Collaborate with Regulatory Affairs and the AI Safety & Ethics Lead to ensure AI-driven clinical features meet regulatory validation, explainability, and bias monitoring requirements.  

  

**Team Leadership & Talent Development

jobs.title: Senior Director, Technology Compliance & Regulatory Engagement
jobs.description:

This role will report directly to the Global Chief Compliance Officer and serves as the accountable executive for technology risk and compliance matters, including related regulatory engagement, most notably with the FFIEC, and provides global oversight of IT risk, compliance, and technology-focused audits.

This executive will act as a trusted advisor to senior leadership, regulators, and boards, ensuring the policies, procedures and controls related to SEI’s technology development, deployment and environment meet applicable regulatory expectations and are clearly understood, well-positioned, and defensible in regulatory examinations. A core expectation of this role is the ability to shape, package, and communicate SEI’s technology risk story in alignment with regulatory expectations in multiple jurisdictions, while supporting modernization and innovation initiatives, including the use and deployment of artificial intelligence internally and externally.

**What You Will Do:**

**Regulatory & Examination Leadership**

* Serve as the primary point of contact and owner for FFIEC examinations.

* Provide oversight of any technology-related subsidiary examinations.

* Lead end-to-end exam management, including exam scoping, response strategy, evidence orchestration, examiner communications, and issue resolution.

* Frame and present SEI’s technology risk, control environment, and maturity in a manner that aligns to examiner focus areas and supervisory priorities, not just individual controls.

* Interpret applicable technology, cybersecurity, and data-related regulatory requirements and provide clear, regulator-ready SEI positions and messaging to the applicable regulator.

**Technology Risk & Compliance Oversight**

* Oversee technology risk assessments, identifying control gaps, compliance risks, and emerging vulnerabilities.

* Drive remediation strategies and ensure outcomes are sustainable, auditable, and defensible under regulatory scrutiny.

* Collaborate with the relevant internal stakeholders to establish and evolve technology compliance policies, standards, controls and governance aligned to meet applicable regulatory expectations.

* Support internal and external technology audits and second-line risk assessments, ensuring consistency of messaging across exams, audits, and management reporting.

* Provide concise, executive-level reporting to senior management and boards that clearly articulates risk posture, trends, and regulatory implications.

**Strategic Advisory & Governance**

* Partner with senior leaders across Technology, Risk, Legal, and Compliance as a strategic advisor on regulatory expectations, supervisory risk themes, as well as horizon scanning for potential emerging risks and working with the relevant internal stakeholders to design appropriate mitigation strategies.

* Guide the responsible integration of data, analytics, automation, and AI within compliance and risk operations, ensuring that regulatory expectations are met and solutions remain regulator-ready and explainable.

**Leadership & Collaboration**

* Lead cross-functional efforts across Technology, Operations, Information Security, Audit, and Compliance to ensure that the policies, procedures and controls meet regulatory expectations and deliver coordinated, exam-ready outcomes.

* Translate complex technical environments into clear, cohesive regulatory narratives, supported by appropriate evidence and documentation.

* Build and maintain strong, credible relationships with regulators, auditors, and internal stakeholders at all levels.

**What we need from you:**

* Strategic, solution-oriented mindset with sound judgment and high integrity

* Executive presence with the ability to simplify complex technical and regulatory topics for senior leaders and regulators

* Decisive, credible communicator and active listener, able to influence outcomes at the executive and regulatory level

* Collaborative leader committed to continuous improvement and strong cross-functional partnership

* Deep understanding of technology risk, cybersecurity, and IT controls (applications, infrastructure, cloud, data, access management)

* Strong working knowledge of FFIEC guidance and global technology regulatory standards, including how regulators assess risk and maturity

* Proven experience leading regulatory examinations with direct accountability for exam outcomes and regulatory positioning—not just coordination

* Demonstrated ability to manage multiple, concurrent initiatives while maintaining clarity, consistency, and regulatory credibility

**Attributes we Value:**

* Hardworking

* Smart

* Effective

* Solution-Oriented

* Team Player

* High Integrity/Ethics

* Good Communicator/Listener

* Sound Judgment

* Dedicated to Self-Improvement

* Self-Aware

* Open-Minded

* Thoughtful

jobs.title: Sr. Technical Program Manager, Differentiated Security Team
jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------

Do you want to turn recurring security gaps into enterprise-wide solutions that protect millions of customers? As a Senior Technical Program Manager on Amazon's Differentiated Security Team, you will lead a program that identifies systemic security challenges surfaced through acquisitions and partner engagements, proves solutions work in real environments, and transitions them to long-term owners. This is a high-visibility role where you will define program strategy, influence senior leaders, and drive cross-functional delivery across security engineering, business security, and infrastructure teams. If you thrive in ambiguity, build consensus across organizations, and are energized by turning complex problems into simple, scalable solutions - we want to talk to you.  
  
This is not a maintenance role. You will build the program's operational framework from the ground up by defining how security signals enter the pipeline, how initiatives are prioritized, and what "done" looks like. You will work at the intersection of mergers and acquisitions, security engineering, and enterprise infrastructure, giving you a vantage point into security challenges that most teams never see.  
  
What makes this role unique:  

* You see security problems before anyone else. M&A integrations and partner engagements surface gaps in non-standard environments that standard security teams do not encounter
* Every initiative has a finish line. You prove solutions work, then hand them off. You are a transient owner by design, not a permanent operator.
* You shape the program, not just run it. The operational model, lifecycle framework, and prioritization rubric are being built now. You will have direct influence over how this program works for years to come
* Your work has enterprise-wide impact. Solutions born from this program scale across dozens of business units and hundreds of thousands of applications.

  
Key job responsibilities  

* Own the end-to-end lifecycle of a security solutions program from signal identification through proof-of-concept, investment pitch, and transition to a funded long-term owner
* Define program strategy, build prioritization mechanisms, and create measurable success criteria that keep a portfolio of concurrent initiatives on track

- Drive cross-functional delivery across security engineering, business security, and infrastructure teams - often in environments with non-standard technology stacks  

* Write strategic narratives and present trade-offs, progress, and investment recommendations to Directors and VPs
* Build mechanisms such as intake rubrics, initiative registries, and stage-gate frameworks that make the program repeatable and scalable beyond any single person.

  
A day in the life  
You might start the morning facilitating a cross-functional design review to evaluate whether an existing security solution can close a newly identified gap, or whether a new approach is needed. After lunch, you could be writing an investment narrative to transition a validated solution to its long-term owner. When an active acquisition closes, you may step in as the integration TPM - coordinating security workstreams across engineering, infrastructure, and the acquired business to drive Day 1 readiness and post-close milestones. No two days look the same; the program spans concurrent initiatives at different lifecycle stages, and you keep them all moving forward.  
  
About the team  
Our team enables Amazon to securely capture new revenue streams through mergers and acquisitions. We lead security integration for newly acquired businesses - coordinating across engineering, infrastructure, and compliance teams to drive risk reduction and security posture parity in environments where standard solutions do not yet reach. Our Security Initiatives program operates as a solution incubator: we identify systemic security challenges surfaced through acquisitions and partnerships, prove solutions work, and hand them to funded long-term owners. You will join a globally distributed team of security engineers and technical program managers who value data-driven decisions, partnership, and building durable capabilities for the enterprise.  
  
Diverse Experiences  
Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.  
  
Why Amazon Security?  
At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.  
  
Inclusive Team Culture  
In Amazon Security, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Ongoing DEI events and learning experiences inspire us to continue learning and to embrace our uniqueness. Addressing the toughest security challenges requires that we seek out and celebrate a diversity of ideas, perspectives, and voices.  
  
Training & Career Growth  
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.  
  
Work/Life Balance  
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve

We thrive on a culture of relentless innovation, ownership, and accountability, where every team member takes pride in their work and drives it with excellence and urgency. As an Nscaler, you'll build trust through openness and transparency, where everyone is inspired to do their best work. If you join our team, you'll be contributing to building the technology that powers the future.

**About the role**
------------------

We're hiring a Technical Program Manager to lead delivery of Nscale's Technology Operations program portfolio: the platforms, endpoints and collaboration tooling that every Nscale employee depends on. You'll help deliver these services as the company scales across offices, data-centre locations and remote teams.

This is an individual contributor role reporting to the Senior Director, Global Technology Operations. You'll own delivery outcomes personally, working closely with TechOps engineers to turn technical designs into sequenced, deliverable plans. You'll need to understand the technology well enough to challenge a plan and build lightweight mechanisms that improve execution without creating process drag.

**What you'll be doing**
------------------------

### **Program Delivery**

* Own end-to-end delivery of the Technology Operations program portfolio, including device management platform migrations, global office build-outs and productivity tooling transformation.
* Run technology implementation, migration and remediation projects at scale, covering pilot groups, rollout waves, rollback criteria, cutover runbooks and early-life support.
* Partner with TechOps engineers to translate technical designs into delivery plans, maintaining accurate program documentation, decision records and delivery artefacts.
* Support technical changes with clear communications, adoption planning and support readiness.
* Drive blockers and escalations to resolution, rather than simply reporting them onward.

### **Delivery Standards and Cross-Team Alignment**

* Define delivery and reporting standards for technical projects within TechOps, aligning with Corporate Engineering and Information Security where appropriate.
* Establish and run weekly programme reviews, roadmap tracking, escalation paths and action follow-through.
* Build intake and prioritisation mechanisms that make clear what's being done now, what's deferred and what risk is being accepted.

### **Reporting and Communication**

* Maintain a single executive-ready portfolio view covering scope, milestones, blockers and risks.
* Translate technical delivery detail into clear business impact for leadership.
* Use device inventory, enrolment state, licensing and ticket data to drive delivery and adoption reporting, reducing manual status gathering.
* Distinguish real progress from activity and surface slippage before milestones are missed.

**About You**
-------------

### **Required Experience and Skills**

* 6+ years' experience in technical program management, IT program delivery, corporate or enterprise engineering, or a related discipline.
* Demonstrable delivery of large-scale endpoint, identity or collaboration platform migrations across complex or distributed environments.
* Hands-on familiarity with identity, device management, productivity and other core workplace technologies, sufficient to challenge a technical plan, not just track it.
* Strong change management and end-user communication skills, with an understanding that a technically successful migration can still fail if adoption and support aren't addressed.
* Experience defining delivery standards, reporting frameworks or operating mechanisms adopted beyond your immediate team.
* Ability to translate technical detail into clear executive-level reporting.

### **Highly Desirable**

* Experience in a fast-growing international technology, cloud, infrastructure or AI organization.
* Experience working alongside Enterprise Security and Identity teams on device posture, conditional access, MFA or local admin reduction.
* Comfort querying platform data to automate reporting rather than collecting status manually.
* Familiarity with compliance frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001 or Cyber Essentials Plus.
* Experience using AI or automation to improve program tracking, reporting or corporate engineering operations.

**What we can offer you**
-------------------------

At Nscale, you'll find a collaborative, supportive, and innovative environment where your contributions spark real impact. We're building something extraordinary, and we want you at the core.

Highly competitive US compensation package (base + bonus + equity), with performance reviews every 12 months.

Join one of the fastest-growing AI infrastructure companies — your chance to directly shape how global AI capacity is planned and deployed.

Expect a dynamic progression plan tailored to your ambitions. Grow by leading critical cross-functional initiatives and shaping capital strategy — always with our full support.

Human-First Flexibility: We treat you as humans first. Our flexible workplace trusts Nscalers to deliver, giving you the autonomy to shape your day around life's moments.

**Equal Opportunities Statement**
---------------------------------

We strongly encourage applications from people of colour, the LGBTQ+ community, people with disabilities, neurodivergent people, parents, carers, and people from lower socio-economic backgrounds.

If there's anything we can do to accommodate your specific situation, please let us know.

jobs.title: Deputy Information Technology Director
jobs.description:
Deputy Information Technology Director

Information Technology

The Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, a global network of policy research centers, is seeking a full-time Deputy Information Technology Director to serve as the deputy to the CIO and lead day-to-day IT operations and cybersecurity. The position supervises the Cybersecurity and Network Administrator, the Cloud Systems Administrator, and the Help Desk Administrator, and oversees the IT office when the CIO is unavailable.

The position oversees Carnegie's cybersecurity program, including security tools, incident response, and network infrastructure in Washington, DC and at Carnegie's five global centers. Key tools include EDR, SIEM, vulnerability management, threat exposure, email threat protection, phishing simulation, DLP, and other security and network management systems. The position works with the CIO to set security priorities, assess emerging threats, and report on security posture to management.

In partnership with the CIO, the position also helps develop multi-year IT and network plans, build business cases and budget recommendations, manage key service providers, and align technology initiatives with organizational goals. The role also contributes to business continuity and disaster recovery planning and keeps IT policies and documentation current.

The position oversees Carnegie's cloud environments and productivity suites. Knowledge of firewall configuration, PowerShell, and network architecture is highly valued; experience with enterprise AI solutions, agentic AI governance, and MCP configurations is a plus.

Candidates should have 15+ years of progressive IT leadership experience, including overseeing helpdesk operations, developing IT strategic plans, and partnering with executive leadership. Experience managing cybersecurity programs and cloud environments at scale is highly desired, as is experience at nonprofits. A bachelor's degree in a related field (or equivalent experience) is preferred; certifications such as CISSP, PMP, ITIL, or Cisco/Microsoft credentials are a plus. The ideal candidate is a strong communicator and mentor, comfortable working at both strategic and hands-on levels.

This hybrid position requires working onsite at Carnegie's Dupont Circle office in Washington, DC at least 3 days a week, with occasional off-hours onsite work, including for security incidents. Carnegie offers an outstanding work environment and generous benefits, including health insurance. The expected salary range is $150K - $170K.

Please apply via the Carnegie Endowment website by submitting a resume and cover letter.
Equal Employment Opportunity.

jobs.title: Director of Technology and AI
jobs.description:
Fireclay Tile is here to revolutionize the tile and design industry. By implementing an innovative digital platform paired with unmatched artisan-crafted products and client service, we've made it easier than ever to specify and purchase beautiful, sustainable tile sourced and handcrafted in the US. Our tireless commitment to innovation, transparency, and sustainability has not gone unrecognized. We aim to grow 25-35% annually and are the first tile company recognized as a B Corp for how we use Business as a Force for Good. With an innovative product, an ambitious team, and an inspiring mission, we're changing the way you think about tile. Come join the makers who support the dreamers!

Location: Northern California preferred

Team: Two developers, with capacity to build the team over time

Compensation: 160K-180K Base

**The Team You'll Work With**

You will report to Fireclay's VP of Technology, Dave Meagher, and partner closely with both the VP of Technology and our CEO to shape the next version of Fireclay's technology: a company that runs on AI, end to end.

You will lead a small team of developers building across Salesforce, Google Cloud, Shopify, and our Snowflake data layer. The VP of Technology owns the broader roadmap. You will own the AI rollout across every team, the hands-on engineering leadership, and the applied-AI work that turns that roadmap into durable business value.

**The Challenge**

Fireclay is AI-forward, and we want someone to own the AI rollout across the entire company, from the factory floor to marketing to sales.

We envision a near future where every knowledge worker at Fireclay uses AI all day long, as naturally as email. Production planners, customer service, sales reps, designers, marketers, and finance should each have AI woven into how they work, backed by systems they trust. Getting there is your job.

Fireclay Tile has always used technology to do things differently. We were early to the cloud, and over the last few years we have gone well past experimentation: we now run production AI skills, agents, and internal applications that our teams use every day.

We are a vertically integrated, employee-owned B Corp that makes beautiful, sustainable tile and helps clients carry a project from inspiration through installation. The work is real: complex product data, factories, supply chain, sales, design, customer service, showrooms, installation, finance, and thousands of decisions that need to happen well every day.

Owning AI here means owning more than tools. You will define and run the enterprise architecture, security, governance, and process controls that let AI scale safely across every team. That includes how models and agents access data, who can do what, how work is reviewed, how we audit and observe it, and how we decide what gets built, bought, scaled, or stopped.

This is not a role for an AI futurist who stays at 30,000 feet. You will be in the weeds: mapping work, finding constraints, building solutions, coaching teammates, and holding a high bar for security, quality, and measurable impact.

**How We Work**

We run our technology team like a software startup inside a manufacturing company. The pace is fast, the team is lean, and shipping matters more than planning decks.

In exchange, you get a lot of autonomy. You will have the room to learn the business deeply, decide where technology and AI can add value, and act on it quickly without waiting on layers of approval.

With AI, the distance between an idea and a working application is now days, not quarters. It is normal here to scope a problem with a business owner on Friday, build the application with AI over the weekend, and put it in front of real users on Monday. We want someone who finds that energizing, and who knows how to move that fast without cutting corners on security, data integrity, or review.

**Our Stack**

Claude, MCP, custom skills and agents, Google Cloud, Salesforce, Shopify Plus, Front, Dialpad, Slack, Hyros, HubSpot

**The Opportunities You'll Have**

* Own the AI rollout across every Fireclay team, from production and supply chain to customer service, marketing, sales, and finance.
* Partner with the VP of Technology and the CEO to define the next vision of Fireclay's technology, built on AI.
* Design and run the enterprise architecture for AI: how agents, skills, and applications connect to Salesforce, Google Cloud, Shopify, and Snowflake, and how data flows between them.
* Own AI security, governance, and process control: access and permissions, data privacy, human review, audit trails, observability, and clear ownership for every production workflow.
* Lead, mentor, and grow Fireclay's development team, and raise the bar for how we build.
* Learn Fireclay deeply, from customer journey and order flow through manufacturing, fulfillment, installation, and support, and find the real points of friction, delay, rework, and opportunity.
* Build and ship AI-enabled workflows and applications quickly, often in days, that improve productivity, decision quality, customer experience, revenue, or cost.
* Identify and pursue customer-facing AI opportunities that make it easier to discover, design, purchase, receive, and install Fireclay products.
* Run a disciplined intake and prioritization process. Every meaningful AI investment should have a defined problem, baseline, owner, cost, expected value, success metric, security review, and scale-or-stop decision.
* Make the right build-versus-buy decisions. Use external tools, partners, and emerging models where they create leverage, without creating a fragile or ungoverned stack.

**What Success Looks Like Early**

* First 30 days: Map Fireclay's stack across Salesforce, Google Cloud, Shopify, and Snowflake, along with current AI use, developer capacity, core data flows, security posture, and highest-friction business processes. Meet the people doing the work, including in the physical operation. Ship something small and useful.
*

**The Miami Valley School (MVS).** Our mission is to challenge young people of promise to become self-sustaining learners and compassionate global citizens. * **Develop Character and Wellness.** To support the overall wellness of our vibrant community,you’ll have the opportunity to meaningfully connect and collaborate with students and families.
* **Innovate.** As we continue to develop our Immersive Learning programming, you will be part of a team that is enhancing professional learning nationwide and becoming a thought leader for immersive learning experiences that stretch beyond the traditional school experience.
* **Couple Academic Rigor with Increased Accessibility.** Through your intentional support and empowerment, our students will explore their unique learning needs, utilize critical thinking, and begin to think about and create solutions for today’s pressing challenges.

Most importantly, they are compassionate and caring educators committed to lifelong learning.
* **And of course, you will get to make an impact!** As the Director of Technology, you will get to join young people on their journey through discovering their sense of self, building healthy relationships, and growing both personally and socially. You will have the privilege of being a supportive resource and guidepost for students, families, faculty, and staff.

**Expectations:**

* **Relational leadership:** Build trusted, collaborative partnerships across administration, faculty, staff, parents, and students with a "listen-first" philosophy.
* **Proactive communication:** Deliver clear, transparent, and timely communication tailored to diverse audiences (prospective families, faculty, tech-novices, and leadership).
* **Operational agility:** Prioritize and execute complex, multi-stakeholder initiatives independently while meeting hard deadlines.
* **Community investment:** Engage visibly in campus life beyond core technical duties (e.g., advising, attendance at major school traditions).
* **Availability mindset:** Maintain flexibility for evening/weekend critical maintenance windows or crisis response.

**Primary Responsibilities:**

* **Strategic Vision & EdTech Integration:** Partner with division heads and the leadership team to align technology roadmap with institutional strategic planning, modern pedagogy, and AI/digital literacy trends.
* **Infrastructure & Cybersecurity Oversight:** Oversee enterprise systems, network architecture, cloud services, and school-wide cybersecurity posture, student data privacy compliance, security and camera systems, and disaster recovery.
* **Faculty/Staff Capacity & Professional Learning:** Design and coordinate targeted pedagogical technology training, coaching faculty/staff to integrate digital tools meaningfully through direct, hands on instructional support.
* **Leadership & Tier-3 Support:** Guide technical operations (supported by internal staff/student tech cohorts where applicable), stepping in for high-impact tier-3 troubleshooting and user empower

Production experience with Databricks, Spark, and Delta Lake.
Strong experience with Microsoft SQL Server and SSIS.
Experience modernizing a large legacy ETL or data-processing estate.
Expertise in canonical, semantic, dimensional, operational, and analytical data modeling.
Experience supporting hybrid cloud and on-premises infrastructure.
Demonstrated success building reusable engineering frameworks.
Strong SQL and distributed-processing performance-tuning skills.
Ability to communicate architectural decisions to senior business and technology leaders.
Bachelor’s degree.

**Department Information**
--------------------------

**Together, we innovate for a stronger Colorado**

The work of employees at the Governor's Office of Information Technology (OIT) is challenging and diverse because the needs of agencies, customers and Coloradans constantly evolve. But our focus never changes: improve the lives of all Coloradans through innovation and collaboration. We're building one of the nation's leading government IT organizations by reimagining how we support agencies, building first-of-their-kind applications, and creating an inclusive, collaborative culture, together. Join us in the important work of providing equitable access to services.

  
  
Watch this video to learn more about how we're Serving People. Serving Colorado.

**Description of Job**
----------------------

**IMPORTANT NOTE:** Please review your application to ensure completion. For the most equitable applicant experience, OIT’s hiring team considers only the contents of your application to review your qualifications. Please do not include any attachments (such as resume or cover letter) with your application as these items are not used by OIT’s hiring team.

  
  

The Colorado Governor's Office of Information Technology is in the middle of a transformation worth joining. We're building cross-functional pod teams that partner directly with agencies to design, deliver, and continuously improve services that work for Coloradans. Good government depends on technology that works. And OIT exists to make that true for every Coloradan. The State of Colorado is seeking a Director, Technology to help build the next generation of public services. We're looking for people who want to do the best work of their careers in service of the public.

  
  

The Director, Technology is the Leader in OIT’s agency service model. You will determine the appropriate approach in working with OIT and Agency executives in aligning and implementing OIT and agency business needs. This position operates proactively as a strategic partner, embedding in agency planning before problems surface, rather than reactively as a service provider. You will build credibility with agency leadership quickly and maintain it through demonstrated delivery. The role oversees technology used to support all aspects of any supported agency's technology needs and collaborates with agency leadership as a strategic partner to provide in-depth technical expertise in support of business decisions.

  
  

**What you'll do...**

  
  

* Communicate and translate between technology initiatives and mission requirements with senior agency stakeholders, including Executive Director, CFO, and program leads.
* Facilitate discussions with agency stakeholders and operational staff to identify competing priorities and elicit clear decisions.
* Develop and maintain a living technology roadmap that is focused on agency priorities, which can be shifted to meet changing needs.
* Oversee advisory teams as a matrixed leader coordinating agency technology portfolios.
* Monitor vendor contract performance in terms of agreed outcomes and escalate failure to deliver on standards.
* Identify, assess, and communicate technology risk effectively to non-technical agency leaders.
* Understand and align OIT services with customer expectations to achieve high satisfaction.
* Develop outcome-based performance agreements with agency stakeholders that define success in terms of mission impact and constituent benefit, not system availability or ticket volume.
* Drive compliance with enterprise architecture standards (EA), while maintaining focus on agency missions and program needs; flag exceptions and engage OIT’s EA function.
* Implement user centricity, agile, product ownership, modular procurement, and continuous delivery at conceptual and operational levels.
* Work with cross-functional teams at agency and OIT to efficiently navigate State governance and procurement laws, considering factors such as SOO vs SOW, as well as T&M Structures.
* Develop, drive, and hold staff accountable to team expectations tied to outcomes rather than activity metrics.
* Conduct regular 1:1s and performance conversations that are developmental and coaching-oriented, which provide direct, honest feedback and accountability to team members. Build an environment where team members surface problems early rather than hiding them.
* Provide proactive intervention to mitigate issues arising from workload, skill-gaps, etc., that are not dependent upon performance review cycles.
* Conduct human resource management activities such as developing performance plans, and approving performance reviews; oversee disciplinary/corrective, and separation actions.
* Coordinate with the OIT HR team to drive recruitment and selection processes that consider user-centered outcomes, and candidate experience.

  

**What you bring...**

  
  

* Ability to speak credibly to an agency's Executive Director, CFO, and program leads, to translate between technology and mission. This includes the ability to identify, assess and communicate technology risks to non-technical audiences.
* Ability to navigate complex political dynamics, while maintaining focus on outcomes.
* Ability to influence agency program staff and political leadership through collaboration and complex relationship management.
* Ability to develop and maintain a multi-year roadmap that aligns technology investment to mission priorities
* Ability to manage budget and resources, and influence thinking in regards to technology investment.
* Ability to set individual and team performance expectations tied to outcomes, conduct developmental performance conversations, and navigate performance issues constructively across a cross-functional team of specialists.
* Ability to manage across disciplines — providing meaningful feedback and accountability to team members — without needing to be a practitioner in each craft.
* Ability to quickly understand state agency

At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems; from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business. You will work directly with Security Engineering, Identity Infrastructure, Machine Learning, and Core Platform teams to design, build, and deploy systems for authentication, access control, and anomaly detection.

Working embedded within engineering groups, you will translate identity protocols, privacy-by-design principles, and threat mitigation models into clear technical specifications, system dependencies, and actionable execution roadmaps. * Strong strategic thinking, with the ability to see the big picture, translate vision into execution, and drive alignment across senior stakeholders.
* Deep technical literacy in IAM (OAuth 2.0 / OIDC), data privacy controls, anomaly detection pipelines, abuse prevention systems and risk assessment, comfortable partnering directly with engineering leaders and architects.
* Ability to develop scalable solutions, optimize processes, and foster a “security by default” mindset across engineering and developer teams.
* Data-driven approach: skilled at defining effective metrics, surfacing insights, and using results to shape strategy and demonstrate impact.
