jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager, Annapurna Labs
jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------


Annapurna Labs designs the custom silicon that powers AWS's machine learning infrastructure, including the Trainium and Inferentia chip families. Our next\-generation ML accelerator is a multi\-die chiplet using state\-of\-the\-art packaging technology, and it is the most complex hardware program Amazon has undertaken. We are looking for a Principal Technical Program Manager to own end\-to\-end program execution for this chip, from RTL freeze through tape\-out and into production readiness.  

  

This is not a status\-reporting role. You will be the person who connects a sprawling set of engineering workstreams into a single coherent schedule, identifies the real critical path week to week, and drives the cross\-functional decisions that keep the program on track. The program spans multiple concurrent silicon development efforts with significant interdependencies across engineering disciplines, external partners, and infrastructure.  

  

Key job responsibilities  

Own the integrated schedule and critical path analysis across multiple die tape\-outs through engineering samples and production ramp. Understand dependency chains deeply enough to calculate the impact of any slip or pull\-in, and update the timeline weekly with real data.  

Drive the weekly chip status cadence by synthesizing inputs from RTL/DV, physical design, packaging, power, infrastructure, and post\-silicon teams into a single view that tells leadership where we actually stand, including what is getting worse and what needs action.  

Track verification convergence as a leading indicator by monitoring the progression from feature completion through RTL closure, bug trends, and regression pass rates by block. Recognize when convergence is stalling and drive the engineering response before downstream milestones are affected.  

Manage the external design partner interface, owning the netlist delivery calendar, tracking your partner's physical design timeline, and negotiating schedule trades with a clear understanding of downstream cost.  

Drive infrastructure readiness and external IP delivery by partnering with compute and EDA platform teams on capacity planning, and tracking third\-party PHY, memory interface, and controller IP deliveries against consuming blocks to escalate gaps before they become tape\-out critical.  

  

A day in the life  

You start your morning reviewing verification convergence dashboards and regression results, spotting a block where bug closure rates haven't flattened. You pull the DV lead and RTL owner into a quick sync to agree on a recovery plan before the weekly chip status review. In that review, you walk leadership through an updated critical path that reflects a netlist delivery shift from your external design partner, quantifying the downstream impact on tape\-out timing. After lunch, you join an infrastructure capacity review to confirm that compute clusters can handle the regression load through freeze, then close out the day preparing an executive summary for an upcoming program milestone review.  

  

About the team  

The Annapurna Labs ML Accelerator team builds the Trainium and Inferentia silicon that trains and serves machine learning models across AWS. We work at the intersection of chip architecture, physical design, verification, and infrastructure to deliver products that push the boundaries of performance and efficiency for our customers. Our team values people who bring strong technical judgment, clear communication, and a willingness to get into the details. If you want to shape how Amazon builds its most ambitious hardware and work alongside talented engineers solving real problems at scale, this is the role for you.

**BASIC QUALIFICATIONS**
------------------------

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field
* 10\+ years of hands\-on work managing complex technology projects experience
* 10\+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
* Deep working knowledge of the chip development lifecycle: RTL verification milestones, physical design convergence, DFT, and timing closure.
* Experience managing programs with external design partners and IP vendors where you don't control the resources but own the outcome.
* Demonstrated ability to build and maintain integrated schedules with real dependency modeling — not just Gantt charts, but an understanding of which paths have float and which don't.
* Strong technical communication skills: ability to present crisp status to VP\-level audiences, distinguishing signal from noise, and framing decisions clearly.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**
----------------------------

* Experience with multi\-die / chiplet / advanced packaging programs (2\.5D/3D integration).
* Familiarity with HBM integration, die\-to\-die interfaces, or high\-speed serial subsystems.
* Experience with leading\-edge foundry nodes and their specific flow and schedule characteristics.
* Background in ML accelerator or high\-performance compute silicon.
* Experience driving infrastructure capacity planning for large\-scale chip development programs.

  

Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Program Manager, NuRoots Community
jobs.description:
**POSITION:** Program Manager, NuRoots Community  

**EXEMPT / UNION GRADE 14**  

**DEPARTMENT:** Ensuring the Jewish Future  

**SALARY:** Union Grade 14 Range: $77,029 \- $103,797 **Budgeted Salary**: $77,029


**TIME LIMITED:** DECEMBER 31, 2027 (EXTENSION DEPENDENT ON GRANT FUNDING)


**SUMMARY DESCRIPTION OF TEAM:**  

As an integral part of Federation’s Ensuring the Jewish Future Strategic Initiative, The Young Adult Engagement (YAE) Department is responsible for helping Jewish young adults (18\-40ish) feel a sense of connection and belonging by living a Jewish life that is joyful, meaningful, and relevant to their lives.  

NuRoots serves as Federation’s young adult community building initiative with the aim to inspires and mobilizes young adults to create meaningful connection to Jewish community across Los Angeles. When every young Jewish Angeleno feels connected to their identity and their community, we will have a thriving, resilient, and interconnected Jewish LA. Our values serve as the road map for how we operate in and with our community:  

Our values serve as the road map for how we operate in and with our community:  

* Modern Interpretation: There are endless possibilities to connect with what it means to be Jewish.
* Hyper\-Local Roots: Be in constant conversation with the diversity of people, places and stories across Los Angeles.
* Warm Invitation: Meaningful community develops through personal relationship, intimate moments, and purposeful inclusivity.
* Creative Integrity: Reimagination of Jewish ideas requires interrogation of our diverse past and ancient traditions.
* Communal Table: Collaboration builds trust which leads to the greatest community impact.

**SUMMARY DESCRIPTION OF POSITION:**  

Reporting to the Vice President of Young Adults, the Program Manager, NuRoots Community works with Jews in their 20s \& 30s to reinvent and reimagine what it means to be Jewish.  

Who you are: A Program Manager, NuRoots Community is a dynamic and engaging position for an energetic, personable, and well\-rounded person with a keen interest in community building. Serving various “micro\-communities,” NuRoots’ Program Managers, NuRoots Community (warmly referred to in the field as “Creators”), are passionate about building Jewish community and galvanizing the 20s and 30s in L.A. to “do Jewish” in a way that’s meaningful, relevant, and creates longevity. We hope you approach our impact work in the following ways:  

* Depth \& Breadth: You are social, enjoy deep conversation, don’t care much for small talk, and are equally comfortable putting together an intimate gathering for 10\-20 peers as they are contributing to a large\-scale\-150\+\-person experience.

jobs.title: Director, IT PMO
jobs.description:
The Company:

Czarnowski Collective is a leading experiential marketing and brand activation company, designing and delivering trade show exhibits, environments, and events for enterprise clients. It's been over 75 years since we opened our doors, but we're still not resting on our reputation or accolades. We're wondering "what if…" — anticipating what's next and building the systems and data platforms that power a business built on forward-thinking work for forward-thinking brands.

Joining the Czarnowski Collective means the opportunity to be more than a number, more than a job title, more than a spectator. We are a collective of dreamers and thinkers, doers, and makers…and we're searching for more of the same to join the ranks.

The Purpose:

We are looking for a Director, IT PMO to join our team in Atlanta! In this role, you'll run governance, budget, vendor, and contract management for Czarnowski Collective's IT project portfolio, chairing the IT Steering Committee and driving executive alignment on priorities and risk across our Microsoft estate — including Dynamics 365 F&O, D365 Sales, Project Operations, and our Power BI/Fabric analytics environment.

This is a hands-on leadership role: rather than delegating our most complex or highest-risk projects, you'll personally lead them while overseeing the broader portfolio through your PMO team. You'll partner closely with the CIO on ERP and digital transformation initiatives, own capex/opex budgeting and forecasting, and be the person who keeps vendors, contracts, and cross-functional stakeholders aligned when priorities and trade-offs get complicated.

You'll build and lead a project management team, set the delivery standards they're held to, and drive the governance and methodology (hybrid agile/waterfall) that keeps ERP, data, and infrastructure projects moving. If you've established a PMO from the ground up or thrive translating technical initiatives into business impact for executive audiences, this role gives you the room to do both.

The Job:

Governance & Executive Alignment

Design and run IT governance, including chairing the IT Steering Committee and defining intake, prioritization, and stage-gating.
Drive executive and cross-functional stakeholder alignment on priorities, investment trade-offs, and risk.
Report portfolio and project status to executive leadership, covering risk, budget, schedule, and resourcing.

Portfolio & Project Delivery

Personally lead the most complex, high-risk, or high-visibility IT projects, while overseeing the broader portfolio through the PMO team.
Oversee delivery across the Microsoft estate (D365 F&O, D365 Sales, Project Operations, Power BI/Fabric), coordinating internal teams and implementation partners.
Define and enforce a consistent delivery methodology (hybrid agile/waterfall) across ERP, data, and infrastructure projects.
Own portfolio resource capacity planning, surfacing constraints and trade-offs.
Lead change management for IT-driven initiatives to ensure business adoption.
Drive post-implementation reviews to continuously improve delivery maturity.

Budget, Vendor & Contract Management

Own IT capex/opex budgeting, forecasting, variance management, and financial reporting to the CIO and finance.
Own vendor management: selection, performance, relationship governance, and issue escalation.
Own contract management: negotiating and administering SOWs and commercial terms through full lifecycle.

Team Leadership

Lead, mentor, and develop the project management team; set delivery standards and hold the team accountable.

The Person:

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
10+ years in IT project/program management, including 3+ years leading a PMO function.
Hands-on track record personally running complex, high-stakes projects, not just managing through a team.
Experience managing ERP implementations/upgrades (Microsoft Dynamics 365 or comparable strongly preferred).
Direct ownership of IT capex/opex budgets, forecasting, and financial reporting to leadership.
Experience designing and running IT governance structures, including an IT Steering Committee.
Proven executive stakeholder alignment on priorities, investment, and risk trade-offs.
Strong vendor management: selection, performance, and relationship governance.
Contract management experience: negotiating and administering SOWs and commercial terms.
Solid grounding in Agile, Waterfall, and hybrid project/portfolio management methodologies.
Proven people leadership: building, coaching, and developing a project management team.
Excellent executive communication skills, translating technical initiatives into business impact.
Experience leading change management for enterprise system or process rollouts.
Preferred: PMP, PgMP, or equivalent certification; experience in manufacturing, exhibit house, events, or professional services; familiarity with Power BI/Fabric; experience establishing a PMO from an early stage of maturity.

Please note that we are not partnering with third-party recruiting agencies for this position. Additionally, visa sponsorship is not available now or in the future for this role.

This position is eligible for health care benefits, life insurance, time off benefits and participation in the Company's 401(k) plan.

What we offer:

Medical, Dental, and Vision benefits effective within 30 days (or less) of your start date
401K matching with no vesting period (you are fully vested as of day 1)
Generous Paid Time Off (PTO)
Paid Holidays
Collaborative Work Environment

Collective Culture Core Values:

We recognize that the success of our business rests with the skills and efforts of our people, and in return for their contributions, our employees can expect a flexible work environment that delivers on the 10 principles that define our company culture:

We celebrate creativity, curiosity, innovation and imagination.
We are humble and respectful.
We act with honesty and integrity.
We empower and trust one another.
We embrace individuality and an entrepreneurial spirit.
We champion initiatives that bolster diversity, equity and inclusion.
We prioritize safe, ethical and sustainable business practices.
We foster a culture of meritocracy - rewarding skills and abilities, instead of influence.
We always deliver.
We don't take ourselves too seriously.

Through several existing and future initiatives, Czarnowski Collective is exploring thoughtful and creative ways to embrace individuality, and more effectively champion diversity, equity and inclusion across our network.

EEO Statement

Czarnowski Collective is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We don't just accept difference — we honor, nurture, and celebrate it! All aspects of employment including the decision to hire, promote, discipline, or discharge, will be based on merit, competence, performance, and business needs. We don't discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex/gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

jobs.title: Director of Technology & Chief Architect
jobs.description:
The role

High 5 Games is hiring a Director of Technology who is first and foremost a hands-on chief architect. You will shape the technical vision and grow into owning the architecture of a cloud platform built on hundreds of Java microservices that process millions of real-time transactions every day.

You will join a mature, high-volume platform that is already running in production. You'll spend your first 90 days learning it deeply, embedded with the teams that built it, and take ownership of its architecture domain by domain: starting with the data and transaction layer, then service architecture and the cloud platform. By the end of your first year, you'll own the platform's architecture end to end and set its direction for the years ahead.

This is not a slide-deck architect role. You will design systems, review code and schemas, set engineering standards, and lead the engineering and technology teams that build and run the platform. You must be comfortable explaining technology strategy and trade-offs to executives, business partners, and regulators.

The platform you will own

Hundreds of microservices, primarily Java, running in the cloud.
Millions of real-time transactions per day, where latency, consistency, and auditability matter on every one.
Regulated, money-adjacent workloads for social and sweepstakes casino gaming: wallets, purchases, game outcomes, and promotions.
24x7 availability for players across web and mobile.

Responsibilities

Architecture and system design

Take ownership of the microservices platform's architecture, domain by domain, through the first year, and then own it end to end: service boundaries, APIs, data ownership, and inter-service communication.
Design for high-volume, low-latency, real-time transaction processing with strong consistency and idempotency guarantees.
Define patterns for distributed transactions (sagas, outbox, event sourcing where appropriate), retries, and failure recovery.
Lead architecture reviews and keep a living record of decisions (ADRs) across hundreds of services.
Identify and pay down architectural debt; plan the evolution of legacy services without disrupting live traffic.

Java and data platforms

Set Java engineering standards: frameworks, libraries, build tooling, coding practices, and JVM tuning.
Own the database strategy across relational, NoSQL, caching, and streaming platforms, including schema design, partitioning, replication, and capacity.
Diagnose and resolve performance bottlenecks across the JVM, the network, and the data layer.

Cloud, reliability, and operations

Guide the cloud architecture: containers, Kubernetes, managed data services, networking, and infrastructure as code.
Set SLOs, observability standards (metrics, tracing, logging), and incident response practices.
Drive scalability, resilience, disaster recovery, and cloud cost efficiency.
Ensure security, data protection, and auditability meet gaming regulatory and payment requirements.

Leadership

Build, lead, and mentor the engineering and technology teams; raise the bar on hiring.
Translate business goals into a technology roadmap and project plans.
Manage technical vendors and third-party platforms.
Evaluate new technology and tools and bring in what moves the platform forward.
Communicate technology strategy and risk clearly to the CEO, executives, and partners.

Required Qualifications

12+ years in software engineering, including 5+ years as an architect of large distributed systems.
Expert-level Java (Java 17+), with deep knowledge of Spring Boot / Spring Cloud, concurrency, and JVM performance tuning and garbage collection.
Proven track record designing and operating a microservices estate of 100+ services in production.
Hands-on experience with systems handling millions of real-time transactions per day, with measurable latency and uptime targets.
Deep database expertise: relational (PostgreSQL, MySQL, or Oracle) including query tuning, indexing, sharding, and replication, plus NoSQL and caching (e.g., Cassandra, MongoDB, DynamoDB, Redis).
Event-driven architecture with Kafka or a comparable streaming platform.
Production experience on AWS or GCP, with Docker, Kubernetes, and infrastructure as code (Terraform or similar).
Strong grasp of distributed-systems fundamentals: consistency models, idempotency, partitioning, backpressure, and failure modes.
Experience with API design (REST, gRPC), API gateways, and service mesh concepts.
Observability and reliability practice: Prometheus/Grafana, OpenTelemetry, Datadog or similar; SLOs and incident management.
Experience leading and growing engineering teams, and evaluating and interviewing technical candidates.
Clear communicator with executives, peers, and individual contributors.

Preferred Qualifications

Background in gaming, iGaming, sweepstakes/social casino, sports betting, fintech, or payments.
Experience with wallet, ledger, or payment systems where every transaction must reconcile.
Familiarity with gaming regulatory, PCI DSS, or SOC 2 compliance requirements.
Led a migration or re-platforming of a monolith or legacy services to microservices with no downtime.
Experience with reactive or non-blocking Java (WebFlux, Vert.x, Netty) for high-throughput services.
Cloud cost optimization (FinOps) at scale.
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent experience.

Compensation And Benefits

The base salary range for this role is [TBD- Negotiable] per year, based on experience and skills.

Benefits include medical, dental and vision coverage; 401(k) and any match; paid time off and holidays; other programs

About High 5 Games

High 5 Games is a leader in casino gaming entertainment, developing for land-based, online, mobile, and social markets. We have created hundreds of games played in 150 countries on six continents, and we are building the most entertaining social casino experience on web and mobile.

Our team includes mathematicians, software engineers, game designers, data scientists, and artists. It is a dynamic, multidisciplinary, high-learning environment. See us at high5games.com.

To apply

Apply through our careers page with your resume and a short description of relevant experience. Links to GitHub projects, architecture write-ups, or talks are welcome.

High 5 Games is an equal opportunity employer. As a US employer, we verify that all employees, regardless of citizenship or national origin, are eligible to work in the United States. Principals only; recruiters, please don't contact us.

jobs.title: Internal Audit Executive Director – Global Audit Lead, Cybersecurity, Information Security & Cyber Resilience
jobs.description:
The cyber risk landscape is changing rapidly, and the Firm requires audit leadership equipped to meet the moment. We are seeking an Executive Director to lead internal audit technology coverage across the global Firm and its banking entities, including Morgan Stanley Bank, N.A. (MSBNA) and Morgan Stanley Private Bank, N.A. (MSPBNA). This role demands a forward-looking leader who can address both today's threats and the emerging risks now reshaping cybersecurity, information security, and cyber resilience — with deep cyber risk expertise and a strong understanding of how artificial intelligence, agentic and frontier AI models, cloud transformation, and digital assets are actively changing the risk landscape and regulatory expectations. The successful candidate will translate these developments into practical, risk-based audit strategies, deliver insightful challenge to management, and evolve the Firm's assurance approach to address current and emerging threats.

The Internal Audit Division (IAD) drives attention and resources to vulnerabilities by providing an independent and well-informed view and impactful messages about the most important risks facing our Firm. This is accomplished by performing a range of assurance activities to independently assess the quality and effectiveness of Morgan Stanley’s system of internal control, including risk management and governance systems and processes. IAD serves as an objective and independent function within the Firm’s risk management framework to foster continual improvement of risk management processes. This is an Executive Director (P6) level position within the Technical Specialist function, which is responsible for providing extensive subject matter expertise and reinforcing the ability of business and technology audit teams to appropriately assess risk and determine and execute coverage.

Since 1935, Morgan Stanley is known as a global leader in financial services, always evolving and innovating to better serve our clients and our communities in more than 40 countries around the world.

What You’ll Do In The Role

Prioritize and lead coverage of emerging risks related to artificial intelligence and frontier models — including generative and agentic AI — assessing build time, run time, and life cycle controls, data protection, identity and entitlements for autonomous agents, and the expanded attack surface these capabilities create, as well as adversaries’ growing use of AI to accelerate and scale attacks.
Provide coverage of the idiosyncratic risks arising from cryptocurrency and digital assets, including digital asset custody, private key generation and lifecycle management, and the security of both online (network-connected) and offline (air-gapped) custody infrastructure — highlighting the associated cyber threats such as private key compromise, transaction and address manipulation, smart contract exploitation, and the irreversible loss of assets.
Assess quantum computing and post-quantum cryptography readiness, and other frontier technology risks, ensuring these are reflected in the audit plan and in the Firm’s forward-looking resilience posture.
Monitor the intensifying threat landscape — including advanced attack techniques and regulatory change — and continuously factor emerging threats into audit scoping and assurance coverage.
Provide independent assurance over the design and operating effectiveness of the controls that protect the Firm’s and Banks’ technology environment, customer data, and critical business services
Set and lead the multi-year, risk-based audit strategy for cybersecurity, information security, and cyber resilience across the Firm and its Banks, spanning the full technology stack (infrastructure, network, platform, application, and data layers) and each business unit to form an integrated, Firm-wide view of control effectiveness, and how cyber threats, information loss, and a cyber attach could affect business lines, critical services, and legal entities across the Firm.
Direct execution of the audit plan across the core cyber and information security domains — identity and access management, endpoint security, network security, data protection, threat detection and response, and vulnerability management.
Lead assurance activities assessing cyber resilience capabilities, including incident response, disaster recovery, business continuity, and third-party/vendor security.
Evaluate compliance with regulatory expectations (e.g., FFIEC, OCC, FDIC, NYDFS, GLBA, RGF, DORA) and industry frameworks (CRI Profile, NIST CSF, ISO 27001).
Oversee root cause analysis on control failures and audit findings, and track remediation to closure.
Comprehensively articulate actionable insights regarding the criticality and impact of cyber risk, and how well it is managed, to senior management and regulators. Prepare materials for the Chief Audit Executive’s updates to the Audit Committee and the Board,
Coordinate with second-line risk and compliance functions and with external auditors and regulators, and collaborate with global peers to identify risk themes and implications across business segments and legal entities.
Mentor and develop audit staff and manage a global team; help inform and address talent needs and identify stretch and development opportunities for team members.

What You’ll Bring To The Role

Advanced understanding of cybersecurity, information security, and cyber resilience risks and the relevant regulations, including banking regulatory requirements.
Experience assessing emerging technology risks and their control implications — including AI and agentic AI, frontier models, cryptocurrency and digital asset custody, and quantum/post-quantum cryptography — and the ability to translate a rapidly changing threat landscape into practical audit coverage.
Strong knowledge of cybersecurity frameworks (NIST CSF, ISO 27001, CRI Profile) and experience auditing identity and access management, cloud security, and network architecture.
Expertise in audit principles, methodology, tools, and processes (e.g., risk assessments, planning, testing, reporting, and continuous monitoring).
Ability to analyze data and prioritize coverage and assurance activities based on the criticality of risk.
Ability to articulate risk and impact clearly and succinctly to different audiences, including senior stakeholders, the Board, and regulators.
Ability to inspire and support others to do their best work through active coaching, feedback, and development opportunities, and by ensuring trust and inclusion among team members.
Experience in overseeing resource utilization and monitoring progress against deliverables.
A bachelor’s degree in Information Security, Computer Science, or a related field.
At least 12-15 years’ relevant experience in IT/cyber audit, information security, or risk management — ideally in banking or financial services — would generally be expected to fulfill the skills required for this role.
Relevant certifications (e.g., CISA, CISSP, CISM, or equivalent) preferred.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with incident response or red team/penetration testing programs.
Familiarity with the MITRE ATT&CK framework.
Prior experience at a large financial institution or a Big 4 consulting firm.

We are committed to maintaining the first-class service and high standard of excellence that have defined Morgan Stanley for over 89 years. Our values — putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back — aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what’s best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. We are constantly looking to add to our core talent. If you are seeking a career that is challenging and rewarding, a work environment that is diverse and dynamic, look no further — Haemonetics is your employer of choice.

Job Details

The Director of Commercial Technology Strategy and Deployment serves as the critical bridge between the commercial business and the technology teams that support it. This leader sits at the intersection of sales strategy and platform execution — fluent in the language of both revenue operations and enterprise technology, and trusted by both sides to translate needs, drive alignment, and deliver solutions that move the business forward. This role leads the strategy for the commercial technology ecosystem across the organization — Salesforce CRM, BI & Analytics, and supporting tools — with a mandate to build a scalable, well-governed foundation that enables sales teams to operate at their best.

Key Responsibilities

Business Process Optimization

Assess existing commercial processes across operating units to identify gaps, redundancies, and opportunities for standardization
Establish new or improved workflows that can be effectively operationalized within Salesforce and downstream reporting environments
Ensure that platform capabilities are matched to how the business actually works — and that the business is equipped to take full advantage of what the platform can do
Partner with commercial stakeholders to document, validate, and continuously improve the processes that underpin pipeline management, account planning, forecasting, and performance tracking
Serve as the process authority that grounds technology decisions in operational reality rather than technical preference

Platform Ownership & Strategy

Own the commercial technology roadmap for Salesforce(CRM), Tableau(BI & Analytics), and the broader commercial tool stack across all operating units
Define business requirements and functional priorities that IT translates into platform design, configuration, and development
Balance near-term business needs with long-term platform scalability, ensuring foundational decisions support future growth
Evaluate and rationalize the tool portfolio, eliminating redundancy and ensuring each investment is tied to measurable business outcomes
Manage vendor relationships with accountability for value delivered, not just contract compliance

Salesforce CRM

Own the functional vision for Salesforce as the system of record for all commercial activity — defining how the platform should reflect the business goals around driving growth, creating consistency and scalability in operational processes and improving how performance is tracked
Translate commercial requirements into clear, actionable specifications that IT and platform teams execute against
Champion the sales rep and sales leader experience — ensuring the platform reduces friction, surfaces relevant information, and supports the full commercial motion to drive market visibility, sales growth and service penetration.
Own broader commercial data quality as critical business assets, partnering with IT to enforce governance standards that protect data reliability and drive informed decision-making
Enhance sales experience through meaningful integrations of tools across the commercial technology stack, creating a more seamless sales process, optimizing utilization of resources available to the sales team, and improving sales effectiveness in the field.

Data Integrity & Governance

Own the strategy and execution of commercial data governance, ensuring that core datasets — particularly installed base, account, contact, party relationship and pipeline data — are accurate, complete, and trusted across the organization
Establish and enforce data standards, definitions, and governance processes that ensure consistency of commercial data across Salesforce, ERP systems, and downstream reporting environments
Partner with Sales, Service, Finance, and IT to define clear ownership and accountability for data quality, including stewardship models, validation rules, and ongoing monitoring mechanisms
Drive continuous improvement of data accuracy to support critical business outcomes, including account planning, whitespace identification, service penetration strategies, and lifecycle asset management
Implement processes and controls to proactively identify and remediate data gaps, duplication, and misalignment across systems, ensuring data integrity is not reactive but systematically managed
Ensure that installed base and asset data structures are designed to support scalable reporting, segmentation, and advanced analytics — enabling more precise sales strategies and territory planning
Champion a culture of data accountability within the commercial organization, reinforcing that high-quality data is a foundational asset for driving growth, productivity, and customer insight

BI & Analytics

Define the KPI framework and reporting requirements that matter to the commercial organization, ensuring metrics are consistent, trusted, and accessible at the right levels
Partner with IT and data teams to ensure commercial reporting needs are clearly understood and reliably delivered
Enable executive dashboards and visibility into business performance across operating units, establishing key performance indicators aimed to measure and enhance sales productivity.
Drive a shift toward proactive, insight-driven decision making by ensuring the right information reaches the right people

Team & Stakeholder Leadership

Manage team resources to support commercial technology initiatives and business priorities
Operate as a trusted strategic partner to sales leadership, operating unit heads, and IT — credible on both the business and technology sides of the organization
Partner with cross functional leaders across Finance, Sales Operations, Sales, Marketing and IT to ensure alignment and collaborative execution of strategic roadmap.
Communicate platform strategy, roadmap progress, and tradeoffs clearly to executive stakeholders, translating technical complexity into business impact

Qualifications

12+ years in commercial operations, sales operations, or revenue operations with demonstrated accountability for business outcomes
Strong working knowledge of Salesforce as a commercial platform — including how it supports pipeline management, forecasting, account management, and sales performance — with the ability to define requirements and evaluate solutions
Proven ability to assess, document, and improve commercial business processes with a view toward scalable operationalization
Track record of delivering in a multi-segment or multi-business-unit environment with complex stakeholder dynamics
Strong analytical mindset with the ability to define, measure, and communicate commercial KPIs
Ability to operate fluidly between business and technology stakeholders — equally comfortable in a sales strategy conversation and a platform requirements discussion

Preferred

Familiarity with BI and analytics platforms used in commercial settings (CRMA/Tableau CRM, Tableau, Power BI, Looker, or similar) at a functional, business-user level
Experience working in a matrixed environment where business and IT teams share accountability for platform outcomes
Background supporting organizations with differentiated go-to-market models across business units
Experience in a growth or transformation environment where commercial operations infrastructure was established from the ground up
Salesforce certification a plus, not a requirement

Pay Transparency

The pay range for this role is:

$149,200.00-$254,000.00/Annual

***Join Hilo Benioff Medical Center and be part of a team that proudly cares for our friends, family, and neighbors across East Hawaiʻi.***

Hilo Benioff Medical Center is seeking an experienced Regional Director of ITl Services to lead and oversee technology operations across the East Hawaii Region. This is a fully on\-site position based in Hilo, Hawaii, responsible for ensuring reliable, secure, and high\-performing information technology (IT) services that support clinical care, patient safety, and business operations. This position reports to the Regional Chief Information Officer and supports regional facilities including Ka’u Hospital, Honoka’a Hospital, East Hawaii Health Clinics and Yukio Okutsu State Veterans Home, playing a critical role in advancing technology capabilities that directly impact patient care and operational excellence.


The IT Director will also drive strategic initiatives, including infrastructure modernization, cybersecurity, and service excellence in a complex healthcare environment.


The East Hawaii Region recently transitioned to Epic as the organization’s electronic health record (EHR) system. This position works in collaboration with the EHR Director who owns Epic application strategy, build, optimization, training, and application support. The IT Director owns the technical platform and operational services that Epic depends on in addition to the technology services required for the facilities.

Prior leadership experience should be at the Director or Executive level, or equivalent.

You might think printing is a business of the past \- but let us help you understand why it is a platform for the future. We dominate our market segment and are highly profitable, enabling us to focus on growing our business in new and unique ways.


At TPI, printing is the visible output of a business powered by data, technology, and people. We have built a strong position serving the casino industry through data\-driven marketing and variable\-data production. Our next chapter is about building on that success: modernizing our technology infrastructure, applying AI and automation in meaningful ways, and expanding what we can accomplish for our customers.


We are looking for a VP of Technology who wants to help lead that next chapter**.**


This is an opportunity to do more than manage an IT department. You will shape our technology direction, develop our people, challenge how work gets done, and turn good ideas into measurable business improvements. You will have a seat at the leadership table, direct access to the CEO, and the opportunity to help determine where the business goes next.


TPI is also an employee\-owned company through an **Employee** **Stock** **Ownership** **Plan** **(ESOP)**. That gives this work added meaning: the improvements you lead can strengthen the business and help build long\-term value for the employees who own it. You will be leading technology in a company where the people doing the work have a stake in its success.

jobs.description:
**Role Overview**


The PMO Program Manager is accountable for the governance, portfolio management, and execution discipline that turns nine independent Advanced Manufacturing and Digital Transformation SME roadmaps into a single, governed, fundable, trackable portfolio. This is a foundational, Year 1 role: it must be stood up early, alongside the SMEs themselves, so that the standards, technology roadmaps, and capital requests coming out of Joining \& Surface Finishing, Functional Test, Manufacturing Quality, Material Flow, Automation \& Robotics, Maintenance \& Reliability, Manufacturing Systems/ERP, Digital Twin, and Industrial IoT are prioritized, funded, and executed against one common framework rather than nine separate ones. The role owns the operating model, prioritization framework, consolidated capital plan, and execution tracking across every factory in the network — Stiva 1, 2, 3, and 5, Durango, and Cienega — and reports directly to the VP of Advanced Manufacturing. This is explicitly not a desk\-bound or office\-based role: it is run through modern, purpose\-built digital program\-management tools — live visual dashboards, digital action\-plan and governance platforms, AI\-assisted meeting capture — rather than static spreadsheets, and it is led from the factory floor and the finance conference room in equal measure, not from behind a screen. The PMO Program Manager must be equally fluent partnering with finance on capital business cases and ROI, and with factory personnel — schedulers, engineers, operators, and plant leadership — at Gemba, seeing firsthand how initiatives are actually landing. Success requires the credibility to act as a leader of leaders: holding nine technical SMEs and plant leadership accountable to a common governance model without owning any of their technical domains directly; the financial and program\-management rigor to consolidate capital decisions across a multi\-site, multi\-country network; and an intense, urgent, hands\-on, highly organized approach that converts the roadmap into funded, executing, benefit\-delivering initiatives rather than a well\-organized backlog.

 **Key Accountabilities**

**A) Governance \& Operating Model**


Establish and maintain the portfolio governance charter that defines decision rights across SMEs, plant leadership, and finance — what can be approved locally versus what requires steering committee sign\-off. Own the RACI across the SME network, plants, and finance, and run the recurring steering committee cadence with the VP of Advanced Manufacturing and plant leadership so the portfolio gets discussed and decided, not just reported.

**B) Portfolio \& Prioritization**


Own and continuously maintain the master technology and capital roadmap, consolidating the initiatives coming out of all nine SMEs into one sequenced view by factory and by year. Establish and apply a standard prioritization framework — SQDIP impact, investment tier, and speed\-to\-value — so initiatives across every SME and factory are compared on the same basis. Own the stage\-gate process (Identify Pilot Business Case Deploy Scale Sustain) that operationalizes the organization's experiment\-deploy\-scale philosophy and keeps initiatives from stalling indefinitely at any one gate.

**C) Financial \& Capital Management**


Consolidate the capital plan across all factories and SMEs — committed versus available capital, by site and by year — and partner directly with finance to keep it current. Own the business case template and ROI standard used by every SME so capital requests are comparable and auditable. Track benefits realization after deployment, closing the loop on whether a funded initiative actually delivered the safety, quality, delivery, inventory, or productivity improvement it was funded to deliver.

**D) Execution \& Delivery Tracking**


Maintain the portfolio through modern, purpose\-built digital program and project management tools — live visual dashboards, digital action\-plan and governance platforms, and AI\-assisted meeting\-minutes and action\-item capture — covering status, spend, schedule, and risk across every active initiative, SME, and factory. Manual spreadsheets are not an acceptable substitute for this: decisions, action items, and status must be current, visible, and easy to update in real time, not buried in a static file that goes stale between updates. Own the RAID log and the escalation path for risks and issues, with particular attention to anything on the critical path of a capital\-speed priority. Manage resource and capacity planning across the SME and plant engineering network so competing initiatives don't silently collide over the same scarce plant teams in the same quarter.

**E) Standards, Knowledge \& Change Management**


Build and maintain the template and tools library — charter, business case, stage\-gate checklist, status reporting, lessons\-learned — used consistently across all nine SMEs, delivered through the same modern digital platforms rather than emailed spreadsheets. Stand up and run the center\-of\-excellence/lessons\-learned repository so a solution piloted at one factory doesn't get silently re\-invented at another. Track not just whether a global standard was published, but whether it was actually adopted at each factory.

**F) Hands\-On Gemba Leadership \& Results Delivery**


This is not a desk position. Spend the majority of working time directly at the factory sites and with the SMEs — not in a home office building reports — to see firsthand whether governance is translating into real execution. Be equally fluent and comfortable in two very different rooms: the finance conversation, where capital business cases, ROI, and budget trade\-offs have to be made credibly and precisely; and the factory floor, where schedulers, engineers, operators, and plant leadership have to trust that this role understands their reality, not just their status reports. jobs.title: CTO & Co-founder for Quantum computing company
jobs.description:
About QuLattice

QuLattice is building foundational software and architectural tools to accelerate practical quantum computing. Focused at the intersection of quantum error correction (QEC), lattice surgery, fault\-tolerant compiler design, and hardware\-software co\-design, QuLattice enables the transition from noisy intermediate\-scale quantum devices to scalable, fault\-tolerant quantum systems.

As an early\-stage co\-founder, you will partner directly with the founding team to establish the core technical vision, architect our core IP, recruit elite technical talent, and build the software stack powering the next generation of quantum computing infrastructure.

The Role

As **CTO \& Co\-Founder**, you will own QuLattice’s technical strategy, architecture, and engineering execution. You will bridge advanced quantum theoretical frameworks (topological codes, stabilizer formalism, syndrome decoding) with high\-performance software engineering (C\+\+, Rust, distributed systems).

Beyond writing code and designing algorithms, you will be a strategic partner in company building—pitching to deep\-tech venture capitalists, shaping commercial product roadmaps, and representing QuLattice in the scientific and industrial quantum ecosystem.

Core Responsibilities1\. Technical Vision \& Product Architecture

* Architect and lead the development of QuLattice’s core software stack, including fault\-tolerant quantum compilers, real\-time syndrome decoders, and lattice\-surgery simulation engines.
* Translate theoretical breakthroughs in quantum error correction and topological quantum codes into robust, performant, and production\-ready software tools.
* Define technical standards, CI/CD pipelines, benchmarking suites, and software architecture to support fast iteration.

2\. Team Building \& Technical Leadership

* Build, mentor, and lead an exceptional engineering team spanning quantum information scientists, compiler engineers, and high\-performance computing (HPC) developers.
* Foster a rigorous, collaborative, and mission\-driven engineering culture focused on scientific precision and rapid prototyping.

3\. Strategic Execution \& Fundraising

* Partner with co\-founders on company strategy, milestone planning, and resource allocation.
* Co\-lead technical due diligence and pitches for venture capital, strategic grants, and non\-dilutive deep\-tech funding (e.g., NSF, DARPA, DOE).
* Establish technical relationships with quantum hardware providers, research institutions, and national quantum initiatives.

4\. Ecosystem \& Thought Leadership

* Serve as a public technical voice for QuLattice at top\-tier industry conferences (e.g., QCE, APS March Meeting, IEEE Quantum Week).
* Oversee patent filings, IP strategy, and selected scientific publications in relevant peer\-reviewed venues.

Minimum Requirements

* **Education:** Ph.D. in Quantum Information Science, Physics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related quantitative field.
* **Postdoctoral Experience:** At least 1 year of postdoctoral research experience focused directly on quantum computing (e.g., quantum error correction, fault tolerance, topological codes, quantum algorithms, or quantum hardware\-software interfaces).
* **Work Authorization / Citizenship:** Must be a **U.S. Citizen** or **U.S. Permanent Resident (Green Card holder)** (required due to export controls, ITAR/EAR regulations, and eligibility for federal research grants/programs).
* **Technical \& Software Rigor:** Demonstrated track record developing high\-performance scientific software (C\+\+, Rust, or Python) applied to quantum simulations, tensor networks, decoding routines, or quantum circuit compilation.
* **Builder Mindset:** Strong passion for early\-stage venture creation, comfort operating with high autonomy under ambiguity, and the ability to balance rigorous scientific theory with rapid MVP engineering.

What We Offer

* **Founding Equity:** Substantial equity stake commensurate with a co\-founder role.
* **Impact:** Direct ownership in defining the technical backbone of fault\-tolerant quantum computing.
* **Autonomy:** Full authority over technology stack selection, hiring decisions, and engineering methodology.

Pay: $75,000\.00 \- $100,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Relocation assistance

Work Location: Remote

Our fax\-delivery suite of products allows our clients to exchange millions of patient information, insurance and other documents safely, swiftly and securely every business day. The Director of Internal Audit Information Technology will be responsible for planning, executing, and overseeing all aspects of IT audit activities within the credit union. Partners with all levels of management and line of business to develop creative and innovative business-oriented solutions to improve controls, mitigate risks, and influence positive change.

Continuously monitor for changes in the organizational risk profile and/or operational environment and modify the audit schedule, risk assessment, and audit universe as necessary.
Builds and maintains strong relationships with business partners across the organization to help them align their business strategy with appropriate risk management practices and controls.
Leads the development and implementation of an audit plan and strategy using an appropriate risk-based methodology, including performing and designing assigned audit entity risk assessments to support a forward-looking, strategically aligned audit plan. Designs process improvements and standardization of audit processes, methodologies, and guidelines. jobs.description:
Director, Emerging Technology and Innovation Programs - Remote

Job Description:

Internet2 is a non-profit, member-driven advanced research and education (R&E) technology organization. Founded in 1996, we provide high-performance infrastructure and integrated cloud solutions, a secure trust fabric, and collaborative forums that allow U.S. higher education and research institutions to drive the next generation of scientific and academic discovery through National High-Performance Infrastructure , Seamless Global Access , Community-Powered Cloud Solutions , Advanced Identity & Security and Community-Driven Innovation . Read our 2025 Annual Report and visit our website ( www.internet2.edu ) to learn more about us.

Position Summary:

The Director, Emerging Technology and Innovation Programs leads Internet2's NET+ emerging technology portfolio, setting strategy, managing active service offerings, and building industry partnerships that support the research and higher education community. This role combines strategic vision with hands-on operational leadership, guiding emerging technologies such as AI, advanced wireless, and quantum-enabled services from evaluation through adoption as sustainable, community-supported offerings.

This role will provide leadership for communities of practice and develop resources that help institutions evaluate, adopt, and implement emerging technologies. As a member of the Vice President's management team, the Director, Emerging Technology and Innovation Programs will represent NET+ across industry and higher education forums, fosters collaboration among stakeholders, and helps align emerging technology initiatives with Internet2's strategic priorities. The Director also supervises and develops the program development team, supporting professional growth and program success.

This role provides a unique opportunity to influence how the higher education and research community evaluates, adopts, and scales emerging technologies, helping shape the future of AI, advanced wireless, and quantum-enabled services across hundreds of institutions.

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Portfolio strategy and program leadership: Set strategic direction and manage day-to-day execution for the NET+ emerging technology portfolio, focusing on artificial intelligence (agentic AI, AI security, foundation models), advanced wireless (private 5G, neutral host, LEO satellite), and quantum as a service / secure research enablement while maintaining a forward view of the market and recommending where NET+ should invest, wait, or exit.
Service ownership: Act as primary owner for two to four active NET+ service offerings, with day-to-day accountability for vendor relationships, business model and pricing, contract negotiation and renewal, service health, and long-term sustainability, working with Internet2 contracting, finance, and legal colleagues.
Industry partnerships and portfolio growth: Build and scale strategic, high-value partnerships with industry leaders to translate emerging technology capabilities into funded, structured programs for higher education and research, while identifying, evaluating, and recruiting new providers to expand the NET+ portfolio.
Community engagement and knowledge mobilization: Provide operational support and leadership for existing communities of practice (e.g., Advanced Wireless, AI) by developing authoritative, enduring community assets, including reference architectures, best practice guides, and implementation playbooks, and represent NET+ across multi-institutional working groups and industry forums.
Supervision and staff development: Directly supervise, coach, and evaluate the program development team, including hiring, performance management, and professional development.
Cross-organizational leadership: Serve as an active member of the Vice President’s management team; align emerging technology initiatives with Internet2 priorities; and partner with marketing and communications, community programs, and other business units on shared goals.

The Ideal Candidate is a:

Strategic technology leader with a proven track record of advancing enterprise, cloud, and emerging technology initiatives while building strong industry partnerships and driving service innovation.
Technical and business translator who can bridge complex technologies and business needs, effectively communicating with technical experts, executives, and community stakeholders.
Collaborative people leader with experience developing teams, building consensus across diverse stakeholders, and working within higher education, research, or other mission-driven environments.

Demonstrated experience evaluating emerging technologies, assessing market opportunities, and developing strategic recommendations that inform investment, adoption, or portfolio decisions.

Experience hiring, supervising, coaching, and evaluating professional staff, or comparable experience leading professional teams.

Preferred Qualifications :

jobs.title: Senior VP, Technology
jobs.description:
About The Role

Virtium is seeking a Senior VP, Technology to help define the next chapter of our technology strategy as we expand from our strong foundation in industrial memory and storage into broader embedded computing, Edge AI, connectivity, and integrated system-level solutions.

This is a highly visible executive role for a senior technology leader who can combine deep technical credibility, customer insight, product vision, and practical business judgment. The Senior VP, Technology will partner directly with the CTO, executive leadership, customers, technology partners, and internal teams to shape where Virtium invests, differentiates, and grows.

About Virtium

Virtium is a Rancho Santa Margarita, California–based designer and manufacturer of high-reliability industrial embedded solutions for customers whose systems must operate consistently in demanding, long-life environments. For more than 25 years, Virtium has supported global OEMs with industrial-grade SSDs, DRAM memory modules, compute and system-on-module solutions, AI accelerator modules, connectivity modules, and supporting software.

Our solutions are used in applications across networking and telecommunications, industrial automation, aerospace and defense, medical, transportation, rugged computing, Industrial IoT, and other mission-critical embedded markets where reliability, lifecycle stability, qualification, and supply continuity matter.

Why This Role Matters

Virtium’s customers are navigating increasing complexity across embedded computing, Edge AI workloads, memory and storage requirements, semiconductor transitions, security expectations, and long product lifecycles. The Senior VP, Technology will help identify where customer requirements, emerging technologies, supplier roadmaps, and market opportunities intersect—and translate those insights into differentiated solutions, strategic partnerships, and scalable product opportunities.

The right leader will have the chance to influence Virtium’s technology direction at a meaningful stage of growth, with direct access to executive decision-making and a clear connection between strategy, customer need, product development, and market impact.

What You’ll Lead

Reporting to the CTO, the Senior VP, Technology will serve as Virtium’s senior technology strategist and trusted technical voice with customers, suppliers, partners, and internal teams. This leader will guide through technical credibility, strategic judgment, collaboration, and cross-functional influence while partnering closely with engineering leadership responsible for development execution.

Key Areas of Impact

Customer and Market Strategy: Build trusted-advisor relationships with strategic OEM customers, understand their embedded system architecture and future requirements, and identify where Virtium can create differentiated technical and commercial value.
Technology and Product Roadmap: Define and maintain Virtium’s long-term roadmap across industrial SSDs, DRAM memory, compute/SOM platforms, AI accelerator modules, connectivity modules, and related software-enabled solutions.
Technology Ecosystem Leadership: Develop strategic relationships with semiconductor manufacturers, processor and controller suppliers, memory and NAND partners, AI accelerator providers, connectivity partners, and other key technology ecosystem partners.
Architecture and Technical Direction: Guide major platform, architecture, and technology decisions across hardware, firmware, software, edge workload performance, system integration, thermal and power constraints, reliability, qualification, validation, and lifecycle requirements.
Executive Alignment and Growth: Align executive, commercial, product, engineering, operations, and supply chain teams around focused technology priorities that support customer value, differentiation, revenue growth, manufacturability, and time to market.

Ideal Candidate Profile

Executive-level technology leader with 15+ years of relevant experience in embedded systems, edge computing, memory, storage, semiconductors, computing hardware, connectivity, industrial hardware, or complex hardware/software platforms.
Strong customer-facing Senior VP, Technology, VP Engineering, Chief Architect, Distinguished Engineer, Fellow, or senior technology leadership background with credibility across OEM customers, engineering teams, suppliers, and executive stakeholders.
Deep understanding of how to balance innovation with reliability, lifecycle stability, manufacturability, qualification, security, performance, and supply continuity in demanding embedded or mission-critical environments.
Proven ability to translate customer and market insight into technology roadmaps, scalable product opportunities, strategic partnerships, and practical execution priorities.
Comfortable operating in a hands-on, collaborative, growth-oriented environment where influence, clarity, judgment, and customer proximity matter.
Bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related technical discipline

Location and Logistics

Reports to: Chief Technology Officer
Compensation: Total compensation range of $200-350K. Competitive and based on experience and alignment with the role; bonus eligible.
Location: Onsite, executive leadership role based at Virtium’s headquarters in Rancho Santa Margarita, California, where close collaboration with executive, engineering, product, and operations teams is central to the role’s impact.
Schedule: Full-time, Monday through Friday.

jobs.title: Director, Infrastructure & IT Operations
jobs.description:
About the Opportunity

The hiring organization is seeking a strategic and hands-on Director, Infrastructure & IT Operations
to lead the technology capabilities that keep digital products, cloud platforms, and internal teams secure, reliable, and productive.

This role oversees cloud infrastructure, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), production operations, bot mitigation, corporate IT, and helpdesk support, while providing architectural leadership across cloud platforms, networking, identity, observability, and operational tooling. This position spans both internal employee technology and the production infrastructure supporting high-traffic, customer-facing applications.

This is a full-time, remote position based in the United States.

Key Responsibilities

Lead teams responsible for cloud infrastructure, SRE, production operations, corporate IT, helpdesk, and bot mitigation, establishing ownership, operational standards, service-level objectives (SLOs), escalation procedures, and performance metrics.
Develop managers, technical leads, and IT staff through coaching, career development, and building a culture of accountability, documentation, automation, and continuous improvement.
Build quarterly and annual infrastructure roadmaps aligned with business priorities, growth, security, reliability, and cost, partnering with engineering, product, data, marketing, finance, HR, legal, and executive leadership.
Own the reliability, scalability, security, performance, and cost-effectiveness of cloud infrastructure, primarily within AWS.
Provide architectural leadership across cloud services, applications, APIs, networking, identity, databases, storage, observability, and integrations while establishing architecture standards, reference patterns, governance, and technical review processes.
Partner with engineering to improve deployment safety, performance, and readiness, driving automation, configuration management, and infrastructure as code.
Lead capacity planning for growth and demand spikes, eliminating single points of failure, undocumented systems, manual processes, and single-source dependencies.
Ensure production and nonproduction environments are properly separated, secured, and monitored, reviewing new systems for architectural fit, supportability, security, and total cost of ownership.
Establish and maintain service-level indicators (SLIs), SLOs, availability targets, and error-budget practices for critical systems.
Improve observability through centralized logging, metrics, distributed tracing, application performance monitoring (APM), and actionable alerting.
Lead major incident management, coordination, executive communication, root-cause analysis, and corrective-action tracking to improve mean time to detect, respond, and recover.
Develop and test backup, disaster recovery, and business continuity procedures, and establish sustainable on-call practices.
Own strategy and tooling for bot mitigation, scraping protection, automated abuse prevention, and traffic-quality management using technologies such as Cloudflare, DataDome, web application firewalls (WAFs), rate limiting, CAPTCHA alternatives, and device fingerprinting.
Partner with cross-functional teams to distinguish malicious automation from legitimate customers, search engines, partners, and approved AI crawlers, establishing monitoring and response procedures.
Oversee internal IT services and helpdesk support, establishing service-level expectations for response times, resolution times, user satisfaction, and backlog reduction.
Manage the employee technology lifecycle, including onboarding, offboarding, equipment provisioning, access management, asset recovery, and device inventory.
Standardize endpoint configuration, encryption, patching, and endpoint detection across laptops, collaboration platforms, productivity software, and telecom services.
Establish consistent identity and access management practices across corporate and production systems, implementing role-based access, least privilege, multi-factor authentication (MFA), periodic access reviews, and secure administrative account handling.
Support vulnerability remediation, security assessments, audits, vendor reviews, incident readiness, and applicable privacy requirements in partnership with legal and security teams.
Manage infrastructure, security, IT, telecom, monitoring, and support vendors, handling evaluations, contract reviews, renewals, licensing, service level agreements (SLAs), and budget management.
Improve cloud cost visibility through tagging, allocation, forecasting, tool consolidation, and contract optimization.

Required Qualifications

10+ years of experience in cloud infrastructure, SRE, platform engineering, DevOps, IT operations, or related disciplines.
5+ years of experience leading engineering or technology teams, including managing managers or technical leads.
Demonstrated experience operating high-traffic, customer-facing platforms in AWS or a comparable cloud environment.
Strong understanding of cloud architecture, networking, identity, security, observability, databases, APIs, storage, and distributed systems.
Experience managing production availability, incident response, root-cause analysis, disaster recovery, and business continuity.
Experience with infrastructure automation, configuration management, CI/CD, and infrastructure as code.
Experience managing corporate IT, employee support, endpoint management, software licensing, and access provisioning.
Experience establishing operational metrics, SLOs, and support standards.
Demonstrated ability to manage vendors, contracts, departmental budgets, and cloud costs.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to communicate technical risks, architecture, and tradeoffs to executive audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Cloudflare, DataDome, or comparable bot-management and web application protection platforms, including leading bot mitigation or traffic-quality programs.
Experience with AWS services, containerized environments, infrastructure as code, centralized logging, and APM tools (such as AppDynamics).
Experience supporting large-scale consumer subscription, public-record, data-as-a-service, advertising, or ecommerce platforms.
Experience modernizing legacy infrastructure, transitioning systems from external vendors, and consolidating cloud accounts or IT services.
Familiarity with privacy requirements and secure handling of sensitive consumer data.
Experience building or maturing SRE, DevOps, or platform engineering functions.

Measures of Success

Improved availability, performance, and stability of customer-facing platforms.
Reduced impact and infrastructure costs associated with bots, scraping, and automated abuse.
Faster incident detection, response, and recovery, alongside a reduction in recurring incidents.
Enhanced observability with reduced alert noise, validated disaster recovery capabilities, and optimized cloud spend.
Consistent helpdesk performance, reliable onboarding and offboarding, and robust endpoint security and asset tracking.
Strong architecture governance, reduced dependency on undocumented systems or vendors, and demonstrated team development.

Compensation and Benefits

Annual base salary: $170,000 - $180,000

Comprehensive health coverage including medical, dental, and vision insurance
Life insurance
Retirement benefits with employer match
