jobs.title: Director, Technology Transformation
jobs.description:
**Your Role**

The Technology team is responsible for the delivery, operation, and governance of secure, compliant, and scalable platforms that support critical healthcare services and enable the successful separation and long\-term independence of the Ascendiun family of companies. The Director, Technology Transformation will report to the Chief Information Officer (CIO). In this role you will for lead cross\-functional teams to deliver large\-scale programs that create sustainable, systematic improvements across technology and business operations.


Our leadership model is about developing great leaders at all levels and creating opportunities for our people to grow – personally, professionally, and financially. We are looking for leaders that are energized by creative and critical thinking, building and sustaining high\-performing teams, getting results the right way, and fostering continuous learning.


  
**Your Work**

In this role, you will:


* Lead strategic technology initiatives that improve operational performance, scalability, reliability, and customer experience.
* Identify systemic challenges and drive sustainable solutions that address root causes rather than symptoms.
* Develop and execute transformation roadmaps aligned with business objectives and technology strategy.
* Partner with business and technology leaders to drive organizational change and process improvements.
* Lead complex, cross\-functional technology programs with multiple stakeholders, dependencies, and delivery teams.
* Establish governance, milestones, success metrics, and reporting mechanisms to ensure program success.
* Drive prioritization, issue resolution, risk management, and decision\-making across initiatives.
* Ensure projects are delivered on schedule, within budget, and aligned with business outcomes.
* Lead efforts to improve system stability, service performance, operational maturity, and supportability.
* Facilitate root\-cause analysis and corrective action planning for recurring issues.
* Build strong partnerships with business leaders, product owners, and technology teams.
* Communicate program status, risks, dependencies, and recommendations to senior leadership.

  
**Your Knowledge and Experience**

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or related field.
* Requires a minimum of 10 years of technology experience, including 6\+ years in leadership roles managing enterprise technology initiatives.
* Proven experience leading large\-scale technology programs and transformational initiatives.
* Strong understanding of enterprise applications, infrastructure, cloud technologies, and operational processes.
* Demonstrated ability to lead cross\-functional teams and drive organizational change.
Experience managing complex stakeholder environments and balancing competing priorities.  
* 

**Hybrid**

This role requires employees to be in\-office based on our hybrid workplace model, balancing purposeful in\-person collaboration with flexibility. For most teams, this means coming into the office two days each week.


Employees living more than 50 miles from an office location will work with their manager to determine in\-office time based on business need.  



\#LI\-CM1


  
**ABOUT THE TEAM  

About Stellarus and the Ascendiun Family of Companies**

Stellarus, launched in January 2025, is designed to scale innovative healthcare solutions that support customers in creating a health care experience deserving of their family, friends, and neighbors.
  

  

Stellarus is part of a family of organizations that is overseen by a nonprofit corporate entity named Ascendiun. The Ascendiun Family of Companies also includes Blue Shield of California and its subsidiary, Blue Shield of California Promise Health Plan and Altais, a clinical services company.


Stellarus’ vision is to empower its customers to create a healthcare experience that is worthy of their family, friends, and neighbors. Stellarus’ objective is to offer innovative, modern, scalable solutions that challenge the health care status quo. This very closely aligns with Blue Shield of California’s vision by using innovation to improve quality, affordability, and experience for members.


To achieve our mission, we foster an environment where all employees can thrive and contribute fully to address the needs of the various communities we serve. We are committed to creating and maintaining a supportive workplace that upholds our values and advances our goals.


**Our Values:**

At Stellarus, our core values of agility, trust, drive, courage and service shape our approach to developing innovative product offerings.


**Our Workplace Model:**

We believe in fostering a workplace environment that balances purposeful in\-person collaboration with flexibility \- providing clear expectations while respecting the diverse needs of our workforce. Our workplace model is designed around intentional in\-person interaction, collaboration, connection, creativity and flexibility:


* For most teams, this means coming into the office two days per week.
* Employees living more than 50 miles from an office location, out of state employees, and employees in certain member\-facing roles should work with their manager to determine in\-office time based on business need.
* For employees with medical conditions that may impact their ability to work in\-office, we are committed to engaging in an interactive process and providing reasonable accommodations to ensure their work environment is conducive to their success and well\-being.

The Company reserves the right to require more presence in the office based on business needs, and requirements are subject to change with periodic reviews.


**Physical Requirements:**

Office Environment \- roles involving part to full time schedule in Office Environment. Based in our physical offices and work from home office/deskwork \- Activity level: Sedentary, frequency most of work day.

jobs.title: Director, IT and Digital Transformation
jobs.description:
#### **About GenScript**



Founded in 2002 in New Jersey, GenScript Biotech Corporation accelerates innovation in biotech and healthcare by providing researchers and companies with the building blocks needed to develop groundbreaking treatments and products. Guided by its mission to Make People and Nature Healthier Through Biotechnology, and its role as a well\-recognized biotechnology company, GenScript has a team of approximately 6,165 employees and has served more than 200,000 customers across over 100 countries and regions.

**Job Title:** Director, IT \& Digital Transformation  

  

**Job Location:** Piscataway, NJ



The estimated salary range for this role is $175,000 \- $195,000 depending on experience. Please note that this role is requiring a candidate that is bilingual in Mandarin Chinese and English.


**Job Summary:**



This position is designed to further advance our Glocalization strategy, with three key focus areas:


* Driving Digital Enablement \& Solution Execution
* Building Tech Ecosystems \& Strategic Alliances
* Evangelizing AI \& BioSecurity Technologies


**Key Responsibilities**



1\. Driving Digital Enablement \& Solution Execution


* Act as the primary digital interface for all business units at the US site, gaining a deep understanding of local business pain points and regional characteristics.
* Execute the Glocalization strategy by promoting and implementing the group's digital products and solutions locally. Enhance business efficiency through professional user services and in\-depth digital operations.
* Identify and provide feedback on US industry technology trends, driving the continuous optimization and iteration of the global product portfolio.


2\. Building Tech Ecosystems \& Strategic Alliances


* Forge and manage strategic partnerships with top\-tier US tech companies, startups, and research institutions.
* Lead negotiations on technology collaborations to bring in cutting\-edge capabilities and strengthen the group's global tech footprint.
* Design sustainable, mutually beneficial partnership models that elevate the group's technological reputation and influence in the US.


3\. Evangelizing AI \& BioSecurity Technologies


* Serve as the face of the group's AI and BioSecurity technologies in the US — showcasing innovation to clients, partners, and industry bodies.
* Drive ground\-up implementation of AI solutions in real US business use cases — from pilot to scale — creating flagship references for broader adoption.
* Build and operate a structured technology advocacy program to boost awareness, credibility, and adoption of the group's frontier tech across US.


4\. Manage US IT Operations and maintenance Team's optimal performance.


* Oversee the performance of the US IT Operations and Maintenance team by setting clear goals, coaching team members, ensuring timely completion of operational tasks, and fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and high\-quality service.


**Qualifications**


* Fluent in Mandarin Chinese \& English
* 8\+ years of experience in technology, digital transformation, or business development.
* Deep roots in the US tech ecosystem, with proven success operating in complex multinational organizations and cross\-cultural environments.
* Exceptional communicator and influencer — skilled at "tech evangelism" and persuading key internal and external decision\-makers.
* Keen business\-technology acumen with strong expertise in AI, BioSecurity, and other emerging tech trends and their commercial applications.
* Highly self\-driven, resilient, and culturally agile — thrives in fast\-paced, ambiguous, international settings.


\#LI\-EB1



\#GS

**Benefits:**



Benefits include medical, dental, and vision insurance as well as a 401(k) retirement plan with a company match that vests fully on day one. We offer paid parental leave after just three (3\) months of employment, and a paid time off policy that includes vacation time, personal time, sick time, floating holidays, and company holidays. Additional benefits include flexible spending and health savings accounts, life and AD\&D insurance, short\- and long\-term disability coverage, legal assistance, and supplemental plans such as pet, critical illness, accident, and hospital indemnity insurance. We also provide commuter benefits, well\-being initiatives, and peer\-to\-peer recognition programs; demonstrating our ongoing commitment to building a culture where our people feel empowered, supported, and inspired to do their best work.



GenScript USA Inc/ProBio Inc. is a proud equal opportunity/affirmative action employer committed to attracting, retaining, and maximizing the performance of a diverse and inclusive workforce. It is the Company's policy to ensure equal employment opportunity without discrimination or harassment based on race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, national origin, marital or domestic/civil partnership status, genetic information, citizenship status, uniformed service member or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.



GenScript USA Inc./ProBio Inc. maintains a drug\-free workplace.  



Please note: Genscript USA Inc./ProBio Inc. will only contact candidates through verified application sources. GenScript/Probio does not request personal information from candidates through individual email or any other platform.

jobs.title: Deputy Program Manager for Propulsion Development
jobs.description:
Who We Are:  

Venus Aerospace is revolutionizing rocket engine propulsion. With the first generational leap in rocket engine technology since Apollo, our proprietary Rotating Detonation Rocket Engine and Venus Detonation Ramjets deliver historic efficiency and performance across aerospace applications. We are building the next generation of propulsion platforms that enable breakthrough capabilities in space, defense, and commercial high\-speed flight. Our team thrives on solving the toughest engineering challenges and pushing the boundaries of what’s possible in aerospace. At Venus, we’re looking for bold engineers and innovators who want to make history and redefine the future of propulsion.

The Role: Deputy Program Manager for Propulsion Development
The Deputy Program Manager for Propulsion Development will partner with leaders from manufacturing, engineering, test, purchasing and sales to develop Venus propulsion systems. You will own program requirements, schedules, and budgets and ensure the integrated team delivers propulsion systems with exceptional performance and propellant mass fraction that are manufacturable and marketable. This is a hands\-on program leadership role in a rapidly evolving startup environment.
### **What You’ll Get To Do**


* Program Leadership: ensure alignment between Venus Aerospace business plan and technology roadmap.
* Program Execution: Deconflict resources and set priorities. Manage cost, schedule, and technical performance from design through manufacturing, integration, test, and deployment.
* Cross\-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with engineering to translate mission needs into product requirements, guide design reviews, and manage technical or contractual changes. Work with manufacturing to ensure designs can be manufactured; supply chains can support timelines and prioritize work. Work with test to ensure the design of experiments meet exit criteria and achieve product performance.
* Customer Engagement: Lead program reviews, present technical and schedule briefings, negotiate requirements, and maintain strong relationships with customer stakeholders.
* Risk Management: Identify program risks early, develop mitigation plans, and maintain schedule fidelity under aggressive timelines.
* Proposal \& Contract Management: Lead proposal efforts and contract negotiations, ensuring technical feasibility, cost effectiveness, and compliance with FAR/DFARS requirements.
### **What You Have**


* Bachelor’s degree in Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field or equivalent experience.
* Excellent communication and technical writing skills, including preparation of CDRLs and technical data packages
* 15\+ years of experience in aerospace, defense, or national security programs
* 5\+ years of experience as a Program Manager in aerospace
* Proven track record of excellence and achievement
* Demonstrated success managing complex, multi\-disciplinary engineering programs to cost and schedule.
* U.S. citizenship with the ability to obtain and maintain a Secret clearance.
### **What Will Set You Apart**


* Familiarity with USG programs, acquisitions, and operational concepts.
* Understanding of U.S. Government acquisition processes, contracting, and operational concepts.
* Familiarity with government acquisition processes, requirements decomposition, and systems verification.
* Familiarity with rapid prototyping, OTA contracts, and accelerated development environments.
**Location:**On\-site in Houston, TX

**Benefits:**Venus Aerospace employee benefits include a 401(k) plan, stock options, and medical benefits, including dental and vision. We have a flex\-Friday flexible schedule, unlimited PTO, and receive professional development opportunities.  

**ITAR Requirements**

jobs.title: Director, Technology - Implementation
jobs.description:
The Machine is Code & Theory's AI orchestration platform — the engine that operationalizes AI across our work and, increasingly, across Stagwell, the global marketing and communications network Code & Theory is part of. The Machine integrates with the tools customers already use (Figma, Slack, Teams, Adobe, performance dashboards) and serves both Stagwell's internal agencies and enterprise brand customers including Qualcomm, TIME, and Stanley Black & Decker.

We're looking for a Director of Implementation to own how the Machine lands inside customer and agency environments. This is the role that turns a powerful platform into working systems for real teams: scoping engagements, leading deployment, integrating with existing tooling, and driving adoption through to measurable outcomes. You'll lead a team of implementation engineers and solution architects, and you'll be the connective tissue between the platform's capabilities and what each customer needs from it.

Our engineers are AI native and engage in and advance the state of the art in the practice of software development with AI.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Own end-to-end implementation of the Machine across customer and agency environments, from technical scoping through deployment, integration, and adoption – you will write code and lots of it – daily
Stand up and lead a team of implementation engineers and solution architects, setting delivery standards and accountable for the quality and pace of every engagement
Translate customer requirements into deployment plans, working closely with the platform engineering team to surface gaps, prioritize integrations, and feed real-world needs back into the roadmap
Design integrations against the tools customers already run, making the Machine work alongside Figma, Slack, Teams, Adobe, performance dashboards, and the rest of a customer's stack
Drive adoption past go-live, defining what success looks like for each engagement and steering teams toward it with the right enablement, instrumentation, and follow-through
Partner across engineering, account, and customer stakeholders, coordinating reporting lines and expectations so delivery holds together as one effort

WHAT YOU'LL NEED

A track record of leading technical implementations or professional-services delivery for a software or platform product, ideally in environments with demanding enterprise customers
Strong technical fluency across cloud, integrations, and APIs — enough to architect a deployment, debug an integration, and earn the trust of the engineers you lead
Fantastic verbal communications and presentation skills, since this is a customer-facing role and you must have experience owning customer relationships through delivery, including the hard conversations about scope, timelines, and tradeoffs
People leadership experience, including in matrixed or cross-functional structures where influence matters as much as authority
A bias toward adoption and outcomes, with conviction about what separates a deployed tool from one a team actually uses
Comfort leveraging AI-enabled development tools and workflows to accelerate engineering, automation, debugging, and operational tasks
Experience orchestrating multi-step AI or agent-driven workflows, including selecting appropriate models, tools, and execution patterns for different use cases
Strong judgment reviewing and hardening AI-assisted output for security, scalability, maintainability, and architectural fit
Experience building or maintaining prompts, evaluation frameworks, documentation, or operational context systems that improve engineering velocity and reliability
Familiarity with automated evaluation and feedback loops for AI-enabled systems and workflows

ABOUT US

Born in 2001, Code and Theory is a digital-first creative agency that sits at the center of creativity and technology. We pride ourselves on not only solving consumer and business problems, but also helping to establish new capabilities for our clients. With a global client roster of Fortune 100s and start-ups alike, we crave the hardest problems to solve. We have teams distributed across North America, South America, Europe, and Asia. The Code and Theory global network of agencies is growing and includes Kettle, Instrument, Left Field Labs, Create Group, Current, and TrueLogic.

Striving never to be pigeonholed, we work across every major category: from tech to CPG, financial services to travel & hospitality, government and education to media and publishing. We value the collaboration with our client partners, including but not limited to Adidas, Amazon, Con Edison, Diageo, EY, J.P. Morgan Chase, Lenovo, Marriott, Mars, Microsoft, Thomson Reuters, and TikTok.

The Code and Theory network is comprised of nearly 2,000 people with 50% engineers and 50% creative talent. We’re always on the lookout for smart, driven, and forward-thinking people to join our team.

The compensation range for this role is $150,000 – $225,000 and spans multiple levels. We're open to hiring at the level that best matches the right candidate's experience. Actual compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, budget, and location.

By combining deep technical expertise with a forward-looking perspective on emerging technologies, this role ensures the agency remains at the forefront of digital experience development, automation, integration, quality assurance and AI-driven innovation.

Define and lead the agency's technology and AI vision and roadmap, ensuring investments align with client needs and future growth opportunities
Establish and champion the agency's AI strategy, identifying where and how AI can create value across internal operations, client work, workflows and service offerings

Foster interconnected ways of working across core strengths, ensuring technology and AI considerations are integrated throughout project life cycles
Establish and improve documentation standards, workflows and operational processes that strengthen collaboration across disciplines and create greater visibility into how systems, tools, teams and technologies work together

Build, mentor and develop high-performing technology teams while cultivating a culture of innovation and continuous learning
Continuously assess the performance, structure and maturity of the Technology & AI core strength, making recommendations that strengthen capabilities, improve delivery and support long-term agency success.

Demonstrated success leading technology and AI strategy within an agency, consulting firm or complex marketing organization
Deep understanding of web technologies, marketing technology ecosystems systems integration and digital platforms
Experience evaluating and implementing AI technologies that drive measurable business outcomes
Strong understanding of SEO, AI optimization (AIO), generative search and the evolving search landscape

Working knowledge of AI governance, privacy, security and the evolving regulatory landscape

An entrepreneurial, forward-thinking spirit
Happy to build relationships and trust, connect the dots, find a better way to solve existing problems

Ability to embrace our core value of freedom — to be bold, to experiment, to challenge, to act and to celebrate — and a history of doing so throughout their career.

Open-minded and active listener
Continually grows people and business
Truthful and transparent

Forward-thinking
Proactive and communicates in a positive manner

Description & Requirements

Maximus
is currently seeking a Senior Technology Project Manager
to lead and track the development and implementation of a complex, strategic initiative across multiple development or service teams. This role requires strong project management skills and the technical acumen to understand and coordinate system-level functions. The successful candidate will ensure alignment with strategic goals, manage dependencies, and support execution from planning through delivery.

This is a remote position.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Serve as the point of contact and client interface for project technology related issues.
Manage project expectations, evaluate project needs, and communicate with stakeholders to ensure that program needs are met with respect to urgency and priority.
Develop trust, credibility, and strong client relationships; seeks opportunities to add value to internal and external client initiatives.
Review all project deliverables to ensure quality and accuracy meet project, stakeholder, and contractual standards.
Execute all project management functions including; work breakdown and cost estimation, scheduling, monitoring and tracking of technical progress against the defined timetables and budgets, and staff assignment and development.
Lead and direct the successful delivery of application development, systems integration, infrastructure, and product installation/customization services while ensuring that assigned projects adhere to the approved life cycle work patterns, standards, and procedures for solution delivery.
Define and implement development plans for assigned projects.
Typically responsible for providing guidance, coaching, and training to other employees within job area.
Ensure staff is knowledgeable on the applications and technologies in use on the project and that project team understands and follows processes and procedures.
Provide detailed direction during various stages of the lifecycle to include requirements analysis, testing, and potentially programming support.
Identify and assess new functional capabilities supporting engineering change proposals and additional follow on work.
Identify, track, manage, and communicate risks and issues with stakeholders and upper management.
Coordinate, prepare, and manage technical presentations and functional demonstrations to internal and external stakeholders.

Serve as the primary point of contact between program leadership and external (government) client representatives to ensure clear communication and alignment across the project lifecycle (initiate, plan, execute, monitor/control, close).
Strong communication skills, including executive briefings and clear written status reporting.
Coordinate daily with Chief Engineer and Lead Product Owner to manage the full project lifecycle with a focus on maintaining the requirements register, cross-team dependencies, risk assessments, and reference architectures.
Build and manage client relationships; align expectations with sponsors and stakeholders in accordance with the contract or program scope; and proactively surface risks, decisions, and tradeoffs to maintain alignment to contract scope, priorities, and outcomes.
Plan and lead program kickoffs and provide weekly updates and monthly/quarterly program management reviews
Ensure Chief Engineer and Lead Product Owner are synchronized to drive recurring delivery ceremonies (e.g., dev/test standups, sprint reviews, integrated planning sessions, stakeholder briefings) in order to meet requirements and technical program milestones.
Facilitate cross-functional coordination among business operations, engineering, security, and senior leadership to ensure requirements, priorities, and approvals are understood, documented, and executed.
Lead and develop program resources (direct reports and/or matrixed team members) through clear goal setting, prioritization, coaching, performance feedback, and escalation management; drive accountability by influence across engineering, product, operations, and vendors to deliver integrated program outcomes.
Provide routine status reporting and executive-level briefings; identify and escalate schedule, scope, cost, quality, and resource impacts; and support change control by ensuring change requests are documented at the appropriate levels and driving approvals with appropriate stakeholders.
Work with Chief Engineer to stay apprised of release and delivery schedules in order to ensure Transition Schedules and/or Contract Deliverables are met.
Manage action items and the RAID log (risks, assumptions, issues, dependencies), including identifying and analyzing risks, developing realistic mitigation plans, communicating impacts and recommendations to leadership and stakeholders, and incorporating updates into the integrated project plan.
Partner with finance and business operations to manage budget execution, staffing plans, and resource forecasts, including tracking burn and variance against plan.
Partner with Contracts to manage and review project/contract deliverables and to proactively inform customer of any variances that may arise (due to schedule, scope creep, etc.).
Coordinate with Chief Engineer and Lead Product Owner to ensure quality and traceability to requirements and coordinate internal and client/government reviews to support timely acceptance.
Develop and maintain integrated project plans (e.g., WBS and schedule), including estimates, milestones, dependencies, and resource assignments; monitor technical progress against baselines with Chief Engineer and Lead Product Owner; and implement corrective actions to keep delivery on track.
Use standardized tools to manage and track initiative status, and provide clear visibility and transparency into progress for internal and external stakeholders
Oversee delivery across application development, systems integration, infrastructure standup, and product installation/customization to ensure adherence to approved lifecycle standards, security requirements, and operational readiness expectations.

Bachelor's degree in relevant field of study and 7+ years of relevant professional experience required, or equivalent combination of education and experience.

Job-Specific Minimum Requirements:

Bachelor's Degree from an accredited college or university within preferred field of study in Computer Science or Business Management. Equivalent work experience will be considered in lieu of degree.
7 years' experience working as a project manager or program manager, delivering IT related complex projects in a medium to large size organization.

Strong understanding of the software development lifecycle (SDLC) in Agile environments.

Experience in developing and implementing technology solutions (applications, platforms, and integrated systems) that support complex business processes focused on customer/client identification, service delivery, and ongoing relationship management.
Experience successfully developing and deploying IT solutions using various Agile development methodologies (e.g., Scrum, Kanban, etc.).
Skilled in Microsoft Office Software including Word, Excel and PowerPoint.

Experience working within federal contract governance and ensuring continual compliance with contract requirements, including formal and informal deliverables.

The organization operates within the technology sector, focusing on designing and securing infrastructure for its clients. It addresses the challenge of maintaining high standards for internal technology environments in a remote-first setting, ensuring that its own operations reflect the quality delivered to clients. The company integrates AI governance and security practices to enhance both internal and client-facing technology solutions.

About the Opportunity:

The DIRECTOR OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY is responsible for leading and managing the internal technology environment. This role involves setting the technology strategy, building and developing the IT team, and overseeing the adoption and governance of AI within the organization. The position plays a vital role in ensuring that the internal IT infrastructure operates at the same high standard as client-facing solutions, contributing to overall organizational effectiveness and security.

Responsibilities:

Develop and execute a multi-year internal technology roadmap covering identity, endpoints, networking, collaboration, and service management
Align technology investments with business outcomes and define success metrics
Determine which IT functions are handled internally versus through partners
Establish IT governance, standards, architecture review, and change management processes
Design and build the internal IT team, including headcount planning and hiring
Mentor the team and define ownership, on-call, and escalation procedures
Develop an internal service catalog with defined service levels

Manage Microsoft 365 collaboration tools and enforce device requirements for a remote workforce

Manage cloud and hosting resources, including capacity and cost
Ensure backup, recovery, and business continuity with tested recovery objectives
Establish and mature IT service management processes
Publish operational metrics and reduce employee friction points
Manage onboarding and offboarding technology experiences with HR
Oversee IT budget, forecasting, and software license management
Rationalize SaaS applications and manage vendor relationships and contracts
Partner with security leadership to execute security programs and support compliance audits
Manage vulnerability assessment and remediation for internal systems

Minimum 10 years in information technology with leadership or technology ownership experience
Proven ability to build and scale IT in a distributed or remote-first fast-growth environment
Experience presenting technology strategies and metrics to executives
Expertise in Microsoft 365, Entra ID, endpoint management (Intune or equivalent), and SaaS at scale
Experience with internal AI adoption, governance, and change management
Strong security knowledge and ability to collaborate with CISOs and communicate risks to executives

Effective communication skills with technical and executive audiences
Industry certifications such as ITIL, Microsoft, CISSP/CISM, PMP are valued but not required

jobs.title: Chief Technology Officer
jobs.description:
About Innovas

At Innovas, we are transforming the way government innovates by delivering the mechanisms that turn ideas into action. We bring together the right people, processes, and technologies to accelerate progress where it matters most.

With a focus on impact over bureaucracy, collaboration over silos, and solutions over status quo, we we're built to act. Our team is made up of passionate problem-solvers, innovators, and experts who thrive on tackling meaningful challenges and delivering results. At Innovas, every role contributes to something bigger. Whether you’re supporting technology acquisition, improving processes, or enabling collaboration across organizations, your work helps move critical missions forward.

Join Innovas and help shape the future of government innovation.

Why Work At Innovas

Work on problems that matter.

At Innovas, your work directly supports innovation that shapes our nation’s future and delivers solutions with real-world impact.

Be part of something built differently.

Our teams are empowered to focus on solving problems, creating value, and exceeding expectations.

Bring ideas to life.

Work alongside passionate problem-solvers who thrive on tackling complex challenges and turning possibilities into progress.

Grow alongside a team of experts.

Our people bring diverse experiences from government, military, industry, technology, and entrepreneurship.

Job Description

The Chief Technology Officer (CTO) sets and leads the technology strategy that powers the next generation of government innovation. This is an opportunity to build technology capabilities, products, and platforms that remove barriers between innovative ideas and critical solutions that support our clients' missions.

As Innovas grows, the CTO will advance the current internal technology environment while developing market changing external products, platforms, and capabilities that shape its future. The CTO provides executive leadership across enterprise applications, product development & engineering, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity & internal IT, infrastructure, data strategy, and systems integration. Working closely with executive leadership and business stakeholders, this role develops technology capabilities that improve organizational performance, accelerate product innovation, strengthen cybersecurity, and deliver secure, scalable solutions for government customers and employees. The CTO ensures technology investments align with business strategy, protects Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), and positions the company for long-term growth.

The successful candidate is an executive builder with a demonstrated ability to lead multiple technology disciplines and attract and develop exceptional talent. They bring strong business acumen and experience managing technology investments, budgets, and resources in support of strategic priorities and profitable growth. The ideal candidate leads with accountability and a willingness to roll up their sleeves to deliver results.

Executive Technology Leadership and Strategy

Develop and execute an enterprise-wide technology strategy that supports organizational growth, operational efficiency, and long-term scalability.
Provide executive guidance on technology investments, modernization priorities, and digital transformation initiatives.
Own technology budgeting, investment planning, and resource allocation, evaluating build, buy, partner, or acquire options through cost, ROI, capacity, risk, and long-term value analysis to determine the best use of company resources.
Build, mentor, and oversee high-performing teams across all internal and external technology functions including enterprise applications, product development & engineering, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity & internal IT.
Manage relationships with technology vendors, SaaS providers, MSPs, and system integrators, and support contract evaluation, renewal strategy, licensing optimization, and cost management.
Work with executive team to strengthen cross-functional engagement and drive organization-wide adoption of technology and security practices.
Provide coaching, development, and clear expectations to ensure operational excellence and professional growth.

The CTO Is Accountable For Building And Leading The Technology Organization, Establishing Strong Functional Leadership, And Ensuring The Performance And Success Of The Following Teams And Capabilities

Product Development & AI Strategy

Partner with Product, Innovation, Growth, and business leaders to evaluate new product opportunities, determine technical feasibility and investment requirements, and move solutions from concept through deployment.
Lead software engineering, overseeing technical architecture, application development, DevOps, QA and testing, and the release and production support lifecycle.
Establish engineering standards, development practices, release management, documentation, and technology governance across all product lines.
Define and execute the company’s AI strategy, identifying opportunities to embed AI into products, enterprise platforms, and internal operations.
Establish the architecture, data, security, governance, and development standards required to deploy AI capabilities in government environments.

Enterprise Systems, Infrastructure, & Data

Governance

Lead enterprise system implementations, including CRM, ERP/finance, CLM, member platforms, and program management systems.
Establish enterprise standards for system architecture, resilience, performance, and service continuity.
Oversee integration strategy using APIs, middleware, automation frameworks, and MDM principles to maintain a single source of truth.
Partner with operations on change management, system sustainability, documentation, and operational performance across all major platforms.
Build and maintain secure and scalable data environments, including an enterprise data lake, data warehouses, and reporting ecosystems.
Define and enforce data governance standards covering taxonomy, metadata, lineage, retention, and quality.
Ensure data architecture supports analytics, forecasting, reporting, and emerging AI-enabled capabilities.

Cybersecurity, Compliance & Risk Management

Lead the company’s cybersecurity program, including policy development, identity and access controls, vulnerability management, and continuous monitoring.
Ensure compliance with federal frameworks, including NIST 800-171, CUI handling, DFARS requirements, CMMC readiness, and FedRAMP-aligned controls.
Develop systems and processes to manage classified data as required.
Own technology and cybersecurity risk management in alignment with federal and contractual requirements.
Oversee incident response, audit preparation, third-party security evaluations, and remediation planning.
Serve as the primary liaison with auditors, compliance consultants, and government technology representatives.

Internal IT & Employee Support

Lead internal IT operations and employee technology support, including help desk, service delivery, Microsoft 365 administration, cloud environments, network administration, and endpoint management.
Oversee employee technology onboarding and offboarding, account provisioning, device deployment, access management, and IT ticket escalation.
Establish service standards, SLAs, escalation procedures, and support processes that ensure responsive and reliable employee technology support.
Own endpoint and device management, including configuration, security, patching, monitoring, and ongoing administration.
Oversee IT asset management and the full asset lifecycle, including procurement, inventory, assignment, maintenance, replacement, recovery, and disposition.
Ensure business continuity, disaster recovery readiness, infrastructure reliability, and long-term modernization of the employee technology environment.

Qualifications

Must be a U.S. citizen with an ability to obtain security clearance.

Education Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, or related field.

Experience And Skills

15+ years of progressive technology leadership, including experience as a CTO, CIO, or senior technology executive leading and scaling multidisciplinary technology organizations.
Proven success building technology teams and capabilities through significant organizational growth, maintaining an entrepreneurial, hands-on approach while establishing the structure required to scale.
Demonstrated ownership of enterprise technology strategy, budgets, investment priorities, workforce planning, and resource allocation.
Proven expertise evaluating and executing build, buy, partner, or acquire strategies, including technology due diligence, M&A integration, and investment analysis.
Strong business and financial acumen with the ability to connect technology investments and resource decisions to growth, profitability, customer value, and long-term enterprise value.
Demonstrable success leading the development and commercialization of complex software products and platforms, with a strong understanding of software engineering, product development, AI/ML, technical architecture, and modern development practices.
Proven ability to build and lead cross-functional technology organizations where engineering, product, business, security, and operations work together to move products and capabilities from concept through deployment.
Demonstrable success leading distributed teams and developing strong functional leaders who can scale their organizations while maintaining accountability, speed, and execution.
Proven expertise in advising executive leadership on technology strategy, emerging technologies, cybersecurity and enterprise risk, M&A, and major investment decisions.
Experience operating in government or highly regulated environments, with responsibility for CUI, cybersecurity, compliance, and technology risk strongly preferred.

Preferred Experience

Experience supporting CLM systems, CRM ecosystems (such as Salesforce), ERP/finance platforms, membership or subscription platforms, and low-code/no-code tools.
Background working with DoD agencies, federal program offices, government contract service firms, or entities operating under Other Transaction Authority (OTA) environments.
Familiarity with professional services or consulting environments serving U.S. Government clients.
Advanced certifications such as PMP, ITIL, CISSP, CISM, or equivalent.

Location:

Equal Opportunity Employer

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), national origin, age (40 or older), disability, or genetic information.

What We Offer

We strive to be one of the best places to work in America. We offer competitive salaries and benefits that include:

**Opportunities Abound at SOUND**  

SOUND Behavioral Health is growing, and we are excited to welcome a Director of IT Operations to our growing team in Tukwila, WA! If you’re someone who enjoys supporting others and believes in the power of community behavioral health, you’ll fit right in here.  

The Director, IT Operations is responsible for the development, management, and support of SOUND’s technology environment, including network and server infrastructure, cloud services, help desk and end\-user support, hardware, business applications, and technology security. The Chief Information Officer (CIO) is a strategic executive responsible for developing and executing Alabama Credit Union's technology strategy in alignment with its strategic plan, business objectives, and member needs. The CIO ensures Alabama Credit Union maintains a secure, reliable, scalable, resilient, and innovative technology environment that enables exceptional member experiences, operational efficiency, business growth, and organizational agility. As the Enterprise Compliance Program Manager, you’ll play a key second\-line role in strengthening Southland Credit Union’s Compliance Management System and providing independent oversight across the organization. Reporting to the VP, Enterprise Risk Management, you’ll evaluate compliance risks, challenge business practices, monitor controls, oversee regulatory change, and help leadership understand where attention is needed.  

This is an individual\-contributor role with no direct reports. Your influence will come through sound judgment, thoughtful challenge, strong cross\-functional relationships, and the ability to turn complex regulatory requirements into clear, actionable risk guidance.
Major Duties and Responsibilities:
**Where Your Compliance Expertise Makes a Difference**
------------------------------------------------------


You’ll help design, maintain, and assess Southland’s enterprise Compliance Management System as part of an independent second\-line governance function. That includes maintaining the compliance risk inventory, governance calendar, monitoring and testing plan, issue\-escalation protocols, training oversight, management information, and program documentation.
A significant part of the role is independent monitoring and testing. You’ll develop and execute risk\-based compliance reviews that are separate from first\-line quality\-control activities, evaluating whether controls are appropriately designed and operating effectively. When you identify weaknesses, you’ll document the evidence and conclusions, identify systemic issues, and validate that remediation is sustainable.
You’ll also help the organization respond to regulatory change. You’ll identify applicable developments, document interpretations and impact assessments, identify accountable business owners, challenge implementation plans, track milestones, and independently assess readiness. Business owners remain responsible for implementation, while you provide the independent oversight and challenge needed to help ensure requirements are appropriately addressed.**Turning Risk Into Action**
----------------------------


The work extends across many areas of the organization. You’ll analyze complaint information across channels to identify trends and root causes, challenge corrective\-action plans, and escalate potential compliance, Fair Lending, UDAAP, operational, reputational, and regulatory risks. You’ll provide second\-line oversight of complaint processes without taking ownership of routine complaint handling.
You’ll maintain the enterprise Fair Lending and UDAAP risk\-assessment and monitoring framework, analyze outcomes and exceptions, document issues, and provide objective challenge where potential discrimination or consumer harm may exist. You’ll also provide second\-line review and escalation for marketing, advertising, disclosures, campaigns, and Member communications, working within clear boundaries so content owners retain responsibility for accuracy, approvals, and implementation.
Another important part of the role is helping the organization manage compliance risk as things change. Before new or modified products, services, systems, channels, vendors, disclosures, or Member journeys are implemented, you’ll perform second\-line compliance risk assessments, document conditions, challenge unresolved risks, and escalate material concerns through established governance.**Giving Leadership a Clear View of Compliance Risk**
-----------------------------------------------------


Strong compliance programs depend on information leaders can understand and act on. You’ll maintain the enterprise compliance issue inventory, assign risk ratings and escalation thresholds, monitor corrective\-action commitments, and prepare concise reporting for management committees, Senior Leadership, and the Board or an appropriate Board committee.
You’ll also facilitate the collection of compliance materials for regulatory examinations and compliance audits, coordinating request logistics, evidence control, and finding tracking with Audit and Controls or other designated partners.
Throughout the work, you’ll maintain clear boundaries between the second line and other functions. You’ll collaborate with BSA/AML/OFAC, Fraud Risk, Operational Risk, Legal, Information Security, and Internal Audit while maintaining the independence required of a second\-line risk function.
When significant or unresolved compliance exposure arises, you’ll use independent judgment, provide documented challenge, and escalate appropriately to the VP, Enterprise Risk Management and established governance committees.
Knowledge and Skills:
**What Helps You Succeed**
--------------------------

### **Experience**

* Demonstrated experience leading or materially supporting an enterprise\-wide Compliance Management System or second\-line compliance program within a regulated financial institution.
* Experience challenging and advising senior business owners across lending, deposits, payments, marketing, digital, operations, and Member\-facing channels while maintaining constructive relationships with Legal, other risk functions, and Internal Audit.

### **Education \& Certifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Risk Management, Law, or a related field preferred; an equivalent combination of relevant education and progressively responsible experience may be considered.
* A recognized consumer\-compliance certification, such as CRCM, is preferred.

jobs.description:
**Overview**


Join a team where innovation meets mission. Our AI, cloud, cyber, and modernization solutions save agencies thousands of hours, safeguard national security, and strengthen health and humanitarian missions worldwide. With more than 1,700\+ team members, 1,500\+ AI \& data experts, and 100\+ prime contracts, we deliver on a scale and with purpose.


We’ve been recognized as a Top Workplace by The Washington Post for six consecutive years and named to the Inc. 5000 list of Fastest\-Growing Private Companies in 13 of the past 14 years. Credence is a welcoming environment for those looking to grow and make a meaningful impact. We encourage employees to push boundaries and help solve critical, world\-changing federal challenges.

**Position Summary**


Credence has an upcoming need for a Senior Program Manager who will be primarily responsible for supporting the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center WAM (AFLCMC/WAM) directorate, F\-16 division at WPAFB, OH.


F\-16 “Viper” AFLCMC/WAM is headquartered at Hill Air Force Base with units located at Wright\-Patterson Air Force Base, Tyndall Air Force Base, Eglin Air Force Base, and Davis\-Monthan Air Force Base. The F\-16 “Viper” is a multi\-role fighter jet delivering air\-to\-air, air\-to\-ground, and surveillance capabilities for the United States Air Force (USAF) and Coalition Partners.


The F\-16 program has the largest Foreign Military Sales (FMS) program in U.S. history producing over 4,500 jets for 24 countries. Each F\-16 FMS case is uniquely tailored to country requirements / development / funding. Presently, FMS production orders exist through 2030\. Additionally, the F\-16 program includes the Multi\-National Fighter Program (MNFP). MNFP is not a typical FMS program, but a unique, cooperative USAF and development program implemented through the FMS process under the framework of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU). MNFP began in 1975 with the countries of Belgium, Denmark, the Netherlands, and Norway; Portugal joined in 2000\.

**Responsibilities include, but are not limited to the duties listed below**

* Assist in risk management, cost, schedule, and performance of various software development efforts in a program management role, and report on them monthly through use of the Project Management Resource Tool (PMRT).
* Assist to interpret, organize, execute and coordinate assignments within the context of the Government acquisition process.

* Support the program director at executive levels within the Government and other Contractor organizations, including major program reviews, inspections, conferences, and other program evaluations and major milestone events.

* Assist with strategic planning, program planning, systems integration, weapons integration, requirements assessment, and program evaluations.
* Assist to apply integration, communication, coordination, organizational, and planning expertise to technical and acquisition efforts across multiple F\-16 integration activities.
* Support Technical Interchange Meetings (TIMs) and working groups, serving as a liaison between user requirements and organic engineering activity.
* Assist to develop concise, coherent program status briefings to senior staff.
* Support the chief engineer in investigation and resolution of fielded program deficiencies, to include support of Crisis Management Teams (CMTs).
* Support and conduct studies and analysis of tradeoffs for incorporation of potential capabilities in future USAF OFP software.
* Advise and assist the Government with complex program management tasks, coordinating and managing multiple contracts, and identifying and confirming the annual funding requirements for those contracts.
* Assist with project cost estimates and have knowledge of the system engineering process and project Configuration Management (CM) requirements.
* Assist to investigate, analyze, plan, design, develop, implement, and evaluate solutions for project / program efforts; provide expert\-level issue resolution and recommendation support to achieve desired program outcomes to situations that may include, but not be limited to, the following functional areas: program management, logistics, maintenance, supply, financial management (FM), test, security management, information management, and contracting.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Tech Integration, Global Energy Sustainability & Automation (GESA)
jobs.description:
**DESCRIPTION**
---------------


The Technical Program Manager (TPM), Technology Integration \& Support is responsible for the end\-to\-end onboarding, integration, and deployment of automation vendor technologies (AGVs, AMRs, autonomous floor care, etc.) across Amazon's fulfillment and sortation network. This role serves as the primary technical liaison between external vendors and internal Amazon stakeholders — ensuring that all vendor technologies meet Amazon's network, security, and compliance standards before deployment.  

  

Key job responsibilities  

Vendor Technology Onboarding (40%)  

* Own the full lifecycle of vendor IT onboarding for AGV/AMR and automation technologies — from initial kick\-off through production deployment
* Conduct technical kick\-off meetings with vendor engineering teams to review Amazon IT requirements (network architecture, security, IoT device standards)
* Guide vendors through Amazon's onboarding documentation process: network diagrams, IT overview questionnaires, data element inventories, and wireless device assessment forms
* Manage 4–5 concurrent vendor onboarding projects at steady state; scale to 10\+ during peak periods
* Track onboarding status across all active vendors using Asana and/or SmartSheet dashboards


Network Architecture \& Configuration (20%)  

* Review and approve vendor network diagrams for compliance with Amazon network standards
* Configure VLANs, assign static IPs, generate PPSKs (pre\-shared keys) for WiFi 802\.11ax connectivity
* Coordinate ACL port configurations and firewall rule deployments with local IT and network engineering teams
* Validate that vendor IoT devices operate within approved frequency bands, protocols, and power levels


Security \& Compliance (15%)  

* Manage Third\-Party Security (TPS) assessments with Amazon InfoSec — submit tickets, gather vendor responses, track remediation
* Author and submit ANOW (Access Network Operations Workflow) requests for vendor network access
* Coordinate IoT device certification through Amazon's hardware qualification pipeline
* Ensure vendor technologies meet mTLS, SSO, and SiteConnect/VPN requirements before go\-live


Technical Assessments \& Documentation (10%)  

* Author formal Vendor Technical Assessment reports evaluating integration risk, network impact, and deployment readiness
* Document conditional approvals, pilot constraints, and scaling requirements for each technology
* Maintain a centralized knowledge base of approved devices, network configurations, and onboarding playbooks


Infrastructure Deployment Coordination (10%)  

* Coordinate physical infrastructure work with general contractors (GCs) — network rack installation, LVC/power cabling, IPC housing, fire alarm panel integration
* Develop and distribute BOMs (Bills of Materials) for site\-level technology deployments
* Establish and run weekly coordination meetings for multi\-site rollouts


Cross\-Functional Stakeholder Management (5%)  

* Serve as the single\-threaded owner for vendor IT integration across legal, category management, IT security, safety, demand intake, and local IT teams
* Manage escalations from site teams, EU/international stakeholders, and Amazon leadership
* Provide regular status updates to program leadership on vendor onboarding pipeline health

  

A day in the life  

A Day in the Life  

Every day as a Technical Program Manager on the Technology Integration \& Support team brings a dynamic mix of technical problem\-solving, vendor collaboration, and cross\-functional coordination. Here’s what a typical day looks like:  

You start your morning by reviewing your Asana and Taskei dashboards to check the status of 4–5 active vendor onboarding projects. You flag any blockers — maybe a vendor’s network diagram needs revisions before it can be approved, or a Third\-Party Security (TPS) assessment is awaiting InfoSec feedback. You prioritize your day around what will keep these projects moving forward.  

By mid\-morning, you’re leading a technical kick\-off call with a new AGV vendor’s engineering team. You walk them through Amazon’s IT requirements — network standards, security protocols, IoT device certification — and outline the onboarding documentation they’ll need to complete. You answer their questions about VLAN configurations, WiFi 802\.11ax connectivity, and mTLS requirements, translating Amazon’s standards into actionable steps for the vendor.  

After lunch, you shift into hands\-on technical work. You review a vendor’s submitted network diagram for compliance, configure VLAN assignments and static IPs for an upcoming pilot site, and generate PPSKs for wireless device connectivity. You coordinate with the local IT team on ACL port configurations and firewall rules that need to be deployed before the vendor’s equipment arrives on\-site.  

In the afternoon, you join a weekly coordination meeting for a multi\-site robotics rollout. You provide updates on the technology integration workstream, review the Bill of Materials for the next site, and align with general contractors on network rack installation timelines. After the meeting, you draft a Vendor Technical Assessment report evaluating a new automation technology’s integration risk, network impact, and deployment readiness.  

Throughout the day, you’re the single\-threaded owner connecting the dots between vendors, site teams, IT security, legal, and program leadership. You might field an escalation from a European site team about a connectivity issue, submit an ANOW request for vendor network access, or update leadership on the health of your vendor onboarding pipeline. No two days are exactly the same, but every day centers on making sure the right technology gets integrated safely, securely, and on schedule.  

  

About the team  

The GESA Development Engineering Automation Team is here to help provide Automated Solutions for projects ranging from AGV Tugger Systems and Floor Cleaning AMRs to Automated Tu

* Conduct technical kick\-off meetings with vendor engineering teams to review Amazon IT requirements (network architecture, security, IoT device standards)

jobs.description:
Job Description

As a global technology leader, Honeywell Process Technology (PT) enables the energy evolution, provides solutions that reduce emissions, and delivers innovative sustainable materials to our customers across industries. We are committed to driving sustainable practices and enhancing energy efficiency through cutting-edge technology and innovative solutions. Our team is dedicated to creating a sustainable future by empowering industries to transition toward cleaner energy sources and reduce their carbon footprint. Join us in our mission to make the world a more sustainable place while delivering exceptional value to our customers.

As Director of IT for OT, you will play a pivotal role in shaping and delivering technology capabilities that enable resilient, efficient, and scalable supply chain and plant operations across PT. This role will lead OT optimization and maintenance, with a strong emphasis on governance, cybersecurity, execution and compliance, while building and managing a high‑performing, multi‑disciplinary team to ensure technology investments deliver measurable business value and align with PT priorities.

Responsibilities

Key Responsibilities:

Define and execute PT OT strategy to optimize manufacturing systems—including MES, SCADA, PLCs, and data historians—to improve plant reliability, scalability, and operational performance.
Ensure standardization, lifecycle management, and cyber-secure deployment of OT systems across manufacturing sites, ensuring consistency, resilience, and risk mitigation.
Align OT architecture and data flows with ENIT systems to enable smart factory capabilities, digital manufacturing, and integrated operational insight.
Partner with site leadership and operations to prioritize OT investments, balance innovation with operational stability, and minimize disruption to plant execution.
Ensure robust governance, support models, and compliance frameworks are in place across OT environments, with a strong emphasis on cybersecurity, regulatory compliance, and safe operations.

Leadership & Financial Management

Lead and develop a high‑performing, multi‑disciplinary global team across OT, setting clear expectations and driving accountability for results.
Lead the M&A Infrastructure, Operations and Security Team
Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement, enabling teams to deliver results in a fast‑paced, matrixed environment.
Own and manage OT technology budgets, ensuring investments are aligned with PT business priorities and deliver measurable value and return on investment.
Establish and monitor KPIs and value realization metrics, making data‑driven course corrections to ensure operational, financial, and strategic objectives are met or exceeded.

Qualifications

Must Haves

A minimum of 8 years of experience in IT infrastructure management and/or ISC platforms.
Proven experience managing OT initiatives.

WE VALUE 

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
Master's degree in IT or related field
Leadership experience in two or more Information Technology, Engineering or Strategy functional areas 
Proven experience leading ERP transformations
Strong understanding of network architecture and security principles.
Excellent leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills.
Proven ability to drive strategic initiatives and foster collaboration across cross-functional teams.
Familiarity with compliance standards and regulations related to IT infrastructure.
Strong technical, quantitative, and analytical skills 
Experience in the manufacturing or chemical industry
Knowledge of cybersecurity and data privacy best practices Project management certification (e.g., PMP)
Understanding of key information technology solutions and practices 
Strong business/financial acumen and ability to translate new technology into business value 

The annual base salary range for this position in Illinois is $177,000 - $221,000. This position is incentive plan eligible. Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. Honeywell considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations.

In addition to a competitive salary, leading-edge work, and developing solutions side-by-side with dedicated experts in their fields, Honeywell employees are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package. This package includes employer subsidized Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance; Short-Term and Long-Term Disability; 401(k) match, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Accounts, EAP, and Educational Assistance; Parental Leave, Paid Time Off (for vacation, personal business, sick time, and parental leave), and 12 Paid Holidays. For more information visit: Benefits at Honeywell

The application period for the job is estimated to be 40 days from the job posting date; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.

About Us

Honeywell Technologies is a global, pure-play automation company with a legacy of innovating to help solve the world’s most mission-critical challenges, enhancing the quality of life for people and communities around the world. We serve the building, industrial and process sectors with a broad portfolio of services, solutions and products, underpinned by our Honeywell Technologies Accelerator operating system and Honeywell Technologies Forge intelligence layer. By combining the deep domain expertise of our more than 50,000 employees with decades of data from our global installed base, we are uniquely positioned to lead the industrial sector’s transition from automation to autonomy.

jobs.description:
Your opportunity

At Schwab, you’re empowered to make an impact on your career. Here, innovative thought meets creative problem solving, helping us challenge the status quo and transform the finance industry together. We believe in the importance of in-office collaboration and fully intend for the selected candidate for this role to work on site in the specified location(s).

As Schwab continues to expand its technology footprint across cloud, artificial intelligence, digital platforms, applications & APIs, and infrastructure services, the Technology Risk Management (TRM) team plays a critical role in helping ensure the company maintains a strong risk posture through independent oversight and risk-informed assurance activities.

TRM has an opening in the Cyber Threat & Insider Risk discipline for an individual contributor to serve as the primary subject matter expert for second line oversight, effective challenge, and risk reporting of Security Operations, Digital Forensics, and Incident Response capabilities, processes, and controls. More specifically, this role reviews risks and control activities over cyber detection, monitoring, investigation, containment, and response. You will assess control effectiveness, identify systemic weaknesses, and ensure alignment with enterprise policies and standards, regulatory expectations, and industry best practices. You will review and challenge issue identification, closure, risk acceptances related to risks in your domain. You will maintain visibility into the firm's emerging threats and implementation of AI technologies and influence the implementation of expected monitoring, investigation, and response control activities. Success requires a self-starter attitude, strong desire to learn, building collaborative relationships with business partners, and the ability to assess and communicate technical risk clearly to executive, committee, regulatory, and technical audiences.

Please note: This position is Monday through Friday during standard business hours and follows a hybrid work model with four days in the office and one day working from home. The role is available only in Indianapolis, IN; Omaha, NE; Austin, TX and Southlake, TX (DFW). Candidates must reside in or be willing to relocate at their own expense to one of the listed locations.

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis without employer sponsorship.

What you have

To ensure that we have fulfilled our promise of "challenging the status quo," this role has specific qualifications that successful candidates should have.

5+ years of experience in Risk Management, Cybersecurity, or Internal Audit
Demonstrated Risk Assessment, Risk Identification, and Risk Prioritization experience
Ability to apply Analytical Thinking and Problem Solving to complex technology risk information
Strong Communication skills with the ability to present clear conclusions to technical and executive audiences
Demonstrated Collaboration and Stakeholder Management Influence skills across multiple functions and organizational levels

Preferred Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree
CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC, or an equivalent technology risk, cybersecurity, audit certification
Experience identifying and assessing risks associated with security operations, digital forensics, and/or cybersecurity incident response
Financial services industry experience
Demonstrated Self-Starter, Influencing Others, and Building Collaborative Relationship competencies in an evolving environment

In addition to the salary range, this role is also eligible for bonus or incentive opportunities

At Schwab, you’re empowered to shape your future. Our Hybrid Work and Flexibility approach balances our ongoing commitment to workplace flexibility, serving our clients, and our strong belief in the value of being together in person on a regular basis.

We offer a competitive benefits package that takes care of the whole you – both today and in the future:

401(k) with company match and Employee stock purchase plan

Create and maintain Power BI dashboards to communicate project performance, portfolio status, milestones, and management metrics.
Develop and execute change management strategies to support system implementation and organizational adoption.
Engage stakeholders across departments to gather requirements, communicate progress, and resolve project-related challenges.

15+ years of project management experience.

jobs.title: Vice President of IT Management
jobs.description:
Company Description
Merchant Serv is a comprehensive merchant services provider that supports businesses with payment processing, point-of-sale (POS) systems, and virtual assistance solutions. The organization focuses on reducing or eliminating processing fees so businesses can reinvest savings into growth and operations. It offers secure, affordable, and powerful POS hardware tailored to small business needs, along with tools for online transactions, invoicing, recurring billing, and acceptance of major credit cards. Merchant Serv emphasizes personalized service, with local account executives collaborating closely with business leaders nationwide to design custom plans aligned with specific objectives. Prospective team members join a company committed to innovative, client-centric solutions in the payments and business services space.
Role Description
The Vice President of IT Management is a full-time remote role responsible for leading Merchant Serv’s overall information technology vision, strategy, and operations. This role oversees IT governance, infrastructure, security, and application environments that support payment processing platforms, POS solutions, and internal business systems. Day-to-day responsibilities include driving IT strategy and roadmaps, prioritizing and managing technology initiatives, and ensuring high system availability, scalability, and data protection. The Vice President of IT Management collaborates with executive leadership, product, operations, and client-facing teams to align technology investments with business goals and regulatory requirements. This role also leads and mentors IT teams, manages vendor relationships, monitors budgets and performance metrics, and continuously improves processes to support a secure, efficient, and innovative technology environment.
Qualifications

Strong foundation in information technology, including enterprise systems, infrastructure, cybersecurity, and cloud-based solutions.
Demonstrated experience in IT management and leadership, including building and guiding high-performing technical teams.
Proven ability to develop and execute IT strategy aligned with business goals, particularly in payments, financial services, or technology-driven organizations.
Expertise in project management and strategic planning to oversee complex, cross-functional IT initiatives and deliver them on time and within budget.
Excellent communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences.
Experience working in or supporting remote, distributed teams and using modern collaboration tools.
Knowledge of regulatory, compliance, and security standards relevant to payment processing and financial data (e.g., PCI-DSS) is highly beneficial.
Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field; advanced degree or relevant certifications (e.g., PMP, ITIL, CISSP) are a plus.
