jobs.title: Senior Manager, Technology & Security Compliance
jobs.description:
Are you an experienced technology risk and compliance leader ready to make a significant impact on how technology controls protect the integrity of a major enterprise? Join us as Senior Manager, Technology and Security Compliance
and take the lead in strengthening our Sarbanes-Oxley and IT General Controls framework while modernizing how technology risk and compliance are managed across the organization! You’ll shape a controls program that is critical to financial reporting and enterprise risk management, influence key decisions with senior leaders, and drive meaningful improvements across Technology and Cybersecurity. You’ll also build and lead a high-performing team that helps set the standard for technology compliance across the enterprise. This position is in Richmond, VA with a hybrid work schedule. We will consider a remote working option for the ideal applicant.

In this role, you’ll provide both strategic direction and day-to-day leadership across IT systems and security controls, audit readiness, issue remediation, and continuous improvement. You’ll engage closely with Technology, Information Security, Financial Operations, Internal Audit, External Audit, and business stakeholders to strengthen compliance and effectively manage technology risk. We’re looking for a leader with deep SOX and ITGC expertise, a strong understanding of technology risk and security controls, and the executive presence to provide focused program leadership and influence senior stakeholders.

What you will be doing:

Leading the SOX/ITGC controls team in planning, coordinating, and delivering technology control activities across the annual SOX lifecycle, while establishing clear roles, expectations, development plans, and accountability for quality execution.
Overseeing ITGC control design, control ownership alignment, evidence requirements, testing readiness, deficiency evaluation, issue remediation, management responses, and validation of corrective actions.
Establishing consistent standards, procedures, and quality expectations for control documentation, evidence collection, testing support, audit coordination, and remediation governance.
Driving continuous improvement of the SOX/ITGC control environment through simplification, automation, control rationalization, stronger accountability, improved reporting, and risk-based prioritization.
Coordinating SOX and ITGC activities across Technology, Cybersecurity, Finance, Internal Audit, External Audit, application owners, control owners, and business partners to maintain audit readiness and alignment.
Guiding control owners in strengthening control design, clarifying operating expectations, improving evidence quality, identifying root causes, resolving recurring control gaps, and integrating controls with broader technology risk practices.
Translating control risks, audit findings, remediation needs, testing status, control health, and readiness concerns into clear executive communications and decision points while presenting key risk themes to senior leaders and governance forums.

We want you to have:

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Finance, or a related field; Master’s degree preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in SOX compliance, ITGCs, IT audit, technology risk, internal audit, compliance, or related disciplines, including demonstrated experience leading SOX/ITGC activities.
5+ years of leadership experience managing controls teams, audit programs, compliance programs, or multi-functional technology risk initiatives.
Deep knowledge of SOX 404, ITGCs, automated controls, application controls, control dependency mapping, COSO, audit methodology, deficiency assessment, remediation governance, and management response development.
Solid understanding of technology operations and security controls that underpin financial reporting, including IAM, PAM, user access reviews, leading system modifications, infrastructure operations, cloud environments, logging, monitoring, backups, and job scheduling.
Demonstrated ability to establish effective control documentation and evidence standards, coordinate audit and testing activities, manage issue tracking and remediation, improve control execution, and deliver executive-level reporting.
Validated ability to influence senior team members, lead through ambiguity, guide high-performing teams, and communicate technology control risks and sophisticated compliance matters in a clear, executive-ready manner.
CISA, CISSP, CISM, CPA, CIA, or equivalent professional certification required; additional credentials such as CRMA, CGEIT, ISO 27001 Lead Auditor, or other relevant security, audit, risk, or governance certifications preferred.

jobs.description:
About Powerfleet

Powerfleet (Nasdaq: AIOT; JSE: PWR) is a global leader in the artificial intelligence of things (AIoT) software-as-a-service (SaaS) mobile asset industry. With more than 30 years of experience, Powerfleet unifies business operations through the ingestion, harmonization, and integration of data—regardless of source—and delivers actionable insights to help companies meet their strategic objectives around Safety, Compliance, Efficiency and Sustainability. Our people-first culture and relentless innovation empower customers to achieve measurable, sustainable business improvements. Powerfleet serves over 2.6 million subscribers across more than 48,000 customers in 120 countries, with commercial operations across every major continent.

Position Summary

Powerfleet is seeking a Vice President, Product & Technology PMO to lead strategic portfolio management and execution across Product, Engineering, Technology, and enterprise transformation initiatives. This role will establish and drive the operating model, governance, and execution discipline needed to translate Powerfleet’s strategic priorities into measurable business and customer outcomes.

The Vice President, Product & Technology PMO will provide a single, integrated view of major initiatives across the organization, ensuring alignment around priorities, capacity, dependencies, investments, risks, and delivery. Partnering closely with Product, Engineering, Finance, and executive leadership, this role will strengthen portfolio decision-making, improve delivery predictability, and create clear accountability for outcomes.

The ideal candidate is a highly experienced technology and transformation leader who combines strong portfolio management expertise with business and financial acumen and thrives in a fast-paced, global environment.

Key Responsibilities

Portfolio Strategy & Governance

Lead the Product & Technology PMO, including program management, project management, scrum, and delivery resources.
Establish and maintain portfolio governance across Product, Engineering, Technology, and enterprise transformation initiatives.
Develop and manage annual and quarterly planning, prioritization, capacity, and investment processes.
Create a single executive view of strategic initiatives, including milestones, dependencies, risks, investments, resource requirements, and expected outcomes.
Establish clear governance, decision-making, and accountability frameworks to support effective portfolio execution.
Ensure strategic investments remain aligned with organizational priorities and measurable business and customer outcomes.

Program & Delivery Excellence

Partner closely with Product and Engineering leaders to improve roadmap execution, delivery predictability, and time-to-market.
Oversee major technology and enterprise transformation initiatives, ensuring effective planning, execution, and risk management.
Drive cross-functional execution across complex programs involving multiple business functions, technologies, geographies, and stakeholders.
Identify and proactively address organizational, resource, technology, and delivery dependencies that may impact strategic initiatives.
Establish consistent program and portfolio management practices while enabling teams to operate with appropriate flexibility and agility.
Promote a culture of accountability, transparency, and continuous improvement across portfolio execution.

Executive Reporting & Performance Management

Develop executive dashboards and KPIs that provide clear visibility into portfolio health, delivery performance, investment, business value, and customer outcomes.
Provide executive leadership with timely, actionable insights into portfolio progress, risks, dependencies, and decisions required.
Establish mechanisms to measure value realization and business outcomes associated with strategic technology investments.
Improve transparency and consistency in how program performance and portfolio health are communicated across the organization.

Financial & Resource Management

Partner with Finance and executive leadership on portfolio investment decisions, resource allocation, capacity planning, and value realization.
Develop frameworks to evaluate and prioritize investments based on strategic alignment, expected value, resource requirements, and organizational capacity.
Monitor portfolio investments and resource utilization to support informed decision-making and effective allocation of resources.
Balance strategic priorities with available capacity to improve organizational focus and execution.

PMO Transformation & Innovation

Build and continuously evolve a modern, outcome-driven PMO focused on enabling execution rather than traditional project reporting.
Leverage automation, AI-enabled tools, and data-driven insights to improve planning, reporting, forecasting, risk management, and decision-making.
Identify opportunities to simplify processes, reduce administrative burden, and increase the speed and quality of portfolio decisions.
Establish scalable practices and tools that support Powerfleet’s continued growth and transformation.

Qualifications

15+ years of progressive experience across technology, product, program management, business transformation, and/or enterprise PMO leadership.
Significant experience leading global Product and Technology portfolios and complex, enterprise-wide transformation programs.
Demonstrated experience leading and developing program management, project management, scrum, and/or delivery teams.
Proven ability to partner effectively with C-suite executives and influence decisions across organizational and functional boundaries.
Strong understanding of software and product development, enterprise technology, and business transformation.
Experience supporting or leading major ERP, CRM, technology rationalization, SaaS, data, AI, and cloud initiatives.
Strong knowledge of portfolio management, strategic planning, capacity planning, resource allocation, and investment governance.
Demonstrated financial and business acumen, including experience evaluating investments and measuring value realization.
Strong executive communication and presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex portfolio information into clear, actionable insights.
Experience implementing modern portfolio management practices, tools, automation, and data-driven reporting.
Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, global, highly cross-functional environment.
Builder mindset with demonstrated success establishing or transforming a PMO into a strategic, outcome-focused function.

Success in the Role

Success in this role will be demonstrated by establishing a transparent and integrated Product & Technology portfolio; improving delivery predictability, prioritization, and capacity management; strengthening visibility into investments, risks, and dependencies; and creating clear accountability for the outcomes of Powerfleet’s most important technology and business transformation initiatives. This leader will help make strategy executable, improve organizational focus, and create greater predictability across execution.

The annual salary range for this full-time position is $230,000- $250,000
USD. Actual compensation within this range will be determined based on the candidate’s experience, skills, and location.

**Overview**
Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey, is a leading national research university and the State of New Jersey’s preeminent, comprehensive public institution of higher education. As one of the largest employers in the State of New Jersey, Rutgers University is committed not only to the students and the State that we serve, but also to the faculty and staff who work on our campuses.
For two consecutive years, Rutgers is ranked on Forbes’ list of America’s Best Large Employers. Rutgers holds \#64 of 500 employers and is the \#1 New Jersey employer on the publication’s 2023 list. Rutgers’ commitment to its employees includes maintaining and fostering a safe, diverse, and respectful workplace environment, creating employment opportunities for our nation’s military veterans, and ensuring accessibility and accommodation for individuals with disabilities.
  

**Posting Summary**
Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey is seeking a Director, Information Technology for the School of Environmental and Biological Sciences. Reporting to the Sr. Associate Dean for Finance and Administration, the IT Director provides strategic leadership and oversight of all information technology operations within the New Jersey Agricultural Experiment Station (NJAES) and the School of Environmental and Biological Sciences (SEBS). This includes web development, IT research and innovation, information security, and advanced research computing. The position also has overall responsibility for the day\-to\-day management of the unit’s technological infrastructure, equipment, and associated staff and budgets.
  

  

The IT Director will ensure alignment between functional leads, departmental staff, and central university IT initiatives. This structure will foster improved communication, reduce redundancy, and enhance the efficiency and quality of IT services delivered to faculty, staff, and students. Ultimately, this approach balances the benefits of embedded departmental expertise with the advantages of coordinated, school\-wide IT governance. Working directly with the Office of the Chief Information Officer (CIO) and OIT leadership, the Director will receive institutional guidance and implement central IT policies and initiatives under the purview of the CIO’s office and will represent SEBS/NJAES in all OIT functional groups and committees as requested.
  

  

Working closely with the CIO’s office and university IT leadership, the Director provides timely, accurate, and strategic guidance to the administration, faculty, and staff of SEBS/NJAES with regard to technology needs, changes, and opportunities. Under the Director’s leadership, SEBS/NJAES researchers benefit from high\-performance computing resources, analytics, and custom software solutions that streamline data processing, web development, and laboratory management. The position also leads the Programming and Web Development Office, supporting faculty, staff, students, and research centers on campus and across the state. The Director ensures secure, scalable, and reliable systems; develops and enforces IT policies; and provides expert guidance on cybersecurity, infrastructure modernization, and emerging technologies. Representing SEBS/NJAES in university\-wide IT initiatives, the IT Director fosters innovation, efficiency, and data accessibility to advance the teaching, research, and outreach missions of the unit.

Chief Technology Officer (CTO)

**AirParts Aero**  
**Northern Virginia / Washington, D.C. Area**  
**Executive Leadership \| Full\-Time**

Build the Technology Platform for the Future of Aviation Commerce

AirParts Aero is building the digital infrastructure for the global aerospace aftermarket.

We are creating a platform designed to connect aircraft operators, airlines, government customers, OEMs, distributors, MROs, repair stations, service providers, and aerospace suppliers through a unified commerce, data, and intelligence ecosystem.

We are looking for a **Chief Technology Officer** to help lead that transformation.

This is not a maintenance role.

We are looking for a deeply technical executive who can help define the architecture, engineering organization, development standards, and long\-term technology strategy behind a platform intended to operate at significant scale across the aerospace industry.

The right candidate will be both a **builder and a leader**—someone capable of setting long\-range technical direction while remaining close enough to the technology to challenge architecture, review critical decisions, and help solve difficult engineering problems alongside the team.

AirParts is expanding beyond traditional ecommerce into a broader aerospace operating platform.

* Enterprise integrations

The CTO will own AirParts’ overall technology architecture and engineering execution.

You will work directly with the CEO, Chief Strategy Officer, product leadership, operations, quality, and engineering teams to translate business requirements into durable technical systems.

The platform must bring together information from many different sources, including:

* OEM data
* Supplier feeds
* ERP systems
* Technical documents
* Government sources
* Historical transactions
* Seller\-provided product information
* Inventory records
* Certifications and traceability documents

The CTO should have experience designing systems that can normalize, reconcile, enrich, govern, and search large and complex datasets.

Experience with areas such as master data management, entity resolution, knowledge graphs, semantic search, or data provenance is highly valuable.

**AI**

Lead the technical strategy for AI across the AirParts platform.

Potential areas include:

* AI\-assisted search
* Procurement automation
* Seller and buyer assistants
* Document intelligence
* Data enrichment
* Classification and extraction
* Retrieval\-augmented generation
* Knowledge systems
* Workflow automation
* AI\-assisted operations

The successful candidate should understand the difference between a compelling AI demonstration and a secure, reliable production AI system.

**Search \& Discovery**

Help build a world\-class search experience for aerospace.

AirParts search must ultimately understand far more than keywords. It must help customers discover relevant parts, related products, technical information, inventory, suppliers, repair capabilities, and other commercially relevant information.

Experience with enterprise search, semantic retrieval, search ranking, vector search, or graph\-based discovery is strongly desirable.

**Engineering Leadership**

Build and lead a high\-performance engineering organization.

The CTO will establish and enforce strong development practices around:

* Automated testing
* CI/CD
* Code review
* Version control
* Architecture documentation
* Infrastructure as code
* Security

The goal is to create an engineering organization capable of shipping quickly without sacrificing reliability or technical discipline.

jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

About The IRC

The International Rescue Committee helps people whose lives and livelihoods are shattered by conflict and disaster to survive, recover, and gain control of their future. Founded in 1933 at the request of Albert Einstein, the IRC works with people forced to flee from war, conflict and disaster and the host communities that support them, as well as with those who remain within their homes and communities. At work today in over 40 countries and 26 U.S. cities, we restore safety, dignity and hope to millions who are uprooted and struggling to endure.

The IT department provides end-to-end solutions for the organization including application development & integration, system deployment, quality assurance & testing, and overall Project Management in an effort to help the organization build and implement the best solutions for its business needs.

The Opportunity

Every donation processed, every campaign that lands, every supporter who stays engaged — that's the technology you'll help build and deliver.

As IT Program Manager
, you'll manage the digital platforms behind one of the world's leading humanitarian organizations, directly enabling the fundraising that funds life-saving programs for displaced communities across the globe. This is a high-impact, fast-paced role at the intersection of technology delivery, stakeholder engagement, and mission-driven purpose.

You'll be a core member of our Project Management team, working across a modern MarTech ecosystem — including donation and e-commerce platforms (Fundraise Up, Springboard)
, our website (Drupal)
, Salesforce CRM
, Databricks
, email marketing (Pardot)
, and SMS platforms (Mobile Commons, Mogli)
. You'll own the delivery of enhancements, integrations, and new capability launches that keep the IRC's digital supporter experience best-in-class.

Why Join Us?

Real-world impact — your work directly supports humanitarian programs serving millions of people in crisis.
Breadth and ownership — lead a complex, multi-platform portfolio with genuine strategic influence from day one.
Collaborative culture — work alongside Product Managers, Data Engineers, Business Analysts, and business stakeholders in a distributed, multicultural team that's deeply committed to its mission.
Modern delivery — Agile/Scrum at the core, with room to shape how the team works.
Remote-first flexibility — work from anywhere in the US as part of a truly global organization.

What You'll Do

Drive end-to-end program delivery
Own the full lifecycle of multiple concurrent MarTech initiatives — from scope definition and roadmap planning through to launch and post-delivery review. Develop and maintain detailed project plans, work breakdown structures, and product backlogs, ensuring delivery against time, budget, and quality targets.

Champion Agile ways of working
Serve as Scrum Master for your project and product teams — coaching on Agile principles, facilitating sprint planning, standups, retrospectives, and reviews, and proactively removing blockers to keep delivery on track.

Keep stakeholders informed and aligned
Prepare clear, timely status reports covering scope, milestones, risks, and budget. Communicate confidently with audiences from engineers to senior executives, tailoring your message appropriately. Manage expectations and build trust across business and technology teams.

Manage budgets and vendors
Oversee budget tracking and vendor invoicing for your portfolio. Support cost estimation, validate expenditure, and contribute to the annual budget planning process to ensure initiatives are delivered within financial targets.

Lead business analysis activities
Work with the team to define and track functional and technical requirements, document current and future state processes, and coordinate testing activities. Partner closely with Business Analysts to ensure delivery is grounded in well-understood business needs.

Manage risk proactively
Maintain risk registers and mitigation plans. Surface issues early, escalate where needed, and keep the project leadership team ahead of potential blockers.

Shape the roadmap
Partner with Product Managers to build out product and project roadmaps that reflect both business priorities and technical realities, contributing to a coherent long-term vision for the MarTech portfolio.

What You'll Bring

You'll need:

3-6 years of experience in IT project or program management, ideally across e-commerce systems, donation platforms, website CMS, or other Marketing Technology.
A strong track record of delivering multiple concurrent projects on time and within budget.
Hands-on experience with Agile methodologies (Scrum, SAFe, or similar).
Experience using project management tools such as Jira or Monday.com.
Excellent stakeholder management and communication skills - comfortable engaging with variety of project collaborators from developers to executives.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to synthesize data and drive decision-making.
High levels of organization, initiative, and the ability to work independently in a distributed and fast-paced environment.

It'd Be Great If You Have

Experience with any of the platforms in scope: Fundraise Up, Springboard, Drupal, Salesforce, Pardot, Databricks.
Familiarity with non-profit fundraising, digital marketing, or supporter engagement processes.
Experience managing third-party vendors and project budgets.
Knowledge of SDLC methodologies (Waterfall and Agile).
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Visio for producing high-quality project artifacts.

Bonus Points For

A PMP, CSM, CSPO, or SAFe certification.
Experience working in international development, human rights, or a related field.
An understanding of payment processing platforms (Stripe, PayPal, etc.).

Benefits And Working Environment

Standard office working environment.
Currently the team is working in a hybrid model with one day per week in the office (unless the employee’s location is outside of NYC or London).
This role may require working remotely full or part time.
Some domestic or international travel depending on portfolio and project needs
UK-based candidates will need to work at a modified schedule of 12 PM - 8 PM at least 3 days a week.
Some domestic or international travel depending on portfolio and project needs

(US Pay Range: $88,277 - $103,222/yr; UK Pay Range: £49,598 - £60,040/yr) Posted pay ranges apply to US-based candidates. Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

Professional Standards:
All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**ArcSource Group, Inc.** is an award\-winning, woman\-owned small business providing program and project management, business optimization, training development and delivery, digital accessibility, administrative, and information technology support services to federal civilian and defense customers for more than 20 years. ArcSource combines agile project management expertise and technical skills with innovative, effective solutions to help our customers achieve mission objectives. ArcSource’s commitment to delivering high\-quality services is demonstrated through its appraised processes and ISO certifications for quality and IT management.


We are seeking a Digital Accessibility Program Manager to support the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Office of the Secretary (OS), Digital Accessibility Program.


As the Program Manager, this individual oversees contract performance, personnel, deliverables, governance, stakeholder coordination, resource allocation, risk management, and service quality. As the program’s Solutions Architect, this individual directly leads and performs the technical architecture, solution design, systems integration, web\-crawler strategy, data integration, automation, and technical\-improvement activities.


Position Location: Remote/telework


Clearance Level Required: None


Key Responsibilities:


Program Management


* Manage and coordinate all core and optional contract activities, ensuring performanceremainsaligned with HHS Digital Accessibility Programobjectivesand Government priorities.
* Develop,maintain, and execute the Project Management Plan and supporting Communications, Risk, Scope, Change, and Quality Management Plans.
* Manage contract deliverables, schedules, quality requirements, Government review cycles, priorities, dependencies, and deadlines.
* Manage contractor resource assignments and workload priorities, align staffing with Government needs, and matrix resources across task areas to prevent single points of failure.
* Collaborate with Government personnel toestablishand maintain key performance indicators; monitor performance and emerging trends; and recommend corrective actions and process improvements based on performance data.
* Maintain program governance, work breakdown structure, and backlog oversight, strategic planning, the program roadmap, risk and issue management, program records, and program\-maturity documentation.
* Coordinate with Government stakeholdersregardingpriorities, dependencies, risks, strategicobjectives, and resource needs;facilitateexecutive\-level communications and decision\-making; andidentifyand escalate significant program risks and issues.
* Plan and conduct Quarterly Program Management Reviews or Quarterly Business Reviews and communicate program status, performance, risks, issues, and decisions to Government and executive stakeholders.

Technical Solution Architecture


* Directly provide technical architecture and solution\-design leadership across the HHS Digital Accessibility Program.
* Assess program requirements and recommend technical solutions, tools, integrations, workflows, and automation opportunities.
* Support the administration and optimization of the enterprise accessibility web crawler, including its configuration, scanning strategies, integrations, calibration, and governance.
* Collaborate with accessibility testers to evaluate automated scan results, resolve false positives or inconsistencies, and improve scan calibration.
* Ensure technical solutions support applicable Section 508 and WCAG Level AA accessibility requirements.
* Design scalable approaches for collecting, integrating, analyzing, and reporting accessibility program data from service requests, testing results, web\-crawler outputs, helpdesk activities, and other program sources.
* Support theappropriate integrationof artificial intelligence, machine learning, natural\-language processing, dashboards, and automation into accessibility operations.
* Providetechnical guidance supporting Digital Accessibility Solution Center operations and embedded accessibility SME services.
* Identifytechnology risks, integration dependencies, technical constraints, and opportunities for modernization.
* Develop or contribute to technical standards, operating procedures, governance documentation, user guides, and solution roadmaps.
* Collaborate with HHS stakeholders, vendors, accessibility specialists, analysts, and program personnel to recommend sustainable technical solutions.
* Support the development and continued improvement of customer\-facing digital accessibility tools and Microsoft 365 or SharePoint\-based capabilities whenrequired.
* Participate directly in technical troubleshooting and the escalation of significant tool, platform, or service issues.

Education and Experience:


* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent relevant professional experience.
* Minimum of 10 years of experience in digital accessibility, solution architecture, systems integration, technical program management, and Federal program management.
* Current DHS Trusted Tester certification.
* Expert knowledge of Section 508, WCAG AA, DHS Trusted Testermethodology, and Federal digital accessibility requirements.

Preferred Skills and Experience:


* Federal contract and program management, including governance, performance management, risk, scope, change, quality, communications, KPI development, resource management, and executive stakeholder engagement.
* Enterprise solution architecture, systems integration, accessibility testing and monitoring platforms, web crawling, and automated accessibility scanning.
* Microsoft 365, SharePoint, project\-tracking tools, data architecture, analytics, dashboards, reporting, workflow automation, and process improvement.
* Application of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and natural\-language processing to operational data.
* Technical documentation, governance, stakeholder communication, technical consult

Vice President of Technology Management
jobs.description:
Company Description
FundsFlow - Deal Services is a specialist provider of deal close modelling and coordination services for investment funds operations, corporate M&A, and fundraising activities. Using one live model built from transaction documents, the company manages every close output for all stakeholders, ensuring accuracy and transparency. FundsFlow delivers coordinated closings across private equity, real estate, venture, and infrastructure transactions within three to four working days. The team focuses on efficient, technology-enabled processes that reduce operational risk and improve deal execution. Applicants can expect to work in a fast-paced, detail-oriented environment that supports complex, high-value transactions.
Role Description
The Vice President of Technology Management is a full-time, remote role responsible for leading the technology vision, strategy, and delivery for FundsFlow - Deal Services. This role oversees the design, implementation, and optimization of technology platforms that support live deal models and closing processes across multiple asset classes. Day-to-day responsibilities include directing IT strategy, supervising technology projects, managing vendor and stakeholder relationships, and ensuring systems are secure, scalable, and compliant. The Vice President collaborates with operations, product, and client teams to identify requirements, prioritize initiatives, and drive continuous improvement in tools and workflows. This position also mentors technology team members, sets performance goals, and establishes standards and best practices for technology management.
Qualifications

Strong analytical skills, including the ability to interpret complex transactional data and translate it into actionable technology requirements.
Expertise in Information Technology and IT Strategy, with a track record of designing and managing technology solutions in a financial services or transaction-oriented environment.
Proven experience in Project Management, including planning, execution, risk management, and delivery of technology initiatives on time and within budget.
Demonstrated capability in Strategic Planning, particularly in aligning technology roadmaps with business objectives and growth priorities.
Experience leading distributed or remote technology teams, with effective communication and collaboration skills across time zones.
Familiarity with tools and platforms used in financial operations, data management, and workflow automation; experience with cloud-based architectures is beneficial.
Background in investment funds, M&A, or deal operations is an advantage, with understanding of closing processes and stakeholder requirements.
Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field; advanced degree or relevant certifications (e.g., PMP, ITIL) are a plus.
Ability to operate independently, make informed decisions, and adapt to evolving business and technology needs in a high-pressure environment.

jobs.title: Program Manager (One Year Term)
jobs.description:
**Salary Grade**
----------------

  

Case Western Reserve University is committed to providing a transparent estimate of the salary range available for this position at the time of its posting. The salary range is between $49,257 and $62,311, depending on qualifications, experience, department budgets, and industry data.


Employees receive more than just a paycheck. University employees enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that includes excellent healthcare, retirement plans, tuition assistance, paid time off, and a winter recess.


**Job Description**
-------------------

  

POSITION OBJECTIVE


Our research in Alzheimer's disease aims to identify genetic factors associated with dementia, specifically Alzheimer's type. We are focused on increasing the representation of our study population by enrolling individuals from various ancestries. Through this, we seek to better understand the genetic underpinnings of memory loss and dementia. By collecting comprehensive data and biological samples, we will conduct genetic studies to identify potential genetic markers for dementia. The Program Manager will play a key role in managing these efforts, including participant recruitment, enrollment, and data oversight, while collaborating with study sites to ensure the success of recruitment and data collection initiatives. This is a full\-time, 1 year term position.

  

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS


* Identify and enroll eligible individuals and meet enrollment goals. Cultivate relationships with potential study participants; providing education, building trust and promoting interest in study activities. Work within human research protection processes: create and maintain appropriate protocol documents, confidentially and sensitively obtain and review family and medical histories and perform study specific interviews, instruments, and exams and identify, obtain and review appropriate medical records. Draw blood for genetic studies (training can be provided on the job). Prepare detailed participant exam reports for adjudication. Oversee and maintain complete research files and comprehensive databases including: consent forms, demographics, family and medical history forms and all other study specific forms and data. Document and maintain records to show effort that may not be reflected in enrollment numbers; events attended, sign\-ups, declines, phone calls, messages left, etc. Ensure compliance with IRB approved protocols and maintain data integrity. (70%)


* Collaborate with study leadership to create strategic approaches to identify and engage community and clinic partnerships. Build community partnerships through effective outreach efforts. Develop and implement community recruitment strategy and methods. Design and manage community events; reach out to various groups including but not limited to the Alzheimer's association, churches, community senior centers, social groups and caregiver support groups. Maintain open communication with physicians and office staff participating in the studies in the community. Working closely with the research staff, monitor and oversee research activities for the ascertainment, recruitment and enrollment of study participants for the DAWN study and ensure timelines and goals are met. Evaluate outreach efforts, identify areas for improvement, advise leadership of alternative methods/efforts, and implement adjustments. (10%)


* Facilitate communication and provide regular research updates for meetings. Work with the team to prepare a yearly participant newsletter. Participate in research group meetings locally and with the national network and communicate with the Research Project Director and Principal Investigators to ensure that work on the studies is being performed as needed and expected. Attend regular meetings locally and nationally with the principal investigators/coordinators and collaborators. Maintain open communication/collaboration between departments within and outside of institution. (10%)


* Provide training and instruction regarding enrollment and data entry procedures for others working on the study. (7%)

  

NONESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS


* May serve as a co\-author on research publications. (1%)


* Provide training regarding enrollment and data entry procedures for others who work with the studies. May supervise students and technicians. (1%)


* Perform other duties as assigned. (1%)

  

CONTACTS


Department: On\-going contact with supervisor. Contact with Research Project Director and PI as needed, staff, faculty, postdocs, and study participants. Will work closely with any other team members who work on the same study, coordinate research activities for the ascertainment, recruitment, and enrollment of study participants for the human genetics research studies in their area.


University: Contact as needed with purchasing, human resources, space, and facilities planning, environmental health, safety/contact, Research Administration, IRB, and Sponsored Projects Accounting.


External: Regular contact with community leaders, collaborators at other universities, institutions, and industry. Occasional contact with vendors.


Students: On\-going contact with students.

  

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITY


This position has no direct supervision of staff employees. May train new staff; direct the work of students.

  

QUALIFICATIONS


Experience 2 to 5 years of experience with minority community and familiarity with the aging population, preferably in the Cleveland area;


Education: Bachelor's degree required. Prefer Nursing degree. Must have and maintain a valid driver's license and be able to travel to participant homes, exam locations and community events, primarily within the local area.

  

REQUIRED SKILLS


* Ability to concisely and effectively communicate methods, concepts, and study designs to all groups as appropriate, relevant and indicated.


* Effective and professional interpersonal skills. Demonstrated expertise and strong leadership

jobs.description:
Husky TechnologiesTM is a company with a strong foundation built on innovation, close customer relationships, a strong sense of community and a unique culture and values. We are looking for people with the inspiration and talent to develop with us as we pursue our ambitious growth strategy.


Husky TechnologiesTM offers a wealth of opportunity for personal growth and development. Most importantly, Husky TechnologiesTM offers an opportunity to work with – and be challenged by – a team of great people. Our success is possible because of the creativity, intelligence and passion of our people around the world and their desire to lead change. At the same time, we are not afraid to expect a lot and strive for leadership in all of our key markets. We are a company taking on new challenges and for the right people this means exceptional career development opportunities, the chance to be part of a team that is the best in the world at what we do and the experience that comes from working in an environment that demands constant transformation and innovation.



Husky TechnologiesTM United States manufacturing facility is located in Milton, Vermont on a large, beautiful campus located just 30 minutes north of downtown Burlington, Vermont. Features include an onsite cafeteria, open office concept, fitness center, intramural sports activities and clean, state\-of\-the\-art manufacturing facilities with outstanding safety records. We offer a great work environment, competitive total compensation and attractive benefits package.  

  



Additional things you might like to know about working at Husky TechnologiesTM in Milton, Vermont;


* 200,000 square foot bright, clean machine shop
* Shift work premiums (25% afternoon shift and 40% evening shift)
* Annual incentive bonus
* Outstanding 401k contribution and match program
* 700 acres of private land to walk, bike, run or cross country ski
* On site gym facility
* On site cafeteria
* Opportunity to work for a world class company with great people

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Global Trade Compliance team operates across the Americas, EMEA, and APAC regions in close collaboration with Husky’s Legal department. The team defines, implements, and continuously improves processes and policies to ensure compliance with global export control, sanctions, and customs regulations.



As the Global Trade Compliance Program Manager, you will report to the Director, Global Trade Compliance \& Customs and serve as the program lead for enterprise\-wide trade compliance initiatives. This role will focus on managing global compliance projects, optimizing processes, and ensuring the successful integration of trade compliance requirements into Husky’s systems.



You will partner with cross\-functional teams—including Supply Chain, Engineering, IT, Finance, and Sales—to strengthen Husky’s global trade compliance framework, enhance operational efficiency, and reduce compliance risk across all regions.

Program and Project Management



Lead the planning, execution, and delivery of global trade compliance initiatives, including process optimization, technology integration, and system enhancements.



Manage the implementation of trade compliance modules within the ERP system to ensure alignment with global regulatory requirements.



Establish and maintain project governance, milestones, KPIs, and reporting mechanisms for trade compliance programs.



Coordinate global stakeholders to ensure timely completion of key deliverables and consistent global deployment of compliance practices.



Regulatory Compliance and Oversight



Stay current on international trade laws, import regulations/tariffs, export control regulations, and sanctions programs applicable to Husky’s business activities.



Translate complex regulatory requirements into actionable business processes and internal controls.



Collaborate with Engineering and Legal teams to establish export control measures and export authorization processes globally.



Monitor the effectiveness of trade compliance procedures and implement corrective actions as needed.



Classification, Licensing, and Documentation



Lead efforts to standardize global product classification processes, including export control, HTS, and country\-of\-origin determinations.



Develop and maintain processes for end\-use/end\-user certifications, license applications, and transaction due diligence.



Ensure accuracy and consistency in trade data, documentation, and system configurations supporting export and customs compliance.



Risk Management and Continuous Improvement



Conduct global risk assessments and audits to evaluate compliance performance and identify improvement opportunities.



Develop risk mitigation strategies to prevent export control or import customs violations.



Drive continuous improvement initiatives leveraging digital tools and automation to enhance compliance monitoring and reporting.



Support internal investigations and voluntary disclosures, when applicable.



Training, Communication, and Stakeholder Engagement



Develop and deliver global training programs to increase awareness of export control, sanctions, and customs requirements.



Promote a culture of compliance through proactive communication and cross\-functional collaboration.



Partner with IT, Supply Chain, and Finance to ensure trade compliance considerations are embedded in business processes.

jobs.title: Director - Finance & IT
jobs.description:
If you’re looking for a special place to build or grow your career, you’ve found it. Whether you’re an experienced professional, a recent college graduate or somewhere in between, IDEX is a place where you can apply your existing skills and learn new ones in an environment where you can make an impact.

With interesting opportunities in engineering, marketing, sales, supply chain, operations, HR, finance, and more across more than 40 diverse businesses (https://www.idexcorp.com/our-businesses/business-segments/) around the globe, chances are, we have something special for you.

Advanced Flow Solutions (AFS) includes the Liquid Controls and Corken branded products that make fluid transfer safe, accurate, and efficient. Liquid Controls primarily provide metering, fluid handling and data ecosystem for truck-based custody transfer of highly valuable fuels as well as product solutions to support other downstream oil & gas custody transfer applications. Corken offers a wide variety of industrial compression and pumping solutions for the process, energy, and transport industries. Applications include Autogas filling stations, bulk plant pumps, tank-car unloading, delivery truck, and transport. AFS is headquartered in Oklahoma City, OK with a sales/service office in Chicago, IL and an employee base of approximately 220+.

Our $115M+ growth‑focused business unit operates across two distinct revenue streams. The position reports to the Group Vice President, Finance Fire Safety Diversified Products and provides operational finance support to the AFS President and senior leadership team.

Duties/Responsibilities

Direct Finance & IT team and assist business unit President and senior leadership teams in the development of strategic plans and supporting objectives, while proactively managing supporting events to assure attainment of agreed upon performance.
Manage the company’s accounting & IT functions including general ledger, monthly closings and statutory requirements. Direct the financial reporting, financial planning, forecasting, budgeting and product & business line profitability analyses. Indirect management of Accounts Payable & Accounts Receivable (includes facilitation of credit process when holding shipments).
Responsible for the reporting, analysis and review of the AFS Consolidated Financials to Corporate Finance and AFS Leadership. AFS Consolidated includes AFS Core (OKC), Energy Asia and SAMPI. Financials to include monthly, quarterly and year-end actual, forecasted and Annual Operating Plan results.
Ensure effective cost accounting, inventory accounting and project costing / tracking processes across the business including control of physical inventories.
Instill financial discipline and rigor into investment analyses and justification, capital appropriation and capital budgeting processes.
Ensure BU’s compliance with IDEX internal policies and procedures to include, but not limited to, Finance Policies, IT policies, FP&A practices and changes, Controllership and other Accounting Policies, Sarbanes-Oxley compliance, Tax, Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and other legally mandated external financial reporting requirements that may be requested from IDEX corporate Finance and Accounting staff.
Manage the Interface with both internal and external auditors as well as provide the primary source of contact for all Corporate requirements of the aforementioned Policies and Regulations, including Trace Compliance and Anti-Corruption Policy
Deployment and application of IDEX Operating Model core processes based on needs of the business to assist in achieving defined organizational, financial, and business goals.
Build and develop a high performing and scalable team including talent pipeline and succession planning
Direct preparation of detailed financial analyses and management reporting results for presentation to the business unit President and senior leadership team (AFS), Segment and IDEX Senior Management.
Coordinate and administer an effective financial plan for the control of the company’s operations by implementing and effectuating an adequate control environment.
Drive, support and utilize the company’s OPEX process improvement initiatives including 8020.
ISO Role – Information Security Officer for AFS, reviews and approves certain IT changes regularly, reviews Cybersecurity risks with IT team monthly, quarterly review of IT Risk Assessment
Lead, direct and ensure the accuracy of forecasting and AOP Process including monthly, quarterly and ad hoc forecasting processes.

Education/Experience

Bachelor’s degree in accounting or finance required.
10+ years of relevant work experience in a similar-sized operation, including heavy management experience in financial and manufacturing accounting. Cost accounting expertise is required.
Experience in a process focused organization (80/20, Value Streams, Lean) and experience working with JDE and OneStream is highly desirable.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications.
Must have a proven track record, demonstrated by a progressive level of growth in responsibility.

Required Skills & Abilities

Deep understanding of accounting principles, practices, procedures, and internal controls across manual and automated systems; exercises sound independent judgment.
Strong analytical and forecasting skills with the ability to translate complex information into clear insights that support business growth.
Demonstrated leadership and supervisory capabilities, fostering teamwork, inclusivity, and high performance.
Excellent organizational skills and project management expertise, with strong oral and written communication abilities, including active listening.
Solid commercial and operational acumen with knowledge of markets, customers, competitors, and key manufacturing drivers.
High energy, hands on, results oriented leader who excels in cross functional environments.
Strategic thinker and problem solver capable of balancing detailed analysis with a broad business perspective.

Supervisory Responsibilities

This role oversees three direct reports and nine indirect reports.

Up to 10% domestic travel may be required.

Apply incident response, recovery, crisis communications, business continuity, and crisis coordination practices during high-pressure events.

Integrate FDA, HIPAA, SEC cyber disclosure, sanctions compliance, and other reporting considerations into response processes.

jobs.description:
Locations

Who We Are

Boston Consulting Group partners with leaders in business and society to tackle their most important challenges and capture their greatest opportunities. BCG was the pioneer in business strategy when it was founded in 1963. Today, we help clients with total transformation-inspiring complex change, enabling organizations to grow, building competitive advantage, and driving bottom-line impact.

To succeed, organizations must blend digital and human capabilities. Our diverse, global teams bring deep industry and functional expertise and a range of perspectives to spark change. BCG delivers solutions through leading-edge management consulting along with technology and design, corporate and digital ventures—and business purpose. We work in a uniquely collaborative model across the firm and throughout all levels of the client organization, generating results that allow our clients to thrive.

What You'll Do

BCG Federal operates within a federally regulated environment supporting consulting, cloud, software, data, and emerging AI technology capabilities. The Director, Federal Security Governance, Risk & Compliance (SGRC) serves as the senior accountable lead for the SGRC pillar. This role drives the strategy, risk governance, regulatory compliance, certification readiness, and control maturity agenda across all BCG Federal offerings.

The Director leads enterprise readiness and audit defense across key federal frameworks; including CMMC Level 2, NIST SP 800-171/53, FedRAMP and DFARS. Working closely with Security Architecture, the Director translates complex regulatory requirements into policy and control objectives, establishing the governance framework while Architecture designs the technical controls and secure cloud baselines.

Furthermore, this role pioneers Federal AI Governance, establishing guardrails, risk assessment protocols, and approval pathways for Generative AI and machine learning tools deployed across federal boundaries.

YOU’RE GOOD AT 

You excel at leading complex federal cybersecurity and compliance programs by combining technical GRC expertise, executive communication, organizational change management, and trusted stakeholder relationships.

YOUR DUTIES WILL INCLUDE

Lead the Federal GRC pillar strategy, roadmap, operating model, governance rhythm, reporting structure, and control maturity agenda across BCG Federal.
Direct enterprise compliance initiatives supporting DFARS, CMMC Level 2, NIST 800-171/, FedRAMP, AI governance, cloud security, and related federal cybersecurity requirements.
Partner closely with Security Architecture to align policies with technical engineering; defining what control outcomes are required while Architecture designs how technical controls and baselines are configured.
Own organizational readiness for federal assessments and certifications, including assessment scoping, SSP development, evidence preparation, stakeholder preparation, audit defense, C3PAO engagement, and executive reporting.
Establish and mature Federal AI Governance, including risk methodologies, safety frameworks (e.g., NIST AI RMF), boundary protections, and approval pathways for secure adoption of Generative AI and LLMs.
Own the federal risk register governance model, including risk identification, severity assessment, mitigation planning, exception management, escalation, and reporting.
Lead cybersecurity review of federal contracts, RFPs, client opportunities, software approvals, cloud service reviews, and third-party vendor risk management to support secure technology adoption.
Lead organizational change management for federal cybersecurity and compliance initiatives, including stakeholder alignment, communications, training, readiness tracking, and sustainment of new governance processes.
Oversee continuous monitoring (CONMON) governance, evidence traceability, recurring review cadences, POA&M tracking, and management reporting.
Define and deliver executive-level metrics, dashboards, QBR content, risk reporting, compliance status updates, and decision-ready materials for leadership.
Lead, mentor, onboard, and develop GRC personnel while improving team operating rhythms, accountability, prioritization, and delivery quality.

What You'll Bring

10+ years of experience in cybersecurity, information security, GRC, audit, compliance, risk management, or technology governance environments.
Demonstrated experience leading federal cybersecurity compliance programs (preferably supporting CMMC Level 2, NIST 800-171/53, FedRAMP) in consulting, cloud, SaaS, or federal contracting environments.
Direct experience leading or materially supporting external assessments, regulatory inquiries, audit readiness efforts, C3PAO assessments, evidence preparation, and audit defense.
Proven track record establishing AI Security Governance, evaluating machine learning/GenAI security risks, and applying federal AI risk management frameworks.
Proven ability to partner with Security Architecture, DevSecOps, and IT engineering teams to translate complex legal and federal requirements into practical operating baselines.
Strong organizational change management experience, including leading cross-functional process adoption, stakeholder readiness, communications, training, and sustainment of new operating models.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience developing executive briefings, policies, audit materials, and management-level reporting.
Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government Secret Clearance where required.

Additional info

*** For US locations only ***

In the US, we have a compensation transparency approach.

Total compensation for this role includes base salary, annual discretionary performance bonus, retirement contribution, and a market leading benefits package described below.

The base salary range for this role begins at $176,000.00 in our lowest cost US region and goes up to $199,830.00 in our highest cost US region. Your recruiting contact can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process.

This is an estimated range, however, specific base salaries within the range depend on various factors such as experience and skill set. It is not common for new BCG employees to be hired at the high-end of the salary range. BCG regularly reviews its ranges to ensure market competitiveness.

In addition to your base salary, your total compensation will include a bonus of up to 30% and a generous retirement contribution that starts at 5% and moves to 10% after 2 years.

All Of Our Plans Provide Best In Class Coverage

Zero dollar ($0) health insurance premiums for BCG employees, spouses, and children

Paid sick time on an as needed basis
